First of all: I am from Germany, so I apologize for eventual gramatical mistakes I will do in this review.
Portal Stories: Mel is a great example why free 2 play games are not automatically bad, it's quiet the contrary, because it is an awesome game.
Story
You play as Mel (surprise), a woman who has to test a vital chamber, known for example from the beginning of the original game. But it seems like there has been a problem, and when you awake, the entire facillity is dilapidated and you are all alone, except for a voice, leading you through the halls. That's all I will say, to not spoil anything. But I can say that PS:M has a cool story, not revolutionary like Silent Hill or Metal Gear, but it's more calm and easier and not so dramatic, but funny and with a nice plot twist at the end.
Graphic
PS:M is a Mod for Portal 2, so it uses the same engine, which is good, because Portal 2 still looks beautiful, and so does Mel's Spin Off. Textures have high resolutiones, the frame rate never falls beneath 60 fps and the lighting is also gorgeous. Plus the artistic aspectsshould be mentioned. New posters, the working facility and the new (old) Portal Gun show that their creators are full of creativity and also know how to put their ideas into the game.
Sound
All sound effects are ripped from the main game, so they sound awesome, like the Portal Gun, the buzzing of the hardlight bridges or (of course) the turrets. But the new acustics fit to the old ones perfectly. There are just three new voices, and all are clear and powerfull and bring the player the kind of person behind the voice nearer. The main voice is  from Stig Sydtangen, who already voiced Simon from Cry of Fear brilliantly. Plus, the musician behind the soundtrack is Harry Callaghan, also known as Harry101UK. If you don't know him, check his music on YT. Great stuff.
Puzzles
Last but not least, the main job the player has to do: the Testing Chambers. I played the so called Advanced Mode, and all I can say is: The name is justified. This game IS hard, but fair, like Dark Souls. Three of four times, I had to use a walkthrough to finish a chamber, because I just couldn't solve it. But even if I had to, I recommand everybody not to cheat like this. The solution is most times pretty near and easy to reach. Just hold on, don't think too complicated, but in small steps and you will make it, I promise!

Having played this for 400+ plus hours on the Xbox 360 (and I'll probably be ending up with the same if not more on Steam since steamworks is almost finished) I can safely say this is one of my favourite entries in the Resident Evil franchise.
Yes, it's not Resident Evil 4 but to me Resi 4 was EXTREMELY overrated. Its been released 3 times for gods sake. I didnt really enjoy 4 and
Resi 5 doesnt have the horror of the first few games but thats not a reason to not buy 5. 5 is a gem on its own.
The story is cheesy but in a good way. The locations are great through out the game, always changing. The characters are fantastic although Sheva does start to get a little annoying towards the end.
People often complain about how and why Chris is so beefy. I mean c'mon, he's got Albert f*cking Wesker as a nemesis! Chris got his♥♥♥♥♥handed to him back in Code Veronica!
Anyway, all in all this game is fantastic. Its got a ton of replay value. The weapons upgrading is a neat little system that will keep you busy. There's also Mercenaries when you've finished the story and that will keep you occupied for days. And as Im writing this review, Steam achievements have just been added and they include all DLC achievements too.
So when Resi 5 is moved to steamworks, you'll have even more content to play with!
Lost in Nightmares is fantastic, it tells the story of when Chris and Jill went to find Ozwell E Spencer and is creepy as hell.
Desperate Escape is just as good too, telling you how Josh and Jill escaped near the end.
Then theres also Mercenaries Reunion and Versus mode. There is an absolute ton to do on this game. I've 100% this game at least 5 times and I'd gladly do it all over again.
If you dont mind the missing element of survival horror then get this entry, for the love of god man.
Thank me later.

Saints Row 2 is f#cking good (not as good in PC, but that’s another story), we are all in agreement there. However, there’s people who hate The Third, while many others love it to no end. And me? I’m more on the love side, although I do see why many people hate it, and I agree with a lot of those points. So, is it worth buying? As usual, I will start with the stuff the game does poorly, then move up to the good sh#t:
First and foremost, completely gone is the half-serious stories of previous games. This one does have some half-serious moments but they’re overshadowed by a wacky storyline that goes more for goofiness and random crap all over the place. Is it THAT bad? At some points. Think of it this way: Saints Row 2 had it's share of toilet humor and it's share of good writen story. The Third bathed itself on the toilet humor and threw up on the story-line. If you did like how the story was done in Saints Row 2 you might end up disappointed with this one in that part. While it gets better as you play through it, the feeling of gang bands trying to dominate a city just fades away mid-way the game, and it's pretty much gone completely on the IV game.
Second, and a big problem the game has, is the game-breaking weapons. This game offers a weapon upgrade options that is actually quite a good idea, however the way it’s executed is poorly thought out. While character upgrades are mostly okay as the truly game-breaking stuff won’t be available until you pretty much finished the game, gun upgrades are there from the start and can be gotten in less than 30 minutes of gameplay by just searching for Genki and killing him, which rewards the player with INSANE amounts of money. And having guns with explosive bullets, SMG’s with fire bullets and shotguns with a ton of barrels is just game-breaking and makes the game insultingly easy even on Hard-core difficulty.
Something that I must also mention is that the new map feels really… Dead. As in, the previous one felt alive and unique. There’s also way less stuff to do, less activities, barely any buildings that matter, stuff like that do matter in open world games such as this.
There's also the animations. In cutscenes, characters are well animated, however out of them pretty much noone moves their eyes or mouth, it looks lazy, creepy and wrong in every way possible.
Lastly, the DLC’s. This game has way too many, however only THREE of them actually add anything GOOD (and that "GOOD" can be discussed), story missions which aren’t THAT great to begin with, and they’re pretty much ignored in the sequel as non-canon. Don’t bother with them, seriously. And if you do, only touch the story ones. There’s even DLC’s to make the game EVEN MORE EASY, and that’s just greedy and insulting. It also doesn't help that DLC's are unlocked seriously early on and most of them add vehicles and weapons that are just game-breaking so early on.
That being said, is the game good? You bet your♥♥♥♥♥ As I’ve said, the point of this game is more or less “Be unique” rather than the gangsta style the first games had. I do like the change as it brings some seriously memorable missions to the game, even though it lacks on secondary activities.
The story, while debatable, is fun as d#cks. There’s less enemy gangs to fight with, although you also sort of unlock a new over-powered new enemy later on which the story will focus on in the last act. The new characters are charming, feel alive and are fun to f#ck around with, specially Zimos and Kinzie, although it does lack on characters from previous games making cameos.
The game also has a way different look to it, going for a semi-cartoonish style that really fits all the crazy bullsh#t you’ll be doing on it. It also has a mega-truck-f#ck of cosmetic options to make your character feel unique, although the webpage to upload them and reuse them for SRIV has been broken for pretty much YEARS and doesn’t seem that it will be ever fixed.
Gameplay, ignoring the broken-#ss weapons, is fun. Specially the vehicles, which drive extremely well, while also delivering a good variety of them and the option to modify them for extra stupidity. Seriously, golf cars with nitro and spikes or transforming jets from any Michael Bay movie,  there’s tons of crap to choose from.
It must also be said, the game is fun as hell alone but it’s just SO MUCH DAMN FUN with a friend, playing through coop. The entire game is compatible with Coop and it’s been build with that in mind. It would be cool if the second player did appear on cutscenes however, but hey.
Lastly, something that most people usually ignore: the sound-track. SR2 usually only had licensed music for everything, but it changed with The Third, were there’s an OST behind the game for important parts of it, which I must say sounds f#cking great. It also has a total of 6 voices for the player character, 3 for males, 3 for females, and an extra joke voice, the zombie one, which I don’t recommend using for your first playthrough as you’ll miss on lots of sh#t.
In the end, is it worth it? Well, as Saints Row 2 on PC is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ port that barely seems to work, I’d say this is the best SR game you can get in Steam to begin with the series. Long, with ton of variety and other crap, it’s biggest drawback is a distinct lack on activities that were so much fun on previous games, such as Septic Avenger. Do I recommend it? Yeah, on a sale it’s a safe purchase, although IGNORE the DLC’s entirely, as they’re for the most part a complete rip-off and waste of mega-bytes. If you have a friend who could play it with you from the beginning to the end then you should buy it right away, as the amount of fun you'll have pretty much breaks Vegeta's scouter. Oh and, the end of Dex was never explained, that♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off quite a bit.
TL;DR Edition: The game is okay, works fine and it’s extremely fun with a friend through Coop. Servers to upload and download characters are long dead by lazy devs but the rest seems to work well. Overall, good game on a sale, although ignore the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DLC’s.

Plants VS Zombies is a defense game, you must place your plants on your lawn in one of 5 lanes to defend yourself from the oncoming zombies, in one of 5 lanes. It has a wealth of different plants and zombies, as well as 3 different maps, a few special levels, & a ton of minigames.
The game controls entirely with the mouse. I believe there are keyboard shortcuts, but i never used them. Regardless, the controls work well 10/10
The game sounds great. Every plant type has unique hit sounds, and the music is quite good. However, there isn’t much music, and the songs will get repetitive, because there are such a limited number of tracks in the game. 8/10
The games look beautiful, despite its 2009 release date. I have no complaints about how it looks to this day. This game is also a prime example of how a game should preform, given its content. We’re looking a game with zero 3D objects. The most intense thing you’re going to have to process are the sprites flying across the screen and your computer processing the hits. So what do you need to run this game? 1gig of ram, a 1.2Ghz processor, and 50MB of hard drive space. Perfection, proper optimization. I can enjoy this game on my Netbook, and my gaming pc, at almost equal rates of performance. 10/10
The game Gives you a main story mode to go through, which I’ll admit, had me re-do a couple of levels due to mistakes. But overall, it’s not that hard. However, there are tons of minigames that can get quite difficult. And if you still want a challenge, let’s see how long you can survive in infinite mode. 9/10
The story revolves around you, protecting your house from zombies, and your neighbor, Crazy Dave, who wishes to assist you. It’s cute and funny, but most importantly, it gets the job done. It’s really nothing special, but its polished enough to follow, and get you to the next level. 9/10

Broken, buggy, unfinished mess. This game was released on Greenlight, with the devs claiming that they would continue development. I understood this to mean that I was buying into an alpha that was in development still. The game feels about 40% complete. It's playable, but..
1. The AI is terrible. Both townie and mob.
2. The way you construct things is really hard to use, reminescent of RCT2 in that the isometric way the roofs tile makes it difficult for you to see if you placed a roof properly or not, but with the added annoyance that you need to have it so that your townies can reach it, so you need to place scaffolds everywhere. It's not fun, it feels like a chore.
3. The GUI seriously leaves a lot to be desired. Things with no tooltip, weird buttons that do unclear things, annoying flashing notification buttons every single time you pause/unpause..
4. Complete(or near complete) lack of satisfactory tutorials. It's not extremely hard to grasp like DF is, but there are strange things that I still don't understand, like why the entire underground of the map appears to be a giant dungeon and there is no underground stone.
5. Bugs.
6. No where near as much customization is possible as DF has, the environment is basically the same generic map each time.
All of these things are totally fixable. The problem? The devs have halted development. There hasn't been a patch in several months, no offical posts on the (horrible, echo chamber of a) forum, total silence. They kept complaining about being bogged down by all the work, and being burnt out. Plenty of devs are, but you don't just stop development completely. You take breaks, not quit. Ask people for ideas, don't quit. Open up your code so that others can work on it with you, don't quit.
Really disappointed I supported this project and got a broken, unfinished product. It's made me more cynical about buying into alphas, which isn't a good thing to be, either, I guess.
Don't buy this broken, unfinished mess. Truly a disappointment.

If you want a Dwarf Fortress Clone with graphics, please play Gnomoria.
This game is a very low quality and not fit for release.
It is a bummer that this was one of the first game to be ever Greenlit. Contrary to the public belief, this game is not and never was Early Access, yet we got an Alpha Version of the game sold. The store page also says that it will be continuously updated, but this does not happen. We get a patch all few months, which tends to break even more things.
The visuals are okay, but the menus are just downright amateurish, the tutorials useless and the game absolutely explains nothing. Hello Developers, it is 2013, wake up. You don't need to hold my hand, but if you don't explain how your game works, then there is not fun to be had. Crawling through half the internet to understand how the game works is not something you want.
Gnomoria is way more intuitive and has a clear progress line, even if you never played this genre.
Don't touch it with a 10 ft pole held by someone else on the other side of the street.

Boy was I in for a surprise.. and not the good kind.
I can sum up this game in one single word - Awful.

I started up a game and within minutes my villagers with their fantastic AI decided to disregard all common sense and took it in turns to throw themselves at a monster, resulting in most of my population dying right away.  Those who survived died of starvation a few in-game days later because I had no idea how I was meant to feed them, despite throwing food down right infront of them.
The game is filled with bugs, and there's been very little care and attention given to the game from the devs.  They've tried to pass off this game as being a full release, yet it's clearly still in alpha stage. Now that the devs have made a cool $2mil from this game, they couldn't care less, and it clearly shows.
Don't buy this game, not even for a laugh/joke.  These developers don't deserve any of your money.

A rather cute sandbox game set in medieval time.
The graphics is really nice retro. It is in a 45 degree turned isomettric view. This is also the low-point of it, it can't be turned that I know of. The menues are in the tiniest format, it's as easy to delete a game as it it to load it. That said, the menues inside the game are much better. Which is where the main production value seems to have been spent.
The sound is very nice, slightly reminiscent of Settlers, the very first game, in the mood at least. I wouldn't say it's intrusive but you won't remember it either, which to me is a good point for game music.
The actual game is fairly straight up management with the added fun of actual being able to lose quickly. The learning curve is steep, not overly but it will take a few games to get it like you want it. The management increases over time as you gain more people living in your town.
You are very much victim of circumstances with this game. Sometimes you find iron at the surface, sometimes there is none to save your life. The caravans are an offset but dreaming of gold statues after a few hours, you've really struck gold. This makes every game a new challenge which is nice. Pretty much as Civilization was.
The main thing to say about this game is that it's a time thief. You constantly look for the next thing you'll 'just do before quitting'. It sort of reminds you of minecraft in that aspect.

Something old, something new. Something borrowed, someone blue. Shovel Knight digs up snippets of past legendary classics while remaining its own game. The controls are so nice, so smooth. The amount of items you can get add variety to the gameplay, but don't cheapen the experience or force you to use the "best one". The music for each stage is wonderful and the boss battles are exciting, shoveling on just the right amount of challenge. You have to think of how to approach the combat situation, but not long enough to interrupt enjoyment.
The level design is no different. There will be moments where your tension peaks from just having cleared a difficult part, say bouncing off rising and falling enemies to make it across a bottomless chasm, but it makes the reward all the sweeter. In the same (ore) vein, secrets are littered across all the levels. You need a fair bit of ingenuity in the later levels, which pleases the mind. The game is not long, but not short; the ideal length of a game this price.
All of the characters you come across (bar the nameless passerbys) are definitively memorable and hold definitive, charming personalities. In fact, this entire game has personality and you can see the amount of work put into it.
In short, this game is more than worth the price and is a welcome addition to any Steam library. Dig inside yourself (and your wallet) and purchase this game as soon as you can! For Shovelry!

Shovel Knight was a game that I have followed from day one, and unfortunately, could not support it through Kickstarter. I always knew that it was going to be an amazing game that easily surpasses other games attempting to be retro, yet fresh. I'll say it now, Shovel Knight is the best game that I've played in years. This game's controls are all SNES-TIGHT (that's a good thing). You can easily follow the momentum of Shovel Knight as he runs and jumps. The difficulty is perfectly in place for the era it is portraying and truly feels like a SNES game. The penalties for dying aren't unforgiving, but it's enough to make you think twice before running around without precaution in certain areas. In the game, you have to collect treasure to earn money and buy upgrades for your health, magic, and equipment. This adds a very nice drive to exploring all of the secret areas available in order to become as strong as possible. On top of superb music, bosses, level design, and a "perfectly basic story," (in the sense that it's not complex because it doesn't need to be for this type of game, which is another good thing) the shovel is what makes this game EXTREMELY unique; you can do so many things with it, like finding magical weapons that a hidden merchant will give you in secret areas of the levels throughout the game. Everything about this game is absolutely fantastic! I literally walked away from this game after beating it with nothing bad to say about it. If you are a gamer that appreciates well-made retro games, it is an absolute must-buy that I would recommend everyone playing.

As playing this game for more than a hour, I can safely write this review.
I played this game back in 2009 and I had a blast. The last time I played this game was about 2 years ago. I'm back playing it, though. If you want a awesome Plants vs Zombies game that isn't infested with EA then buy this. Or in general, if you want a awesome tower defense, go with this.
There is only one downside. This game works perfectly with Windows 7 and lower. I have Windows 8.1... So what does that mean?
It means that if you play with 3D acceleration and Fullscreen there would be constant frame drops (this isn't my computer, there are people on the steam discussion page that have the same problem.) and weird blocky pixelated shapes around the zombies, the plants, everything... and the game would look really pixelated. But if you play in windowed mode and turn off 3D acceleration then everything is fine. I'm able to play the game in a good 120 FPS.
Overall, It's a really good tower defense. I would recommend it to anyone, not just gamers, but everyone. I had a blast back in 2009 when I played this game, and now I can play it again.

The commands are leaned towards automation so you dont have so much direct control, but enough for sure.
Note: this game was supposedly made by one programmer and one artist and the programmer has allegedly quit this project (and there's rumors this project was never a high priority thing for him) so dont expect the bugs to be fixed. I did enjoy the game, but that's because I like to discover new things, even find out the game mechanics instead of having them explained to me. Anyone who feels differently, you shouldn't buy this game because there's a lot finding-out to do with game mechanics, and that's most likely not gonna change.
The game mechanics work though, it's just a long try & fail process often. But you can also make up for your failures, like build new if buildings get destroyed (they shouldn't), get new villagers if old ones die (how compassionate) and even buy new animals from the visiting vendors.
I feel this game has a lot of potential, but is poorly polished. I dont know how much the developers make with this, but they could make 10 times more bucks if they polished it, hired the crew and decided to listen to people.

Tactical Intervention is amazing and very challenging (and really, really gory :D). Saying this is another counter-strike from a glance is fair enough, but once you sink into the game you realise that that statement is completely false. The depth in the game is incredible, while looking like a basic fps set in the style of counter-strike, it actually holds some of the most unique gameplay elements ive ever experienced.
You are constantly being shown new button presses that will show off new mechanics available to your, from holding 'e' and 'q' together (or seperately) , to pressing 'x' there are so many little hidden features to learn about, but the real excitement is trying new ways to use them in battle.
To extend on this, the animations and camera movements they use are really immersive, you'll really feel like you are one with your character, and thats where the rush comes from.
The game modes and missions are the most impressive. Never have I enjoyed missions online as much as I have in Tactical Intervention.
VIP ESCAPE IS ONE OF THE MOST IMPRESSIVE, IMMERSIVE AND FUN GAMETYPES I HAVE EVER PLAYED. Nothing feels better than selecting which car you want to ride in, choosing your seat, then drive-bying in a beautiful FULL FPS camera. Even just looking around the car to see all its detail is to be amazed about, the depth is insane and the way the car takes damage is spot on accurate.
The environment features are great too, the way glass beaitfully is torn apart by bullets is stunning, rappling (or running across) down the side of a skyscaper as you pass windows filled with enemies is a blast (and a thill when you can go through a window and sneek behind them).
All in all this is a excellent FREE TO PLAY game. 100% worth a download nad if you do, please take the time to try the whole game, its brutally hard at first, but give it time.

Very well done! I really hope the fan who created this decides to continue with more. This game looks fantastic, plays just as good as the original versions, and many of the puzzles are deliciously difficult! If you enjoyed Portal 1 & 2, but thought the single player game could have had a few more challenging test chambers, then you need to play Portal Stories: Mel. I'll admit I had to go to the Internet for hints on three different puzzles, something I never had to do with the other Portal games.
Portal Stories: Mel also incorporates almost all the game play elements from the first two games, so played in order (Portal 1 -> Portal 2 -> Portal Stories: Mel) there is a nice gradual and rewarding learning-to-challenge curve, in addition to interesting and storyline which keeps building upon itself. I personally loved the Portal 2 storyline and those characters the best though. Sorry Mel. ;)
Although horribly cliché, the best advice I have for Portal Stories: Mel is to not take anything for granted and to think outside the box. The puzzles in Portal 1 & 2 were visually designed to lead you to the answer. The Valve team did this purposely and very well by having certain interactive elements, like important portal-able surfaces, move or standout very obviously from the background. IMHO, Portal Stories: Mel made the puzzles much more challenging by having fewer visual clues and often including elements which looked significant but were not required for the solution. There are also a few test chambers where I had to use the Portal Gun and other game mechanics (weighted cubes, light bridges, etc.) in a way I never did in the previous games. The games physics and mechanics stay true to the original; the puzzle designers simple devised a couple subtly different combinations to solve their puzzles

A slightly souless successor to the epic Resident Evil 4. Resident Evil 5 stumbles around trying to recreate what was loved about Resident Evil 4, either by adapting from certain elements or completely copying the exact same events.
Thing is that it sort of works. You have the same combat as Res 4, same sort of atmosphere and style, it's all in there and works in the gameplay's favour. However Resident Evil 5's major flaw is that it seriously lacks the charm and personality Resident Evil 4 flourished in. In story, Resident Evil 4 comes across as a B-movie with a sense of self-awarness that the Resident Evil series should pretty much just always have considering how blatently stupid the writing is (although funny as hell). Resident Evil 5 once again starts trying to take itself seriously in it's story and enviroment which doesn't really help since the story this time around has lost any of the mystery elements that kept Resident Evil 4's balance of action and horror and is now more action oriented when now it's more about straight up saving the world from ultra bad guy man person.
Resident Evil 4 had it's set pieces moving at a very good rate. Soon enough while in the Village it becomes night, as new terrors emerge from the darkness, or the island and how
and of course there is the Castle to which any absurd thing can be just slammed right in there at any moment. It's designed in such a way that anything could be in the next room.
Resident Evil 5 doesn't really have anything new or continiously varied to it, and with the atmosphere now being kind of dead, there isn't too much to be remembered. The game for the most part repeats the same set pieces (Village, mines, labs) without adding to much to the mix or having the same twists and turns each place could have. There is really nothing in this game that could take you by suprise.
Is the game fun? I guess it depends from how much you can get out of it. It's more arcadey this time around, more bent on action than survival and atmosphere, plus a new co-op feature which at the most is "neat and occasionally enjoyable" while also being "a completely destructing element". Cooping with a buddy CAN be fun, sure all atmosphere of horror is now completely dead and burried at least 60 feet under concrete, but meh, it can work out as an action game. The partner AI however is so absurdly bad that it forces me to make a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ joke that questions whether or not the partner AI was symbolism of the mindless zombies of the past because you're AI partner clearly does not have a functioning goddamn mind.
You're AI partner can shoot the things. That's about it. It will shoot the things, and can do nothing else. Want to give your partner a weapon to help with shooting the things? She (your partner Sheva) will use her pistol unless either 1. She runs out of ammo for the pistol (although sometimes will literally go find pistol ammo to use over using her fully stocked shotgun) or 2. You take the pistol away from her forcing the AI to use the other weapons. It's actually really astounding.
Well, what else is there? A new inventory system. The cache case system is now thrown out and replaced with a real time 9 slot inventory overlay. This benefits the online play and the balance of pacing but also makes room for some massively stupid moments considering that every single item can take up a single space, aside from treasures. Occasionally you have to do trade offs if you have a full inventory and you gotta keep constantly switching around items just to either get some ammo, or health, or what have you. Possibly the stupidest part of all the inventory system is that armor takes up a inventory space. Beyond making no logical sense in any known universe, it is also obviously ridiculously inconvenience.
So that's Resident Evil 5. It's not techincally bad, but it's hallow and forgettable. Mediocre overall. That, and Resident Evil 4 got it's HD re-release on pc so there is no reason to not buy that.

You'll hate yourself for playing this game. You really will. You see, this entire game revolves around using an annoying UI to control villagers with an intensely annoying AI to handle logistics poorly and theoretically command them to eventually get around to doing the things you'd like to do. Sort of like Majesty, if you had to build your buildings from scratch, the only part of them that was technically necessary outside of aesthetics was the floor and your kingdom had a rule of law that all new citizens born in the nation must be dropped on their head.
You start out with about 11 morons to shepherd around, gradually kit them out in safety harnesses and protective helmets so that they'll be safe when you shove them out the door and hope that you'll lose as few as possible. Eventually you start getting heroes and such that you can use to explore the dungeons that extend deeper and deeper into the map and who protect your village from the increasingly difficult sieges laid by enemies, which can feel satisfying as hell to watch them fight after getting used to your moron brigade's perpetual failure.
This is also one of those games where you open a wiki while you play, just so you know. Otherwise your village will completely and totally fail because the only way to get new villagers depends on the happiness of the village, which is designed in a way that either you intentionally build your village with them in mind, or else you die and start over.
I dumped about thirty hours into it over the course of a week, then didn't touch it again afterward. That's pretty much the type of game this is.
: About a year later, coming back to this review I'm changing my review to negative and adjusting the sarcastic-praise slightly. The game is still fun (and from playing it a bit more, the AI is less moronic than I recalled), and the UI is tolerable now that I remember how it works (though it's still not good). That said, you shouldn't buy this game. Buying it supports the developer, and he abandoned it without shame. If you want to play it, by all means do so, just don't give the developer money in order to do that. I'll leave figuring out how to obtain the game without paying the absent dev up to you, but that's my suggestion.

I must admit to having been excited about this game for nearly a year before release, but I definitely was not disappointed in the slightest.
While Shovel Knight is clearly an homage to the oldschool NES platformers, they manage to go above and beyond. Yacht Club hit all of the best parts of that era while avoiding many of the mistakes that similar retro platformers make, namely in a willingness to improve on the mechanics rather than faithfully replicating the missteps and limitations of old games.
I think many who are major afficionados of the genre may be disappointed in the lack of difficulty at first, but Shovel Knight allows you to choose your own difficulty in many ways, which I think makes the game approachable for new players without compromising it for the veterans.
If I were to make one criticism, it's that the game felt a little bit short, but I think it has the Portal quality of being exactly as long as it needs to be. Always something new on every stage without a chance for any mechanic to go stale. They are also at work on additional content, meeting Kickstart stretch goals and such, so there is surely more on the way.
Between clever and tight gameplay, a breadth of appeal, gorgeous art, and one of my favorite game soundtracks of all time, I give Shovel Knight a hearty recommendation.

I must admit to having been excited about this game for nearly a year before release, but I definitely was not disappointed in the slightest.
While Shovel Knight is clearly an homage to the oldschool NES platformers, they manage to go above and beyond. Yacht Club hit all of the best parts of that era while avoiding many of the mistakes that similar retro platformers make, namely in a willingness to improve on the mechanics rather than faithfully replicating the missteps and limitations of old games.
I think many who are major afficionados of the genre may be disappointed in the lack of difficulty at first, but Shovel Knight allows you to choose your own difficulty in many ways, which I think makes the game approachable for new players without compromising it for the veterans.
If I were to make one criticism, it's that the game felt a little bit short, but I think it has the Portal quality of being exactly as long as it needs to be. Always something new on every stage without a chance for any mechanic to go stale. They are also at work on additional content, meeting Kickstart stretch goals and such, so there is surely more on the way.
Between clever and tight gameplay, a breadth of appeal, gorgeous art, and one of my favorite game soundtracks of all time, I give Shovel Knight a hearty recommendation.

Controls in SR3 are fluent and responsive. Activities are expansive and genuinely fun. (besides insurance fraud, I can never seem to get a good momentum going for it.). Cars feel kind of "floaty", but it's something you get use to quickly. Large amount of customisation in terms of your character, cars and clothing. (yet I can't find any good clothes or a good look for my male character, might just be me.)
AI isn't all that amazing, they do take cover and all, but most of the games difficulty comes from either them swarming you down or the specials, like the brutes or cyber ninjas, whom also help keep the game fresh. Your teammates on the other hand are completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥- they hardly ever kill enemies, they are completely useless against specials and if you're in a car waiting for your teammate and that teammate is under attack, you're done for. (Especially in an event like Trafficking, where the AI has to drive the car and you can't drive for♥♥♥♥♥♥)
Missions are great fun and well built, with every mission being different. Guns are sluggish and weak at the start (as expected), but after a few upgrades, you'll be mowing down enemies and shredding specials in no time.
Don't expect anything close to realistic here.

Atmosphere in SR3 for the most part is pretty good. Graphics are quite nice and cartoony and the games looks grand when it's night-time or when it rains, but don't expect anything Crysis 2 or even GTA IV level here. Cutscenes are pretty rough, especially when they do close-up shots of the characters. NPC's and vehicles pop up noticeably when driving, but at least it isn't SR2 level horrible, where the cars despawn the minute you turn your back. There are some smaller touches that are quite nice though, like how NPC's take out their umbrellas when it rains or how you can sometimes come across police officers arresting people. Voice acting is superb. (Even the zombie voice actor is spot on, he's my favorite.) I especially love hearing the commentary of the two announcers when playing Professor Genki's Super Ethical Reality Climax.
You also have a wide range of music on the radio, ranging from Classical music to my beloved Metal Rock.

Story is pretty straight forward. You're the notorious leader of the Saints and are on a quest to conquer Steelport and get revenge for those responsible for "killing" Gat ( *wink wink* (; ) and crashing the guys funeral, I mean that's just rude. Don't expect anything huge or worth noting here, the games priority was gameplay first, story second. There are sections in the game where you're given a choice, but these are nothing more than small boosts to certain things, like getting extra respect or extra money. These don't effect the ending at all, besides the very last choice, which is a nice welcome.

The game is a solid shooter, offering up a lot of hours of great murdering fun. While the story isn't all that interesting, it keeps the game moving and the content in this is impressive considering the price point. If you're here for a good deep story, you should probably look into the Grand Theft Auto series, for everyone else who are just looking for a good time, definitely pick this up.

Example: The game tracks how many hours you play each character; so why not introduce a system where as you play every 10 hours as a character, you earn a skill point to "morph" it's ability/gadget (skill points can be reset on the fly to build characters different ways each match). Bandit has shock batteries which could easily then (with this new system idea) have the choice of having a %damage increase of batteries he places, making them strong enough to counter Thatcher nades (but at the cost of 1 less battery to balance it out) OR instead of that, give him 1 less battery than default however they power 2 reinforced walls instead of just 1 for more defensive coverage (but don't do as much damage when electrifying a wall/razorwire, again to balance it out).
Just my thoughts.

This is, without a doubt, a fantastic example of what the modding community has to offer. Portal Stories: Mel is a Portal 2 mod that not only brings new puzzles to solve with the always reliable Portal Gun (which has a new "old" model here), but also a great story that could rival Valve's own.
This mod puts you in the role of Mel, a test subject during Aperture's early period (the 50s). However, as it tends to happen in Aperture, what was supposed to be an easy test turned out in disaster. I won't go into any more details, as that would spoil the story, but I must say it's great, and it takes place in the Portal timeline we all know and love (although with a different character).
As far as gameplay goes, it's pretty much Portal 2, although with a reskinned Portal Gun which, by the way, looks incredibly great. The player character, Mel, also has her own model, with matching attire for her 1950s origin as a test subject. The puzzles are quite challenging, and the game offers a Story Mode which has easier puzzles if you're having difficulties or just want to enjoy the story; even then, they don't rely on complicated maneuvers or speed; once you find the solution to a puzzle (which will take you some time to figure out), you'll realize how simple it is in execution, and that is, in my opinion, a positive. Difficulty in a Portal game should be about how hard it is to find the solution, not how fast you can execute it.
Another great detail is the soundtrack, with a similar feel to the one found in Portal 2, yet feels very differently, and fits the mod perfectly. Even before playing the mod, I loved listening to the soundtrack.
So, as I mentioned above, this is an excellent mod, and one that every Portal fan should play.

Towns could be a great game. It has a lot going for it. From the unique perspective to pleasing graphics it has the base to be a enjoyable time sink. Unfortunately the execution leaves a bit to be offered.
The game itself is quite good. You control a group of townspeople who have started a town that happens to be on top of an active dungeon system. You go through the usual gathering and building phases, but are also tasked with dealing with monsters. As you begin to dig into the earth looking for resources you find caverns and tunnels populated by the genres classic baddies. Everything from spiders to ogres await you hapless townsfolk as they dig deeper. You have to build up a guard force to keep you town safe from these creatures, and at a certain point you can even attract "adventurers" that are much more powerful and able to really beat down some baddies. It's a fun mix of dungeon discovery and building and offers quite a bit of content as is.
The bad part of it is that you can only pretty much count on it "as is" the "early access" part of this game is seriously slow. There have been exceptionally long gaps between developments, at some points even rumors development had stopped. Issues between developer and publisher have not helped things. So if you're willing to shell out for the game as it is now you will get quite a bit of content, just don't rest any solid hopes on it advancing. The chances of it ever actually being finished and brough inline with the initial goal of  the game is even less.
Because of the issues I simply cannot recommend this game to someone. If there were regular updates and some progress towards completion I would completely back this game, but as I can't recommend a game I don't think is ever going to be completed for someone to buy.

Shovel Knight is like walking into an old icecream shop, you walk to the counter and curiously ask any special deals, the man serving gives you a welcoming nod and directs you to a machine, as you approach the machine you see several differant flavours of icecream, however the man taps your shoulder, handing you a flier showing all icecream flavours combined into one glorious icecream cone.
You have your helping of Ducktales, a good scoop of Castlevania, an aftertaste of Mario 3, the Satisfaction of Zelda 2, Megaman toppings and even some sprinkles of Dark Souls, the man asks you to pay quite a bit for you to walk away with your cone, but it's one good and satisfying cone.
Icecream analogies aside, this is one good container of frozen desert! Sorry I'll stop now, but seriously, Shovel Knight manages to take all the elements of the previously mentioned games, blend them all seamlessly together, yet maintains an original feel whilst giving nostlagia for a simpler time, if that makes sense. Heck even the walking animation of Shovel Knight reminds me of Arthur from Ghosts 'n' Goblins.
You feel as if in you're in control at all times during gameplay, jumping, attacking and platforming all feel excellent and reliable, level design also never came off to me as cheap simply due to actually how good the control of Shovel Knight himself was.
Art style is enticingly retro with great sprite work, colour palettes and sound choices, the OST is pretty solid as well, A personal favourite being the track that plays during the first level. The plot is rather cliche, but still enjoyable, for me it was the likability of the main hero that made not shrug the story off.
For it's asking price, I did feel rather bothered by it, £7 would of been a perfect price for this game, but there is replayabillity in the form of New Game +s, achievements and unlockables. However this is a fine, fine tribute to an older time yet with fantastic gameplay. Definately worth considering.

The Good: If you like Portal, you want to play this. Levels are professionally designed, and the fact that they're fandom developed adds a few tricks that the original games didn't use, making them challenging, but beatable. I was worried the puzzle chambers would be naff, but they're right on par with Valve stuff. The off-track areas are incredibly detailed and well thought out.
The Bad: The voice acting isn't fantastic, but I appreciate the effort that went into it. It's designed to be a full stand-alone episode with it's own story and place in the Portal Universe.
The game is slow to get going... the first level is an obvious homage to the Half-life-style See Everthing Before It All Goes Down The Tubes, but the problem with that is we all know that the first section of half-life is just boring and takes too long. You could more or less skip the entire first chapter.
The writing is good, but not great... There are times when I found myself thinking 'Why am I doing this again? Who is this core and why do I care?' but you can dismiss it as 'Because Portal, here are puzzles, solve them.'
TL;DR: If you like portal you'll like this. Great mix of modern and old portal chambers, off-track sections, and story progression. It's not perfect, but I bet it didn't have a multi-million dollar budget behind it either. Because it's FREE. And I'd pay a lot more than free for something half as good as this.

I'm always up for a challenge when it comes to cooking a dish with many, many steps. But, sometimes my confidence gets the best of me and I end up miserably failing at cooking whatever it is I decided to make.
For years, I had my eye on this layered Bon Appetit magazine cover recipe, Devil's Food cake with a beautiful white fluffy peppermint frosting, silky dark chocolate ganache and smooth white chocolate cream. My mother collects magazines, so during Thanksgiving and Christmas I frequently read through them searching for the perfect recipe to make. A couple Christmases ago, I decided to try this one. As I attempted to assemble the dessert, everything went wrong. My ganache was too runny, the frosting was not thick enough and my cakes were too delicate; I ended up supporting the leaning tower of three cake layers with chopsticks, hoping and praying it would not collapse on my kitchen counter. I should have read the recipe more before I began making it because I was way in over my head.
Despite my failed efforts at making a cover-worthy recipe, I still don't back down from challenges, I just use better resources to figure out what I am doing. So, for all of you risk-takers and over-achievers, here are the ten most difficult recipes to make at home with some references to help you not only finish the dish, but make it a tasty one, too.
The salt crust must be packed tightly, otherwise the fish will be like a salt lick.
The salt crust must be packed tightly, otherwise the fish will be like a salt lick.
Photo by Molly Dunn
10. Salt-Crusted Fish
Having a chef make salt-crusted fish for you at a restaurant is a splendid treat. Despite an entire fish being covered in salt like someone being buried in sand at the beach, the plated result is not overly salted. But, if you don't pack the salt and egg white mixture tight enough, you risk salt crystals leaking into the fish as it cooks and when you break into the shell, creating an almost unbearable flavor. Ease your stress by having your butcher clean and gut your fish, then check out this video from Fine Cooking for a demonstration on preparing the salt dome and properly covering the entire fish.
9. Baked Alaska
If you thought making an ice cream cake was hard, try making Baked Alaska. This dessert not only requires you to form a mold of ice cream around a cake, but you must also cover it with a meringue, then bake it in the oven. After several hours of assembling and freezing, you pour a liquor over the baked meringue and ignite with a flame. Cold desserts on fire are pretty sweet.
Macarons are some of the most difficult pastries to make.
Macarons are some of the most difficult pastries to make.
Photo by Molly Dunn
8. Macarons
Not only are macarons challenging to perfectly execute, but if you make them in a city with so much humidity, like Houston, you're going to have a much more difficult time. Even if the weather is perfect, things can easily go awry. Every step is crucial -- from combining the egg whites with the sugar and almond flour and piping the mixture onto a cookie sheet to baking and cooling the pastries for the appropriate time. Bakers strive to create the perfect macaron and some have yet to accomplish that feat. Watch this video from Fine Cooking which demonstrates how to make the classic French dessert.
7. Breakfast
I don't know about you, but making breakfast for a family of four, or more, is a daunting task -- my mom and I always had a difficult time even working as a team. Props to every short order cook because I can never seem to find a way to put breakfast on the table at the same time or at the same temperature for each person. Pancakes never come out perfectly and they require constant tending; French toast makes a mess and you have to be careful not to cover your counter in eggs; you always burn some toast (even though it's the easiest task); and don't even try to make eggs for everyone, unless they all agree on scrambled. You're using practically every appliance in your kitchen at the same time. Just talking about it stresses me out.

Shovel Knight is one of those games that after I finish, I wish up to the heavens for there to be a sequel in a few years or sooner.
Shovel Knight is a great Mega Man-like clone, with little bits of story here and there, but the main focus here is the gameplay aspect.
Your main weapon is a shovel, which doesn't really sound right, but it makes sense why. Throughout stages, you can dig up piles of dirt that reveal treasure, which you can then use to buy upgrades, armor, and helpful items to give yourself a boost for that one area that really makes you want to break your keyboard or controller.
I disagree when people assume that graphics make a better game, because those people are wrong and are judging a book by its cover.
Take a look at the old NES games, and tell me that graphics make a good game.
Shovel Knight is a take on the old 8-bit classics we all grew up with and loved to play after school and on summer vacation.
Everything is there, the 8-bit graphics, chiptune music, and the difficulty: YES, I said difficulty.
This is a game at times makes you want to rip your hair out, but with trail and error, you succeed, and you feel satisfied. This game gives you satisfaction when you finish your goals.
Modern games today don't really serve any kind of punishment for failing, they just keep holding your hand, giving you handicaps all the time; there is no challenge anymore.
Shovel Knight is a great gem of a game that deserves its praises; everything about what makes a game a game is here.
This soon-to-be modern classic, hopefully get the sequel it deserves.

Coming from Counter-Strike 1.0, and having played all of the subsequent games in the franchise, I felt immediately at home when playing Tactical Intervention. The starting gun is bad, but after a few matches you will be able to afford a better gun, which you can keep for a week! Win a few more matches and you can afford all the kit you'll need for the week. During that week you will have saved up enough to buy it all over again.
Most people complaining about the game being pay to win are delusional. I was top of every server I played on while people were saying "pay 2 win" in chat. Well guess what? I didn't pay, and I still owned you over and over and over again. So get some SKILL. Because this game requires the same skills as CS plus the fact there is sprint, lean, roll, blind fire and melee which adds many flavours of gameplay.
The comparison to COD, especially in TDM, can't be ignored. Having played COD:MW2 extensively, it felt natural to patrol a portion of the map, sprinting from cover to cover - map knowledge giving you the edge. But the comparison only goes as far as sprint and melee. The gun mechanics are straight out of CS. With the added lean and roll mechanics, this is a fast-paced, tactical shooter unique to the genre with a feature-set to rival any AAA title.
The animations could be described as janky or quirky. But I prefer "hilarious". Many theraputic chuckles were had at the knockback and blindfire animations. They add charm to the game and it does not detract from the experience unless you really care about that sort of thing.
As far as game-modes go, there's plenty to explore here. The, CS equivalent, bomb/defuse mode is basically what you'd expect, except the spawn locations and bomb sites change from round-to-round. Hostage rescue missions are also a unique challenge, as you make entry into a building which may be filled with terrorist and many hostages, good target selection and accurate fire is important. Last but not least, VIP mode has you driving cars. There are 24/7 car servers if that's what you're into.
There's so many little things about this game which make it fun to play and being free-to-play it has a large player base and gets regular updates!
So, to summerise, WORTH PLAYING and NOT AS BAD AS PEOPLE SAY.

I had to stop fishing Trophy Rainbow Trout out in colarado just to write this review!
First of all I am not an avid fisherman in real life, I have gone fishing a few times as a kid as most people have, however I never really had the ability or drive to make it a real hobby. With that being said, I was still able to really enjoy this game, and am continuing to enjoy  it so far.
Now it should be noted that this game is very realistic, every fish has its own specific set of baits, water depths, and areas/ times of day they like. So if you have fished before, or know a bit about fishing it makes this game a bit easier. However even if you really don't know too much about fishing, a lot of the fun i personally had with this game, was researching what different fish liked, and trying to find my own areas and baits that worked for me.
Fish fights have been improved since the inital launch of this game, you can really feel the difference between a normal fish, and a trophy fish. Sometimes forcing you into a fish fight between 60 seconds, to a few minutes! It's really an exciting feeling when you first catch that big catch.
It should be noted that for the first hour of playing will be spent catching 0.5lb Blue Gills, and such. This is too introduce you to bobber fishing, once you are level 3, you should go buy a spoon, and try casting in the reeds for some bass, or throw some petfood on your bobber, and set the line to max and try to catch some catfish.
YOU SHOULD TRY THIS GAME.

BACKGROUND:
Saint's Row: the Third is the third entry in Volition's Saint's Row franchise. Much like the previous entries, the game offers a more humorous take on the standard third-person shooter franchise. The game incorporates custom characters and custom vehicles and allows players to feel like they are a part of the game. The witty humor and foul-mouthed protagonists make this game stand out from among the rest.
FACTORS AFFECTING REVIEW:
-I have not played this game in at least half of a year.
-I have not played much if any of the previous entries in the franchise.
-I could not have cared less about the vehicle customization because I did not care for making vehicles.
REVIEW:
My younger brother played this game on his old Xbox 360. I did not think it looked appealing at the time because I was mostly the stereotypical Nintendo nerd, but a few years later, I had beaten it and learned to love it. I had originally gotten this game in a Steam sale, and I have to say, I thoroughly enjoyed it. It was a funny game that did not take itself too seriously and had some great weapon variety and vehicle selection.
The story is pretty simple: you are the leader of the Third Street Saints, a criminal organization that has since licensed it's name to various merchandises and has become a global conglomerate. As you progress, you take over the city of Steelport and defeat any other organization that gets in your way. There are also a variety of side-missions and challenges that will help you stay entertained for hours on end. Additionally, there are multitudes of vehicles to collect and to customize that provide an interactive experience with the environment and provide an endless amount of enjoyment.
I cannot say much else about the game because it mostly follows the lines of a standard third-person shooter. You can shoot civilians, cops, and zombies and you can steal cars. It essentially follows the mechanics of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, but it adds a sense of dark humor to the otherwise serious genre. Oftentimes, the game will make fun of a serious situation such as a recent rampage or a mass shooting, but it works well with the execution and the impact of it.
FINAL THOUGHTS:
While not a unique, groundbreaking game, Saint's Row: the Third will provide hours of gameplay that will invoke both laughs and enjoyment. It offers the player a massive world to explore and a bundle of interesting characters to fall in love with. If you are a fan of Third-person shooters, this game is a must-have. If I could, I would replay this game all over again.
SCORE: 6.5/10

Saints Row The Third, as you can tell from the title, is the 3rd game of the franchise. I would say SR3 is the weakest game of the series, but the whole series is very good and very strong. In terms of the whole series, SR2 is my fav, hands down. I will end up comparing SR2 and 3 a lot in this review.
After the events of SR2, the Saints become total sellouts and go from being a badass gang, into celebrities. Right away this makes it not as interesting than the second game. As a great man once said, "Where Saints Row 2 is silly but is still grounded, Saints Row 3 drinks whackers aid from a clown's shoe." The game doesn't really give a reason on why things are happening. It just does things "Because it looks cool and has lots of action, AND EXPLOSIONS!!" The progression in this game is sloppy. The fact you can max out your character and achieve near god mode before you even finish Act 1! On top of that, this game throws you attack choppers and tanks pretty much right at the beginning of the game, taking away what little challenge this game offers.
The new gang members you get to join in your crew are all well written out and are all entertaining and fun to have around. Not only can you have a luchador named Angel who Hulk Hogen voices, but you can have Burt Mother F***ing Reynolds join you!
The character customization is, sadly, a step back from what SR2 had. SR2 had the ability where you could make a shemale, or the ugliest thing to ever grace the planet. Now you only have 2 gender options with nothing in between, where all males looked ripped to super f**king huge ripped, and females are always smexy looking. There is color options to make your character to look red or neon green. The clothing options have also took a step back. SR2 clothing options allowed for multiple layers like undershirt, shirt, dress coat, jacket, scarf, etc. The clothing options in SR3 is now upper body, lower body, head, shoes, etc. You can still make some great characters though!
The vehicles have been improved in terms of handling. The driving/flying in SR2 was a little wonky and could be aggravating at times (mostly the flying.) Thankfully they have improved them in SR3. The only drawback is the vehicle customizing is a little lackluster and not very interesting. Like I stated above though, this game just gives you attack choppers and tanks pretty much close to the start of the game, so it makes it too easy.
SR3 has many "Activities" to complete, which all involve driving around killing things, or running around killing things, or just drive around real fast. None of them are really new in terms of the SR2 activities.
The weapons in this game, I felt like they didn't have enough "weight" to them. I personally found them to not feel powerful enough, or feel like I was actually shooting the weapons. They just felt like they were going "pew pew pew" and not much else. I mostly just stuck to using the RPG when I hit infinite ammo just so I could kill people and move on.
The radio stations are great. You have everything from Metal, classical, rock/punk, the Adult Swim station that plays music from the shows like Metalocalypse and Aqua Teen Hunger Force, to pop music as well.
The graphics in this game still hold up today. They still look great and the game runs at a smooth 60FPS. Never had the game crash on me. The world of Steelport has tons of detail in it, like all the clothing stores such as Let's Pretend having a lot of cool stuff in it.
The only problem I really noticed was the sound. I've had where even if an NPC was standing in front of me, the audio from them sounded like it was coming from way behind me. A minor complaint though.
There is a co-op mode to play with a friend... 1 friend though. This has 2 player co-op, which is sad cause this game would have been much better if you were able to have 4 people in a game, even if you were not able to do missions, but just go around the city doing stuff.
Pros:
- Good character creator.
- Good selection of music.
- Great open world.
- Great characters. (Burt Mother F***ing Reynolds!!)
- Ok story.
- Over the top sillyness/action.
- Co-op.
- Easy achievements. (Only took me 46 hours to 100% complete everything.)
- Steam Cards.
Cons:
- Not as strong as Saints Row 2 in many ways.
- Gets very repetitive in terms of being "crazy/over the top."
- Most of the filler is activities and not so much in story.
- Most DLC is pointless or offers very little in terms of content.
- Only has 2 player co-op.
- Can't be a shemale (TRIGGERED)
The game is a solid 8/10 from me. (Saints Row 2 being a 9/10.) If you are looking for a "FUN" open world game that doesn't take things serious, this is a great game to pick up and have fun with a friend.

BACKGROUND:
Saint's Row: the Third is the third entry in Volition's Saint's Row franchise. Much like the previous entries, the game offers a more humorous take on the standard third-person shooter franchise. The game incorporates custom characters and custom vehicles and allows players to feel like they are a part of the game. The witty humor and foul-mouthed protagonists make this game stand out from among the rest.
FACTORS AFFECTING REVIEW:
-I have not played this game in at least half of a year.
-I have not played much if any of the previous entries in the franchise.
-I could not have cared less about the vehicle customization because I did not care for making vehicles.
REVIEW:
My younger brother played this game on his old Xbox 360. I did not think it looked appealing at the time because I was mostly the stereotypical Nintendo nerd, but a few years later, I had beaten it and learned to love it. I had originally gotten this game in a Steam sale, and I have to say, I thoroughly enjoyed it. It was a funny game that did not take itself too seriously and had some great weapon variety and vehicle selection.
The story is pretty simple: you are the leader of the Third Street Saints, a criminal organization that has since licensed it's name to various merchandises and has become a global conglomerate. As you progress, you take over the city of Steelport and defeat any other organization that gets in your way. There are also a variety of side-missions and challenges that will help you stay entertained for hours on end. Additionally, there are multitudes of vehicles to collect and to customize that provide an interactive experience with the environment and provide an endless amount of enjoyment.
I cannot say much else about the game because it mostly follows the lines of a standard third-person shooter. You can shoot civilians, cops, and zombies and you can steal cars. It essentially follows the mechanics of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, but it adds a sense of dark humor to the otherwise serious genre. Oftentimes, the game will make fun of a serious situation such as a recent rampage or a mass shooting, but it works well with the execution and the impact of it.
FINAL THOUGHTS:
While not a unique, groundbreaking game, Saint's Row: the Third will provide hours of gameplay that will invoke both laughs and enjoyment. It offers the player a massive world to explore and a bundle of interesting characters to fall in love with. If you are a fan of Third-person shooters, this game is a must-have. If I could, I would replay this game all over again.
SCORE: 6.5/10

Saints Row The Third, as you can tell from the title, is the 3rd game of the franchise. I would say SR3 is the weakest game of the series, but the whole series is very good and very strong. In terms of the whole series, SR2 is my fav, hands down. I will end up comparing SR2 and 3 a lot in this review.
After the events of SR2, the Saints become total sellouts and go from being a badass gang, into celebrities. Right away this makes it not as interesting than the second game. As a great man once said, "Where Saints Row 2 is silly but is still grounded, Saints Row 3 drinks whackers aid from a clown's shoe." The game doesn't really give a reason on why things are happening. It just does things "Because it looks cool and has lots of action, AND EXPLOSIONS!!" The progression in this game is sloppy. The fact you can max out your character and achieve near god mode before you even finish Act 1! On top of that, this game throws you attack choppers and tanks pretty much right at the beginning of the game, taking away what little challenge this game offers.
The new gang members you get to join in your crew are all well written out and are all entertaining and fun to have around. Not only can you have a luchador named Angel who Hulk Hogen voices, but you can have Burt Mother F***ing Reynolds join you!
The character customization is, sadly, a step back from what SR2 had. SR2 had the ability where you could make a shemale, or the ugliest thing to ever grace the planet. Now you only have 2 gender options with nothing in between, where all males looked ripped to super f**king huge ripped, and females are always smexy looking. There is color options to make your character to look red or neon green. The clothing options have also took a step back. SR2 clothing options allowed for multiple layers like undershirt, shirt, dress coat, jacket, scarf, etc. The clothing options in SR3 is now upper body, lower body, head, shoes, etc. You can still make some great characters though!
The vehicles have been improved in terms of handling. The driving/flying in SR2 was a little wonky and could be aggravating at times (mostly the flying.) Thankfully they have improved them in SR3. The only drawback is the vehicle customizing is a little lackluster and not very interesting. Like I stated above though, this game just gives you attack choppers and tanks pretty much close to the start of the game, so it makes it too easy.
SR3 has many "Activities" to complete, which all involve driving around killing things, or running around killing things, or just drive around real fast. None of them are really new in terms of the SR2 activities.
The weapons in this game, I felt like they didn't have enough "weight" to them. I personally found them to not feel powerful enough, or feel like I was actually shooting the weapons. They just felt like they were going "pew pew pew" and not much else. I mostly just stuck to using the RPG when I hit infinite ammo just so I could kill people and move on.
The radio stations are great. You have everything from Metal, classical, rock/punk, the Adult Swim station that plays music from the shows like Metalocalypse and Aqua Teen Hunger Force, to pop music as well.
The graphics in this game still hold up today. They still look great and the game runs at a smooth 60FPS. Never had the game crash on me. The world of Steelport has tons of detail in it, like all the clothing stores such as Let's Pretend having a lot of cool stuff in it.
The only problem I really noticed was the sound. I've had where even if an NPC was standing in front of me, the audio from them sounded like it was coming from way behind me. A minor complaint though.
There is a co-op mode to play with a friend... 1 friend though. This has 2 player co-op, which is sad cause this game would have been much better if you were able to have 4 people in a game, even if you were not able to do missions, but just go around the city doing stuff.
Pros:
- Good character creator.
- Good selection of music.
- Great open world.
- Great characters. (Burt Mother F***ing Reynolds!!)
- Ok story.
- Over the top sillyness/action.
- Co-op.
- Easy achievements. (Only took me 46 hours to 100% complete everything.)
- Steam Cards.
Cons:
- Not as strong as Saints Row 2 in many ways.
- Gets very repetitive in terms of being "crazy/over the top."
- Most of the filler is activities and not so much in story.
- Most DLC is pointless or offers very little in terms of content.
- Only has 2 player co-op.
- Can't be a shemale (TRIGGERED)
The game is a solid 8/10 from me. (Saints Row 2 being a 9/10.) If you are looking for a "FUN" open world game that doesn't take things serious, this is a great game to pick up and have fun with a friend.

If you're a fan of any kind of tactical shooter, I highly recommend giving this one a shot. I'll try and lay out a few reasons as to why I feel like you should or shouldn't pick this one up. Also, if you feel like you're tight on money, definitely pick up the starter edition. It is 100% worth the price, because everything is included in the starter edition that is included in the standard edition. The only difference is that you will have to play more to get the operators, but that's it. No extra fees, nothing exluded, the whole game.
PROS+++
1. The community for this game (while still having a few bad apples like every community does) is so helpful and so willing to work together. When you tell someone to stop, they hold position. When you tell them when to go in, they listen. People are also willing to understand if you are new, and apologize if they teamkill. Hell, sometimes when you accidentally teamkill them, they will already forgive you for it before you say anything, or sometimes even apologize for getting in your way.
2. The gunplay is smooth, and highly engaging. The leaning system in this game really sets it apart from other games and allows you to peek with ease and smooth movement.
3. Customization is top ♥♥♥♥ing notch here. From the different operator perks, to the customization of your guns attachments, to camos and skins you can unlock for your guns, charms you can have on your gun, even outfits and headgear for your operator. If you're a fan of customization at all, it definitely does not let up here.
4. Competitive replayability.  Anyone who has played any kind of ranked game knows that a ranked system with a competitive community allows for thousands of hours of replayability.
5. Updates to the game have been pretty good. The recent Operation Health received many different views, but I completely love it. My queue times got cut almost into a fourth of the time that I was in queue before, I can do other things in queue rather than staring at the screen, and i notice the hitreg being a lot smoother and better than before. Really enjoying it.
6. The graphics are absolutely gorgeous. Not much more to say here. It's also really well optimized. (at least now it is.)
CONS---
1. Uplay. It's not too big of a deal, but it's just annoying at times. Not too big of a gripe here, often forget I'm using Uplay.
2. No story mode. The situations allow for a good single player experience, as well as the terrorist hunt, but the game really shines here with the multiplayer. It was clearly designed around it.
3. (THIS COULD BE CONSIDERED A PRO) If you do get the starter edition, the operators will take some time, and you will have to play the game a bit of time to unlock all of the operators. However, you can do just fine with just a couple operators, and the game gives you a couple operators that are friendly to beginner players.
Overall, If you're a fan at all of Counter Strike, Rainbow six previous titles, or played SOCOM in the past, this is a must buy. I don't have the MOST hours on the game, but so far I've been having a blast. The game is gorgeous, fun, and an absolutely awesome time with a few friends, or solo. Being a huge fan of Portal 2, I followed this mod for months. I forgot about it until yesterday. Decided to check on it and sure enough it was out! So I downloaded it and just completed it.
Overall: This mod is very well done! A lot of effort went into creating it, with original models, new textures, and a portal gun that fits in pretty well with the lore this series has. The work put into this mod is well appreciated by me. It has a lot of nice touches that make it feel like a proper game. The people who worked on this were clearly passionate about it and it shows.
Now there are pros and cons to this mod. I'll start with the pros:
It greatly expands on old Apeture, which is my favorite part of Portal 2. You get to see Apeture back when it was designed by humans. Things are more colorful and have more of a human touch, as opposed to GlaDos' sterile designs. Virgil is a pretty well made character and very likable! The story is pretty good, and could possibly fit in with continuity if there was a little explaination as to why these characters aren't even hinted at in Portal 2.
I won't spoil too much here, but I will say that the tests were challenging, and that playing Portal 2, and getting good at Portal 2 are required before taking this mod on. The puzzle solutions are creative at times, with cube respawning being an interesting new way to solve puzzles. I did get stuck a few times, once for over an hour which makes me feel like an idiot since the solution was obvious. Things are a bit more cryptic with this game which personally I didn't like, but to each their own. You go off the tracks more in this game which is a plus.
Now there are some negatives I spotted while playing. Some things can be improved, others simply can't be helped. These are nitpicks more then anything.
The first really can't be helped. Cave Johnson's voice in the beginning. I realize getting J.K. Simmons to reprise the role is beyond the capabilities of the mod team, but it would have been nice if it were feasible. Some of his lines also seemed a bit out there for 50's Cave.
In the beginning you can walk around the town, but there isn't much to see. Too many out of order bathrooms, too many locked doors. The 50's cars have a slightly too low res texture, there are only 2 designs, with the black car being featured way too much.
There are no people to interact with in the beginning, which is strange since there are people there, but the closest you come to interaction is one guy sleeping in a ticket booth. The sheer lack of people, apart from a few in inaccessible background areas gives the beginning a rather creepy feel. Keep in mind this was 50's Apeture. Things weren't supposed to be completely automated yet. You just get a pre recorded voice guiding you to a sleeping chamber, nobody to talk to, and just an air of creepiness and desertion.
The beginning also features a few models directly reused from Portal 2, which means you get old looking catwalks and loudspeakers which clash with the otherwise near pristine looking surroundings.
Getting into the game properly I noticed a pattern with the test chambers, a repeating theme: Get cubes past fizzlers. While it's a novel idea for solving puzzles, it's used way too much in my opinion. The gameplay becomes less about how to get the exit open, then how to get a cube there without fizzling it. Even a test chamber that's said to have been made by GlaDos has this mechanic. and just feels like yet another test chamber.
Another theme running throughout the gameplay is pulling old fashioned double pole switches. It works for the beginning, but later on it would make more sense to have buttons to press instead.
Again, these are nitpicks. They're just minor things, some which could be improved, others that I suppose can't be helped. Even with these minor flaws, this mod is very much worth playing for Portal 2 fans.

Shovel Knight is a game that's tough as a combination of nails, rocks, and steel. Perhaps I'm bad at video games, but this is possibly the hardest video game I've ever played, and I must say it was an enjoyable experience.
The graphics, sound, and most other aspects of the game would probably give instant nostalgia to those who were alive and old enough to witness the NES era, as the game copies all of these points perfectly. Perhaps they cheated in some areas, but I wouldn't know, as I wasn't alive during the NES era to experience it. Nontheless, whether you were alive then or weren't, the game's music and graphics are amazing and work well for the whole game.
The level design is ingeneous, reminding me of Mega Man's level designs as the game teaches you how to play it while you play it. Meaning, as you play the game, you'll learn techniques and information about the game due to the ingeneous structure of the levels. It's brilliant, and each death or defeat that you have feels justified, because it was your screw up, not the game dev's.
Apparently the game should only take about an hour or so, but it took me over fourteen, mostly because I'm terrible at the game, but it didn't stop me from enjoying it. I would say this game is beyond a reasonable doubt worth full price, but if you're not willing to pay it, I'm sure it'll be up for sale eventually. In the mean time, watch some LP's to ebb your ever-hungry... hunger for this game's spectacularness.
I give this game a 9/10, and recommend it to everyone that I know or anyone that likes a good vidya game.
