Another Portal Mod that manages to perfectly recreate the Aperture aesthetic, screw it down, then can and sell it to you (in a can!) for only 25 cents. Chilled to just 3 Kelvin!
The portal universe gets a little bigger this time, and we get to see what aperture looked like back in its heyday (take a look around, check everything out, get behind the scenes, and read all the posters and flyers) before things go awry (as they usually do down in the salt mine) and Mel is woken up about 60-something years past her wake-up time.
At times the antagonist of the piece didn't ring all the right bells for me, but it's hardly a deal-breaker. Also: if you don't love your portal gun you have absolutely no soul. None. I'm not going to spoil anything more than that.
The tests this time around are different, and in a good way. Not different enough to be impossible, but the designers have relied on some different mechanics to solve problems, ones that are easy enough to grasp once you realise what they're doing, they're also complicated enough to keep tripping you up even when you know what's going on. This actually adds to the game's replayability. I'll never forget the few times I looked up solutions to a chamber and just facepalmed at how simple the solution I was missing was. So there's some real lateral thinking required here, and when you solve the really tricky chambers on your own, it's a really good feeling.
All in all, for a free mod, you are getting an absolute bargain. I would highly recommend this game at up to $10 and beyond (although how much further depends on the amount of content it has). Prism have done an amazing job, and to get this game for free feels almost like stealing.

Plants vs. Zombies is an alltime classic that has, for many years, provided a fun and strategic yet surprisingly simple style of game play. You are the overseer, a man of mystery who manipulates plants grown in gardens onto the front lines of your lawn, rows up to 6, all facing one direction... the graveyard across the lawn. There, evil zombies rise from their grave to pass through your lawn and eat your brainz. Progressively getting more and more difficult as each level passes, the game however never stretched away from impossible odds, but some levels get pretty intense. Whether it's on the front lines of your lawn to the darkest of places, to your backyard, even up at your roof, these resiliant zombies will not rest until you are dealt with. How will you respond!? You use plants... ok hear me out. These plants have been trained to combat zombies, each with their own perks. You are also given an inventory allowing you to choose a variety of plants, choose wisely. The sun drops 'sun' which allows you to purchase plants to fight off the hoards. There are also minigames, boss battles, puzzles, shops, farms for money, and more. Each time you win a level, you earn a new gift. See money on the floor? Grab it! You use it for your tree, farm and shop, all of which give you tips and additional money. Patience though, all good things come to those who wait. Anyways it is a fenomenal game then, and it still is now. GIVE IT A TRY. Also thank you to all to who created the game, through the years, I have always came back to this game due to its originality, no wonder it has gotten a GAME OF THE YEAR AWARD. Will you become a hero? Play PvZ TODAY!!!

So, I heard a lot of stories about this game and they weren't good ones. "It's not Resident Evil anymore" they said. "Resident Evil 4 is better than this" they said. "Every Resident Evil after the 4th iteration is bad" they said. And what can I say? They're not right. It's as simple as that.
As harsh as this truth may be, Resident Evil has shifted its focus from classic survival horror to a more action oriented gameplay experience. But this already happened after Resident Evil 3: Nemesis. The fixed camera angles are missing in favor of a 3rd person perspective, the classic zombies from the first three games are no more and the story of the Umbrella corporation ended long before the setting of Resident Evil 4. So it shouldn't come as a surprise that Resident Evil 5, just like it's predecessor, is more action oriented than the classic Resident Evil titles.
In fact, a lot of people liked Resident Evil 4, but the fifth iteration wasn't all that well received. And I am asking myself: why is that? To me, Resident Evil 5 has numerous changes that made it better than it's predecessor. The controls on PC are marvelous compared to Resident Evil 4, the graphics are more advanced, some animations are nicer, the mercenaries mode is better and it features some new enemies. But I also have to say that Resident Evil 5 plays a lot like Resident Evil 4.
A lot of the animations are recycled or reused, especially those for the Majini (which are basically reskinned Ganados from Resident Evil 4), it is still not possible to move whilst shooting and it just feels like Resident Evil 4, the only real change being the setting in Africa (so you're fighting against black Ganados, kind of) and the partner-mechanic, allowing for co-op or a single player mode with benefits (or annoyances). Well, the UI's different, too. Especially the inventory. It's gotten pretty small actually, compared to the Resident Evil 4 inventory when maxed out. You got nine inventory slots in total which means that you can only afford to take 3 weapons with you at most, I recommend carrying 2 weapons for each character so that you can still fit in first aid spray/herbs and grenades - or a bullet proof vest.
Also, the merchant from Resident Evil 4 is gone, that iconic figure. You will be missed. Aside from that, the health bar system is different, too. Instead of featuring a segmented bar which can be increased by consuming yellow herbs in combination with green herbs and red herbs, you have a full bar with a set amount of health - rendering the yellow herb obsolete in the process, which is why it was removed.
But aside from all this... Resident Evil 5 plays like Resident Evil 4 - just a little bit more simplified and with better looks. The puzzles, the combat, movement, boss battles and most of the animations are still the same. And what can I say? I liked Resident Evil 4 for what it was. The PC port was a horrible mess but I liked it nontheless. And so, Resident Evil 5 is also a game I would call a "nice game". Not outstandingly great by any means. It's a 3rd person action shooting game in the Resident Evil universe.
Fans of the original games won't like Resident Evil 5 nor will they like Resident Evil 4 all that much. But if you don't give a damn about the "true Resident Evil experience" and just want to play a nice 3rd person shooter with mutants and zombies in it, featuring some of your favourite characters from the Resident Evil universe and a bit of interesting lore, I recommend this game to you. Is it worth the price? Maybe, maybe not. But if it's on sale, you should get it. Definitely.

It's like time travelling. Shovel Knight is easily the best representation of the modern retro game. The ui design, sound effects and music, and the pixel count are reminiscent of 8 bit, while the vibrancy of the colors and smoothness of the gameplay are more 16 bit. Regardless, Shovel Knight is a lot of a fun, with humorous dialogue, and simple, but intuitive and sometimes challenging combat and platforming. It takes some ideas from games like SMB3, LoZ II, and Mega Man, among others, such as a very SMB3-esque overworld, villages, items, and upgrades somewhat similar to LoZ II, and a good assortment of Knight bosses, similar to how Mega Mans bosses were. Throw in things like the Anchor sub-weapon that is basically the axe the Castlevania, and you have a game that takes some great feature from old-school games that you love and know, but still forges it's own unique identity without becoming a parody or mashup of what's come before it. And with a New Game+, and loads of cheat codes, Shovel Knight offers a lot of replayability. If you like retro action-platformers, and/or fun, you should probably pick up Shovel Knight.

I have three complaints with this game: 1- Every time I went to power slide Megaman Style, I would jump into an enemy. 2- I can't pogo on spikes like in Ducktales. 3- I don't have a classic NES controller with a USB connection.
With that out of the way, I LOVE this game. This game is old school NES hard, and I loved every minute of it. When you die, you loose a portion of your loot, but you get a chance to recover your lost loot Dark Souls style. And whenever I did die, the controlls are so tight that I could only ever be mad at myself. Trust me, when you walk into a room and go "WTF how is this possible?" and then manage to do it on the first try, there is a huge sense of accomplishment. With the hard parts where i died a lot, I found myself genuinely having fun when I would finally get past it.
This game has a huge amount of attention to detail, the tiny changes in the music between different parts of the map is just one sign of this. Every level has hidden loot stashed everywhere, and it is a real thrill to find them all. The randomly dancing NPC's also made me burst out laughing. Fortunately you can trigger the dancing manually, so I did it multiple times.
There is an achievement to finish the game in under 90 minutes, but I spent a good 6 hours on my first walk through. I'm looking forward to New Game+ and I sincerely hope that there is a sequil in the works.

I honestly think that if the devs were to retitle this game as "Hollywood Car Chase Simulator 2014", this game would sell like hotcakes. Dead serious.
Anyway, let's get on to the actual review: Tactical Intervention is an FPS that is quite ironically the least tactical game you will ever play. But does that make it bad? Of course not. Tactical Intervention has quite a few charm points, which I genuinely think you should try out at least once.
THE GOOD:
As stated in the title, Tactical Intervention features a car chase game mode, in which the Terrorist team is given 1-3 cars to chase after a Counter-Terrorist VIP, who is also in a car. The mode is hilariously glitchy, but in an incredibly fun way, as referenced by STAR_ in his "Tactical Intervention 1.6" video.
Another thing I genuinely appreciate from the dev team is their attention towards the playerbase. A lot of people (myself included) complained about the recoil system in that it was too spazzy (your screen would literally shake up and down frantically as you fired). Within a month, they fixed the recoil system, so shoutout to FIX Korea for their totally bro devs!
The guns in this game are something which I feel more game devs should take note of. All of the guns are very well balanced (with 1 or 2 outliers, but you can't be perfect), and each have a role- Sniper/Marksman Rifles are for Long Range, Assault Rifles are for Mid Range, SMGs are for Close Range, and Shotguns are for Point Blank. The guns have a customization system, allow you to purchase silencers, optics, compensators, flashlights, and weapon camos.
Oh, and did I mention that this game does a great job of the whole F2P thing? The in game economy is similar to TF2, in that the only cash-only items in the game are character models and weapon skins.
THE BAD:
You probably only heard of Tactical Intervention because you clicked on the "Free-To-Play" section in the Steam Store. Well, that's another problem with TI. The playerbase is very, very, very small. The number of concurrent players is literally smaller than the entire population of Vatican City. Go ahead and take a moment to Google that if you wish. It's not uncommon to meet the exact same people day after day, and that means that if you happen to come upon a toxic player, guess what? You're probably gonna see them again before the day's over.
I did say that most of the weapons in TI are well balanced, but there are some outliers. And quite frankly, those outliers are really damn powerful. The AS50, a semi-automatic .50 caliber anti-material rifle, has the ability to kill a player in one shot- yes, you read that correctly- to ANY part of the body (unless you buy armor, but most people don't know about the existence of armor). Sure, it has a ton of scope sway to compensate, but you can noscope with it very easily, making it a threat in CQC. Another unbalanced weapon is the M4 STAR 10, known commonly as the M4 Super 90. The Super 90 is a 12 guage, semi-automatic shotgun with a very high rate of fire, and an uncomfortably long range. Its running accuracy is damn high, too, meaning that you can literally bumrush a group of people face first, and probably kill them. All of them. What makes it worse is that all the guns in the game can be bought with IGC (in game currency), so your average noob can buy a Super 90 literally the moment he boots up the game (all players start with $50000, just enough to buy a Super 90)
THE UGLY:
As mentioned in the Bad section, the playerbase is very small. And I really don't mean to make fun of anyone by saying this, but 90% of players literally have no clue what they're doing. Like, if you go into an S&D server, you'll see people shooting at the bomb. Even if you tell them to hold down F. Which is another problem with the game- since its F2P, the vast majority of players are from BRIC (Brazil/India/Russia/China), or some equally foreign country like Poland or Peru. I don't know if it's out of ignorance or hatred or both, but pretty much no one speaks English, and some people will even go as far as to make fun of you for doing so. Which is ironic, since everyone plays on the AMERICAN servers. Speaking of servers, why do the non-americans play on American servers, and then complain about all the lag?!?! Like, go into your average lobby, and I guarantee at least 80% of the pings will be above 100.
CONCLUSION:
Don't take the game too seriously (or seriously at all, for that matter), and you'll be just fine. TI is a nice game to blow off some steam, but just like Quake, it's a minimalistic game, meaning there's no unlockables or anything like that, so don't be surprised if you quickly decide that you're bored of the game.

I've played the Arma series on and off since the original operation flashpoint, so it's fair to say I have quite a bit of experience with these games, but I'm also in no way a BI fanboy. I'm painfully aware of the games faults.
Firstly the cons, yes multiplayer performance is not as smooth as you might like, and yes sometimes the physics engine will produce moments that you won't quite believe. (There's nothing quite like watching a tank do a back-flip after hitting a rock the size of a football) But the level of content in the vanilla game and available in mods will keep you coming back to the game and you'll be immersed enough that a lower than normal frame rate is just a fair trade.
Though I will add that when people tend to slate the FPS they get, they tend to forget to mention that this is on a 64 player server, with mods and custom mission scripts running, so you can't really blame Bohemia if something a modder has put into the game destroys performance.
That said, as long as you aren't greedy with the mods you want to run simultaneously they really are the backbone of what makes the Arma series as a whole so fantastic!
Like a survival game? Exile
Zombies? DayZ or a few clones
Enjoy cap and hold game-play from battlefield but miss the big maps? Wasteland
Want harcore MilSim? ACE with ACRE/TFAR
Want a strategy game? Find a MilSim group and try it with real people.
PvP? Battle Royale/KoTH or all of the above
Flight sim with a relatively shallow learning curve? The vanilla game has it
The fact that you can switch this game up to something completely different every session makes this one of the best value games EVER in terms of £/hour of entertainment. And the icing on the cake is that these aren't arbitrary game modes shoehorned in or bolted on by the developer because they think they know what the player wants, but features added by the community because the players KNOW what they want.
TL;DR
In short the game has some minor performance issues with heavily modded online play, but this is more than outweighed by the sheer volume of options you have with how you want to play. If there isn't something for you with this game, you probably shouldn't be gaming!

Plays well, cover system doesn't♥♥♥♥♥♥you off all the time (it's entirely optional), controls work reasonably with the XBox 360 Controller. Most of the levels are well thought-out, the outside areas look nice enough. I think it would work reasonably well as a single-player game, but what really stands out is the co op mode. Play the whole story with a friend and have a bunch of fun with back-to-back shooting, screaming "FIRE IN THE HOLE!" and running for cover as well as blaming each other why you died again. Healing items give you both health points back if you are standing close enough and the boss fights are in some cases a lot easier with a partner who actually understands what is happening (if you have a strategy, that is).
The character design is quite good, Sheva standing out as the female lead with very good voice acting, great modelling and animation, while Chris seems bland at first (but he'll grow on you during the game if he didn't already in RE4). All in all the animations look great and not nearly as clumsy as you would expect from a game that's already a bit older. The assisted jumps are fast and cinematic and the action scenes always keep the tension up.
The game itself is pretty simple: You go from level to level, enjoying the occasional cut scene and shoot a bunch of beasts in the head. You find a bunch of guns, although ammo is pretty scarce; you can cope most of the time if one partner specializes on one kind of weapon and you on another.
The inventory handling seems like it has been stolen from an early 90's RPG (without the weight info for all the items and a max. weight you can carry, luckily). You have nine slots that make no sense most of the time and only four of them can be set to hot keys. Healing items never stack (although they are probably the smallest you can collect), while ammo does to insane amounts. Still, ammo empties pretty fast and at the end of some levels we were leaving with half a mag left. Of course you cannot buy ammo at the end of a level but with all the cash you find mysteriously scattered everywhere you will always find a handyman to pimp the cylinder on your S&W revolver to carry more ammo (however that works). Carrying two weapons with you is usually the best you can do (in the end I converged on three: pistol, magnum and a shotgun) if you want to carry a few grenades and some healing items and backup clips. All in all the inventory seems kind of realistic in a way that you couldn't really carry more but the restriction on first aid just seemed like a very artificial way to balance out game difficulty.
Speaking of which: The easiest tourist mode is pretty hardcore at times. While dying in normal situations was usually a problem us employing the wrong strategy or just being unable to aim well at moving targets the action scenes were sometimes requiring an insane amount of button mashing that is almost impossible. The final fight has an button mashing sequence for Sheva which was too hard for us so we used a glitch to work around this issue. For some boss fights it wasn't at all clear what you are supposed to do, it's just a lot of experimenting and dying (which isn't too bad in the end, you can use your first try to figure out tactics on how to do damage and then it usually goes well on the second run). Also, I'm not a big fan of "press a button in less than a second" action scenes, especially when they suddenly pop up mixed with cutscenes. If you don't manage to do one of those scenes, which can take more than a minute, you have to start all over again, seeing the same crappy dialogue over and over again. Mixed with some really insane "mash A for 10 seconds" parts, where even piano-trained fingers didn't help, most of the scenes which would've been nice to watch were ruined for me.
While we are at dialogue: The lines of most of the dialogue is pretty embarrassing to a sane person. No one would talk like most of the NSCs do. The accents spoken by some villains are just ridiculous. The whole story is pretty much unbelievably stupid and the scarce good parts in the cut scenes, where the carefully and cinematically thought-through animations could make you forget the whole voice acting, get ruined by button mashing.
I loved to play the game with a friend. We had a laugh at the ridiculous story and voice acting, which can in the end be a good thing (it's like playing a B-movie and those can be fun, too). While looking at it from an objective point of view, you'll find a lot more negative points than pros. Then again I can forgive most of the cons: The story and voice acting isn't that important if you have a lot of fun playing a game where the story is simply not that important, I can forgive the gamism with the inventory, upgrading weapons in ridiculously unrealistic ways and not being able to buy ammo as well as all the non-stackable first aids (most games do stuff like that and RE5 turned out to be nicely balanced most of the time). Those are all minor issues that didn't really ruin a pretty fun co op game for me. I don't know how it would've been working out if I had played it by myself, but with a friend you can have at least twenty hours of fun for as much as five USD (75% off price if I recall correctly).

I'm not one for easy and simple reviews, so if you don't want to read the entire history of me playing this game and just want me to get to the point:
Team Fortess 2 is worth playing.
Now then, I started playing Team Fortress 2 in the year 2012 (In the Pyroland update), a friend of mine recommended it to me and told me that it was free-to-play. I was at first hesitant, it was my first ever real shooter, yeah I was rather new to PC gaming back then. But I downloaded it and just started playing with him. I was awful, of course. As a Gibus wearing, Pyroland exploring, free to play I had really no reason to be good. I then heard about one of my favorite youtubers playing the game and I just joined him. I exactly remember how it went, he was still rather small in comparison to now but I just wanted to talk to one of my idols. He accepted my friend request and we started trading and talking.
I am now a admin on his Steam group and a staff member of his Discord. Why do I bring this up? To display the kind of connection I have to the game, it made me meet my idol and befirend him and meet so many more likeminded people who loved the game. I then decided in 2013 to finally buy a Key within the MvM update and I was never so satisfied with a purchase in my life. I met many more people, some I'd today consider to be "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s" and some that I still consider some of my best friends ever. This community and the love that many of it's members have for the game still astounds me. It was like a daily routine, always joining a pub server and having fun with a bunch of people.
Flash forward to 2015 and things don't look as good anymore. I started playing other games and my interest in the game fell. Sure, I'd join into a match or two or open a crate with some rest money I had left from a purchase, but really:
It was not the same anymore.
You'd get one or two updated every few months that added nothing more but cosmetics and maybe a weapon that sucked.
And in 2016 it happened, the "Meet your match" update.
Suddenly all of the interest I had left was gone. The matchmaking, the changes, the interface, it was all just bad and terribly handled. I went on to play more new stuff and TF2 was nothing more but a memory and I seperated myself from all of my friends that I got to know because of TF2.
In late 2016 I got an invite to a discord chat.
It was one of my old friends talking to me about a discord server for the Youtuber at the start. I joined and was instantly greeted with love and surprise, by a community I thought that had forgotten me. A bunch knew me, alot had heard of me, alot got to know me. While I was not completely back into the game, I finally felt welcome in a world that I started to believe was only there to kick me in the stomach. I felt good and even if I fell into depression or tough times, a few were there to help me.
Now back to TF2 (Can't believe I sidetracked so much): A month ago I got a message from a friend telling me about how great the new "Jungle Inferno"-Update was. I reinstalled the game after a month of having it deinstalled and...
I'm in love again.
To be fair the matchmaking is still not good, there is no elo system and especially ranked needs a rework. But by god, it feels like the game is in hands again that actually like this game and want it to succeed, I can finally join a pub again in like 5 seconds and have 4 Snipers and Spies on my team, one of them wearing the Gibus and the other 3 standing in one place. I can finally play a class again that makes me feel ultra powerful while I stomp all the enemies or play Pyro and hate myself.
I can play with my friends again.
I love TF2.
And I thank TF2.

Few games attempt Lovecraftian horror, and ever fewer succeed, which makes Amnesia a member of an exclusive club.  An unspeakable horror chases you through this, at times, incredibly disturbing game that holds its eldritch ground against stories like The Dunwich Horror and At the Mountains of Madness.  Amnesia doesn't take the "FPS with horror" route that games like FEAR fall into; you have no weapon in Amnesia, the best thing you can do when confronted with something that can kill you is to hide in a closet.  The game builds a terrifying world where every sound you hear could be a monster shuffling down a damp hallway or just your imagination playing tricks on you, a sensation most of us only remember from our childhoods.  Amnesia comes highly recommended.

As a masochist, I find this game infernal and for that reason very pleasing. Visually, it holds up very well, despite being 5 years old now. It was commonly used as a benchmark for GPUs.
Most of the classic mechanics are here. The Capcom philosophy of survival horror, that is, creating difficulty through sluggish control, is bad design, but somehow it works here. Of course, unlike in many modern games, health does not regenerate. You also have your infernal inventory in which to store your weapons and items.
The game really shines in co-op such that I'd say it's the best way to play it for the first time. Aside from one or two uninspired boss encounters as well as some more minor gripes, any masochist will enjoy this game.

The immersive sound design and well-implemented screen & graphical effects feed the fear of being cornered by other worldly monsters and human abominations. Without any weapons to fight back, this is a genuine "survival horror" game that you should pick up and lose sleep over.

Amnesia borrows from such classics as Thief: The Dark Project and Alone in the Dark in that it creates tension that must be resolved. Shovel Knight is a platformer game in retro style. It is practically a giant love letter to some of the best NES games ever made, like Mega Man, Castlevania and Ducktales. If you like those games, you should get Shovel Knight!
While the influence of the classic games is obvious, Shovel Knight has its own identity. Jump and shovel your way trough the levels while gathering money and subweapons. There are some tough jumps that may kill you several times, but other than that, difficulty is just right in my opinion. It is not as hard as some of the games it's inspired by, but still offers some challenge.
It's clear that this game was made nostalgia in mind, and for me it at least worked! Some interest towards pixel graphics and chiptune soundtrack is recommended, if not required. If you have it, you'll get your money's worth. The game looks great for what it is trying to be, and the soundtrack is excellent! The game was composed by the amazing Jake Kaufman with two tracks by Manami Matsumae, the original Mega Man composer from Japan.
The game is not very long, and replay value is not that great. That is pretty much the only bad thing I can say about this game, it was still a great experience and one of the best games released in 2014. If you need your meal of retro platforming,  Shovel Knight is highly recommended.
In a time when games want to be more and more cinematic experiences, something like Shovel Knight still reminds me of what video gaming is in its purest form.

The game now has two free DLC story modes, and one more is coming in the future. Yes, they are free to everyone who bought the game before the second DPC pack came out!

So this basically means that the new players are getting the worse deal than early players, but with this amount of content, it's still not a bad price at all.
These DLC stories let you play the game as some of the boss characters. The best part here is that it's not just the same game with different character, no no! They are completely new stories that expand the world of Shovel Knight. New music, new items, new bosses, and much more! The stages and the bosses are still there, but they have been changed and remixed a lot, so it feels like a new experience. Each of the characters play so differently that it feels like a completely new game! This is some of the best DLC ever and shows everyone how it should be done!

Shovel Knight is not easy on newbies. The game has an old-school degree of difficulty to go with its retro vibe, and while there are checkpoints scattered through each level (which can be destroyed to earn money, thus cancelling the checkpoint), you will meet many, meany deaths at the hands of agile enemies and lethal obstacles. Deviously, the game subtracts a chunk of cash every time you perish but leaves the money floating in the spot you died, daring you to go back and try to retrieve it.
So yes, Shovel Knight is a great game. But I’ve heard several reviewers describe it as the best game of 2014 so far, and that makes me scratch my head a bit. It’s one thing to be blessed with a game that so wonderfully captures the feel and flavour of old-school classics, but I think some folks are a little too enamoured of Shovel Knight’s retro homages. It’s very clever and exceptionally well-designed, but it’s not a wildly innovative game, and in the years to come I’m not sure it will be as fondly remembered as the games that inspired it.
Still, it’s so very refreshing to find a true gem in the ever-expanding rockpile of retro-influenced games, and Shovel Knight is a wonderful love letter to some of the classics that many of us grew up with. You will dig it.

Arma 3 is not a game for everyone, honestly, this may sound like a suprise to you but, if you're that kind of person that likes to shoot up people by just running at them I don't recommend this game to you, Arma3 is more than that, you have to dedicate time and patience to process and think all of your decisions you're going to take thorughout the situations you are going find yourself in order to take a target down or to just complete an objective you've set up yourself. This game has a very high mechanical process, you have to know the controls for good if you want to play the correct way. I am not saying that you should learn all the goddamn controls and be a professional before even jumping into a game, on the contrary, I recommend on my behalf for you to jump into the game's basic tutorials that are implemented, if you wanna take the baby steps. That's more for the simulation part of Arma3 that has. There are plenty gamemodes with different variety of content. Arma 3 is a simulator, I just dragged in my experience so far. Even so, it sounds complicated overall but maaaan, have I mentioned the graphics? The graphics in this game are gorgeous, breathtaking and unbelievable. I could simply sit hours on end staring at the variety of landscapes the game has to offer. By the way, good job to all the developers for the additional maps in the mods. Shovel Knight is a platformer game in retro style. It is practically a giant love letter to some of the best NES games ever made, like Mega Man, Castlevania and Ducktales. If you like those games, you should get Shovel Knight!
While the influence of the classic games is obvious, Shovel Knight has its own identity. Jump and shovel your way trough the levels while gathering money and subweapons. There are some tough jumps that may kill you several times, but other than that, difficulty is just right in my opinion. It is not as hard as some of the games it's inspired by, but still offers some challenge.
It's clear that this game was made nostalgia in mind, and for me it at least worked! Some interest towards pixel graphics and chiptune soundtrack is recommended, if not required. If you have it, you'll get your money's worth. The game looks great for what it is trying to be, and the soundtrack is excellent! The game was composed by the amazing Jake Kaufman with two tracks by Manami Matsumae, the original Mega Man composer from Japan.
The game is not very long, and replay value is not that great. That is pretty much the only bad thing I can say about this game, it was still a great experience and one of the best games released in 2014. If you need your meal of retro platforming,  Shovel Knight is highly recommended.
In a time when games want to be more and more cinematic experiences, something like Shovel Knight still reminds me of what video gaming is in its purest form.
=================
After release update:
The game now has two free DLC story modes, and one more is coming in the future. Yes, they are free to everyone who bought the game before the second DPC pack came out!
Those who are new to Shovel Knight can still buy the full package that includes the base game and the DLC's but the price has now been increased. So this basically means that the new players are getting the worse deal than early players, but with this amount of content, it's still not a bad price at all.
These DLC stories let you play the game as some of the boss characters. The best part here is that it's not just the same game with different character, no no! They are completely new stories that expand the world of Shovel Knight. New music, new items, new bosses, and much more! The stages and the bosses are still there, but they have been changed and remixed a lot, so it feels like a new experience. Each of the characters play so differently that it feels like a completely new game! This is some of the best DLC ever and shows everyone how it should be done!

Shovel Knight is not easy on newbies. The game has an old-school degree of difficulty to go with its retro vibe, and while there are checkpoints scattered through each level (which can be destroyed to earn money, thus cancelling the checkpoint), you will meet many, meany deaths at the hands of agile enemies and lethal obstacles. Deviously, the game subtracts a chunk of cash every time you perish but leaves the money floating in the spot you died, daring you to go back and try to retrieve it.
So yes, Shovel Knight is a great game. But I’ve heard several reviewers describe it as the best game of 2014 so far, and that makes me scratch my head a bit. It’s one thing to be blessed with a game that so wonderfully captures the feel and flavour of old-school classics, but I think some folks are a little too enamoured of Shovel Knight’s retro homages. It’s very clever and exceptionally well-designed, but it’s not a wildly innovative game, and in the years to come I’m not sure it will be as fondly remembered as the games that inspired it.
Still, it’s so very refreshing to find a true gem in the ever-expanding rockpile of retro-influenced games, and Shovel Knight is a wonderful love letter to some of the classics that many of us grew up with. You will dig it.

Let me start with saying that I never took a interest in the Resident Evil series... never. Somehow when the series started I was into LucasArts games... adventures... Star Wars... many years later I got a quick peek at the PC... and I was sold! The graphics and face animations... the cut-scene quality... the voice acting... the adrenaline shock from the first majini encounter... But playing on PC, there was never the option for me to do some Co-Op. A few months later my PS3 arrived and I had to get that sweet gory game for it. Since then passed something like 2 and a half months and I was still doing Co-Op damage in it.
One thing I have to notice first... I really had the impression, that there were more enemies in the PC version... so that would be one minus point... but I didn't really count them, so whatever!
First impression... the whole thing begins with an amazing cut-scene, featuring some of the best "for game" cinematic's I came across... the camera movement, the angles the editing... it is simply a good movie between the levels with amazing production values... why only a good movie? Well, the plot isn't that great and the dialogs are sometimes idiotic... but the voice-cast is so amazing that you can easily forget that the last line you heard is actually pretty stupid! The voice-cast and the facial animations... which are really outstanding... the eye movement, the eyebrows, the lips it is simply a joy to simply watch them two main heroes!
So now lets talk about our main protagonists... Chris Redfield... as much as I love the way he was animated, I am not quite a fan of his muscularity... I mean the guys looks like a descended of Donkey Kong himself, just watch his ears! But besides that he is quit a likable character. On the other hand we have his always present female sidekick, which is simply anatomically perfect, no over sized silicon breasts (like most of the female characters designed for games), a beautiful face and as Chris a likable character.
But what Sheva really offers is "an excuse" for the possibility to play the whole single player campaign in Cooperative mode with friends on-line! Of course there are in game button assigned commands to communicate within game, but a headset is definitely the way to go! I would especially recommend the original PS3 headset from Sony!
The replay value in Co-Op mode is extremely high, when you got some folks to play with. People say the single player experience vs. the Co-Op experience is radically different... maybe, but the Co-Op is in my opinion the more fun way to play. Gathering the treasures and emblems and trophies together really is much more rewarding and you have to really work together to go through some game points to not waste amo or healing stuff. The difficulty level is somewhat unbalanced sometimes, you start with a very tough set piece followed by some easier points along the way, then you get to another hard point and so on and so on... but that is not really a complaint, more an observation about the games pacing.
A minus point is the engine, which on one hand offers stunning graphics, but on the other hand really narrows your movement options. You can't jump over any given ledge, the game has to allow you this, the cover system is OK, but why do they reload before going back to cover after shooting, leaving you literally out in the open for counterattacks? Some might not like the fact, that you can't run and shoot, but this too isn't really that bad... one has just to rethink his game strategy.
So if you like games which offer a spectacular presentation, but no really strong plot or dialogue (but perfectly voice acted and featuring likable characters), which offer amazing graphics and a ton of fun instead of a complicated game engine, then this one is the right one for you... for weeks, if not months!
This game has some cons, but the pros definitely out wage them... so this is a 10 in 10 for me! The DLC are also worth the purchase (not on PC - which is a shame)!

If you're a fan of any kind of tactical shooter, I highly recommend giving this one a shot. I'll try and lay out a few reasons as to why I feel like you should or shouldn't pick this one up. Also, if you feel like you're tight on money, definitely pick up the starter edition. It is 100% worth the price, because everything is included in the starter edition that is included in the standard edition. The only difference is that you will have to play more to get the operators, but that's it. No extra fees, nothing exluded, the whole game.
PROS+++
1. The community for this game (while still having a few bad apples like every community does) is so helpful and so willing to work together. When you tell someone to stop, they hold position. When you tell them when to go in, they listen. People are also willing to understand if you are new, and apologize if they teamkill. Hell, sometimes when you accidentally teamkill them, they will already forgive you for it before you say anything, or sometimes even apologize for getting in your way.
2. The gunplay is smooth, and highly engaging. The leaning system in this game really sets it apart from other games and allows you to peek with ease and smooth movement.
3. Customization is top ♥♥♥♥ing notch here. From the different operator perks, to the customization of your guns attachments, to camos and skins you can unlock for your guns, charms you can have on your gun, even outfits and headgear for your operator. If you're a fan of customization at all, it definitely does not let up here.
4. Competitive replayability.  Anyone who has played any kind of ranked game knows that a ranked system with a competitive community allows for thousands of hours of replayability.
5. Updates to the game have been pretty good. The recent Operation Health received many different views, but I completely love it. My queue times got cut almost into a fourth of the time that I was in queue before, I can do other things in queue rather than staring at the screen, and i notice the hitreg being a lot smoother and better than before. Really enjoying it.
6. The graphics are absolutely gorgeous. Not much more to say here. It's also really well optimized. (at least now it is.)
CONS---
1. Uplay. It's not too big of a deal, but it's just annoying at times. Not too big of a gripe here, often forget I'm using Uplay.
2. No story mode. The situations allow for a good single player experience, as well as the terrorist hunt, but the game really shines here with the multiplayer. It was clearly designed around it.
3. (THIS COULD BE CONSIDERED A PRO) If you do get the starter edition, the operators will take some time, and you will have to play the game a bit of time to unlock all of the operators. However, you can do just fine with just a couple operators, and the game gives you a couple operators that are friendly to beginner players.
Overall, If you're a fan at all of Counter Strike, Rainbow six previous titles, or played SOCOM in the past, this is a must buy. I don't have the MOST hours on the game, but so far I've been having a blast. The game is gorgeous, fun, and an absolutely awesome time with a few friends, or solo. Definitely a recommendation from me.

In a word, Unfinished.
In many -- Towns is a promising, but rough experience. Nothing seems to work quite as intended, the UI is a little finicky, mouse clicks don't always register in the right place (if at all), and digging is a nightmare. The further down you dig, the more erratic the mouse behavior becomes.
At 15$, I'd say the price is steep -- comparing to Minecraft, which released at a similar price, the level of functionality is far less. Though then again, the requisite functionality is far greater in the case of Towns. However, this game is flawed for a far simpler reason, it was released onto steam with no notice that it was an unfinished, alpha game -- I'm an alpha-player, I love to play and watch as a game evolves, and I am _more likely_ to purchase an alpha game than many non-alpha games. I know many of my friends feel the same way, but  this game released to steam (via Greenlight) purporting to be a fully-ready 1.0 release, and that's just not what it is.
I say wait. Maybe get it if the price drops to the 2-5$ range. It has potential to be quite good, if the development continues, but everything about the more general practice smells of a smash and grab on my wallet, and I don't much care for it.

Portal 2 was probably my favorite game, until this came out. Put simply, it's epic, it's a challenge, and you simply must play it!

IT'S SO GOOD. The controls are tight, the graphics and animations are gorgeous, the dialogue's glorious, there's the right amount of challenge with generous health and mana pickups, and the items are completely optional extras (the phasing mechanic's super broken, but whatever, you can just ignore it. Would be nice for it to last a little longer and be a lot more expensive so as to avoid it being an absolute crutch). Save for the additional areas designed specifically for them, you'll never be forced to use the items in normal play. On that point, though, they greatly compliment them usual stages, so don't think for a moment they're just non-viable throw-away pieces of junk.
The tutorials? What tutorials? The levels are expertly crafted to introduce each concept and obstacle-- heck, they even give you the tell-tale signs of secrets you should keep an eye out for in the beginning --so you're never completely overwhelmed, yet suitably pushed to a comfortable requirement of developed skill. You'll feel like you're given the driver's seat right away, but you'll likely never feel as though you're out of your depth.
And it's not all platforming in this game. Bosses, bosses, so many bosses. Additional bosses, secret bosses, roaming bosses, bosses at the end of every level; you won't be able to move for bosses! Each with their own uniqie gimmicks and tricks, you'd be pushed to have a bad time when one appears. Each is a delight to behold, and great fun to learn and fight.
This is honestly my favourite game of recent memory. It's far better than any classic SNES game could have even hoped to be, and the creators' time, love and devotion oozes from every pore of the game. Buy it now.

Smashed and looted all of the checkpoints (including the ones nestled away in corners), even finished the last boss again in case of badly placed triggers-- nothing. Very disappointing, considering all the hours I've sunk into getting past those couple of poorly designed traps flawlessly (blemishes on an otherwise 10/10 experience of a game). It's a testament to the overall quality of the game when I can only think of three throat-rippingly bad insta-kill areas, but still. It's very disheartening to see this kind of thing, and extremely discouraging in terms of trying the rest of the achievements.
In addition to the reported achievement issues I've been hearing about (and experiencing on a smaller scale), New Game+ is actually an incredible let down. Enemy damage is ramped up, there are less checkpoints, almost all food is replaced with bombs, and you receive less refreshments in that one encounter. All of these are limitations you could more than easily place upon yourself by simply refusing the help the game already gives you. Save for the bomb thing. Good luck trying to punch yourself in the face.
The fact that this lazy NG+ was actually a stretch goal of the original campaign smacks of something I can't quite define without using extravagant absolutes.
Hopefully this'll all be patched in a future update. All I know is, I've run out of Shovel Knight to play. Sad times. (Sell me DLC plz).

Loyal gamers old enough to have played the original Resident Evil and its two successors on the first Sony Playstation console will be surprised to find the new setting for the ever popular series, spanning across the world into far stranger environments. The first of the series set up the story inside a massive creaking mansion, the second saw two protagonists find attempt to find refuge in an infected, overrun Raccoon City (the third included the almighty 'Nemesis') and No.4 outreached to a rural area of Europe (possibly near Spain). Now the franchise takes us to somewhere far less developed, a dusty, desolate Africa. Initially there were half-hearted complaints over the setting and what that entailed - An American, white, male shooting the, albeit infected, black natives. Frankly there seemed no way around this because one way or another, because questions would arise if the 'natives' weren't black, someone would get offended and tragically, the game had some small detest growing for it. Regardless of the content and false accusations of racism, RE5 manages to raise the bar when it comes to action/shooters, thanks to vivid scenery, strong graphics, addictive gameplay and achievements.
"The right to be a god... that right is now mine." (Plot)
Whilst the films spawned from the series takes things way to far with a mary sue character (Alice played by Milla Jovovich), pathetic performances and ridiculous 'mind powers' - the games tend to keep a slight bit of class. Chris Redfield, formally of S.T.A.R.S (Special Tactics And Rescue Service) finds himself working for the BSAA (Bioterrorism Security Assessment Alliance) after events that saw Chris lose his former partner Jill Valentine. Reassigned and offered a new partner in Sheva Alomar, he must investigate suspicious activity in the motherland. Something is clearly up in the area and things quickly turn nasty as a furious dictating man screams down a megaphone. The locals are infected. Before you can find your bearings, your unknown guide is captured and beheaded before your eyes by giant beast wielding a massive axe. The infected spectators cheer his untimely death and draw their attentions to you. After ploughing through endless waves of zombies, hitching rides from teammates and encountering menacing 'creatures', theres the inkling this is no mere outbreak of the fabled T-Virus. This is Uroboros. A new biological weapon that turns those 'unworthy' into mindless, blood thirsty zombs, but more worryingly makes those with some worthy attributes, morph into vine-twisting monsters and abstract demons capable of even greater destruction. Trekking through the desert, marshlands, villages and Umbrella corps industrial buildings, you experience all Africa has to offer, including mines, forgotten ruins and ritualistic tribes. And to top it all of, the one behind it all is your former colleague..
"Locked & Loaded" (Gameplay)
Like the game before it, RE5 is from a 3rd person view with fairly advanced controls to aim, fire and reload. Melee is included as is a 9 item inventory to store weapons, ammo, grenades and medical equipment. Being unable to fire when moving is a bit outdated but a realistic throwback to the older games. Strutting around as a man with arms twice the width of his head, you can alternate to your own style of fighting - equipping close range weaponry like shotguns, multipurpose machine guns or long range sniper rifles. Go for the headshot and save time and ammo or take out limbs to disable your opponents. The addition of an ai or friend in Sheva, is a handy aid to brush of grappling buggers or revive you in times of desperation - this aid is a doubled edged sword though - not only do you have to take equally good care of her (or him if you wish to play as Sheva) if either of you should die - its game over. This also makes for some interesting mix ups in moving around, launching your lighter partner across gaps to venture fourth and find different routes, combining attacks to take down foes (this uses clips of attacks which require you to press the correct button, exciting!). The cutscenes themselves are just as punishing as the enemy on professional mode (V.Hard) so you need to pay attention to whats happening even when you think a level is over because you need to hit all the right buttons in order and in time to proceed. This particular feature really made for edge of the seat action as the first time surprises you while the other times keep you on edge. Menus are really addictive with a merchant to buy ammo and other goods from (selling precious gems and ancient relics for currency) and upgrading you weapons for larger clips, better ammo, damage and reload speed.
"Welcome to Africa" (Environments)
A bright and sunshine bathed Africa may not seem the setting for a suspenseful zombie game but despite the daytime light, the walking, rotting corpses still make a disgusting impact. Some Zombies wield glass bottles, shovels and even guns whilst some are mere hosts to even more sinister origins - acidic flying beasts, spiked caterpillar heads, rock solid cloisters and rabid jaw-busting mongrels. The pair traverse through eerie villages, hostile tribe land, pitch black mines, chemical spattered experimental quarantine zones... Thats right, its a perfect place thats out of the way for the evil Umbrella Corporation to experiment further, who knows what abominations dwell in the abandoned facility... Things get a bit 'Indiana Jones' too when the couple explore a dank underground ruin that's home to a long forgotten tribe - resurrected thanks to Uroboros, and determined to repel any foreign trespassers. Expect flaming boulders, collapsing stairways, forbidden treasures and other deadly traps, lurking amongst the vicious inhabitants.
"I'm not........ Gunna make it!" (Voice Acting, Soundtrack & Options)
Being brutally honest, the background score is rather tame and unmemorable - possibly because of the engrossing gameplay that holds your attention. Voice acting is surprisingly strong most of the time even with embarrassingly simplified accounts of the situations at hand and eccentric lines that downplay the seriousness as future boss yells "I just had an extreme makeover!" when evolving into a humongous tentacle swinging marsh mammoth. One thing that amazed me was that for once, a game has 4 difficulties (Casual, Normal, Veteran & Professional) that are fairly done - enemies don't pull of unrealistic moves, survive rocket propelled grenades to the face or appear infinitely - they make it legitimate with one bite deaths (as an infection would inevitably mean your demise) fatal gunshot wounds and faster 'bleeding out'. The balance being you can unlock infinite ammo for a price..
"Sheva, HUUUUURRY!" (Coop & Verses)
I am always on the lookout for decent games with well made cooperative modes and RE5 was definitely a wild ride for me and many of my friends. The game boast 16 levels (scattered in 6 chapters) to survive which truth be told can be completed nonchalantly over the weekend, making it a superb choice for a rental. The game rewards teamwork too, making sure you stick together being paramount and ganging up on bosses with complimentary tactics. However the single-player modes are full of secrets and little nicknacks' to acquire that the fun can go on for a good few months. The Multiplayer though is a disappointment as you not only take on hordes of enemies but are forced to search out additional 'time' points to continue. The versus mode isn't much to brag about either as you just take on others around the world which doesn't seem to fit the style of the gameplay (plus you have to pay for the privilege of Versus Mode). Not much matches putting a shotgun barrel to the temple of an aggressor, pulling the trigger and celebrating with your comrades in brain chunk raindrops..

The controls are tight, the graphics and animations are gorgeous, the dialogue's glorious, there's the right amount of challenge with generous health and mana pickups, and the items are completely optional extras (the phasing mechanic's super broken, but whatever, you can just ignore it. Would be nice for it to last a little longer and be a lot more expensive so as to avoid it being an absolute crutch). Save for the additional areas designed specifically for them, you'll never be forced to use the items in normal play. On that point, though, they greatly compliment them usual stages, so don't think for a moment they're just non-viable throw-away pieces of junk.
The tutorials? What tutorials? The levels are expertly crafted to introduce each concept and obstacle-- heck, they even give you the tell-tale signs of secrets you should keep an eye out for in the beginning --so you're never completely overwhelmed, yet suitably pushed to a comfortable requirement of developed skill. You'll feel like you're given the driver's seat right away, but you'll likely never feel as though you're out of your depth.
And it's not all platforming in this game. Bosses, bosses, so many bosses. Additional bosses, secret bosses, roaming bosses, bosses at the end of every level; you won't be able to move for bosses! Each with their own uniqie gimmicks and tricks, you'd be pushed to have a bad time when one appears. Each is a delight to behold, and great fun to learn and fight.
This is honestly my favourite game of recent memory. It's far better than any classic SNES game could have even hoped to be, and the creators' time, love and devotion oozes from every pore of the game. Buy it now.
UPDATE: The Checkpointless achievement is indeed on the fritz. Smashed and looted all of the checkpoints (including the ones nestled away in corners), even finished the last boss again in case of badly placed triggers-- nothing. Very disappointing, considering all the hours I've sunk into getting past those couple of poorly designed traps flawlessly (blemishes on an otherwise 10/10 experience of a game). It's a testament to the overall quality of the game when I can only think of three throat-rippingly bad insta-kill areas, but still. It's very disheartening to see this kind of thing, and extremely discouraging in terms of trying the rest of the achievements.
In addition to the reported achievement issues I've been hearing about (and experiencing on a smaller scale), New Game+ is actually an incredible let down. Enemy damage is ramped up, there are less checkpoints, almost all food is replaced with bombs, and you receive less refreshments in that one encounter. All of these are limitations you could more than easily place upon yourself by simply refusing the help the game already gives you. Save for the bomb thing. Good luck trying to punch yourself in the face.
The fact that this lazy NG+ was actually a stretch goal of the original campaign smacks of something I can't quite define without using extravagant absolutes.
Hopefully this'll all be patched in a future update. All I know is, I've run out of Shovel Knight to play. Sad times. (Sell me DLC plz).

While the game is somewhat enjoyable in terms of story, there are a few things that completely kills it. Not being able to move while shoting or reloading is one of them,. While this is something I can live with, thoese quick time events are really frustrating, especially during boss fights. They can change up the sequence, and you have a millisecond to react, which really kills the game.
Speaking of which, the boss fights are really annoying. They are either extremely easy or extremely hard, depending on how fast you figure out what you are supposed to do and whether or not you will be resupplied with ammo. And the final two boss' where some of the most infuriating ones I have ever played. Not only do you have to figure out what to do via trial and error, they are simply unforgiven. First one can kill you with two shots flat, so better bring lots of healing items.
The last one is just infurating and if you dont know what to do going in to it, you will be basically out of luck.
The store is another point of frustration, while it works fairly OK. You can buy all weapons, but you will find most of them in the game regardless. As the game is fairly stingy with ammo, you are better off limiting what weapons you keep on you anyway. But the most annoying part is that you cannot buy either ammo or grenades in the store, making a boss fight you forgot to save up bullets for or went in to with few resources almost impossible as you have to be extremely accurate with the way you do things.
Overall, I would not recommend this game, it can be fun, if you play co op, but in the end it was so furiating I just beat it out of spite. More than once I had to check a strategy guide just to figure out how to deal with a boss, simply because you will not get a single indication in game if you are doing things right. Only redeeming quality of the game is the coop, in which it can be fairly entertaining at times, but overall I feel the frustration it puts you through greatly outweighs the fun you can have.

This game is more than ten years old. It has a thriving community, active developers, and a skill ceiling I can’t even come close to achieving – a testament to great game design. If that alone doesn’t make you at least want to try a free game that has such an accolade, nothing I have to say will.
Team Fortress 2 strikes a balance between a challenging, competitive game and one where the most unpredictable, stupid, and downright bizarre events occur; often simultaneously. If you’re looking for a game where you can go from sweating because you’re trying so damn hard to laughing at the unexpected, look no further.
As I said, the game is challenging. When you first begin playing it’s likely you’ll get trashed. But, take the game in a light-hearted way. Sure, some dude slapped you in the face with a shovel killing you instantly, learn how to counter that! Then go do it to someone else.
If you let it, Team Fortress 2 will be the most fun you can have in an online game. The stupid interaction of people in this game is enjoyable and sometimes pretty damn wholesome. The combat is challenging, rewarding, and will likely become a total time sink. This free to play game has more hours than any of my others (including old accounts and my old X-Box titles), I can’t recommend this game enough. Even if you do only boot it once on a lazy Sunday, it’s at least worth a shot.

This is an excellent F2P game that I recommend for anyone who likes FPS games. The graphics are pretty good, but a little GPU intensive for the shading (which doesn't really make a difference). Also this game is built on the Source Engine if anyone cares. There are sights, lasers, flashlights, and silencers (for those who don't believe), but only select guns come with a sight and the rest are random from different crates. One might be unsure because of the cost of weapons and other equipment, but there are two ways to approach the cost of them: one is to pay to keep them forever or to rent them (also DLC if you really want). If you're only going to be playing for about a week at a time I recommend you rent a good gun and then you can easily get back the GP. However, if you plan on coming back week after week or on random days, make an investment to keep them forever, but you do need to earn back the GP.
Some quick notes about it:
- it was made by the co-creator of the original Counter Strike
- weapons are based off the real thing
- has attack dogs, riot shields, breaching charges and night vision
- has hostages situations, rappelling down buildings, and car chases
(...and a slow ground support vehicle which makes for one funny showdown)
FYI: the fastest way to earn GP is the Mission game mode, NOT Team Death Match (unless you're a pro or are good with a super fast computer). Team Death Match is pretty much for fun only...

Plants vs Zombies is a great game that is definitely worth the price whether or not it's on sale.  In the game you put crazy plants that seem ready for a full scale war somewhere in your property, like on the front lawn, in order to defend your house from zombies.  You fight them in your front yard during daytime and then again during night time in the same location.  After that the zombies change tactics and attack your backyard, where there is a pool.  They do this during daytime.  Then, of course, the zombies come back for more at night time as they are thirsty for more brain juice and other brainy things that humans have in their brains.  During the night, instead of having a nice clear sky to fight under like when you were in the front yard, Mother Nature decides it would be a great idea to plague you with fog, lighting and sometimes even a flickering, pitch black battlefield.  Finally you head onto, actually I won't tell you just to avoid any possible spoilers.
Sadly, Plants vs Zombies is not a perfect game but it is still pretty good.  Some of the things that could be improved are a more difficult adventure mode and a better storyline as at the moment (when this review was written) there hardly even is one.  Anyway, I would rate Plants vs Zombies 94/100 because it is good but it could be better.  But it won't get much better because it is already really good.
There are 53 battle ready plants (the achievement says 49 plants but the Internet says 53, that includes the 8 upgrade plants), 38 unique zombies, 50 fun adventure levels, 20 cool mini games, 11 awesome survival levels, 20 puzzling puzzle levels and many cool Easter eggs including moustaches and Chinese zombies.  With all of this you will never get bored, actually let me rethink that.  After a while you probably will get bored but you will enjoy the game for as long as there are levels to complete and zombies to crush, smash, destroy, chomp and completely obliterate.

An extensive mod like this takes me back to playing Total Conversion .WADs for Doom II.  God, I feel old.
That aside, this is a top-notch mod.  It's not a Portal 3.  Arguably, it's not quite as good as the base Portal 2, either.  But it's great.  It creates a coherent story within the Portal universe that takes you in and out of testing chambers and through all the Portal 2 environments: modern Aperture, historic Aperture, and ruined-and-overgrown Aperture.  It even ties itself into the Portal storyline.
As other reviewers have noted, Portal Stories: Mel is hard, but not exaggeratedly so.  Mel's levels are on a par, difficulty-wise, with the final third of Portal 2.  The real difference is simply that it presumes you're already experienced at the game, and so doesn't waste any time teaching you the concepts; you can expect Gel, Faith Plates, Hard Light, Excursion Funnels and various tricky portal surfaces to be thrown at you at any time, and you'll need to make clever use of them.
Given that this is a huge dose of challenging new Portal 2 content, nearly measuring up to the original in quality, and free on top of it all, I can't imagine why any Portal 2 fan would
play Mel.

Plants vs Zombies is a great game that is definitely worth the price whether or not it's on sale.  In the game you put crazy plants that seem ready for a full scale war somewhere in your property, like on the front lawn, in order to defend your house from zombies.  You fight them in your front yard during daytime and then again during night time in the same location.  After that the zombies change tactics and attack your backyard, where there is a pool.  They do this during daytime.  Then, of course, the zombies come back for more at night time as they are thirsty for more brain juice and other brainy things that humans have in their brains.  During the night, instead of having a nice clear sky to fight under like when you were in the front yard, Mother Nature decides it would be a great idea to plague you with fog, lighting and sometimes even a flickering, pitch black battlefield.  Finally you head onto, actually I won't tell you just to avoid any possible spoilers.
Sadly, Plants vs Zombies is not a perfect game but it is still pretty good.  Some of the things that could be improved are a more difficult adventure mode and a better storyline as at the moment (when this review was written) there hardly even is one.  Anyway, I would rate Plants vs Zombies 94/100 because it is good but it could be better.  But it won't get much better because it is already really good.
There are 53 battle ready plants (the achievement says 49 plants but the Internet says 53, that includes the 8 upgrade plants), 38 unique zombies, 50 fun adventure levels, 20 cool mini games, 11 awesome survival levels, 20 puzzling puzzle levels and many cool Easter eggs including moustaches and Chinese zombies.  With all of this you will never get bored, actually let me rethink that.  After a while you probably will get bored but you will enjoy the game for as long as there are levels to complete and zombies to crush, smash, destroy, chomp and completely obliterate.

4/8/2017: I have to ammend this review some since this went from "Shovel knight" to "Treasure Trove. I really don't have too much to add here except that the the other knights solve the lack of runtime and replayability the base game had.
[original review]
Shovel Knight is while brief, excellent platforming experience that gives many nods to the greatest of platformers. a small dash of many classic platforming series make it into this game while it also having its own merits to stand on as well. from the 8 bosses with refight aspects of mega man, the pogoing with your shovel as a clear nod to ducktales and secret area galore style and world map of Mario games. It also has its own personal charms in making a quasi medieval fantasy setting. I was almost slightly disappointed in the towns that they didn't work like neutral zones like in bionic commando with how the first town dialogue goes haha...
But enough with the charms and homages. Is the gameplay good? You bet it is. The controls are very tight and responsive for a platformer which is very important. The relics can make the game very easy if you bother to seek them out, which makes a very balanced  game, you can make it as hard or as easy as you like by deciding to go for certain things and it also rewards those quite amply for seeking out the secrets. the bosses are interesting to fight and each come with their own themes which a nice attention to detail in a genre where attention to detail is important. The game has all ends of the platforming spectrum covered in its stages with each largely employing its own interesting gimmicks to keep you entertained but none being super frustrating. The game is one very solid "just right" on many of its aspects and easily can be tweaked to fit your tastes by how you play or don't play some areas.
The only thing one might complain on is the game's length, unless you aim to 100% the game an average playthrough is 3-4 hours, 5-7 if you really want to see everything the game has to offer in your first playthrough. But that being said the game is a very solid platforming experience and if you are still hesitant on it wait for a sale, but do at some point play this game.

This hands down, has to be my favorite Resident Evil game to come to PC. The smooth co-op factor made this stand out quite a bit, aside from the occasional connection issues due to running windows live through steam and what not, though works brilliantly the rest of the time.
Now, as for story-line, I really did enjoy the fact it didn't go for the stereotypical crew of Leon, Ada etc, as much as I love those characters, I find there wasn't ever enough about Chris Redfield and Sheva Alomar (A local BSAA agent), though maybe that is just me. This game revolves around Chris and Sheva's investigation of a terrorist threat in Kijuju, a fictional place in Africa, giving it a really nice rural environment from the get go.
Through the RE games, they seemed to lose their horror and survival aspect, but RE 5 manages to bring back a eerie tension with it's mechanics, keeping you on your toes from start to finish. I loved this. The boss fights were actually quite intense, a little bit creepy when you are being chased down in tight area's and with little ammo to spare and find, after all, you don't just find random clips of ammo lying down in the real world, do you?
Enemies no longer politely wait for you to rummage through your things either, because bringing up your armory doesn't pause the action, which brings back the survival feeling to the game, because if you aren't carefully watching when going through your inventory to switch between weapons, you will die. Also, the fact you can't carry THAT many weapons compared to a lot of games which take an RPG and a range of other weapons and just put them in their back pocket to continue sprinting and running like nothing.
It brings some amazing visuals and a few enhancements, In other words, kind of like what RE3 was to RE2. The monsters aren't that imaginative, though lickers get brought back!
To the action aspect, your partner can revive you, relatively quick weapon swapping, colossal bosses and the horror-ish aspect is pulled off with limited controls and the classic over-the-shoulder view, an inventory system that doesn't pause to make enemies wait whilst you ready yourself for them and some pretty intense puzzle solving whilst trying to stay alive.
In all, amazing game, loved the new mechanics, great co-op and the revamp of the creepy horror, survival aspects.

Disclaimer: I fish in real life, I have for several years, I love to fish, I find fish relaxing, I fish for fun (sadly, this game due to its community has become the exact opposite of RELAXING -_-)... so this isn't just a review of "some gamer that bounces from game to game", this is a review of somebody wanting to see a virtual simulation of something I love to do in real life.
Game was fun for the first week.  Then devs rolled out nerfs because of players exploiting the heck out of the game.  Problem is, nerfs only hurt those that WEREN'T exploiting & playing legit.  If they wanted to nerf uniques, so be it. I still never caught one, I'm okay with that, hence the the word "unique".  Problem is, they nerfed the game across the board.  After which, I'd regularly cast out 10-20+ times and pull back an empty line with nothing on it, leading to *honestly* losing track of how many times I dozed off out of pure boredom with this game.  It's not fun anymore, and not at all like real fishing anymore, and doubt it'll ever be the game it used to be.  Which is even more confusing since fishing the same exact fish back at level 4 and level 5 seemed much easier /w lesser gear and it seemed like I was truly PRO fishing and pulling out fish left and right, at least one fish every 3-5 casts, than it does at level 9 with the best gear available for my level where the same exact river now seems like a deserted ghost town.
What was peculiar... is one would think that any sensible dev would have realized when they had to make the first nerf, that there's obviously an issue.  But a week would go by, and the next higher level would be exploited, then nerfed, then another week while the next higher level was expoited, then patched.  Many still believe (check the forums) that the devs were letting friends and family have the "fun, true, and casual fishing game", then locking the door behind them, leaving everybody else left to experience something slower than real-life fishing... which is beyond sad, I love real-life fishing, but I'll even admit, that can be hella boring when there's nothing biting... about as productive as watching paint dry.
A bigger problem, the devs refuse to reset the game, even though it's been exploited to hell and back, and everybody afterwards is left in a miserable state of gameplay that's not fun, not pleasant, and, for lack of a better word, horrid.  That means when they finally roll out the tournaments, it's going to be plagued with all the exploiters with all the same exact BEST gear for gold-coins, only coming down to who gets more lucky... skill won't even matter... just like every other MMORPG, if you're not in best gear, don't bother showing up... which is SAD to see in a FISHING game!
Furthermore, unless you're one that exploited, or a "clique"-type, don't bother sharing your opinion in what you'd hope to be an open-minded discussion on the game's forums.  I attempted it... devs are open-minded at least... a vast majority of this community however, are beyond toxic.  Several were suggesting in a recent pinned upcoming patch notification, that it'd be fair to wipe and have everybody start over, since several got unfair advantages and the game is horrible for anybody that didn't.  I'd even go so far as to say, the ONLY people preaching that "resets never happen when money has been introduced" (which is blatant BS), and defending the stance of "no wipes", are exactly those that exploited and ruined the game for everybody else.
TL;DR version (*flips bird to the jack@$$ on the forums that's intimidated by long posts*)... you can see in the parentheses, I've hit my fill... with a FISHING game, which is sad.  I'm a 32 year gamer... I've played so many games that have come and gone... my skin is thick... and in the course of one night, the toxicity of the community pushed me to my limit and last straw... over a !@#!ing FISHING GAME!?  *facepalms and walks out*
VERDICT: Check out Fishing Hero... it's a blast, it's fun, it's actually relaxing, the game isn't speed bumped every other time you log in, has aquariums that show off your fish, has pretty graphics (not near as realistic obviously)... and even though the game isn't all that close to real-life fishing, it does remind me a lot of fishing in Final Fantasy XIV.  I regret ever wasting any time on Fishing Planet, will be uninstalling it after I post this... as well as giving my honest review/impression on YouTube of how horribly broken BOTH the game and community are. ^_^
PS - The ONLY pro this game has for it, is it's a great NATURE (not fishing mind you) simulator... but then again, the same could be stated for Second Life, and most of us know what happened with that. -_-
EDIT: Sadly had a bigger smile and more excitement uninstalling this game, than I've had playing it for the past week or so (post-nerfs). xD

Not so much a game as a panic attack simulator. In fact, there are barely any "gamey" elements in it at all.  There is really no combat to speak of and what puzzles are there are so integrated into the environment that they are barely puzzles at all. Still, I think this is one of the more revolutionary games of the past decade strictly because it does immersion better than any game I've ever encountered. In fact, in a time when it seems like every game designer is intent on turning video games into crappy, cut scene laden, B-movies, "Amnesia" should be studied as a model of how to make a game that uses the unique mechnaics of a video game (i.e. first person, in the moment, experience and decision making) to their fullest effects, rather than just trying to imitate film conventions. Plus, apart from its laudable and refreshing approach to game design, it also just plain works as a survival horror game and is as visceral and exciting as any horror film I've ever seen. Highly Recommended.
