An extensive mod like this takes me back to playing Total Conversion .WADs for Doom II.  God, I feel old.
That aside, this is a top-notch mod.  It's not a Portal 3.  Arguably, it's not quite as good as the base Portal 2, either.  But it's great.  It creates a coherent story within the Portal universe that takes you in and out of testing chambers and through all the Portal 2 environments: modern Aperture, historic Aperture, and ruined-and-overgrown Aperture.  It even ties itself into the Portal storyline.
As other reviewers have noted, Portal Stories: Mel is hard, but not exaggeratedly so.  Mel's levels are on a par, difficulty-wise, with the final third of Portal 2.  The real difference is simply that it presumes you're already experienced at the game, and so doesn't waste any time teaching you the concepts; you can expect Gel, Faith Plates, Hard Light, Excursion Funnels and various tricky portal surfaces to be thrown at you at any time, and you'll need to make clever use of them.
Given that this is a huge dose of challenging new Portal 2 content, nearly measuring up to the original in quality, and free on top of it all, I can't imagine why any Portal 2 fan would
play Mel.

Shovel Knight is one of my favorite games of all time. Granted, I'm biased because I helped Kickstart the game, but there is so much to love.
Music is fantastic, the style is wonderful, the color really harkens back to the old NES days, and the game is just fun to play.
For anyone who has seen Egoraptor's Sequelitis on Megaman X will appreciate the intro stage. Though, not as story driven as Megaman X (with the whole Vile Encounter), the intro stage offers JUST as much learning for the player. It's brilliantly designed. Just like the rest of the levels and how each stage works very hard to introduce new elements and lets you sweat over the perilous situations you're thrown in.
I've seen lots of complaints about instant death. Well of course there's ton, it's a tough game. Are those stages beatable? Of course they are! Any skilled platformer will be able to beat them. Not to say you aren't ;) Just take a breather and try to recognize the patterns.
The items were, I feel, very lackluster in comparison to the rest of the game. They felt ignorable, and situationally-important. You could beat the game without relics (there's an achievement for that), so they end up feeling quite useless. Tweaking some of the magic costs might help, but they really aren't that useful until you get the armor for them.
Overall, one of the best games you can get today that really tip a hat towards good design. Also, I really liked the story for some reason. It's simple, neat, and I felt something at the end.
Also. Butt Mode: "X&BUTT" Enter that in the name select screen. You'll probably love it.

Resident Evil/Biohazard has been a beloved zombie shooter for many years now. However, despite the praise of its atmosphere and gameplay, the game was regularly criticized for its clunky movement controls and unintuitive U.I. Resident Evil needed to evolve and rework these dated issues if it wanted to survive its own longetivity. In 2005, RE4 hit the market with overwhelming positive reviews. It pioneered the over the shoulder view of shooters, delivering superb gameplay, action, and smooth UI/controls. The community's only issue was they wanted to play the thriller with a friend. Capcom heard the plight and RE5 was announced. We were all ready to pounce on the idea that we could finally RE in co-op....however, we learned the hard way that we might have jumped the shark, as well as received another punishing lesson on "Why we don't pre-order games."
Plot 4/10
In typical RE fasion, the story is bumpy, confusing, littered with holes, and told from the perspective of a 10 yr old that was along for the ride. It's everything you've seen before: the (insert random letter)-virus has broken out this time because - dammit we're not out of letters in the English alphabet yet - and it's turning people into...zombies. Capcom has left their mark on abysmal story telling once more, giving you - once AGAIN - JUST enough of an excuse to slaughter everything in your path from point A to point B, taking brief intermissions to hunt down keys (at least it doesn't happen in a castle this time). So, the formula is: country/location + random letter in the English alphabet + "virus" = RE story. Most of the cast sound like they said their lines on the first take with no director telling them "sound more like this". Every character is one-dimensional with dialogue that is even worse. "What is this place? Where is Jill? What the hell is that?! We need a key." is the plot in a nutshell. Hell, THE WIKI tells the story better than this game does! It's pathetic. I gave it a 4 because Chris does have ONE moment of personality that made his character acceptable.
Sound 5/10
The sounds are all great! Guns, groans, motors, stone slabs moving around, splashing water, and even "some" of the actors are impressive! (I was most impressed with Jill's voice. She was terrific! Wesker is passible too.) The low score comes from the rest of the cast. Their lines are delivered with all the excitement and enthusiasm of a business math teacher. Combine this with the terrible plot/dialogue, you will be skipping every cutscene with no regrets. Capcom's only desparate attempt to keep the player interested in the cutscenes is showing a chick half-nude. "Hi, I'm (name) and my purpose in this plot is.....is um.....it's....uh I don't have one....um BOOBIES!" Does Capcom hate women or what?
The music is awesome! Some of the scores are on par with John Williams' compositions!
Graphics 7/10
I think they're beautiful, but almost everyone disagrees with me. My only gripe with the graphics is the enviornments are so bland; brown/tan washouts with no memorable scenery. They look great, but are just uninteresting.
Gameplay 8/10
Who cares about all that stuff anyway? It's a game, right? So, how's the game play? It works rather well! The controls are almost identical to RE4, which is fine and all, but nothing noteworthy or "all that new" was added aside from minor things. The game plays like RE4.5 instead of RE5. You use the same guns, fight the same guys, use the same controls, but this time, we tossed in Africa to the above mentioned formula. One new thing I loved was the ability to combo each other's melee attacks; tossing an enemy back and forth to your teammate, or getting behind a stunned enemy to kill it instantly. You can upgrade your guns and there's a few new toys like the shock stick that are kinda fun (but very under powered). Another feature is the new inventory and how it allows you to switch weapons on the fly or trade with your teammate. Although co-op, the game never takes advantage of the idea of having 2 players. The only time you "cooperate" is: I stand here 'n kill stuff, you go ober dere 'n kill stuff. I also hate the QTE's. They never give you enough of a warning, and usually are just a free death. It doesn't happen often, but when it does, it feels cheap and hurts the fun factor. In the end, RE5 is fun, and co-op will sate, but you can't shake that feeling that it's half-hearted. (RE5 got a lot of flak for its slow moving characters and sluggish turning. I personally think it's wonderful, and RE should have kept this. When they added free movement of other third-person games, the series went straight to CoD/GoW. I blame most of RE6's failure on this alone. Controls take some getting used to, but you'll learn to embrace it.)
Side notes: I wanted to save extra room to address the game's most controversial topic: racism. The short answer: ludacris. A virus breaks out all over the world in different games, but when it lands in Africia, NOW its racist? So, I can shoot zombies, but if I see a black zombie, now it's unethical. It doesn't make sense. "Racism" is very poorly defined nowadays, and everyone's just jumping in the bandwagon of ERMAHGERD RATHITH everytime a black person is even involved in said topic. Capcom even apologized to the world saying "we learned our lesson: no more racism!" As soon as I heard that, I knew 1 of 2 things were going to happen: either the next RE would happen in Asia (because Capcom is Japanese. It's politically safe.) or we would go back to Europe in RE4 where we killed 1,000s of hispanics, because obviously the community finds that more ethical. Sure enough, RE6 took place in Asia. Hire me. SHEVA'S DIALOGUE FLAT OUT SAYS WHY SHE EXISTS. Not because of character design, not to satisfy a plot hole in the story, but to ease the tensions of a white American killing black zombies...and a souless player-slot. I'm against racism and all, but this whole "racism" fad has derailed and spiraled out of control. Look at this this way for a second: we say this game is racist because its a white male killing blacks. Well, what if it was a black male killing white female zombies? Would that be acceptable? Why or why not? How about attacking the game for a REAL issue of bigotry like it's portrayal of women? I think the boss fight against Jill deserves some criticism. Kill 1,000's of hispanic zombies in RE4, nobody bats an eye. Kill a few black zombies, and everyone loses their s*&%.
A final thing I have to address is the "Gold Edition". Never heard of it? That's because it was a CONSOLE-ONLY RELEASE. After seeing some videos of GE's content, I found that it was had enough extra content to be a whole sequal in itself; as if Capcom deliberately witheld half of the game to release it later (not the first or last time they've done this. Check out Marvel vs. Capcom 3 then Ultimate MvC3). PC fans of RE5 were left in the dust. A nice, big, middle-finger was shot to PC gamers which is another of Capcom's terrible blights on their reputation (google metacritic Chaos Legion).
The Verdict
RE5 does deliver on fun gameplay, but coop is never taken to the height that it deserves. Unlockables do add noteworth replayability, but poor acting, poor story telling, bad plot, actors reluctant to do their jobs, and boring characters will ensure you don't stay for the story. RE5 scores a 7/10. It's a good game and worth buying, even for a solo play, but it's far from great; worth a run though.

"Somehow even more boring than the real thing. Throw your bobber in the water and wait. And wait. And... wait!"
The review:
I got this on a whim. It was hailed as a great time waster by the community, equivalent to a sort of interactive screensaver. You remember back in the 90s and early 00s when cool screensavers were all the rage, right? Nobody wanted some static image or this giant Windows ball just bouncing around aimlessly. We watned something more thrilling. Now don't get me wrong, I wasn't coming into this with the expectation it would be as gratuitous and extravagant as GTA 5. While there is not a lot of content at the present time, what it does it give you a good idea of what's to come. New maps will feature different scenic locales, but at its heart it will be the same thing.
The actual act of catching a fishie does not feel rewarding. It is far too easy and the "striking" as it is called is aided by a nice visual indicator on the side but the actual process of hooking does not feel fluid or thrilling. You basically click the RMB once you see the bobber shake violently.
You're able to move on a narrow set path around a lake, different spots attracting different types of tasty catches, for example, an area with a lot of pads will for the most part house different species than if you're casting directly into some deep open water. This is obviously not with out its caveats but the gist of the game is such that it is mentioned in the tutorial.
There is a lot of variety, at least proposed variety, that appears in the store that aid you in essentially doing the same thing... catching a fish. It seems it can get rather expensive, rather quickly. Most of the store items have not been implemented yet along with certain game modes. The different selections almost assuredly guarantee different species, with the largest being the most sought after, as your trophies and tournaments depend on the size of fish in your bucket (this is how you earn your in-game currency back). So, obviously the better the bait, the more it is going to cost you. And if you're content with the grind on the live baits, you could effectively bypass the sub par baits altogether.
One positive thing I will say is it brings to mind another hardcore outdoors simulator called The Hunter, in that these past-time activities are given new life in a technology dominated era. Where The Hunter failed was their Pay2Play system. In that game, you could only hunt a specific type of animal in a very specific newbie location. You had a lot of interesting gagetry but not enough incentive to keep playing and paying when this could be one of those one-off passing interests, at least that is how it was for me. This game is at least free, and gives you the OPTION of paying, but it is certainly not necessary if you're willing to grind for some line that's .001 thicker.
These simulation games will attract a relatively large crowd at the start, then trickle downward until you're left with the small minority of people who enjoy it for what it is. It was not a good time waster for me, because to truly waste time and enjoy it is to not notice where the last 2 hours went. After the short tutorial and some free casting, I noticed only a half hour had passed and I was already going for the uninstall button. This game is fine for what it is, but it is not for me.

Resident Evil 5 is a great game.  I think it get's heavily shafted as a poor follow up to one of the greatest games of all time, that being Resident Evil 4 obviously.  Sure, it is not as good as the latter, but it is still a damn fine game.
This is the first Resident Evil that went for heavy action as a scare tactic, and it did it very well.  There were plenty of moments where the shear amount of things going on at once kept me on the edge of my seat, and christ, this game is 5 years old and it is still gorgeous.  I mean really, really gorgeous, and the music is even more beautiful!  It's hard to believe this is a last-gen game.
Now for the things that kept this game from being amazing:  The AI is horrendous and makes single-player play a bad level of challenging, and even worse, you STILL control like a tank, but I guess that's one of the things that's still classic Resident Evil.  I also vaguely remember playing this game with a friend on one TV at one point, and I yearned to stop.  There were also some moments where the development screamed "make it more like Gears of War", and I don't want that in Resident Evil.  Let's face it, there's little to no originality in that series, and that impeeded the development of this game for sure.
In spite of those problems, I've had the will to play through this game multiple times.  It was a lot of fun, definitely worth the money despite some flaws.  There is no DLC for the PC version as it didn't sell well enough, which is a shame because "Lost In Nightmares" was so much fun, and I had a lot more fun playing this on PC than I did on a console.
Oh, and of course, the game is not racist.  Come on.
Even after 10 years, this game has still held up.

This game is nothing more than a console port of a really bad console game.  The needless button mashing will aggravate you, the unnecessary 6 second long cutscenes which poorly attempt to weave together a plot that you can't really care about will annoy you, the main characters are apparently mentally ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥,  and the feeble attempt by Capcom to connect this to previous Resident Evil games by inserting little notes, objects, and green and red herbs doesn't really make it a Resident Evil game. The over the shoulder view blocks half your screen and you can't change it, the combat system attempts to emulate something like call of duty except the weapon manipulation is dependant on an RE inventory system which makes no sense at all. I never really played any of the RE games. I heard, of course, about the franchise but that is mainly attributed to the films with the Ukrainian model Milla Jovovich. I bought this one on Steam sale many years ago but only recently have I been able to find someone to complete the game with.
And this is an important part to mention: the game is playable with somebody else as there are two protagonists. In case you do not find any one the A.I. can take control of the 2nd player but does a horrible job. So, grab a friend and make sure you also have a Live account as this is the 2nd annoying thing in this game - it still uses an already obsolete service. Once you start a game only via Live can you send the invite and of course the achievements are logged there.
Now that we have settled these two things we can move on to the actual game itself. The story and the cutscenes are VERY cheesy, however, the cutscenes pack a punch! There are more than 50 videos that are all replayable from the main menu. They are awesome! Cheesy but very-well made! There are 6 chapters divided up further into a couple of stages; you easily spend roughly 15 hours with the first playthrough.
The game itself is difficult at times: the gameplay itself is a bit "redundant" as no dodging is possible and when aiming your character cannot move, at all. You rely on each other and there are certain stages where you have to cooperate closely - only one of you can move while the other must provide protection. Also, bullets are limited so you have to carefully make every shot as each bullet counts.
Are you annoyed by quick time events? Well, RE 5 has many of those. During the cutscenes and also during boss battles. Some combinations popping up require some getting used to and these should be hit hardly very quickly.
Once you have familiarised yourself with the RE characteristics the game can be enjoyed, quite much. In fact, there are many collectibles and as weapons upgrades can be purchased with the collected treasure all upgraded weapons can be transferred to a 2nd gameplay. Just make sure you pick the New Game + option from the main menu. New difficulty is also unlocked if you want more challenge.

But thats not what Arma 3 is about. The vanilla game can be fun for some time, but the outstanding feature of Arma 3 definitely are its countless mods.
The many flaws the vanilla game has are compensated by its amazing community and its modding support. Arma has to be looked at as a modding platform, not neccesarily as a game that is fun to play out of the box.
Arma reaches it full potential with its mods, from realistic military simulation to roleplay, there  certainly is something for everyone, which is quite amazing for a game in our time.
It is also easy for the community to add content to the game without any modding experience, the 3D editor allows for easy scenario building which can then be published in the workshop for others to enjoy.

Gameplay
It’s better than RE4’s because there is a larger variety of enemies and a larger amount of enemies in one area. There is something bad though. El Gigante makes a return and you fight him in an on rails truck. You can’t even fight him in Mercenaries as far as I know. The RE5 fight is so easy too and felt more like a quick cameo. I’m very confused about the guns though. Some guns have special abilities. The first pistol has an upgradable ability to have headshots work as does the first shotty, but the later guns don’t have that. I guess through experimentation I will find out. There’s also some I haven’t tried like the stun rod. There is a large amount of weapons to choose from so that is good. The Mercenaries makes a comeback but no extra campaigns. It’s harder than the first one because when you pick up a new item you don’t know which item slot it will be in (you can quick select items using the number keys). So I end up not using it. (WARNING I’VE ONLY PLAYED 30 MIN OF THIS MODE SO IT MIGHT NOT BE THAT BAD).
There is a big issue with this game, Sheva in single player. Sheva is smart most of the time but that is the bad part. I want to kill the enemies not her, why does she get to have all the fun. You can alleviate this by giving her a cheap pistol but sometimes when I want to shoot enemies first with the sniper she either shoots my target making me miss or alerts them by beginning to shoot before I do. She can be really stupid too. There is a part where you have to fight a bunch of lickers (very strong enemies). What triggers this even is an elevator part where only one person can go. If you go what happens is you make it (with some lickers behind you) but Sheva will run like an idiot inside the room where there is a switch instead of waiting till we kill the lickers. If Sheva goes the same thing happens. It's really funny and probably she is an intended comic relief.
There is also a mod that removes Sheva from the game called ‘Alone in Africa’ but it makes her invincible and invisible to enemies and I don’t know how well it works. She probably is great to have in coop and in a harder difficulty but in Normal single player you are just babysitting her.
Story
RE5 is kind of like The Amazing Spiderman. Not as good as the original (RE4 and Spiderman by Sam Raimi) and makes references. Every time Leon was talking you had a big grin at his smart talking and one liners. RE4’s story was simple: Rescue the President’s daughter. Here it’s kind of hard to understand. The evil pharmaceutical corporations (not Umbrella just piggybackers) are selling BOW samples to terrorists and rebels all over the country. Kijuju is one of them so Chris, a member of the BSAA goes to investigate with Sheva Alomar, a member of the African division of the BSAA. This is where it gets complicated for me because there is a new government in Kijuju but is that government run by terrorists? Also who is the guy who groped Sheva’s butt? Is he a Kijuju official or a member of NATO or something. And I don’t even know if they are using Uroboros or Los Plagas or both. Oh well, the villain still has the same mocking/sexual undertone in his voice so that part matches up with RE4. Also the enemies in the game are more serious (as far as I know they could be saying funny stuff in a foreign language). The enemies in RE4 were kind of comical and said things like “behind you idiot” and “I’m gonna turn you into mincemeat”. That is the only scary part of this game and the fact that the enemy is using innocent civilians and making them kill people.
If you like Resident Evil 4 you should get this game. It’s bigger in terms of enemies and faster.

9.5/10
Third person shooter set in Africa (the first part looks like Somalia/Black Hawk Down, the second like Temple of Doom/King Solomon's mines + a secret bioterrist lab);  a solid game full of action, scares, stress, puzzles, a hot female partner, awesome graphics, no bugs, and a story full of twists which meets all loose ends of the RE franchise (yes, Wesker APPEARS here...)
My only complain is that you can't move while aiming/reloading, but other than that the gameplay is solid, and the game works like a charm with the highest settings  for 2010 (and beyond) computers, no problems with Win 8 either
If you loved RE4 you'll love 5, simple as that, this game is the DIRECT sequel of RE4, very, VERY similar games; the RE franchise may not be Survival Horror anymore, more like a kick♥♥♥♥♥Survival Shooter revamped franchise; anyway, you'll be scared, oh yes, by facing a horde of infected zulu warriors hell bent on killing you...with only 4 bullets left...
Overall this game is the most realistic RE yet: by using a reduced inventory (only 9 items!, and that includes the medicines and ammo), it's clear that the developers want you to make decisions: more ammo or more meds? should I carry just the shotgun and bazooka? will I survive without the always reliable hand gun? will I find enough shotgun ammo? should I sacrifice the vest since I usually kill the enemies from a distance? etc etc. DECISIONS, MAN! DECISIONS!
And there's the ONE BIG FLAW of this game: lack of manual save...
Anyway, you can always load a saved game to collect more ammo/gold since they respawn EVERY time you just reload an autosaved game (NOTE!: the game only saves on auto, you can't manually save, AND the checkpoints DON'T reload if you quit the game; keep that in mind to avoid frustration, unless you're a noob, you should know by now that A CHECKPOINT ISN'T ALWAYS AN AUTOSAVE FILE)
ANOTHER TIP: every time you quit, the game will ASK you if you wanna SAVE THE INVENTORY-> keep in mind that CHOOSING YES will save your current ammo/gold, and that CAN be a problem: for example, I reloaded a saved game with tons of ammo, but a boss kicked my♥♥♥♥♥ tired of dying-reloading-dying-reloading-dying-etc, I called t quits for the day, then I chose "yes-save the inventory" option without realizing what the hell  I was doing (I was sleepy), and the result was that the game saved my inventory with almost NO BULLETS left; I nearly had a seizure...for real; in other words, YOU SHOULD ONLY SAVE YOUR INVENTORY AFTER ADVANCING A CHAPTER OR AFTER DEFEATING A BOSS, BUT NEVER AFTER GETTING KILLED...
Ignore the bitter hipster haters that still think this franchise should have ended after RE3, the RE franchise is alive and well (check out my review of RE6, that game didn't suck at all...)
PD: you'll find a lot of noobs crying here because the game cannot work without GFWL; well, it's not that difficult to just SHUT DOWN the damn thing, bunch of noobs...

While this game does retain some of the token Saints Row insanity, it lacks the clever humor and writing that the second and fourth did so well. The series maintains and adheres to a feeling of immaturity and lunacy, the second and fourth feel like children at heart. The third, however, just feels like a childish game. Instead of clever references and satire, it goes for cheap toilet gags and shock humor, all of which fall flat, making the entire game feel weaker than the rest. If you're a diehard Saints fan, then you'll most likely play through this only once, never again wanting to experience the disappointment and boredom it brings. If you want a humorous GTA satire gangster game, play SR2. If you want the absolute best Saints Row humor the franchise has to offer, play SR4. Pass on this.

Changing my review to not recommended, it was a joke review to start with, but this one is serious. The gameplay as far as simulation itself is the best you'll find in any fishing game, much like theHunter. Also much like theHunter though, the devs decided to go the route of "pay to win".
I've dumped a lot of hours into this game and I thoroughly enjoyed it, but instead of being smart about their microtransactions like adding more customization through paying, or simply keeping the subscription model and make it worthwhile, they went the paywall route.
No matter how good you are at this game (Believe me, I have no problem catching fish as of the most recent patch.) you'll never be ahead and that's horrible balancing and shows that they're having financial issues. It's a bit unsettling what they did with the coins and if you play frequently you're going to have to spend a lot, as the coins are to advance to the next day after you fill your net (Even with a large net it doesn't take long if you're good.)
What once was an amazing fishing simulator and I would have easily recommended it to friends, quickly became a cash grab and that's upsetting. I had high hopes for the game and company; however, I doubt anything will change their mind on the way they currently have it set up.
I would have easily, and did, buy bundles or cosmetics. Even having "tackle boxes" that had random loot in them like CSGO except you get lures/rod skins/clothing would have been awesome, but no, they decided to put you behind a paywall instead.

This game is difficult on levels, you have to try going through the levels and remembering patterns and strategies. At the same time though... it's interesting. It's the first 2D platformer I've played on the PC that I didn't hate the controls of, and that says a lot. Every time I've died, it was entirely my fault, not due to the mechanics. Honestly I couldn't play this for hours on end, I have to set times for myself because it does get frustrating and difficult, but overall, the upgrades, the gameplay, everything feels awesome. This feeling, this game, this product, is what retro game developers should be striving for. 11/10, by far the best 2D platformer I have backed and then played. If you like a challenge, and you loved/currently love 2D platformers that really challenge you, this is your game.

This is probably the best and closest example you are going to get for an NES-era type of game without playing a game from that era. It reminded me a lot of Megaman 9-10 that Capcom put out a while back. Moreso than the other games Shovel Knight has been compared to.  Everything from the soundtrack and general look and feel just reminds me way more of a Megaman 9 vibe than Duck Tales and Castlevania, which is what it is usually compared to.
For story, you go on a quest to go save your love interest Shield Knight who was captured by the Enchantress and standing in your way are 8 knights that you have to battle through. Simple enough, as it should be.
Unlike Megaman, you don't get any powers from killing the boss.  However, you get a themed sub weapon called a relic (think Castlevania) from their stage by exploring. There are a couple problems. With the exception of 3 of them, the rest are essentially useless. You simply use them for one *very* specific instance in a stage and they just collect dust in your inventory. I think this is a massive oversight. Also, you can easily cheese practically any boss thanks to the no cool down one particular relic has that gives you 3 seconds of invulnerability. Essentially, if you time it right and have a high enough  pool, you can basically be invincible and no boss really has any hope of attacking you. Of course, you don't have to use it, but it is important to bring up.
Speaking of powerups, there are only 3 for your shovel. Kind of disappointing. You can also upgrade your armor with 5 different armor types, each with their own perks with the exception of one that just looks flashy. I was happy with the armor upgrades.  There are also two goblets you can collect which can be used to be filled with a potion that can function as a full heal, a 10 second invincibility, or a 60 second grab all treasure magnet effect. You will almost never use the treasure magnet.  You can also max up your health and magic, naturally.
As far as side quests, your main one is collecting 46 music notes. Scattered throughout stages and accomplishing other miscellaneous things will sometimes warrant in a music note. I appreciate their REAL purpose in the stages to force you to try the stages' more challenging segments. There are 4 mini bosses in the game, as well as one minigame and....well that's about it. In terms of side content the game is lacking.
As far as difficulty goes, I was pleased with the difficulty. It wasn't throw your controller difficult, or frustrating. The controls take a little getting used to because of how momentum affects Shovel Knight, but my point is it won't be because of controls that you die. Death in this game isn't unfair, the game teaches you well in advance what to expect usually early in the level and it throws it's most challenging bits at you mid to late game, as expected. Death is all user-error. The bosses become a matter of trading hits really, but their patterns can be exploited for those seeking more of a challenge. They aren't overly difficult.
All in all, it's a solid title. There is a new game+ that supposedly makes the game harder, but I got all I wanted out of the game for now. No real  desire to run through it again, maybe at a later time. Other than NG+, I don't imagine someone wanting to run through it again after they complete NG+. The game doesn't have a lot of replayability due to most of the sub weapons being useless and not enough sidequests or content to keep you busy.
$15 is a fair asking price, but you should wait for a sale. for $5-8 I think it's more of a pargain for what you get. All in all it will take you about 5 hours to run through the game if you are an average player.

Incredibly fun introductory level tower defense game that is great in the way it incrementally adds elements to the tower defense gameplay through its Adventure (campaign) mode. Its other modes include survival, Mini-Game, and puzzle. Each add additional ways to enjoy the game. Mini-games is a variety pack of introductions to different genres of games, survival is a hardcore slow build mode that puts all of your knowledge garnered from adventure mode to the test. Lastly is the puzzle section which is my personal favorite as it makes you think about the game from not only a different perspective but also in a different manner as there are different constraints on gameplay, including removing the real time element. Overall it is a very well rounded game and well worth the price, especially when on sale.

Just got this from a friend for my birthday, have been playing it for some time and thought I might as well write a review, seeing how I was pleasantly surprised about how fun this game is.
As you can see, it's a retro game that draws from classic platformers we have all played sometime in the past, so you're certain to find the style and mechanics quite intuitive and familiar, which makes for a very easy game to master, whose challenge comes from the environment and not from the controls, just the way it should be. So the gameplay is nothing to worry about, it's straightforward and very functional. Full controller support makes it even better, of course.
Storyline is quite simple, some might say cliché, but that's the way the game wants it to be, a classic tale of a lone hero searching for justice. The characters are all quite diverse, interesting and comic, you'll be delighted to talk to villagers and to hear what your enemies have to say.
The game rewards you nicely for exploring, no search for collectibles feels pointless, and even if you have no interest in the music tracks you can bring to the bard to play, the gold reward for retrieving them is reason enough to keep your eyes open.  Most artifacts you can collect are completely optional, but can be unbelieavably useful in the right situations, which will surely motivate you to get them all.
And talking about music, the soundtrack is quite awesome, very diverse, pleasant and adequate to each situation, which greatly contributes to the atmosphere of the various places you'll be visiting in your quest, all of them very unique and with their own peculiarities, which will sure get you curious about where you'll end up next.
Overall it's not a difficult game, and except for some specific points, the challenge feels fair and failure, rather than being frustrating, will just stimulate you to hone your skills enough to beat the obstacle, which likely won't take long, making for a game that flows nicely and won't make you stuck. There's no game over, dying just resets you in the last checkpoint (they can be destroyed for some coins, which makes for interesting reward X risk decisions and a very peculiar gameplay feature) with some coins less, which can be recovered if you get to them without dying. More hardcore gamers might want to play something else, this is more suited to the average joe who likes to keep moving forward without great hassles.
To conclude, gotta say I'm quite happy to not have missed this game, as I didn't give it much thought when I saw it's store page for the first time. Shovel Knight greatly exceded my expectations, and although short (I haven't finished it yet, but I'm nearly there, I suppose it will sum up to 8 hours of gameplay, give or take), makes for a thoroughly enjoyable experience for you out there who is looking for a simple and fun game to pass a few hours with. I'd surely recommend it.

With almost a full day of gameplay I want to start a first impression review for people both in the know how for fishing and new to fishing games (like me. Yep, I'm a CSGO/Team Fortress player, not a simulator/fishing player. BUT I've fished in my life time):

This is the first game in a long time that has had me "hooked" extensively. The gameplay is fluid and accurate. Stepping into the game I was expecting 1 of 2 things: Confusing and unnecessary game mechanics OR pay for the "best" equiptment as do MANY other fishing simulators contain.
BOY WAS I WRONG. Off the bat the tutorial gives you the need to know basics for fishing in general which is easy to use and from experience really an amazing portrail of the sport in real life. After you understand the simple and relaxing controls you're off fishing on your own.
USUALLY, games like this would start you off with fish in tiers (Example: Start bluegill, then catfish, then bass, and so on). However, you're able to start going for either bluegill, catfish, pike, or bass right off the bat. When it comes to fishing in this game, real world knowledge is amazingly potent in this game. A HUGE plus over other fishing simulators! Catching a fish in this game gives a SUPER rewarding and that's why I'm enjoying every bit of the game play.
There are free to play games I play without spending a dime but are annoyingly hard and VERY long to progress through where I just get burnt out and stop playing. Then, there are games where a majority of everything in the shop can be achieved... PURELY BY PLAYING!
You don't need to spend anything to achieve special currency. Yep, "premium currency" is awarded through achievments and special fish. Yep, just like the games of old, you can unlock special stuff just by playing the game! DLCs? PSSSSH. Though their DLCs give you and edge early on, you can completely farm up to get all the items in the DLCs just from playing.
Also, the in game currency is made fast with a bit of work BUT no where near grindy or slow as many other F2P models out there. This game's F2P model is a HUGE plus being a F2P player. Great job!!!

One thing that slows you down is the fact that there's only so many fish you can catch. To many people this can bog down grinding and cause interest to droop off but it's what I expect from a game that just went into release. I know for a fact there's going to be A LOT more content to be added here such as tournaments, quests, missions, and more fish and equiptment.
Though on the plus side to this there are varients of the current fish you can catch and personally that's good enough for an on release game.
Yep, Grindy. Big surprise there from a F2P game right? Well, as to be expected. Every game with progression has a grind but I feel like this game handles it fairly well to a point. Upon reaching lvl 15+ there's a huge gap in exp gain that causes the game to really slow down. However, this is in place so the level split between casual and hard core doesn't grow too far apart.
In all honesty this is a good move to prevent inbalances when tournaments get released. I would like to mention this is changing a week after this post to increase exp gain all around. The low level grind is decent up until level 10 and then you feel the monotonous grind thereafter. Like I stated! They're changing this in a week so this will change for sure!
If you have experience fishing or used to fish like me, then you'll be just at home here. Like I stated in the pros, this game is SPOT ON with relation to real life fishing.
However, if you're completely new to fishing, you might have a hard time getting started since every single fish has their own way of being caught. Though this can be a problem for a little bit, there's PLENTY of guides on youtube, guides here on steam, and help in game.

Honestly, I went in with expectations set by many failed misses in the fishing game genre from years before but I'm knocked on my♥♥♥♥♥with how well this game came to rise up to what has been sorely missing in this genre of gaming. The F2P market is both gameplay derived and not pay to win, the gameplay is spot on and rewarding, the graphics are beautiful as all hell, the physics are nice, and importantly to the genre, this game is really accurate.
Though there are kinks here and there with lack of content and poor entry level, this game hit the spot for an alternative to FPS, RTS, and Strategy games that I'm used to playing.
I really hope the devs continue to keep the game in the positive heading.

I really want to like this game. I loved Rainbow 6 and Rogue Spear, and this sort of reminds me of that. However, the problems with the game go way beyond what they are adressing in the Operation Health update. The latency mitigation actually helps people with high ping get an unfair advantage, which results in people artificially increasing their ping to the 200-300ms range to get a 1-3 second peeker's advantage. This is not something they appear to be doing anything about in the above mentioned update cycle. The fact that smoke and gas grenades as well as hit reg is basically handled client side makes for completely unpredictable gameplay where you can be standing in thick smoke on your screen while the other player sees you clear as day. Or with Smoke's gas grenades which you should be taking damage according to Smoke's screen, but on yours you do not. This is completely unacceptable for a game which is used in the e-sports in 2017.
The hit reg is attrocious and appears to be client based in some sort of weird way, which makes you see hits bloom all over the face of your opponent on your screen, but when you see the kill cam from the other side the other player hasn't even taken damage.
Then we come to the worst part of this game, which incidentally also is a reccuring theme for Ubisoft online games. The cheater problem is not taken seriously. Where other developers ban you, your IP, HWID and your account permanently Ubisoft seems to be more interested in getting the same cheater to buy another license as they only appear to ban your license key. Not only that, but the time it takes to ban these people is problematic to say the least. Not only that, but allowing people to abuse the ping mitigation feature for more than a year without fixing said problem is a really quick way of alienating your legitimate players.
As for the ranking system... It's not worth wasting time on. It certainly isn't working as well as in games like Paladins or Overwatch. You always risk ending up in matches against people who are way above you in the ranks and who use you as a door mat while telling you how crap you are. I pity the newbies who try to play Casual or ranked initially, who are being pitted against players who have 300+ hours in the game. What a rotten way to have to learn the game...
In short this game has a ton of potential, but it's wasted through really bad mechanics and design choices. The only way to play this game is on a LAN with friends. Anything else will just lead you to pull your hair out in frustration. Sadly, the so called Operation Health seems to be omitting the real issues from it's list of fixes. Like the poor design of the latency mitigation system as well as the complete lack of changes to the client side focus in this game, which makes it too unpredictable to be even classified as a mediocre online multiplayer shooter. But the potential it had... Oh the potential...

Shovel Knight is one of those games that you remember for a long time. It is a homage to the old NES classics, but the game really does stand on its own, even without the added nostalgia. Controls are immaculate (when using a controller, at least), the soundtrack is memorable for every stage, and the story and characters goes well beyond what one could reasonably expect from a retro title like this.
One of the best parts of Shovel Knight is the excelent difficulty curve. The game manages to challange you throughout the entire game, without ever leaving you frustrated or bored. The game never holds your hand, and expects you to make your own tactics from the available special powers, of which there are plenty. With infinite lives and a generous checkpoint system though, you really shouldn't find this game more difficult than other games unless you are particularly bad at platformers.
As can be expected of this kind of platformer, completing the game for the first time can be done in about 6 hours. This might seem on the short side, but as the gameplay never go stale, this really is a game that one can play over and over. Even with the game itself complete, there are plenty of achievements that are quite challanging, and helps add replay value to the game. In addition, the developers have more material that will eventually be added to the game for free, so the fact that the game can be completed in one hour and 30 minutes shouldn't deter you from purchasing the title, as it holds plenty of value.

has always been a franchise of a strong story, and an even stronger atmosphere. As a fan of the series since the first game, I find these two elements to be infinitely important in making an entry in the series feel relevant. I found
to fail in accomplishing that in so many different ways that I don't know where to start.
First, I'd like to point out that this isn't a terrible game through-and-through. It has some good moments and its general gameplay is fairly enjoyable, but it's not a great game either. Second, as another disclaimer, I am aware that this game wasn't supposed to follow in the footsteps of the classic games, and the gameplay was already overhauled by
, so that can't be held against this title. However,
was a great game, even if it too distanced itself from its predecessors. It had some major flaws as well, but it was infinitely better than
.
Starting with the better qualities of this game, it's actually relatively fluent and enjoyable to play: the controls work fine and it's fun to shoot things. It also looks good, and just by playing it for a while doesn't invoke that much to complain about.
However, after a while the gameplay becomes grinding, and things like the camera angle start to chafe - you will find yourself spitting profanities in frustration as it becomes impossible to react in time or estimate distances correctly because of the camera, and enemies that move in unexpected ways behind the character model. This is a part of the game, granted, but it doesn't add much to the enjoyment. Save for the clumsiness with the camera and sometimes the controls, the difficulty is mostly fair and provides a decent challenge for those who have the patience to tackle the game.
Also, the further the game progresses, the more it starts to feel like a rail shooter - there is little to no wiggle room in terms of routes to take or directions to approach a target from. This makes it feel less like a well-executed action game and more like a brainless shoot-'em-up.
While a lot of players couldn't care less for the plot, it should be pointed out that
does a terrible job with it. As a standalone story, the plot is unimaginative and sometimes even ridiculous in its clumsy twists, and fails to provide any hooks to keep the player invested in it. It is games like this that encourage cutscene-skipping that reaches out into games that actually could have something relevant to say.
But as a sequel to a number of games with good stories,
is an absolute butcher. It appears the writers were so in hurry with burying the "previous" generation of the series that they entirely neglected making the story believable, interesting or even in keeping with its predecessors. Returning characters don't feel like the same characters at all, unresolved plot points are omitted without explanation, and existing story details are altered in a way that makes it seem like the writers didn't even know the existing story to begin with. It's one thing to start fresh and deviate from the series' style or themes, but to steamroll over the mythology that fans of the series have been interested in and fallen in love with, that's just being an indifferent jerk.
To sum it up, in certain doses,
can be adequate fun to pass the time. But it's not an especially good game. And it's definitely not something I'd recommend to anyone who yearns the experiences they had with the classic titles of the series, but obviously, that's a given. So as a
game, it's terrible, and as a standalone title, it's nothing special.

Before you start telling how my downvote is wrong from the get-go, listen to what I have to say first.
The game is great. Arma 3 is an amazing game that doesn't focus on how many kills you can get or who is better than who. It is a tactical, team-based coordinated game and stuff like this you cannot find/remake easily! Sure there is SQUADS but Arma is the one we're talking about. So let's go through what makes this game good!
Pros:
- The game almost forces you to use teamwork and to utilize a different shooter gameplay style. With the technical vocabulary being one of the many tools, also how play matters as well. This isn't Call of Duty where you can run on walls and get easy picks or Battlefield where you can just find a tank and gun it (Somewhat).
- Graphics are one of the many amazing features yet downside as well (Which will be mentioned later). The game looks absolutey astounding from the smoke textures to the tank tracks to the explosions and clouds in the sky. As said many times by others, the little details are sometimes what matters.
- Voicing/Sounds. Not sure if many people mention this, but the sounds of weapons and voices of the AI are pretty solid. Of course it could use some tweaking here and there, but as of now, I am fine listening to the sounds of machine-gun fire ripping through AI and foliage alike.
- Animations. Every since Arma and Arma 2, the animations have greatly improved! I've seen it firsthand and on
FRANKIEonPC's videos of his recent 2 Arma 3: DayZ videos where they even had proper reload animations. It's come so far and I am proud of what they've done.
Now that that's out of the way, let's go to what makes it bad.
Cons:
- Optimization. Now, if you scroll on over to my profile and look at my Info Box (bottom) you can see my PC specs right there. Now, yes, it may be a bit overkill but if that's the case I should be getting over 60FPS right? Wrong. At even Medium settings, I barely managed to top 32FPS and Low settings makes the game unplayable to most. The fact that everything is so jagged and bland, pixelated at some times? Immersion ruined.
- Graphics. As stated, I would've mentioned this later. The graphics are very great as said above but they could use some serious work. Clipping textures, texture glitches and light flicker (Meaning the lighting from the sun or flashlights sometimes bugs out and just rapidly flickering through walls). With this game being as semi-costly as it is and the DLC's including APEX out, i'd expect at least the light flickering and clipping textures somewhat refurbished.
- Inconsistency. Not going to explain much as this explains itself. Whenever you attempt to get into a vehicle, pull out a gun or do basic actions, the game doesn't understand what you want and just stops. Either the game will freeze or just won't do what you want and that 4 seconds needed to take out your weapon again or enter the vehicle will get you killed. When I last played, I was in a gunfight on a.. believe it was an RP server. Tried to get into my APC and it wouldn't let me in. Wasn't locked, wasn't broke, fully functional. Took me 3 tries to get into it and by then I was getting robbed. Tried to take out my rifle 4 times and it did the animation but put it back, and by then I was dead. I don't know what this would fall under but whatever it is, it MUST be fixed.
As stated, I love Arma 3 and is great to play! But until the many inconveniences are either tweaked or fully fixed, my vote stays the same and I do not reccomend people to buy this.

Sadly, I would say this disappointment of a game does not come as a result of the bar being too high with RE4, but moreso with the game itself being lacklustre. Action and fast paced fighting is pushed more instead of the slower, more controlled survival horror we saw in earlier games, and it results in the game not feeling right often. This, coupled with ridiculous AI from a partner and a storyline that holds its own as an RE plot, but could have been worked more thoroughly, generally leaves the game feeling like a waste of several hours.
It is enjoyable at times, but overall, I would reccomend you stick to RE2 and 4.

What would be considered a truly innovative and immersive evolution in the Resident Evil universe by some, an abomination by others, Resident Evil 5 is what you make of it.  I was one of the die-hards from the old school series that initially frowned upon this new "advancement" in the series, but what I looked down my nose at back in 2009, I can now reminisce upon with affection.  Sure it may not be a true traditional survival horror game, but let's take a look at what it did right.  We are re-united with franchise favorite Chris Redfield, bringing in the old-school fans, and we are introduced to Sheva, who is actually portrayed as a strong woman with character and proves to be a solid partner.  We have a new co-op dynamic that we had never seen before in this form, making it honestly approachable to fresh blood, bringing new fans to the series.  With a solid storyline and an impressive amount of collectibles to find, upgrades to weapons and armor, and the classic "Mercenaries" mode you'll find an overall enjoyable experience.  I personally still find the game visually beautiful, the voice acting solid, and the controls are ace.  It's not something we initially accepted as a great game, but looking back and re-playing it brings me an immense amount of happiness.  Sure, Excellea was an awful character, the portrayal of Jill was pretty terrible, the demise of one of my favorite characters was the worst...but I still smile when I play.  And I think at its core it has its heart in the right place, and that's what's important.

If you're a fan of any kind of tactical shooter, I highly recommend giving this one a shot. I'll try and lay out a few reasons as to why I feel like you should or shouldn't pick this one up. Also, if you feel like you're tight on money, definitely pick up the starter edition. It is 100% worth the price, because everything is included in the starter edition that is included in the standard edition. The only difference is that you will have to play more to get the operators, but that's it. No extra fees, nothing exluded, the whole game.
PROS+++
1. The community for this game (while still having a few bad apples like every community does) is so helpful and so willing to work together. When you tell someone to stop, they hold position. When you tell them when to go in, they listen. People are also willing to understand if you are new, and apologize if they teamkill. Hell, sometimes when you accidentally teamkill them, they will already forgive you for it before you say anything, or sometimes even apologize for getting in your way.
2. The gunplay is smooth, and highly engaging. The leaning system in this game really sets it apart from other games and allows you to peek with ease and smooth movement.
3. Customization is top ♥♥♥♥ing notch here. From the different operator perks, to the customization of your guns attachments, to camos and skins you can unlock for your guns, charms you can have on your gun, even outfits and headgear for your operator. If you're a fan of customization at all, it definitely does not let up here.
4. Competitive replayability.  Anyone who has played any kind of ranked game knows that a ranked system with a competitive community allows for thousands of hours of replayability.
5. Updates to the game have been pretty good. The recent Operation Health received many different views, but I completely love it. My queue times got cut almost into a fourth of the time that I was in queue before, I can do other things in queue rather than staring at the screen, and i notice the hitreg being a lot smoother and better than before. Really enjoying it.
6. The graphics are absolutely gorgeous. Not much more to say here. It's also really well optimized. (at least now it is.)
CONS---
1. Uplay. It's not too big of a deal, but it's just annoying at times. Not too big of a gripe here, often forget I'm using Uplay.
2. No story mode. The situations allow for a good single player experience, as well as the terrorist hunt, but the game really shines here with the multiplayer. It was clearly designed around it.
3. (THIS COULD BE CONSIDERED A PRO) If you do get the starter edition, the operators will take some time, and you will have to play the game a bit of time to unlock all of the operators. However, you can do just fine with just a couple operators, and the game gives you a couple operators that are friendly to beginner players.
Overall, If you're a fan at all of Counter Strike, Rainbow six previous titles, or played SOCOM in the past, this is a must buy. I don't have the MOST hours on the game, but so far I've been having a blast. The game is gorgeous, fun, and an absolutely awesome time with a few friends, or solo. Definitely a recommendation from me.

This review was around for a long time but I happened to stumble upon a bug where it didn't want to be published. Finally, I found a workaround: shorter reviews (but very short) and then edit. Steam support is investigating why I can't publish long reviews for some games and have no problem for others.
You're Mel. You're an Olympian. You've been recruited by Aperture Science to be a test subject. We're in 1952. And you're going to sleep.... until you're woken up and see the surroundings you're pretty sure you just passed having changed.... dramatically. With a device shooting portals, it's up to you to find your way out.
Portal Stories: Mel is a mod requiring that you own Portal 2, though you don't need it installed. And if you're a fan of Portal 2, you'll like this one. The rooms aren't easy at first sight, not like in Portal or Portal 2 where you have a slow progression. Nope, with Mel, you're confronted to gels early enough to tell yourself "Why am I here again?". There is nothing new in terms of gameplay, apart perhaps the red particle fence that kills you too.
And well, you bet you're not in 1952 anymore. I can imagine poor Mel, waking up with someone trying to guide her and that is clearly trying to hide the fact that we're... well, years after. And then, making your way up, meeting technologies you couldn't have never dreamed off. A new enemy trying to kill you too though well, it's not GLaDOS.
The graphics are the same as in Portal 2, which is not really a problem. At least, you're familiar with the structure of Aperture Science facilities. The soundtrack is also quite good. Besides, you get some reference from the official games: Cave Johnson, Caroline, the gels, etc..
Portal Stories comes also with achievements. I just took part of a brainstorming for an achievement guide made by someone else. I'm feeling satisfied to have helped him.
My only complaint is perhaps about the difficulty. I wish I wasn't thrown directly in complex puzzles. While I love them and managed to solve some rooms, I'm still having difficulties to plan the stuff in my head - which is a result of a over-analyzing brain.
Anyway, go ahead. It's free, with a free soundtrack and good too :)

Shovel Knight is the most addicting game I have played since Spelunky was released on the PC... not only is it one of the most original games ever, it is one of the most well designed, polished, clever, funny, and downright fun to play games on the market. Each level feels like someone spent months double-thinking every tiny detail to make it absolutely perfect... which is what many of these levels are, perfect. If you're going for some of the harder achievements, the difficulty may make you want to pull out your hair a couple of times
, but the game will never make you regret your purchase.

So, let me just start by saying this: If you enjoyed Portal and Portal 2, you
to play this game. The puzzles are challenging, the characters enjoyable, and the story fits with what was already established in the other games. It is as close to Portal 3 as it gets.
Time and time again, I'm blown away by what the modding community can accomplish. Building up on what Valve gave us, these people make amazing games that easily compare to - and sometimes surpass - anything a major developer could put out. And while some mods - such as
- eventually get sold, not everyone has that guarantee, so these people make these games purely out of love for the game, without making any money.
And the best thing is: they didn't half♥♥♥♥♥it! From custom models like the old Portal Gun or Mel herself, to new, fully-voiced characters like Virgil and AEGIS,
feels like a whole new game!
So what is the story? Well, as you might have guessed from the title, you don't play as Chell in this game. Instead, you play as Mel, a test subject from the heyday of Aperture Science, back when they could afford to get war heroes and Olympians as their test subjects. Mel gets assigned to test a Short-Term Relaxation Vault, only for something to go wrong (gasp, what a shock!) and for her to wake up an unknown amout of time later. And thus begins her attempt to climb to the top and escape Aperture Science! Pretty simple, but hey, it works.
But enough about that, you probably want to know about the gameplay. Unlike other Portal mods like
,
doesn't really add anything new in terms of gameplay elements, other than maybe the death emancipation grills. But nevertheless, the puzzles it gives you are enjoyable as hell, and have that same thing as the regular Portal games, where you feel like an idiot one second and a genius the next. The way the game originally shipped was apparently very difficult, but it has been overhauled, and now you have the choice of playing the difficult puzzles or the easier ones. One thing I noticed is that there is a lot more thinking outside the box, like in the original Portal. For example, using a cube as a step to reach a higher platform, or fizzling cubes in order to get them off of buttons, you know, stuff like that. The only fault I could find with the game is that, while the game is challenging and quite fun, it lacks a bit in length, however, that can be forgiven, seeing how it is a free modification.
So, basically, this game is the closest thing to Portal 3 that we're going to get. It's great, it's detailed, it gets those gears in your head turning, and it just feels
. And if you still have any doubts about getting it, consider this: it's free! All you need is to own Portal 2, but if you're reading this, you probably already do.
So what are you waiting for? Go do some Science!

Speaking of, there are tons of secrets to discover in Shovel Knight.  Secret treasure, secret areas, secret secrets.  Also lots of great little challenge areas where you can really rack up loot if you're skilled enough.
The whole game runs about the length of any old NES platformer, which I think is exactly where it needs to be.  There's still reason to come back with a New Game+ feature and achievements to unlock.  Of course, if that's not your thing, you can still have a lot of fun just playing it again.  I've beaten the game twice now and still playing.
A+, 5 Stars, 2 Thumbs Up, 10/10... If you have any inkling toward classic 8-bit platformers, this is a must have.

I was absolutely amazed to find just how polished this game was, and I can honestly say that Portal Stories: Mel is worthy to be part of the Portal franchise.
Being set in between the events of Portal and Portal 2, PS:M manages to retain the beautiful atmosphere of the Aperture Laboratories whilst still being  somewhat unique. Between the huge, open areas of the Aperture Facility and abandoned world that I have grown so fond of, it was good to see that everything great about the previous Portals made it's way into the development of this. And while there are cutscenes, they are very well done and don't seem to hinder immersion.
The gameplay was great as well, with puzzles that were at times extremely difficult; requiring ways of thinking about problems that's quite rare in games. This could at times be frustrating, though extremely rewarding once solved. And while there aren't a remarkably large amount of puzzles, there is still 8+ hours of content(for free, mind you) between the freedom of exploration and sheer difficulty of the puzzles.
If you enjoy puzzles, platforming, and Portals, you will almost certainly enjoy this. 9.5/10

Ok so this is my first Steam game review. This game is so good I am spending part of my Fishing Planet time to write this.
I love everything about this game except one thing, which i will get to.
First the pros:
1. The amount of details the developers put into this game is unreal. Every fish species has its habitat you have to fish for it in just as in real life and the habitats are true to life. Even the action of the lure you are using is a big factor just like real life. Same with the bait. Just like fishing in real life combine all those factors and execute your cast and retreival properly and you may have a chance at the fish your hoping for. Odd are though, that it will be just another Bluegill.
2. For an early access game, in my experience this has the least amount of bugs, personally I haven't experienced any.That being said I have heard in game that others have been experiencing visual glitches. As for game mechanics, i have heard nothing.
3. The graphics are quite decent and doesn't bog my graphics card down much, if at all, and im running max settings on an old NVIDIA GeForce GTX 460. The water looks good, pretty realisic. The only thing i would say is add a little more such as the occasional fish jump and more to the fishing gear section such as sunglasses. So if your wearing polarized shades you can see past the glare and be able to see the fish underwater. I know that would be a lot to add but it would just improve the overal appeal of the game and add to the realism of the fishing in this game.
The only con is the license system. Now i know this game revolves around realism but come on, the only thing worse than buying a license to fish in real life is buying one in a game. Every. Time. You. Go. On. A. Fishing. Trip. Unless you wanna spend an absurd amount of in game money for several months worth of fishing.
Here's the thing, I live in Upstate New York, The We'll Charge You For Everything Except Taking A Shi%, Oh Wait We Charge For That Too State. and i only have to buy one once a year. And only for a measly 20 bucks at WalMart. I am just glad they don't make you pay real life money for in game licenses, or else i wouldn't play. But catching fish doesnt earn that much money especially when fishing trips in game are ridiculously expensive coupled with expensive fishing licenses. But if i wanted to not be able to afford to go on a fishing trip i would just shut off my computer and sit at my desk and not go on a fishing trip. Lower the prices of travel and licenses, but if you want to keep the prices so expensive have the fish earn more money seeing as that is your only source of income.
Other than that i love this game and i would recommend it to anyone and everyone. I know some random guy's rating doesnt matter much but ill give it a 9/10, and if the income and/or prices change for the better ill change it to 10/10.

The fps genre is saturated and overcrowded with casual shooters and run-and-gun games. There are some games, like counter-strike, which introduce more tactical and strategic gameplay, but even those games fall to skill based heavily on accuracy and reaction times rather than strategy and coordination. Rainbow Six Siege provides a perfect mix of relying on your skills of aiming and recoil control, and having good positioning and tactics. You obviously need to have good accuracy to hit your targets, and the game rewards you for lining up your shots by having a one-shot headshot kill with every weapon mechanic that favors taking a little time to aim rather than spraying wildly at your enemies. But aim alone won't be enough to win. Game sense plays a large role in Siege, and you have to learn many little things in order to master it. You have to memorize map layouts and where cameras, spawnpeek windows, and camping spots are; you have to figure out when, where, and how to use each operator's gadget, and which operator to pick based on the current map and your team's composition; and you have to coordinate with your teammates about where to enter from, defend from, which areas need reinforcements and/or gadgets, and giving callouts when you die. Another great feature about the game is the importance of information. Gathering information is one of the things that sets Siege apart from other fps titles because in most games you go in blind and it's all dependent on who can react faster and more accurately, however in Siege you are almost undoubtedly going to die if you rush in unprepared. Luckily, Siege provides you with many tools to gather information. All of the attackers get two drones that they can drive around and look at the enemy positions with, and if you want to get a more precise location, you can scan enemies which pings them with a red bubble that your whole team can see over the location you scanned them in. On the defending side, they get a group of cameras in fixed locations spread across each map, and your team gets access to 3 additional cameras that can be thrown anywhere in the map if you or a teammate chooses Valkyrie. These cameras act like stationary drones that can look around and scan enemies, but are incapable of moving like drones. Certain other operators, like Pulse and Jackal, get unique gadgets that help you find out where enemies are. Aside from cameras and gadgets, you get a view of your killer when you die alongside a killcam so making callouts about where you were killed from is vital for the survival of the rest of your team. Audio is the final key to gathering information. Gunshots and explosions will obviously point towards where the action is, but footsteps also make a lot of noise especially when running. Listening to footsteps can help defenders figure out where the attackers are coming from and attackers find roaming defenders trying to sneak up on them. The only way to mitigate the sound of footsteps is to either walk, crouch, or both to create the least sound, but doing so will cause you to move much slower. This all comes together to make a game with a steep learning curve that rewards patience and taking the time to gather information about the enemy position and then hold down angles or slowly and methodically clear out areas. Just because Rainbow Six Siege is a slower paced game doesn't mean it's boring. Because of the variety of maps, modes, objective locations, tactics, and 30 unique operators, no two games play out the same which means it takes much longer before the game starts to get boring. With the exception of "Operation Health," 2 new DLC operators and a new, free map are added around every 3 months to spice up the game and meta so the game stays interesting. Every single map they add is free so the player base isn't split up; all of the additional DLC and most of the cosmetics can be earned using the in game currency as well so there's no need to spend additional money on the game. The competitive/ranked mode is very fun, with long, high tension games and a ranking system that is functional but could use some work. The game also has a more relaxed casual mode where mistakes are more easily forgiven and you can test out new operators, new strategies, or mess around without any repercussions. The casual mode is structured almost identically to the competitive mode, unlike Counter Strike, so you can switch between casual and competitive and feel like you're playing the same game. In contrast to CS:GO where casual is 10v10 and competitive is 5v5, both modes are 5v5 and play the same way. CS:GO's casual mode is more hectic than, less organized than, feels nothing like, and is generally less fun than CS:GO's competitive mode; on the other hand, Siege has a good casual mode that may lack some of the tension and excitement of ranked, but otherwise is just ranked without the consequences. Siege also has 2 PvE gamemodes available to play: situations and terrorist hunt. Situations is a singleplayer mode that is similar to a campaign, but without a story or main characters (It's more like training with a couple operators and their gadgets shown off). There are 10 singleplayer missions that have their own assigned operator and equipment (you play as recruit in the first 3 missions and one of the operators in the other 7), each mission occurs in one of the multiplayer maps and has an objective that is either kill all the enemies, defuse a bomb, rescue a hostage, or protect a hostage. All the missions can be played in either normal, hard, or realistic difficulties, and have 3 challenge stars that can be completed to earn 200 renown per star (one of the stars is always complete the mission with over 50 percent health remaining, but the other two are unique to the mission). There is also one co-op mission after you complete the 10 singleplayer ones. You team up with 4 other players and are allowed to pick any operator you have unlocked. The mission is to defuse two bombs in the Bartlett University map but there's a special twist to this mission. The entire map is covered in gas so your range of vision is limited and you have to wear a suit and mask that blocks out the edges of the screen and your peripheral vision. The unique element of gas blocking your vision makes the mission very fun to play, but it's a shame that it's the only mission to have a special quality that sets it apart from the others. Terrorist hunt, the other PvE gamemode, is like the co-op mission from the situations as is played with a team of up to 5 (there are solo and squad only modes) and you can choose your operators, but there are no random elements, like the co-op mission's gas, thrown in and unless you change your matchmaking settings, the map and mode are randomly. Like the missions, terrorist hunt can be played on either normal, hard, or realistic difficulties and the mission choices are terrorist hunt classic (kill all the terrorists), disarm bombs (defuse 2 bombs), hostage extraction (secure a hostage and escort them outside), and protect asset (defend a civilian from waves of incoming enemies). Although I play much more multiplayer than PvE, terrorist hunt is still a fun way to pass a small amount of time and gain a little renown in the process. It can become challenging when trying to beat a realistic mission or a realistic t-hunt with less than 5 people, but the PvE modes are relatively easy for the most part. The main focus is on the excellent multiplayer that has received so much care and attention, even after its release. Instead of giving up on the mistake ridden product Siege was at launch, the developers took the time and effort to improving and expanding the game in the nearly 18 months its been around. The game will only continue to improve.
TL;DR: Great high skill tactical shooter with a heavy reliance on map knowledge, game sense, and information gathering that provides a great casual or competitive experience. 95/100

Red Crow was fun as hell, it felt balanced, the bugs weren't too bad and you had enemies who were definetely on your level. Inspired by a number of NES classics (Mega Man, DuckTales and Zelda 2 especially), Shovel Knight takes on Retro 2D platforming and does it justice.
I found the difficulty of the main game to be just right personally, not quite as unforgiving as some NES games due to checkpoints and being able to take more hits, but not pathetically easy like many modern games. One nice addition I found to the levels is the ability to destroy checkpoints, a simple 'higher risk/reward' mechanic. The level design takes similar ideas from Mega Man, with each stage having its own unique theme. The hazards, the boss and the stage item are all tied together with a general mechanic exclusive to the level. Some levels are more smartly designed than others, but are all overall well crafted. All of these are nicely complimented with great, tight controls.
The length of the main game isn't too long, probably stretching a bit longer than a typical Mega Man game. That said, with New Game Plus, and achievements which promotes other ways of playing (speed runs, no death runs, etc), there's a ton of replayability to be found in Shovel Knight.
The game has a decent mixture of chiptunes, some being more forgettable than others but the soundtrack isn't short of catchy tunes. The story is simple and straight to the point, with some funny dialogue here and there.
I've honestly had more fun with Shovel Knight than I've had with most of the 'AAA cinematic' games that have come out in recent years. Anyone who enjoys platformers and any of the NES games that Shovel Knight takes inspiration from will absolutely love this. Highly recommended.
