There are plenty of things wrong with this game, but somehow it seems well worthy of a recommendation.
The BAD:
* The controls are clearly designed with joypads in mind, which means your crack soldier will have little difficulty popping heads off the zombie waves, but will probably come a cropper walking around bends, and spend a lot of time stuck in the corner of the room.
* Some of the cutscenes require the player to jab some key combo to avoid being decapitated/disemboweled. A nice interlude, but it does get a bit tedious watching your character run down a hole the 11th time in a row.
* The final boss fight goes well over the melodrama quota for any title. Just die already!
The GOOD:
* Two-player co-op is awesomely good fun. The levels are well-designed for the most part, and have plenty of moments when players really have to rely on one another. Reviving/rescuing your comrade is also nicely tuned.
* There's a DX9 version which runs well on aging hardware. Woohoo!

Full review from a free-to-play(for now):
On the first launch the game was laggy and very slow, it took a crash or two to get into the tutorial for the Soldier class, and looking back I recommend you adjust your settings as soon as you enter, as well as increasing your mouse sensitivity greatly if you've played similar titles, as the default takes forever to turn.
The turotial was fine, I wish there were more for you to understand different classes before joining a casual game. Casual has a lot of modes to play in, but you as a level 1 player may be against several much more experianced players, considering how long the game has been out, as well as there being 150 levels.
The gameplay itself is very engaging, with 12 classes to play as, and the ability to have 3 different weapons on you, and those can be swapped out for better weapons you get from random drops or by trading and crafting using other weapons and the comminity's basic currency of refined metal. The random drop mechanic is a bit off to me, as it doesn't tie to the level system in any way I can see, and I managed to go 2 hours without a drop. This is overshadowed by the fact that there is enough to do in this game that you can sit there for hours playing, and many have! I recommend this game.

Let me preface this review by making one thing clear: I am biased due to the fact that I LOVE old school platformers from back in the day. Mega Man, Mario Bros, Super Ghouls N' Ghosts, DuckTales, Castlevania...you name it, I've probably played the game several times over. That being said...
Shovel Knight is easily one of the best games I've played in a long time, and it is an amazing first title from developr Yacht Club Games.
Some people will undoubtedly make the tired argument that it is too short to be worth your $15, but to them I say NAY! Shovel Knight does nearly everything not only right, but does it all EXTREMELY well. The graphics harken back to the NES era, but does so without the limitations of those classic titles. The sound design is absolutely top notch. Sound effects are varied and the music itself is one of my favorite game soundtrakcs ever, 8Bit/chiptune or not. Then of course there is the gameplay. Level design is superb, with fun, varied design, and lots of hidden secrets sprinkled throughout.
Of course all that wouldn't mean a whole lot if it was marred by boring gameplay or bad control. Thankfully, this game controls very well. Not once did the game feel as if it was being "unfair"...if I died,  it was my own fault. Movement is similar to a lot of Capcom's games, namely Mega Man...which makes sense considering that was a big source of inspiration for the team. You start off with your trusty shovel, which feels very good to swing (especially when you bounce projectiles back at a baddie!), and of course there is the obvious nod to Ducktales with the bouncing attack. After that there are relics you collect throughout the game, all of which are fun to use. The game feel is nothing short of excellent, it just feels
.
I will take a brief moment to address the obvious elephant in the room: game length. I finished the game in about 6-7 hours, and that was taking my time on my first playthrough, and getting all but 10 of the collectibles. Please don't let that dissuade you from checking this game out though, as those 6-7 hours were jam packed with quality. I for one prefer that as opposed to something that overstays its welcome. This is a steal at $15.
Yacht Club Games has made something truly special in Shovel Knight, and I am definitely looking forward to whatever they come up with next. I seriously cannot recommend this game enough. If you even remotely enjoy old-school platformers like Mega Man, Mario, Castlevania, Ducktales, or the like, you should definitely buy this game.

I loved every little bit the game except one thing: puzzles. They are
. At first they are interesting, but as the story goes, they get progressively harder. I spent hours on the ones in the second half of the game. Maybe I am just not so bright, but the original games weren't that difficult, even the advanced chambers.
This game is a must for any Portal fan and/or difficult puzzle lover. If you get stuck, there's always a walkthrough on YouTube. Big thanks to the developers, although they definitely needed to test the game more thoroughly. I'd give the game 4 out of 5 just because of the difficulty.

Let me preface this review by making one thing clear: I am biased due to the fact that I LOVE old school platformers from back in the day. Mega Man, Mario Bros, Super Ghouls N' Ghosts, DuckTales, Castlevania...you name it, I've probably played the game several times over. That being said...
Shovel Knight is easily one of the best games I've played in a long time, and it is an amazing first title from developr Yacht Club Games.
Some people will undoubtedly make the tired argument that it is too short to be worth your $15, but to them I say NAY! Shovel Knight does nearly everything not only right, but does it all EXTREMELY well. The graphics harken back to the NES era, but does so without the limitations of those classic titles. The sound design is absolutely top notch. Sound effects are varied and the music itself is one of my favorite game soundtrakcs ever, 8Bit/chiptune or not. Then of course there is the gameplay. Level design is superb, with fun, varied design, and lots of hidden secrets sprinkled throughout.
Of course all that wouldn't mean a whole lot if it was marred by boring gameplay or bad control. Thankfully, this game controls very well. Not once did the game feel as if it was being "unfair"...if I died,  it was my own fault. Movement is similar to a lot of Capcom's games, namely Mega Man...which makes sense considering that was a big source of inspiration for the team. You start off with your trusty shovel, which feels very good to swing (especially when you bounce projectiles back at a baddie!), and of course there is the obvious nod to Ducktales with the bouncing attack. After that there are relics you collect throughout the game, all of which are fun to use. The game feel is nothing short of excellent, it just feels
.
I will take a brief moment to address the obvious elephant in the room: game length. I finished the game in about 6-7 hours, and that was taking my time on my first playthrough, and getting all but 10 of the collectibles. Please don't let that dissuade you from checking this game out though, as those 6-7 hours were jam packed with quality. I for one prefer that as opposed to something that overstays its welcome. This is a steal at $15.
Yacht Club Games has made something truly special in Shovel Knight, and I am definitely looking forward to whatever they come up with next. I seriously cannot recommend this game enough. If you even remotely enjoy old-school platformers like Mega Man, Mario, Castlevania, Ducktales, or the like, you should definitely buy this game.

I was somewhat skeptical about this game at first due to the free-to-play model, since F2P games have catfished me one too many times and most modern fishing games are pretty crappie. As it turns out, Fishing Planet is a kick bass simulator that has hands-down the most in-depth modeling of fishing as a whole. Licenses, catch/keep systems, leader lengths, tackle box storage, real and artificial baits...it's all here.
Everything from fish activity cycles to river drift is modeled in a way that's accurate, but still fun enough that you won't want the developer's head on a pike for making something that's as slow as the real thing is sometimes. The early game can be annoying since panfish are near-worthless for leveling up and will often make it difficult to get at the more valuable channel cats, which is a load of carp, but once you get over that hump, your options quickly open up for gear and species, and fights can become really cutthroat.
I played a lot of fishing games back on the NES/SNES, and even for someone as pickerel about their fishing games as I am, I'm enjoying Fishing Planet a lot.

I’m an old school gamer, meaning I grew up in the days of games where mascots were the♥♥♥♥♥♥and most games were a blissful adventure that involved the gamer as well as frustrated them. Sadly games like the ones from those days are few and far in-between however there are exceptions. From time to time there is that one game that comes out that seems to recapture that magic  of those years gone by that made most people, including myself enjoy gaming.
Shovel Knight is one those games.
So what exactly is Shovel Knight?
Shovel Knight is a homage of some of the best games to ever grace the 8-bit scene. I’m talking about Mega Man, Super Mario, Castlevania, Metroid and a couple other classic games tossed in for good effect.  Even the story is modeled after those classic games.
In Shovel Knight you are pitted against the 8 lords of “The Order of No Quarter” and their leader, the Enchantress, in order to save the kingdom that you once held dear and attempt to reunite with your former partner, the Shield Knight, who vanished many years again in a tragic event. Did I mention that Shovel Knight is the love child of Mega Man and Link? Well not really, but c’mon the resemblance is there.
The game features 8 bosses that are scattered across the 8-bit landscape that features a world map similar to that of Super Mario Bros. 3 that even has random events that can happen throughout your journey. Each of stage features the standard 2D platforming elements plus a unique spin depending on the stage you’re on that range from conveyor belts to total screen black outs with only a quick flash of lightning to light the way to water that will force you to time your jumps correctly or face certain death. In fact if you’re familiar with the Mega Man series then trust me when I say you’ll be right at home.
So mighty Shovel Knight, it is up to you to right the wrongs in the kingdom, are you up for the challenge?
So you’re not a fan of the 8-bit styled games? Well that’s fine, toss that aside for a moment and you still have several factors that make Shovel Knight stand out from the crowd.
The Sound Track
Oh boy, if you’re a fan of old school chiptunes then you’re going to love this soundtrack.  Composed by the extraordinary Jake “Virt” Kaufman (Mighty Milky Way, Mighty Switch Force, Double Dragon Neon) and Manami Matsumae (Mega Man, U.N Squadron, Magic Sword and the upcoming Mighty No.9), this soundtrack has it all. Each stage is provided it’s own unique flair and the music is catchy, real catchy. Made me feel like I was 10 years old again and had me looking to find my tape recorder that I had stolen from when I was younger (Doh!). Oh well at least the soundtrack will be available shortly and let’s be real, does anyone even have a tape player in their home anymore?
The Controls
Tight Tight Tight! The controls in Shovel Knight are very tight and responsive, which is fantastic as this game requires some slight second timed jumps and the last thing you need to is slide or feel that your on-screen buddy is completely ignoring your commands. Controls are definitely a “Make it or Break it” deal and I’m glad to see and feel that the controls are top notch here!
What Nintendo game is this?
The Combat
Well seeing how you’re called Shovel Knight you might have guessed that your primary attack is based on using that shovel to jab and poke your opponents to submission and you’d be right. However it’s surprisingly odd how effective that shovel can be. You have the standard attacks (Left, Right) as well as the ability to use the shovel like a pogo stick and use it to attack enemies from above as well as using that attack to access out of reach areas. On top of that you can also collect items called relics that can be used to supplement your attacks. Some relics can give you a ranged attack while others can provide addtitonal useful abilities such as limited damage reduction and more.
Customization
Don’t expect a huge selection of customization however you do have the ability to acquire several suits of armor and relics that increase your characters abilities.  You will also be able to upgrade both your health and magic meters that will let you take more hits while also dishing out some extra damage or if you have the right relic, saving your life!
Anything Else?
Well what does one do when they have a shovel? They dig for things and old’e Shovel Knight is no different. In fact it’s a major part of the game as will come across dirt mounds filled to the brim with gems that is basically the currency of the game. You can also collect sheets of music and turn them in to the towns bard who will then let you  listen to those musics anything you please. Remember those games that let you listen to the the games music via in game or title screen? Yep it’s awesome to see that Yacht Club Games tossed that in as well.
Least I forget there are tons of references in the game that reflect on past games such as Zelda II for example. There is a town where it feels like Yacht Club Games had simply ripped it from Zelda II, intact with it’s citizens and bizarre on-goings.
Hint: Try and jump the back of the lady carrying the water buckets.
Yacht Club Games has managed to produce one of the best 8-bit Metroidvania styled games that have been released as of late, which is a tall order as the quality of those past titles have been outstanding on their own merit.  The graphics are beautifully detailed (for an 8-bit styled game), the sound effects are on point and between unholy fusion Kaufman and Matsumae, the soundtrack is one of best i’ve heard in quite some time.
If the game has anything negative going against it, it’s due to the game not being very long. The game will you about 7-8 hours to beat, however there is a +newgame mode that let’s you challenge the baddies again so there is is always that.  The difficulty may also put off some gamers as this is a throw back to when platformers required skill and patience to tackle them but If you’re familiar with even the recent Super Mario Bros. for the Wii or WiiU, then I don’t have any doubts that you’ll enjoy the game, regardless of it’s difficulty.
This is the type of game that will have people asking you “What Nintendo game is this?, which was uniquely funny when I had friends watch me play the game with an Xbox 360 controller in hand and no Nintendo Entertainment System in sight.
I definitely recommend this for the casual gamer, hardcore gamer, brand new game, hell… if you’re any type of gamer then you must play this game! This indie gem is not to be missed and I hope that Shovel Knight receives a proper  sequel (or some DLC?!?)  sooner than later. It has all the makings of a classic and we could use a new blue character who isn’t afraid to kick some♥♥♥♥♥as this world is sorely missing the original!

I backed this project on Kickstarter mainly because the pixel art looked nice and didn't have that high hopes for the game turning out any good. I assumed this would be another retro-platformer that mistakes torturing players for gameplay fun (most old games, while challenging, weren't as hard as people make them out to be).
Boy was I wrong about the game. It surprised me to no end. The difficulty curve is quite gentle and the innovative checkpoint system (you can destroy checkpoints for loot if think if you're good enough) plus infinite lives with loot-recovery a la Dark Souls make the game a blast to play.
The mechanics are like a greatest hits collection of the NES era with clear influences from Mega Man, Duck Tales, Zelda II, Super Mario Bros 3 etc. - yet the game is much more than the sum of its parts / it's a whole new enjoyable experience.
With around 6 hours on first try (depending on your skill it might take more or less time) and no chance to find everything at first (replayablity), there's plenty of bang for your buck. Also, some of the Kickstarter stretch goals like co-op or playing as a boss character haven't been implemented yet (don't get me wrong, the game is otherwise feature-complete), there will be plenty of fun to be had in the coming months too.
Highly recommended!

Tactical Intervention feels somehow like Counter-Strike done right but is of course unique in it's own way by being much more detailed and offering a bigger difference when it comes to variety of game modes to choose from and a much more living environment that you can integrate with on some maps. Now you're probably wondering what kind of game this TI really is, huh? Well let me try to explain it briefly: TI is the way the community always wanted it to be, a better and quicker way of playing where experience points is not required to unlock weapons only in-game credits which is given after every match played and that gives every new player a fighting chance. Below you'll find all sorts of information regarding the game, take a look you might find something helpful.
[▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲|▲]
-=> Tips & Trix <=-
Looking for a guide on how to play TI? Then you've come to the right place, just scroll down to the bottom of this page to find the guide. Hope that you find this review helpful and don't forget to press the: |LIKE| button above & spread it to your friends so more people get a chance to experience TI.
[ Information! ]
A super fast paced first person shooter that offers an intense adrenaline rush when playing "Vip-Escort" or "Team Deathmatch" whether it's in a car-chase, a strategic mission map or blood a splattering deathmatch, either way you choose to play you'll find TI insanely entertaining, every map offers it's own unique gameplay & strategic design and can be used to your advantage if playing tactically. This game is purely based on teamwork and staying close to your teammates will give you accuracy bonus and the possibility to get healed.
[ Modes! ]
Rating: (9/10)
Bomb Plant, Hostage Rescue VIP-Escort including cars & Of course the classic Team Deathmatch. Feels great to have so many modes to choose from in the same game, it makes for a sweet rotation.
[ Content! ]
Rating: (9/10)
TI offers a nice variety of weapons and equipment for customizing your character in many different ways, alot of new content is added frequently which improves it even further. The recoil system provided in TI is one of the most well balanced in any FPS game ever and it just runs & feels really smooth and it reacts properly. The characters are really well made and the weapon models binds it all together nicely, surely animations can be a bit slack but will be fixed in the future. The damage factor is properly divided depending on body part hit so shooting someone in their legs and feet will require many more bullets than shooting him in the stomach etc.
[ Maps! ]
Rating: (10/10)
The maps surely are top-class and the environments are wonderfully crafted and we can barely wait to see the new maps to come in the near future that will be even better and offer even greater strategic gameplay. They feel really light and natural which adds a great atmosphere to the game and a depth not really found in other Source engine based games such as trees, rocks and rays of light. The textures are also very well made and unique in every map which is nice since it doesn't get so repetative.
[ Personal Opinion! ]
Rating: (10/10)
Highest possible rating because of the potential & depth that TI offers and not what it currently lacks. It feels more alive and unique in it's own way than most games out there today and the future looks bright for TI. All the small details really binds this game together and it makes it feel personal. I used to play Counter-Strike since 1999 to recent times and pretty much all the famous FPS games ever released in between too, sure they we're great in their own way. Yet somehow this game just raised the bar to another level that is unmatched by most games today because it feels much more personal and not like mainstream crap made to suit everyone. TI offers hardcore gaming at it's best!

For all the thousands of "retro" cash-ins with nonsense gimmicks, there's one Shovel Knight.  You may be surprised to learn that that one Shovel Knight is, in fact, Shovel Knight.  The game is a legit love letter to the 8-bit hits, with the occasional nod to the newer stuff that's come along since.  It's tough but fair, with an agreeable death system nobody was brilliant enough to come up with in the 80s.  I won't spoil the references made in the design and gameplay, since discovering them for yourself is part of the fun, but as for the most immediate, the game certainly plays Megaman-ish.  If, y'know, Megaman handed in his signature Buster for a shovel.  It's a lot more fun than I made it sound just now.
The story's dialogue is fun to follow, and the music is hella rad.  So get outta here already.  Every second you're wasting reading this review is a second you could be spending playing Shovel Knight purple monkey dishwasher.

When Resident Evil 5 launched, I avoided buying it. I thought the direction of the series was headed in the wrong direction. I said to myself "co-op?!? colorful bright lighting!?!?" and basically dismissed the game for a few months. I forget the reasons, but six months later I finally picked it up. I played the game single player, finished it, and never really fell in love with it. I was indifferent about the game.
A month or so later and I decided to play it co-op with a guy I met on some forums, who happens to be one of the biggest RE fans I've ever met. He has already played the crap out of RE5, so he has a ton of game knowledge about RE5. I wanted to get the Platinum (PS3), so we played on Professional, which is the very hard setting in the game. This time, I completely got it. Everything about the co-op experience was extremely fun! This game ended up being the co-op game I always wanted as a kid growing up. Teamwork was important (especially on hard settings), and playing with friends added a brand new experience to a series I already loved.
Finding all the treasures, upgrading weapons, and the constant high pressure of action horror was extremely fun, challenging, and rewarding. Top that off with some great boss fights, and some extremely good story with some of Resident Evil's best characters. Even the QTE's in this game were fun in co-op! They didn't feel out of place, and if you failed them with your buddies, it always ended up being a laughing affair, especially the next time when they mixed the buttons up on you!
The game didn't have that dark setting of the previous titles, but it still had its own mood and unqiue setting. As I mentioned above, this game had an excellent co-op system. The combos you could perform with your partner added a welcomed mechanic to the series, expanding on 4's action prompts. The boss battles worked really well with your partners too, both of you generally  had to work together and do something unique together to end the boss. Wesker in this game was particullarly bad♥♥♥♥♥too.
Anyway, I could go on and on about how RE5 is great, yeah it's not survival horror, but it's a fantastic action horror game, and one of the greatest co-op experiences I've had in gaming period.
**Play with your best friends, and play on the hardest setting you can!!!**

There's little that I can add beyond what has already been said, but If you want more Portal, this is an excellent and worthwhile few hours.
Puzzles are a magniture of difficulty greater than anything you will have encountered from Valve, and it takes a while to unpick the real solution which for the most part doesn't require split second timing or elite platforming skills. It would have been easy to rely on such things and Prism should be congratulated for not doing so. The creative use, and combination, of gels, grids, funnels and cubes was on the whole very well done.
However (and this is the bit that grated) there is a definite shift away from what I would consider "pure" portal-based puzzles. You move in and out of traditional testing chambers frequently even in the middle of solving the chamber itself. Several times the solution requires you to make use of a pipe, girder or other piece of the environment which aren't always well signposted. Several times I took a "leap of faith" or two knowing that this would either be the intended solution or certain death. Other times I could see a few elements that could interact but didn't have sight of the goal I was working towards, so just tried a few things until progress was made.  Sometimes there were usable surfaces that looked like they may have been part of the solution and turned out to be totally unimportant.  Many times the intended path could have been clearer. I also agree with other reviewers who said that the different behaviour of buttons delivering cubes whenever one was destroyed took some time to adjust to and work into any solution. Still, you do generally know when you have found the intended solution and when you've fudged your way through a puzzle.
Overall, Portal Stories Mel was still an enjoyable and massively impressive achievement. If you have completed Portal 2 and are up for a challenge then Mel is well worth spending a bit of time with.

When Resident Evil 5 launched, I avoided buying it. I thought the direction of the series was headed in the wrong direction. I said to myself "co-op?!? colorful bright lighting!?!?" and basically dismissed the game for a few months. I forget the reasons, but six months later I finally picked it up. I played the game single player, finished it, and never really fell in love with it. I was indifferent about the game.
A month or so later and I decided to play it co-op with a guy I met on some forums, who happens to be one of the biggest RE fans I've ever met. He has already played the crap out of RE5, so he has a ton of game knowledge about RE5. I wanted to get the Platinum (PS3), so we played on Professional, which is the very hard setting in the game. This time, I completely got it. Everything about the co-op experience was extremely fun! This game ended up being the co-op game I always wanted as a kid growing up. Teamwork was important (especially on hard settings), and playing with friends added a brand new experience to a series I already loved.
Finding all the treasures, upgrading weapons, and the constant high pressure of action horror was extremely fun, challenging, and rewarding. Top that off with some great boss fights, and some extremely good story with some of Resident Evil's best characters. Even the QTE's in this game were fun in co-op! They didn't feel out of place, and if you failed them with your buddies, it always ended up being a laughing affair, especially the next time when they mixed the buttons up on you!
The game didn't have that dark setting of the previous titles, but it still had its own mood and unqiue setting. As I mentioned above, this game had an excellent co-op system. The combos you could perform with your partner added a welcomed mechanic to the series, expanding on 4's action prompts. The boss battles worked really well with your partners too, both of you generally  had to work together and do something unique together to end the boss. Wesker in this game was particullarly bad♥♥♥♥♥too.
Anyway, I could go on and on about how RE5 is great, yeah it's not survival horror, but it's a fantastic action horror game, and one of the greatest co-op experiences I've had in gaming period.
**Play with your best friends, and play on the hardest setting you can!!!**

Brains! You'll want to have some if you play Plants vs. Zombies, a tower defense game by Popcap (R.I.P.) designed for cell phones but ported over to PC, and you'll behold all the grainy, unoptimized glory the moment you fire it up. It's a shame really, because it's a fun game that could have been so much more if there was a Steam version.

The pace of the game is pretty slow for a tower defense game. The first few levels are spent easing you into the various concepts and units used throughout the game, and you'll need some (but not all) of that knowledge for the significantly more challanging later levels. Not once did I ever remark "what the heck am I supposed to do here?" Challenge wise, it's pretty casual (duh) until this last handful of stages, which are by far the most fun (and annoying).

Each zombie provides either a laugh or an 'oh crap!' the first time you encounter them, and the Zombiepedia provides some humorous color text for each unit in the game, something that seems to be a lost art in games these days. This might be a good game to show a girlfriend, I had fun watching her play and hearing her commentary on the game.
There are lots of fun side activities, including challange modes, 'themed' games, and my least favorite thing: the Zen Garden, an super annoying click-fest time-sink thing that also happens to be the best way to earn money to purchase further amusements. It's not engaging at all, just a hassle, like an endless game of Whack-a-Mole.

To be honest, I hated it at first. The controls are clunky to say the least. Not being able to move while shooting was really jarring for some one with no previous Resident Evil experience and the characters control like tanks. Then there's the QTEs. They come out of no ware in the middle of a cut scene, barley giving you time to find the keys.
But once I actual sat down and gave the game a chance, I got use to it quite quickly and was able to enjoy the game for what it is. The graphics are amazing, the bad guys plentiful, great atmosphere and above all, it has great replay value.
There are so many things that keep you coming back. Upgrading weapons, collecting BSAA emblems, unlocking cheats, getting perfect scores on all difficulties, and of course, killing more zombies. DEFINITELY recommended.
But be warned, this is not a "horror" game at all so don't go into it expecting one like I did.

The game sets you in a horrifying, dark world, eliminating the comforting heft of any weapons and pitting you against deadly enemies you must sneak around and hide from to survive, all the while solving puzzles and keeping your sanity in check to progress.  The game is a short one, well around 5 - 6 hours, but it took me a week to beat based entirely on the fact that I kept fearquitting, or bringing up the Steam web browser to watch stupid crap on YouTube to get my nerves back. Fans of the horror genre, your search is finally over.

Resident Evil 5 is an excellent port of the 360/PS3 game. The MT Framework powered game looks fantastic on the PC, using exclusive high res texture work and various video resolutions to fit your PC SKU (doesn't require a beast of a machine to play, which is a plus). All the features from the 360 carry over thanks to Games for Windows Live (online play, friends list, gamerscore, and leaderboards), with the inclusion of mods for the PC. Game does support xbox controllers, but is playable with mouse & keyboard (aim-bobbing was implemented to avoid making the aiming too easy, if you were interested in that control type). Overall, still a very fun game even by today's standards, and a must play if your into coop gaming on the PC (not a lot of these kinds of games on PC).

I think I've owned Plants vs. Zombies on about four different platforms:
Xbox 360
iPod Touch
iPhone 5S
and now finally on MAC thanks to Steam.
And each time I've purchased it, I'm immediately reminded as to why I have purchased it again, because it is just so much fun to pick and play, whether that is just for 20 minutes or 2 hours straight. It's a very colourful looking game, the colours pop(cap) right of the screen. But it's all about the deceptively deep gameplay that makes this game such a joy. From it's exterior, you wouldn't of thought PvZ would be a proper Tower Defense game, due to the colourful cartoon characters. And whilst I'm sure that it's not as deep as other games in this particular genre, for someone like me who just wants to pick up and play something tough yet very accessible (something which is extremely hard to nail, by the way) it's right on the money.
Purchase this game at an extremely reasonable price.

Not to everyone's cup of tea, but if you like Mil-Sim and working with others, and you understand what a SANDBOX is, it's great - Slightly let down on the Solo side as the missions / AI are geographically restricted initially, and this goes against the grain of the original Operation Flashpoint.
Where this game shines, is in the MOD community, where literally you can easily mould this game into almost anything you want. It will smash your hardware regardless of how good your rig is, Multiplayer exacerbates the performance issues, but nothing, repeat nothing comes close to this game when combined with TEAMSPEAK, Radios, and CO-OP or TvT. People will ♥♥♥♥♥ about "Not 60fps" whilst sitting on a 270km square Island with 10km view distance, 2km object distance, being attacked by a Company strength enemy element, with a Company of Armour and helicopters in support! It feels like a dynamic warzone, not some FPS. Nothing comes even remotely close to ARMA for size, scale and immersion - It is actively improving all the time and is almost unrecognisable from it's release.
The downside, of this excellent game, is that it's getting a bit creaky with regards to the Engine, Hardware configuration, memory allocation and resource utilisation, put plainly "It is not utilising Hardware developed in the last 5 years" hence my earlier comment of it will smash your rig, it runs on raw CPU Power, it's not elegant, it's not efficient, it's a brute forcer of a hardware config. Hopefully this will be resolved in the next iteration, as to me it's 85 out of 100, if they nail the Engine Hardware utilisation, improve the AI and optomise Clientside performance / Multiplayer, this game will shift to 95 out of 100.

Shovel Knight feels like a long lost classic from the NES. This game plays very similar to the NES Megaman games with the addition of Legend of Zelda items, a Super Mario Bros 3 world map, and a shovel. You can really feel the love the developers put into the game with it's tricky level design and memorable characters. If you think the game looks fun from the trailers, I'd recommend picking this up.
With that being said, there are some design choices that I didn't care for:
-You have unlimited lives as far as I know. Dying comes at the price of dropping gold at that location, Dark Souls style, and having to restart at the last checkpoint. I like my death systems to be more punishing in these kinds of games.
-Levels commonly have 3-4 checkpoints which can be used as expected or destroyed to get a little bit of gold. This abundance of checkpoints coupled with infinite lives makes the game too forgiving of deaths. I understand you could just destroy every checkpoint on sight to make the game harder but that feels like a poor substitute for a built in harder difficulty option with a different live/checkpoint system.
-The bosses are fun to fight but they're pushovers compared to their own cleverly designed levels. I died 85 times total on my first playthrough. Only 5 of those deaths were on boss fights, 4 of which were on the final boss.

My review on Shovel Knight:
This game is a 2D platforming game with lots of NES flair thrown into it. The graphic, the soundtrack etc. The story is a knight caled Shovel Knight who use a shovel (duh) as weapon of choice goes to battle other knights and fight the final boss. The story is not so remarkable and you can see the plot from miles away. No plotholes though. Story progression is so like Megaman (big fan here); fight 8 bosses, go to final stage, re-fight the bosses again, then fight the final boss in 2 round fight. So if you're into great story and plot, you gotta lower your expectation for this game.
The best part is the gameplay. As I mentioned before, this is 2D platforming, so lots of jumping involved. There are many things you can do with your shovel; attack enemies, dig treasures, pogo jump like in Duck Tales, upgrade it to add special attack, bury dead bodies.... forget the last one. There is no difficulty setting, but there is New Game+ which is harder than normal; enemies do more damage, less checkpoints. There are music sheet s to collect if you're into collecting stuff. You can upgrade health and magic in the game with money. There's no heart upgrade or find4-pieces-to-upgrade stuff. You also need money to get upgrades for armor and shovel. And to buy relics.
Unlike Megaman games whre you get special weapon from bosses, this one doesn't have it. Instead, you get relics which is usually buy from store. You can find the store inside the town or secret places in the stages. The relics cost magic when used si you cannot spam them. Some for only help killing the enemis while some helps with the platforming stuff like the sword (air dash ftw) and phase amulet. Relics are fun to use, so experiment with all of them.
Graphic? It's 8-bit style. Need to say more?
The soundtracks is 8-bit music. So if you're not in 8-bit music style, you have hard time listening to it in the entire game. I personally enjoyed the music as well as other 8-bit music from other game. You can listen to the soundtrack for free here
There are some things that I don't like in the game. No double jump (really??), boss fights are kinda too easy, the health tank are cheap way to win a boss fight in normal mode, story itself is not interesting.
There will be more feature added as mentioned in their Kickstarter page. I totally recommend this game for platforming fans, especially those who appreciate the old NES 8-bit style.
Any comments or feedback is appreciated.

Amnesia is, without a shadow of a doubt, the single most terrifying game ever conceived. It will not only get inside your head, but it will tear your brain to shreds in the process. Play this at night, in the dark, alone, with surround sound or headphones, and prepare for one hell of a Lovecraftian roller coaster of horror. Not all will like it, but thats only because the modern generation has generally grown used to multiplayer first person shooters that rely merely on twitch reactions, a steady hand, and vague bits of repetitive strategy, rather than psychological works of art that force to use your brain creatively for a change in order to endure a nightmare unlike any other. Wannabe heroes play first person shooters. Real men of courage play Amneisa.

Shovel Knight is a retro inspired action/platformer that deserves a lot of respect. Instead of trying to go for that "OMG 8 BIT IS AWESOME LOLOLOL" feel that most of these types of games go for these days, it instead tries to make 8-Bit as beautiful as possible. Accompanying the incredible graphics that seem realistic for the hardware it is trying to emulate is a fantastic score composed by Virt (which also, if memory serves, composed the Retro City Rampage soundtrack). The only nagging flaw, if you can consider it as one, is the difficulty. This game is CLEARLY meant for gamers, and the level design and complex boss patterns show it. You will die. And die. And die. And die some more. Until you lose all of your gold, in some cases. I'm still stuck on the very last board, and it took me about eight hours to get there. If you can get past that, and the fact that there is really no way to tweak the difficulty whatsoever (definitely not the game to have your eight year old sibling play!), you'll find a wonderful game.

If you can imagine it, there's a strong chance you can do it in ARMA 3. Constant updates increase the value and rich experience of the game, and new DLC bring further incredible assets to play around with. Highly recommended!

Let's talk about Shovel Knight. Shovel Knight is a nostalgia game. Shovel Knight is a NOSTALGIA game. They make a few things not very obvious at first and force you to fumble through the game to learn them. Breaking checkpoints for money is one. Being able to change the relic button to something actually useful is another.

The music, while catchy, gets very annoying after a while as well. It has a very short loop life and makes me long for something with more meat. MegaMan 2, Mario, Ducktales, they were all able to do better things with the music.

It also expects you to know Mario standards of being able to jump over the wall of the world, but it only lets you do this when it wants you to do this. So thinking this was a regular thing, I attempted to jump over the wall of the world and died because I didn't realize the developers didn't want me to be able to do that trick there when it worked elsewhere.

Getting away from those complaints, Shovel Knight is a fairly simple game with a platforming appeal that is tough, but forgiving, and in general, a fun game. The mechanics are fairly simple, there's a fun bit of exploration involved, trying to figure out every nook and cranny you need to break.

It relies a bit heavily on puzzles: some of them are quite simple, while others might have you stumped for a bit. This is the best horror game I've played since Silent Hill 4: The Room.

Clearly inspired by Counterstrike, Tactical Intervention is a fast-paced FPS. The speed and many functions of the game are appealing, for instance, one can rappel, blind shoot, use sniffer dogs, drive cars etc. However, the cars are virtually uncontrollable and even a small sedan is capable of bringing down a full-grown tree at even moderate speeds thus making it woefully unrealistic. The rest of the gameplay is just as sluggish as the driving. You do have a large arsenal of weapons available to you, but you need to buy them and gathering enough money is quite time consuming job. FInally, the graphics are not exactly high-end. The maps are small and the gametypes are limited. All in all it is a fun game if you just want to pass some time, but if you want the real deal you should stick to the original Counterstrike.

This game is aiming to be a fishing simulator, realistic fish habits, movement, etc. It's not too realistic that it takes away the fun of it being a game. It's very different from other fishing games I've played. I'd love to see what updates they add to make the game even better. It has a lot of kinks but I expected as much.
Pros:
- F2P
- Not pay to win, you can only buy exp boost or extra credits (earned by just playing the game)
- Lots of unique features from other fishing games
- Not just a "catch & reel" game
- Easy to learn after a while
- Different fishing methods
- Pretty graphics/animations
- Other players are pretty helpful, especially when trying to learn a new area
- All DLC content are just items obtainable in-game
Cons:
- Tutorial is bad, by bad I mean, confusing + teaches you almost nothing
- Really heavily targeted at fishers right now
- F1 (help/keybinds) is messy, they should probably color code it
- By multiplayer it means it has a chatbox in-game (Hopefully they're adding other players or something like that)
Overall still a great game, and one of the best fishing games I've played. If you have time, want to try something new, or enjoy fishing, give the game a shot.

Well, my friend asked me "are you going to get Fishing Planet?". I said "No, No I won't be getting Fishing Planet because I don't fish IRL so what is the point?"

EDIT: Times have changed
I have recently got back to this game and it has changed... and not a chnage for the good either. So with that I unfortunantly need to chnage my review to a negative one.
1. Prices to travel to lakes seems to have gone up, yet the XP and price for your fish didn't go up. So you're stuck grinding EVEN MORE now if you want to travel to other locations. Also, on top of that the price of gear also seemed to have gone up.
2. The fast forward feature now has a cool down timer, but don't worry! If you pay baitcoins (buy them with your steam wallet) you can instantly fast forward time!
3. Fishing licenses, you used to be able to use in game cash to buy an infinite license, now they've changed that to baitcoins. Your stuck buying montly licenses if you want to fish at a new lake... Which still cost quite a bit.
4. Some of the lures you COULD buy with in game money either disappeared, or they now require baitcoins. I've never bought anything with baitcoins yet some how I have these lures in my inventory? Seems like they now require baitcoins to me.
While this game does still have a free to play aspect to it, it isn't too fun anymore, at least not for me. While I still may play this game from time to time checking in I won't be playing it too often anymore. The game seems to be going more to the pay to play side. Instead of the developers being for the players, they now seem to be for the money. If you got deep pockets then this game is still for you, but this game seems to be better served as a game you pay for. At least then you'll get all of the features unlocked, not pay an indefinite amount of money to keep those features unlocked.
TLDR: 5/10, the game DID capture the attention of a non-fisher... Now the attention has been lost due to pay to play.

When I heard that a bunch of fans gathered together to make a prequel to the Portal series, I was very exited to see what they could accomplish, and I was very surprised at the results. This ragtag group of minds came together to create an origional story, complete with new characters, amazing new assets, and immensly intense puzzles and tests to suit the atmosphere of this game. And that remains the main point of this review, the puzzles. Sure the origionals have hard puzzles, just as they have easy puzzles, but the main dfference was that Valve knew exactly the limit the challenge needed to be and understood the effects of trying and retrying. I cant tell you how many times I felt completely trapped while playing this game (which may have been the point of the game) and felt stuck while trying to apply mechanichs that I have never learned before. While this game is masterfully crafted, written wonderfully, and even able to tie itself in with the origional narrative, I am not a massive fan of this Mod.
So while I'm not saying that Portal Stories: Mel is a bad game,(quite simply it is the exact opposite), it is truly for those who have dedicated themselves to the franchise and have completely mastered the concept of Portal Physics and and the art of teleportation. I reccomend this game to (and don't take this lightly), HARDCORE Portal fans, and those not willing to refuse a challenge. I'd give this Mod about 4/5 stars for the concept, the story, and the execution, but from my point of view I saw this game more as an Indiana Jones 4, a continuation that even though we said we wanted, proved to be merely an attempt,  with a confusing plot, acting that needed work, repetative soundtrack, mixed with frustrating scenes yet action filled events that leaves the franchise more incomplete than complete.
I still do enjoy the Portal franchise and despite my previous statements, still hold my highest respects to the team of minds that put this Mod together and I sincerely congratulate and thank them for creating this masterpiece of fan work.
PS, (I Put my reccomendation as a thumbs up on this game merely because I still think it is a good game, but it was not crafted specifically for me.)

I spent more hours playing this than playing the main story in Portal 2. That's quite a lot to say for a free mod. The production quality was excellent, from the art and story to the voice acting. I've seen the voice acting get some criticism, but I truly thought it sounded fine. Including the Cave Johnson at the start.
The puzzles started at a step of difficulty above the end of Portal 2, making for a great game to follow that up. By the end, some of the puzzles were intense figuring out what order to do things in and what timing to do it. There are harder fan made puzzles for sure, but play through this and you'll be ready to step into the big leagues of Steam Workshop puzzles.
The story was quite good. While at times it didn't feel as connected as the story in Portal 2, it still made plenty of sense. And the scale of the game was amazing. By the end thinking about where I was it was hard to believe where I had started.
All in all, I honestly felt like I was playing Portal 3 and not just a mod made by fans. I wish they could accept money, because this would be worth it. Get this and play it, it's what a mod should be.

Shovel Knight is an amalgamation of contemporary game mechanics and old-school aesthetics and gameplay. The soundtrack-- composed by the incomparable Jake Kaufman-- is reminiscent of the very best offerings of Manami Matsumae (of Mega Man fame); The 8-bit graphics are nostalgic and gorgeous, incorporating all of the elements that made games like Castlevania so memorable (haunting silhouettes, verdant 8-bit vistas, and a masterful utilization of contrast and color palletes); The difficulty is finely tuned, and players are likely to find it challenging without being merciless; Towns buzz with NPCs that offer useful information, upgrades, and endearing dialogue; Level design rewards exploration, and there's a veritable bevy of spoils to be had for those willing to take the time to look; Bosses are colorful characters that 'feel' like bosses, demanding celerity and focus on the part of the player; The story is engaging in that NES-era sort of way, which is to say that there's a certain amount of elegance to its brevity.
In short, Shovel Knight is a perfect game, and you need to buy it.

Do you want a love letter to classic Mega Man and Castlevania? Add in touches of the Duck Tales pogo and Adventure Time-esque NPCs, and you're getting the idea.  Sure, plenty of games are trying to do 8-bit retro now, but Shovel Knight is possibly the most polished, well designed example of how it should be done right.
Graphics:  Obviously there is more detail than an original NES game, but everything is bright and clear like Mega Man.  Enemies and projectiles stand out so nothing is ever cluttered.  The designs are unique on regular enemies as well as the bosses and NPCs and everything is animated well.  The stages all have their own personality and look great.
Sound: virt (with a cameo by Manami Matsumae of Capcom fame) has made a catchy chiptune soundtrack which fits the game well.  I have to give him extra credit for each Order boss having their own boss theme, which I certainly wasn't expecting.  I'm waiting on the physical cd to see how well it works outside game, but I have every expectation I will still enjoy it and it definitely is enjoyable in game.
Design & Challenge:  Perhaps over everything else, the level design is where the game really shines.  You can tell how much work went into getting this just right.  Playing through just once so far I died plenty, but with repetition over difficult parts you can see just how smoothly a stage flows when done right.  Just as a basic playthrough things were never maddeningly difficult, however the feats (achievements) are certain to test the very best platformer veterans.
Fun:  This game is very fun!  It has it's own style and clearly a sense of humor, but what will get me back to it is the feeling of getting that platformer on Nintendo that you will go back to time and again, even if you blaze through it. I highly recommend this game!

SHOVEL KNIGHT REVIEW
Updated: (Includes New Game Plus and Plague of Shadows)
Shovel Knight is a game by Yatch Club games, and the first I have played from them. Having seen a few previews, and hearing about it, Shovel Knight did look like an appealing game. Originally, I thought it was going to be just another "retro" style game, or rouge-a-like, which we've seen an entire flurry of in the past five or so years (many great, others not so much) so at first it didn't hold my attention as much. Having seen a trailer, prior to its release though, I saw great potential. Not only was it more of an action platformer (more of my genre) but the gameplay and presentation looked fantastic, so I had to pick it up there and then.
My first impressions of the game were excellent. From the moment the title screen comes on, you are greeted to some fantastic chiptune music, which feels both fresh and new, but yet familiar and nostalgic. This game will definnitely appeal to people who grew up on the NES and SNES, but also anyone who wants to get into 2D platformers. I could easily go on tangents to talk about one thing to the next, but I'll seperate them into different categories.
GAMEPLAY:
The gameplay of Shovel Knight is what you'd expect from an action platformer. Your shovel is your main weapon, and it can be used both to bash enemies, as well as using it as a kind of pogo stick, to bounce off enemies and obstacles, much like in Ducktales the game on the NES. Speaking of which, the main influences I got from this game were Legend of Zelda (items and map screen), Ducktales (the pogo mechanic) and Mega Man (music and some stages). The jumping in the game feels slightly delayed, but having played countless amounts of old games on Nintendo systems, it's easy to pick up on it and master, like riding a bike. You start off on an intro stage, which teaches you how to play the game, by unfolding events, rather than the much redundant "text boxes" or hand holding, which most modern games have today. Shovel Knight makes you feel like you've learned, and earned those victories, rather than telling you what to do. You can also collect treasure either by finding them out in the open, or digging up certain rock and dirt piles or blocks. Treasure acts as your currency, and can be used to buy items in shops. When you die, you drop your treasure in floating bags, which makes you try and grab your treasure bags at the place where you died, or be penalised for dying by losing your money and not retrieving it. After fighting a boss, you're treated to a map stage screen, very much like Zelda II or Super Mario Bros. 3, where you get to choose which stage you want to tackle next, as well as visit the stores, which let you buy items that include health potions, shovel upgrades, armour upgrades, as well as anything that you'd normally expect in a staple RPG game. You don't level your character up per say, but you can buy upgrades. You also unlock spells, which you can use to turn the tide in battle. Certain items will replenish your spells as well. There are also collectable items and secrets in the game, which add as a completion bonus.
GRAPHICS & PRESENTATION:
Shovel Knight is a beautiful looking game. Crisp visuals with bright colours, and an 8-bit art style in glorious widescreen. This game doesn't look 8-bit just for the sake of popularity, its art style is beautifully crafted, and best represents its genre. I can't imagine what Shovel Knight would have looked like if it was in 3D (or 2.5D if you will) as I can't imagine it looking any other way. Each boss' stage is unique, and has a different colour palette, making each stage look unique. You'll fight in castles, underwater, deep dark caverns as well as up high in the skies.
SOUND & MUSIC:
The sound effects are what you'd expect from an 8-bit style, with attention to detail down to each characters' text box making a different sound when it scrolls. The music is absolutely fantastic. Composed by Jake Kaufman, with the help of Manami Matsumae (the same person who worked on the soundtrack from the first  two Mega Man games) the music has a very noticeable Megaman-esque influence, as it's bright and very catchy, with each stage having a different but just as memorable tune. If you're a lover of chiptune music, or video game music in general, I highly recommend getting the soundtrack to this game as well. You'll have the tunes in your head for days on end.
LONGEVITY & NG+:
The game offers a lot of hidden secrets and items, for those wanting to get that completion bonus. I'm not 100% sure if you get anything special once you get a 100% completion rate, but for those who aim to get everything, this game offers a lot of replayability, as well as multiple achievements to obtain as well. New Game Plus is offered for those who want an extra challenge. While the base game was quite challenging, it was quite fair as well, and it gave you many chances to learn and try again. This game is easy to learn, but hard to master, so those who want a much harder challenge, New Game Plus will offer that. With less checkpoints, tougher enemies, and more damage dealt upon you, NG+ is definitely more appealing for the "hardcore" gamers. Those who found the vanilla game a bit too easy, should definitely check out New Game Plus, as it is much less forgiving, and will have you trying again, and again, and again. This also extends the replayability of the game as well, and almost makes it feel like a new experience. There's also a pretty achievement for completing NG+.
As an added bonus, Yacht Club games released an expansion pack for Shovel Knight, called Plague of Shadows. In this one, you play as one of the bosses from the base game, Plague Knight. With slightly different jumping mechanics, and a vastly different arsenal at your disposal, playing as Plague Knight offers a fresh take on the base game, and acts as a distinct play-through of the game, especially for those wanting something new after beating the base game as Shovel Knight. Plague Knight is an alchemist, with many different potions and tricks up his sleeve, and can purchase upgrades in the game very much like Shovel Knight can. You'll also get to see the story through his perspective, complete with some new characters that you meet along the way. Best of all, it's entirely free! In a game market of constant DLCs (Downloadable Content) it's refreshing to see a game company care for its players like this.
OVERALL:
There aren't many bad things to say about this game. While the jumping is slightly delayed (though it might be my controller/PC setup) it isn't much of a burden. NG+ did get repetitive when I kept losing over and over again in certain bits, but this happens with most hard games anyway. Apart from these minor issues, I can't say anything bad about this game. It has fun gameplay, great visuals and great sound, and it's a game that will make you want to complete it at least twice, which in today's market of "disposable" games, it's a nice thing to have. Even before the free DLC, Shovel Knight was already a complete game, and it didn't fall under the bad category of some games, where they release "the rest" after the game's initial release. What you get is a finished game, and it delivers. With the flurry of retro style games that have come out in the past, done almost for the sake of selling nostalgia, Shovel Knight surpasses all of that, and what we get is a fresh game that was made for the sake of being a great game. The retro style is not done for parody, and the nostalgic feel comes from within. Shovel Knight is a game that became an instant classic in my books, and to me is easily the best indie game that came out in 2014 (Plague of Shadows was released in 2015). So what are you waiting for? Grab thy shovel, and grab this game. I dig it!

So a quick review.
Cons:-
Matchmaking, this has to be one of the worst matchmaking algorithms i have ever come across, in any type of game. 9/10 you will be put with players ranked 150 levels higher than you, no exception. Thus, giving you a 5% chance of even completing one round. I've done fine up to a point, but it's seriously annoying.
Community, there are some seriously stupid people on this game. You would have to question the mentality. This is NOT a game such a COD / BF. It is a vastly complex game. Some people don't understand that. People will blame YOU for not killing someone 2ft infront of them. It's almost like a community of young teenagers / young adults on here that are in their diapers.
Friendly fire, This is always on (as it should be). However, 5/10 times you will get a group that for no reason what so ever, begin teamkilling one another. It wastes your time, and everyone elses time. There is no punishment for teamkilling, other than a vote to kick.
Cheating community, read up about it on the forums / reddit / actual reviews from youtubers. The community is RIPE with wallhackers (primarily). There was a ban wave i read about not too long ago. However, no other progress is to be made / cared about.  Again, read up on it online.
Communication, No one uses a headset on here. On a game that promotes teamwork and comms, it's shocking to see that it's not promoted by the community.
Players, As an example, i was pulse (a character that uses heartbeat sensor with either shotgun or ump). So i'm a room away from where the bomb is, planning to kill the opposing few players from behind as they walk past (using heartbeat sensor to monitor movements). One player from our team comes to where i'm sitting, blows a hole in the floor, alerting everyone to my location. Yes, we lost. He blamed me for not jumping through the hole to go behind them. THIS is just ONE scenario of many.
Pros:-
Operators, Holy Jesus they hit the nail on the head with this. The vast amount of operators and their functionality allows for a truly dynamic and lethal team. In defence especially, it is important that you pick certain operators to hinder the enemies movement, or to disrupt drones (hint hint).
Tutorials, The three quick tutorials run you through the basics via a quick in game video. I found this to be much better than actually having to do each individual step (like you would in previous games).
Scenarios, These build up on the tutorials running you through the different game modes. These scenarios are a must as help you with a better understanding of the game, for and against for each operator, map awareness, tactical advantages and so on. One of the best things implemented in this game!
Conclusion:-
It may seem as if i'm 'not good enough', or 'raging'. I'll be clear, i've played many FPS games, both tactical and non tactical, and i've never come across a game that's disappointed me more.
I would strongly advise against this game, and i'd advise people to seriously check online for the flaws of matchmaking, and cheaters within the game. It's honestly annoying.

SHOVEL KNIGHT REVIEW
Updated: (Includes New Game Plus and Plague of Shadows)
Shovel Knight is a game by Yatch Club games, and the first I have played from them. Having seen a few previews, and hearing about it, Shovel Knight did look like an appealing game. Originally, I thought it was going to be just another "retro" style game, or rouge-a-like, which we've seen an entire flurry of in the past five or so years (many great, others not so much) so at first it didn't hold my attention as much. Having seen a trailer, prior to its release though, I saw great potential. Not only was it more of an action platformer (more of my genre) but the gameplay and presentation looked fantastic, so I had to pick it up there and then.
My first impressions of the game were excellent. From the moment the title screen comes on, you are greeted to some fantastic chiptune music, which feels both fresh and new, but yet familiar and nostalgic. This game will definnitely appeal to people who grew up on the NES and SNES, but also anyone who wants to get into 2D platformers. I could easily go on tangents to talk about one thing to the next, but I'll seperate them into different categories.
GAMEPLAY:
The gameplay of Shovel Knight is what you'd expect from an action platformer. Your shovel is your main weapon, and it can be used both to bash enemies, as well as using it as a kind of pogo stick, to bounce off enemies and obstacles, much like in Ducktales the game on the NES. Speaking of which, the main influences I got from this game were Legend of Zelda (items and map screen), Ducktales (the pogo mechanic) and Mega Man (music and some stages). The jumping in the game feels slightly delayed, but having played countless amounts of old games on Nintendo systems, it's easy to pick up on it and master, like riding a bike. You start off on an intro stage, which teaches you how to play the game, by unfolding events, rather than the much redundant "text boxes" or hand holding, which most modern games have today. Shovel Knight makes you feel like you've learned, and earned those victories, rather than telling you what to do. You can also collect treasure either by finding them out in the open, or digging up certain rock and dirt piles or blocks. Treasure acts as your currency, and can be used to buy items in shops. When you die, you drop your treasure in floating bags, which makes you try and grab your treasure bags at the place where you died, or be penalised for dying by losing your money and not retrieving it. After fighting a boss, you're treated to a map stage screen, very much like Zelda II or Super Mario Bros. 3, where you get to choose which stage you want to tackle next, as well as visit the stores, which let you buy items that include health potions, shovel upgrades, armour upgrades, as well as anything that you'd normally expect in a staple RPG game. You don't level your character up per say, but you can buy upgrades. You also unlock spells, which you can use to turn the tide in battle. Certain items will replenish your spells as well. There are also collectable items and secrets in the game, which add as a completion bonus.
GRAPHICS & PRESENTATION:
Shovel Knight is a beautiful looking game. Crisp visuals with bright colours, and an 8-bit art style in glorious widescreen. This game doesn't look 8-bit just for the sake of popularity, its art style is beautifully crafted, and best represents its genre. I can't imagine what Shovel Knight would have looked like if it was in 3D (or 2.5D if you will) as I can't imagine it looking any other way. Each boss' stage is unique, and has a different colour palette, making each stage look unique. You'll fight in castles, underwater, deep dark caverns as well as up high in the skies.
SOUND & MUSIC:
The sound effects are what you'd expect from an 8-bit style, with attention to detail down to each characters' text box making a different sound when it scrolls. The music is absolutely fantastic. Composed by Jake Kaufman, with the help of Manami Matsumae (the same person who worked on the soundtrack from the first  two Mega Man games) the music has a very noticeable Megaman-esque influence, as it's bright and very catchy, with each stage having a different but just as memorable tune. If you're a lover of chiptune music, or video game music in general, I highly recommend getting the soundtrack to this game as well. You'll have the tunes in your head for days on end.
LONGEVITY & NG+:
The game offers a lot of hidden secrets and items, for those wanting to get that completion bonus. I'm not 100% sure if you get anything special once you get a 100% completion rate, but for those who aim to get everything, this game offers a lot of replayability, as well as multiple achievements to obtain as well. New Game Plus is offered for those who want an extra challenge. While the base game was quite challenging, it was quite fair as well, and it gave you many chances to learn and try again. This game is easy to learn, but hard to master, so those who want a much harder challenge, New Game Plus will offer that. With less checkpoints, tougher enemies, and more damage dealt upon you, NG+ is definitely more appealing for the "hardcore" gamers. Those who found the vanilla game a bit too easy, should definitely check out New Game Plus, as it is much less forgiving, and will have you trying again, and again, and again. This also extends the replayability of the game as well, and almost makes it feel like a new experience. There's also a pretty achievement for completing NG+.
As an added bonus, Yacht Club games released an expansion pack for Shovel Knight, called Plague of Shadows. In this one, you play as one of the bosses from the base game, Plague Knight. With slightly different jumping mechanics, and a vastly different arsenal at your disposal, playing as Plague Knight offers a fresh take on the base game, and acts as a distinct play-through of the game, especially for those wanting something new after beating the base game as Shovel Knight. Plague Knight is an alchemist, with many different potions and tricks up his sleeve, and can purchase upgrades in the game very much like Shovel Knight can. You'll also get to see the story through his perspective, complete with some new characters that you meet along the way. Best of all, it's entirely free! In a game market of constant DLCs (Downloadable Content) it's refreshing to see a game company care for its players like this.
OVERALL:
There aren't many bad things to say about this game. While the jumping is slightly delayed (though it might be my controller/PC setup) it isn't much of a burden. NG+ did get repetitive when I kept losing over and over again in certain bits, but this happens with most hard games anyway. Apart from these minor issues, I can't say anything bad about this game. It has fun gameplay, great visuals and great sound, and it's a game that will make you want to complete it at least twice, which in today's market of "disposable" games, it's a nice thing to have. Even before the free DLC, Shovel Knight was already a complete game, and it didn't fall under the bad category of some games, where they release "the rest" after the game's initial release. What you get is a finished game, and it delivers. With the flurry of retro style games that have come out in the past, done almost for the sake of selling nostalgia, Shovel Knight surpasses all of that, and what we get is a fresh game that was made for the sake of being a great game. The retro style is not done for parody, and the nostalgic feel comes from within. Shovel Knight is a game that became an instant classic in my books, and to me is easily the best indie game that came out in 2014 (Plague of Shadows was released in 2015). So what are you waiting for? Grab thy shovel, and grab this game. I dig it!

Hardest Portal game to date. Beat this in 11 hours without a walkthrough and I have to say, this is hard. And I mean danm hard. But that's good, because if it weren't hard I could have beat it in the amount of time it takes to beat the first game.
The amount of work that went into this mod is amazing. Granted, it's borrowing a lot of assets, but that doesn't change the fact that this is an actual game. I don't consider this a mod because it is just that good. This is far more than just a series of new test chambers and microsoft sam voices some people decided to add onto the series. This is actually a good prequel to portal 2. This could be Portal 1.5 if it weren't a mod.
That being said, I feel that some things may be a bit frustrating such as the lack of usable surfaces. Most of the white surfaces I try to use are usually grey and cannot be used, which is really frustrating if I'm trying my danmdest to beat a puzzle. The final boss where you have to use turrets to blow up the server is also really annoying because the turrets fall down very easily and don't turn in the direction you want to unless you're in a very specific spot. I seriously had 2 seconds remaining on the timer because of the turrets constantly falling over and now aiming correctly. That was the only part of the game where I started screaming at the screen.
Well done puzzle construction, excellent voice-acting, hidden easter eggs everywhere, great story, and Virgil is Canadian which is always a plus.
Play it. It's free (if you have Portal 2 which you need to play this game) and worth the effort to pass all the chambers, even though you can skip them all and get straight to the final boss room.

I think they should do like League of Legends, you win points that you can use to buy permanent stuff and low cost buffs to get more money or xp for one trip of fishing or something.

If the prices for buying that currency were reasonnable, I would consider buying some, but it's ludicrously high! I will never buy them unless they drop the price to at least half of what it is now... if not down to 25%. It's just too damn high.
No matter the money thing, it's still worth a try. Although they should work less on graphics and more on the game itself.

Like the 4th installment of this franchise, Saints Row: The Third was a truly fresh experience. While most games often take themselves too seriously, Saints Row: The Third is a tongue-in-cheek satire on various aspects of pop culture and city life. Unlike AAA titles like GTA, you can pretty much expect this game to test your funny-bone while still retaining a challenge if you want one. You aren't limited by one particular mode of play here either. It is one of the most awesome and versatile sandbox experiences today and other Saints Row titles still continue to take the style further and fly with it. Don't be deceived by reviews claiming that the previous title was the best of the series. Nostalgia truly only lasts so long until you realize you've been kidding yourself. Try this game. Seriously. Try it. You can pick up a copy for like 8 USD/7 EUR at The Global Digital Gaming marketplace. I encourage you to try any one of the Saints Row titles available here on Steam. While you're at it, check out some of the Saints Row: The Third and Saints Row IV mods at
. These games are moddable and the various contributions from the Saints Row community really take the game further. The mods will pad the game with with even more hours of entertainment. Now go and backhand some furries in Steelport!

As far as survival horror games are concerned, Amnesia is among the best. Rather than bombarding you with the usual cliches (such as boring set pieces that amount to little more than a pile of dead bodies and a few bloody handprints on the wall or enemies that pop from behind doors), Frictional had the common sense to incorporate aspects of gameplay that create an atmosphere of pure dread. At your disposal is a lantern, a few miscellaneous tools, and your wits.
The action is very well-paced for a survival horror title. You think you're alone, and suddendly, a dragging set of footsteps, a groan in the distance. In many other games (Doom 3 and Dead Space spring to mind) you can pull out a gun, but in Amnesia, there's nothing you can do except run like hell, find the nearest door, and barricade yourself behind it. As a result when playing Amnesia, I often feel a palpable sense of anxiety. And that's rare. If you want a fresh new take on a frankly stale genre, look no further.

Many people compare TI to CS, which is understandable, because of the Gooseman’s legacy and that the TI “feels/looks” the closes to CS, but TI is not CS and that is the reason why people like me and all the rest of the dedicated TI players like the game. If I have to describe/compare with a single sentence both of the game I would say “If CS is like a professional boxing with strict rules and limitations, then TI is like MMA (Mixed Martial Arts).” CS is stripped from any kind of “tunings” except the bullet vest/helmet and the defuse kit, which is good for competitive/sport matches (you know what to expect). But in the other hand TI is more arcade, you can tune/create your own “class and style” of game play similar to Team Fortress 2, but without the limitations of predefined classes. You still need some skills to shoot precisely (deal with recoil), use tactics (communicate), use grenades, which I love how they behaves, not like in CS (in CS there are just two useful grenades, flash bang and smoke all the rest are joke), when you throw frag grenade, tear gas, smoke, flash bang you know what to expect and the other side have to get the hell out from there, if they want to survive and even so they still can be blinded for a while after or knocked down from the blast or have a blurred vision, smoke is passive grenade and the incendiary is more or less like the smoke to create a barrier, but not to kill. You can rush/run for your life or to attack, you can peak, you can roll, there is bullet penetration (although not always predictable and sticking guns from the glass walls make greater damage than no sticking, but hey no one is perfect ;)). There is a map and if you make noise (shooting, running or even moving will give your position away) good for ambushing campers. And if you get tired from all that bomb, rescue, escort game play, then you have cars :). There are plenty of weapons, gears and perks to choose from and you start the game with 50000GP enough to buy a decent assault rifle permanent or rent all bunch of stuff. Compared to all that CS is much more limited, plain and simple, which as I said, has its good sides.  TI compared to Call of Duty is still “realistic”, so no any air strikes, missiles etc, maybe just the dogs are that little “too much”, but there is match limitation for them, so it is so so bearable.
Although TI is free to play, it is not (at least by my opinion) pay to win game, you can buy absolutely everything in the game with earned game points (GP) just by playing it, the only thing which cannot be bought with GP are the custom skins, which do not have any direct influence on your player specs.
