This game is AWESOME! By saying that, I also mean it in a sense, because it can also be very horrible. Single player of the game works fine, though I'm sure there are issues out there that I haven't seen or personally had. But the issues on my personal experience came from the co-op. I played the game once by myself and then I played it with my bro twice in co-op and boy, we had gazillion of glitches in that, the game was glitchier than a glitch itself. Also the fuel for game rage came from the glitches, but they were mostly the source of hard laughter and tears.
About the gameplay itself, if you love mayhem and carnage, then this game is for you. Also if you love to laugh, this game is for you. The humor level is brilliant for my own tastes, and not too childish vs. GTA: San Andreas for example. Also the story is not as serious as in GTA series, IMO, so this game actually pushed GTA:SA off the throne and took its place. For what I can tell, this game gave me everything GTA didn't, but which I had always longed for while playing GTA. One of the downsides though, is that you can't really use your own music, without the need of editing files, so I never went for it myself. Also, the soundtrack of the game is not as strong and powerful as in Saints Row 2, but you can take the music off altogether and play your own from windows, so it's not that bad. Though one of the best parts for me, was the character creation because of the cool music lol.
The game is not too hard either, I blasted through to halfway on one go when single playing and the character upgrades makes it easier and funnier as well, also giving you something to aim for, especially because you are rewarded with achievements for your hard work. (Me and my buddy finally got every single achievement, including You're My Hero, which feels soooo good...)
As for the recommendation? Hell yeah, I recommend it! I have a bit over 300 hours in game and that explains something. So overall, the good points defeat the bad ones. Graphics are good, if not the best out there, but it's an older game, though people say it's a bad port to pc. - My system specs are as follows, a dual core i5, 4GB of ram and GeForce GT 420 2GB with a 1TB HDD on which the game is installed and Windows 7 Home Premium, and so I had to turn my graphics down to low and such, also to play on 1024 resolution and DirectX 9, though I was able to play on DX 10 as well sometimes, until it started to peak. Also, when I played single player, I had an issue with my monitor on DX 10 with red dots on the screen, which was fixed by switching to DX 9, but when I played with my bro, I didn't have that issue when I tried DX 10, so I don't know what that might have been, maybe because back then, I used Radeon HD 4670 512MB graphics card.
Pros:
- Funny
- Good graphics
- Fluent gameplay
- Not many glitches in single player
- Music in Create Character
- Not too hard, unless made that way
- Customization options in-game for character/vehicles
Cons:
- Laggy graphics on higher settings (based on the hardware)
- Many and more glitches in the co-op
- No ability to use own music in a folder form
- Occasional crashes, which can happen during the gameplay or when exiting the game
In the end, I can say that I don't regret getting this game with all of its DLC when it was on sale. I have enjoyed it a lot during the years and I will still enjoy it for years to come. And despite the glitches, you should try to play it in co-op as well and be prepared to laugh (and sometimes rage) a lot.

text:
Before the credits roll you'll catsit a tiger, play a hilarious text adventure, get a sex change, hack up Mexican wrestlers with a chainsaw, visit a Tron-like computer world, and participate in many other ridiculous leisure activities. Saints Row the Third can be accused of being many things, but repetitive isn't one of them.
Some games create atmospheric worlds that attempt to draw you in with moving stories about characters seeking a second chance, or cast you as troubled superheroes who push themselves to the limit to fight evil. Saints Row: The Third is not like those games. Rather, it's the kind of game that gives you weapons called apocafists with which you can punch people, instantly making them explode in a bloody mess. The Third won't impress you with knockout visuals, move you with an absorbing story, or engage you with challenging combat. What it does, better than just about any game before, is embrace the idea of an open world as a place for play, constantly giving you access to awesome new toys and providing you with no shortage of exciting opportunities to use them.
One thing you definitely shouldn't ignore is the main story. Within just the first few missions, you plummet out of a plane and into an airborne shoot-out, skydive into a penthouse that belongs to a rival gang, use a UAV drone to call in guided missiles on tanks, and more. The missions eventually become a bit predictable for a while, serving as introductions to the other activities and diversions available to you in Steelport. But before long, they get wild again, packing in numerous surprises before culminating in one of two outrageous final missions.
Saints Row: The Third is buoyed to great heights by terrific mission design and by the remarkable assortment of vehicles and weapons it gives you with which to take over Steelport. Whether you're buying up property to increase your hourly income, cruising the city in your favorite vehicle to collect photo ops, drug packages, and sex dolls, or punching people to bits with those crazy apocafists, there's rarely a dull moment. Saints Row: The Third succeeds tremendously at delivering its unique brand of raunchy, outrageous fun. If you have an appetite for this particular kind of absurdity, you won't be disappointed

I'll get right to it: This is not recommended to anyone who doesn't enjoy logic puzzles.
Because that's what this game is about. Do not play it for the story.
That's not to say the story is bad (quite the opposite in fact), there is just not enough of it to justify forcing yourself through puzzles which you may not enjoy.
But, if you have been longing for a more challenging, gameplay-focused iteration of Portal, this is absolutely worth playing.
The puzzles look great and require some serious thinking.
Solving a chamber you have been stuck on for half an hour is extremely rewarding, and the game has plenty opportunities for that in store.
One thing I would like to criticise is the rather homogeneous style of puzzles.
A few execution-based ones interspersed between the logic puzzles would add a nice change of pace and give your brain some time to rest a little.
Further, while the game did use all of the puzzle components Portal 2 provides, they hardly feel like anything new.
Presumably time and/or personnel contraints made development of new features impossible, but it would have been nice at any rate.
Overall, I highly recommend this game, but it may not be everyone's cup of tea.

Since its original release, Team Fortress 2 has benefited from numerous updates and made the jump to a free-to-play business model. So how well is Team Fortress 2 faring in 2018 among the current crop of competitors for your time?
The short answer is, it's holding up very well. The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.
Staying relevant even a year after release is rare for a competitive shooter, and yet, here's Team Fortress 2, still lively after ten years in the business. At times it feels like the same game you could have played back then, and at other times it feels like no one will ever quite nail class-based shooter competition the way TF2 does. The experience has evolved over the years without compromising what made it so great in the first place, so though your free-to-play options may have increased considerably in the past few years, there are few that do it as well as Team Fortress 2.

Amazing.  That pretty much sums up this not-mod.  This does not deserve the designation "mod".  It is far too good for that.  Though the story is mediocre, everything else was absolutely fantastic.  They even did a good job connecting it to the canon Portal and Portal 2 plotlines.  The puzzle difficulty generally exceeds the difficulty of Portal 2, making it all the more satisfying when you solve it.  The soundtrack is very easy to listen to while you get stuck on puzzles.  I would recommend this to you even if it cost money.  But it doesn't!  So what are you doing reading these reviews?  Download it.  NOW!
Now that i've said all that, I will also say this: If you do not like puzzles for puzzles sake or if you get frustrated easily, I do not recommend this game to you.  These puzzles are far more difficult than Portal or Portal 2.  Both of those games hold your hands with puzzles, giving you subtle hints at what you should do.  This game has far less of that. Amazing.  That pretty much sums up this not-mod.  This does not deserve the designation "mod".  It is far too good for that.  Though the story is mediocre, everything else was absolutely fantastic.  They even did a good job connecting it to the canon Portal and Portal 2 plotlines.  The puzzle difficulty generally exceeds the difficulty of Portal 2, making it all the more satisfying when you solve it.  The soundtrack is very easy to listen to while you get stuck on puzzles.  I would recommend this to you even if it cost money.  But it doesn't!  So what are you doing reading these reviews?  Download it.  NOW!
Now that i've said all that, I will also say this: If you do not like puzzles for puzzles sake or if you get frustrated easily, I do not recommend this game to you.  These puzzles are far more difficult than Portal or Portal 2.  Both of those games hold your hands with puzzles, giving you subtle hints at what you should do.  This game has far less of that.  If Portal 2 was training, this is what it was training you for.

Saints Row: The Third is a somewhat fun time, but the game doesn't seem to know what it wants to do. It's pace throughout the story goes from action to comedy to whatever it wants to do. It's not a bad game, mind you. It's definitely above average of many open world third person games. But it tries to hard to be "so randum xd" that it comes off as incohesive and a moshpit of mediocre to bad design decisions throughout the game. It's pretty fun with a friend, but on it's own it came out to be more obnoxious and boring than anything. Pick it up if this wouldn't deter your enjoyment for the game, but only get The Full Package and only while it's on sale, since it gets pretty cheap.
Also, originally when Saints Row IV came out, people (including I) thought it was going to be a Saints Row: The Third but trying too hard to be more outlandish, but after completing it, the game came out as being overall better executed with more intelligent humor than the Third game, so I would actually recommend it over this one.
tl;dr: The game is ok, but isn't put together well due to trying to be "omg so randum lol xd" and having some poor design decisions, which Saints Row IV actually did a lot BETTER, which I would recommend over the Third game. Only purchase if that doesn't bother you, you have money to spare, it's on sale, AND it is the Full Package version (which comes with all DLC).

If you're looking for a truly excellent, and effectively scary horror title, go right past the big budget titles.
Amnesia is made by a dedicated and very talented team of only 5 people who get horror gameplay exactly right. This isn't their first game, so they've learned a few things along the way, but this is their best horror title to date.
Amnesia is unique in that you are virtually defenseless throughout the entire game. Instead of shooting at enemies, you have to run and hide from them. It is surprising what such a basic mechanic does to evoke feelings of actual terror in the player. But, there's more. The shader effects and excellent audio add to the experience.
This will probably be the scariest game you'll have ever played.

I have a 1000+ hours on Arma so I'll just throw in my 2 cents
Pros
Excellent realistic aspects. Bullet drop increases with distance, you get tired after walking or running after long distances, gun sounds are very real, realistic bullet damage. 6.5 and up 1 hit 1 kill with no armor, 3 hits 1 kill with armor.
Very fun gameplay. Getting kills are extremely satisfying. It's not like mainstream fps. You have to wait and play it smart. When you finally see some one watching him drop is like getting free terimisu. Guns are fun to use. I personally recommend the Katiba. Sniping is by far the most fun. On this you really have to act like a sniper. Get the view distance, wait for the target to get out in the open and DONT MISS. If you do you prob won't get another chance.
The different gametypes service a wide demographic of players.
If you like a military simulator then the co ops are the best bet. There are plenty of communities that are devoted to large scale war like battles complete with the full military Arsenal and Walkie talkie like communication called tasked forced radio. If taking tactical objectives from waves of Russian npcs  fun then this is for you.
If you like survival like games then look no further than wasteland. Join one of the two teams and duke it out or go out on your own and form your own army with the independent faction. Look for weapons or simply take them from those you kill. Build your bases and make others cry by raiding theirs. Fight over one of the many many cities and towns which house gun and clothing stores or accomplish side missions to make money and buy weapons.
King of the hill are for those who like to get into the action and kill squares quick. Advance with your team and try to clear the city house to house catfish to catfish from other players and wrestle control. Become death and reap experience ranking up and earning better weapons and perks. Or maybe get in an aircraft and simply bomb the city into oblivion.
And finally my personal favorite, altis life. Role play any role you like. Become a drug smuggler, harvest heroin, form your own cartel and fight the police for control of altis. Rob other players of their hard earned money and steal their kidney to sell on the black market. Make the civilians pay taxes for usin *your* cocaine fields. or perhaps adopt a benevolent route and help those who are trying to make it. Protect them from other players. Become a police officer and clean up the streets. Get into car chases, stop bank robberies, deal with hostage situations, arrest drug peddlers, and fight for your life when a cartel tries to kidnap you. Or maybe become a medic and get paid bank to revive idiots who can't drive.x
Cons
The game is perhaps too realistic and has a big learning curve. Basically it's like fighting a battle in real life with all strings attached. Your gun bounces all over the place when you walk so fighting is best done from the crouch or prone position. It can be incredible ply frustrating getting killed in 3 shots when you walk out of cover so you really have to play smart.
The game is NOTORIOUSLY buggy. Don't try to go over walls or fences because you'll probably be shot into outer space. Swimming is incredibly annoying and tedious so avoid water. And by ALL THAT IS HOLY AVOID CHICKEN FENCES WHEN DRIVING. Vault jumping is to be avoided.
The npcs teter between forest gump and superman with ray vision.
A lot of communities in the RP realm are pretty toxic with abusive admins. Good servers are a diamond in a dozen so it's best to play with friends first.
All in all is give this game a 9/10. I strongly recommend it to a wide variety of players seeking to adopt different play styles. I hope this is helpful.

Portal Stories:Mel is an incredibly well made free story-driven single player puzzle mod for Portal 2. I said story-driven, because that is a crucial part of the mod IMO. Nonetheless, the other areas of gameplay were not neglected.
On the one hand the mod excels with its hard puzzles, which can get you thinking quite hardly if you've only played Portal1/Portal2 without trying some much harder workshop maps. The learning curve is indeed pretty steep and a bit frustrating if you haven't played Portal in a while.
On the other hand it offers long gameplay and a bit replayability due to 22 detailedly designed levels within 5 chapters and some easter eggs to find. The first chapter is an introduction whereas the fifth is the final bossfight. Additionally, it should be stated, that the soundtrack is suiting very well to the map design and that the voice acting was well done, except for the Cave Johnson imitation in the very beginning of the game, which was quite off. In addition to that I didn't encounter many bugs but one where I fell through a wall in a pit. It wasn't something to worry about but it was there.
Storywise, one can say that it is lined in between Portal 1 and Portal 2, however, the first chapter is situated before the incidents of the first game and just serves as an introduction as mentioned above. The last chapter is immediately connected to the first incidents in Portal 2 and do lead to them. Furthermore, the events in this game reveal some unanswered questions within the main Portal games, although these should not get taken for granted since the mod is not considered cannon.
Conclusion:
If you like the Portal franchise and want to enjoy the old but beloved Portal atmosphere then this game will suit you well. You don't even have to worry about not liking it since it's free. The only thing you could lose is your precious time. I highly recommend this to Portal- and/or Puzzle fans.

Portal Stories: Mel brings the worst of everything that was wrong with Portal 2 together into one tidy little package.  Yes, Portal 2 is an awesome game.  It was probably my favorite game of all time, but it's not without problems.  There are areas of Portal 2 that I did not like.  Any area where the "puzzle" is simply to find a small portable surface in a huge expanse of non-portable surfaces is frustrating.  It's not really a puzzle at all, but simply a searching game.  That's not stimulating and it's not fun.  Luckily, Portal 2 doesn't have too many of these.  PSM has lots of them.
I found myself frequently lost in PSM, not sure what I was supposed to do or where I was supposed to go.  Again, Portal 2 had very few cases of this.  In the first couple of chapters, PSM has more of this than just about anything else.  Luckily, the later chapters are much better in this regard.
One of the "Main Features" listed on the store page is "Logic based puzzles, not execution based puzzles".  I have to call BS on this.  A couple of parts of PSM requires you to jump from platform to platform across electrified water.  Since when is Portal a platform game?  That's clearly execution based.  One misstep and you are dead.  There are plenty of other examples where you have get the execution just right or you will die.  Death is much more common in PSM than it is in the Valve offering and it really detracts from the game.  Portal is not a game where death should occur frequently.  That's just the nature of puzzles.  A misstep leading to death takes you away from puzzle solving and is clearly an execution based mechanic.
There are areas of PSM where it is not possible to solve the puzzle without some knowledge of the environment - knowledge that the player couldn't possibly have on the first play through unless they watch a video on how to solve it.  This issue never occurred in Portal 2.  Portal is a logic puzzle game.  PSM has some elements of this, but there was a clear attempt to make it something else entirely in their attempt to make it unique and difficult.  Difficulty as a result of mind-bending puzzles is fine.  Difficulty as a result of hidden elements or the need for knowledge the player won't have is not.
The game crashes occasionally.  Don't even think of ALT-TABing out of the game or will crash 90% of the time.  If you do want to ALT-TAB, be sure to save your position first.
The first test chamber has a platform that is not necessary and I solved it without using it.  This indicates a lack of play testing or it probably would have been removed.
You can't control the angle of portals in order to direct light bridges properly.  In Portal 2, the angle of the portal was often necessary to get the light bridge to be angled in the direction you want it to be.  PSM has light bridges coming out of the portal in the direction it wants to, which is not realistic.  If the bridge goes into the portal lengthwise, it should come out lengthwise.  Not have a 90% twist on it.
It's possible to get physically stuck in some places which requires a restart from the last checkpoint.  A tractor beam once trapped me against a camera mounted on the wall.  Even after I turned off the beam, I was still stuck on the wall with no way down.  On the very next level, I was trapped by a light bridge.  If you stand where the light bridge appears, you will get stuck in it.  If this happens, you will need to turn off or reposition the light bridge with your portal gun to get free.  If you are unlucky enough to not have one of these options, you will need to restart the level from the menu.
Voice acting is mediocre.  I have seen worse, but it could be better.
There are some good things about the game.  The environment is visually appealing and was very well done.  I love the energy effect in the portal gun itself.
Portal Stories: MEL was somewhat fun, but the large number of annoyances and other flaws make this a game that is probably not worth playing.  If you are huge Portal fan, it might be worth a look.  But you can find many more enjoyable Portal puzzles in the Community Hub.  Despite the huge effort and labor of love that obviously went into making this, I can't really recommend it.

TF2 is a shooting game, were you defend something or attack whatever is being defended. There are hundreds of different weapons you can use to kill your enemies, but you have to find them.
Pros:
-Weapon combinations that can be devestating
-Genrally a good community
-Incorperates community suggestions
-Gets updated roughly 3 times a year
-Hats
Cons:
-Only a few maps are really played, leaving the others in the dust
-Matchmaking can take over 5 minutes if your selection isn't big enough
-Hackers aren't that common, but they come in groups so you can't kick them
-The kick system
-Auto-balance is not there
Overall I realy love this game, and still has a major player base at running for 10 years. If you are into shooters, tradeing to make money, or just designing things that could get on the market, then you should play this game.

Let me start by saying, I have never been more satisfied with a mod in my entire life. I just finished playing it after a few days and the story really gets to you if you choose to get invested in it.  To sum up what this mod is without giving too many spoilers to the story: This is a mod that gives a story to Valve's unused character Mel. It portrays her as a 50's athlete who is testing out an invention created by Cave Johnson. Unfortunately, when things turn for the worst, Mel must work through a series of puzzles with some... extra assistance. Can't say more than that.
About the game itself, the cutscenes were stunning, the music was fantastic, and the voice acting was well done as well. Tthough the Cave Johnson voice didn't perfectly match up, it was an outstanding impression. The puzzles start out with an easy difficulty, but as time goes on, they really make you think. It actually managed to teach me about an aspect of portal I didn't know about involving light bridges and boxes (don't wanna give spoilers to a puzzle solution.) The only thing I did not like about this is that there is a lot of space and sometimes not enough guidance. In a couple of places, I actually managed to get a bit lost. Though I did manage to get back on track, it was slightly annoying. This does not by any means say that the open space is terrible and should be blocked, just that there should be a bit of a push in the larger areas giving the player an idea of the path they should use.
Overall, if I had to give a numerical rating to this mod, I would give it a 9.5/10! Fantastic job!

It's fun, but with so much depth to the controls and in game systems it's not a casual title. I got heavily into mission and scenario making, and had direct insight on a running Epoch server for awhile. There are a few things about the game that ultimately made me put it down for good, since there's a lot of things I'd been waiting on since release. The AI was still atrocious when I stopped playing (Tanoa release), and that content from BI (released instead of addressing core issues/shortcomings with the game) was underwhelming. Updates would play hell with my editor files and scenarios, and sometimes my created content would break for just no understandable reason. FPS issues would make online impossible sometimes, mostly because of server load due to god-knows-what two things happening at once, but wasn't too bad in single player.
It has the makings of a great game, but honestly it's overreaching when explored to it's full potential. If you want to romp around and play Army, it's a great game, but if you really like digging into the whole war sim aspect then it's a frustrating mess. The modding community is awesome, I'll say that. They're who I should thank for the almost 700 hours I put into the game, not BI.

My my my. Where to begin.
Do you find Dead Space scary?
Does DOOM make you look behind your shoulder?
Are you extremely frightened of black people that you can't bear to play Resident Evil 5 for more than 1 minute? Well look no further.
Amnesia will drive you INSANE. This game is by far the scariest game I have, and quite frankly, will ever play. There are no weapons, no uzi's, no co-op, nobody to help you as you go through this game ALONE. You are hunted by a creature not from this world, intent on killing you. And it cannot. Be. Stopped. Armed with only your wits, you barricade doors with barrels and crates, find a hiding spot and pray to god that it doesn't see you.
The storyline is compelling and you'll want to find out what's really going on. You play as a man named "Daniel" who finds himself waking up and suffering from (you guessed it) Amnesia. You can find pieces of his journal as the game goes on and you slowly learn what happened to him... and what's happening around you. It's filled with sinister twists and leaves you wondering how you truly ended up the way you are. Look at me being all cryptic, hah.
The game left me in a bumbling mess, screaming in terror and whimpering throughout. If you want the scare of your life, play Amnesia: The Dark Descent.

So, SO good. Can't believe this is a free mod built by the community. The developers did an amazing job. The puzzles are very hard, the challenge is here that tended to be missing from Portal 1 & 2. I had to consult a walk through a few times for hints but I would rather that than just breezing through them.

This game is a mixture of good and bad, but mainly good. The immersion and world building throughout is very convincing, and feels very portal. It feels very much like Portal 3 in that respect and the the visual design is quite pretty, even if the developers have some kind of fetish for grime. However, the genius of the Portal games was to me down to the humour. I didnt find either of the cores in the game funny, in fact, the villain, I could barely understand what his distorted voice was saying most of the time. Unfortunately Mels companion wasnt very likeable to me. Next up, the difficulty. Okay, so I have beaten the game now and it's very easy to say like i have seen in many reviews and in many very nasty replies to negative reviews, things along the lines of "puzzle games are supposed to be difficult, it isnt the devs fault you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥". Unfortunately I'm not that guy. The game starts off difficulty wise in line with the end of portal 2, and steadily gets even harder every test chamber you pass. I may have bet the game, unnassisted, but it was very stressful. Sometimes I would boot up the game, spend half an hour in the same area making no progress, utterly confused and simply quit again. The music also is more prominent in this game than portal 2, often annoying and difficult to focus through sometimes. So in conclusion, its a gorgeous game thats 100% portal feel, but I would only recommend to the hardcore Portal fan. Theres no humour or likeable characters to motivate you, just an onslaught of unreasonably difficult levels. If the dev team ever read this, I'd suggest focussing more on humour and banter with the cores and also to tone down the difficulty. I expect a challenge, not to want to tear my hair out and be too stressed to even appreciate the feeling when i do succeed at a puzzle.
It's challenging, sometimes as beautiful as original Portal games, sometimes a little bit creepy aaaand it's free. So why not?
If you want a challenge, try this FREE mod.

Phenomenal! This mod features excellent storytelling that fits right in to the Aperture universe. Combined with a relatable character, plot twists, music by Harry101uk, and excellent level design, this story picks up much of the backstory that takes place immediately before the events of Portal 2.
The level design is much more like Portal 1 as the puzzles are more challenging and don't hold your hand. This makes solving them extremely rewarding. Expect to pump your fist in the air in victory after the hardest levels.
There are tons of easter eggs and fun achievements along the way, some of which you may pick up on your first playthrough.
After escaping through the various test tracks, once the story really picks up, the challenge of the levels goes down and this is replaced by epic facility areas, plot changes, and beautiful scenery.
Plus, with arguably the best ending of any of the portal games, this story is definitly worth experiencing. Give it a try.
Personal Playthrough Time: 10hrs

I would give it a mixed review if I could, but seeing how you can only give give games positive or negative reviews, I'm giving it a negative. I'm not saying it's a bad game, just that it's not a very good game ether.
The way I'd use to describe a lot of the puzzles is that they're a bit like programmer humor. Great for when you're part of the target audience, which in this case is other Portal mod community members, but they don't quite make sense for everyone else. A number of the levels require you to do things that in Valve's own puzzles would be trying to glitch things. If you ask me, the game really could have used extensive playtesting with people outside of the mod scene as it seems that the game hasn't really been playtested almost at all outside of the mod scene. The difficulty level was also all over the place with the first hard puzzles coming early and the rest of the game consisting of hard puzzles broken up by medium difficulty puzzles.
In some places after you enter the modern part of Apeture Sciences with configurable walls instead of test spheres it becomes a bit unclear in a couple of places if you're supposed to finish the puzzle or escape it. On the level with a single room split by a physical wall and one that removes your portals and destroys the cube if you pass trough it I spent a good 20+ minutes trying to escape the level trough the missing rear wall as I thought you were supposed to do that.
Another thing that bothered me was the voice messages that were supposed to have been done by the real Cave Johnson. While getting J.K Simmons was definitely outside of the scope of the developers' abilities, the person they did use was simply a wrong choice and completely broke the immersion in the otherwise very well constructed initial areas. Also, while it wasn't as big of an immersion breaker, why would a personality sphere built by an American company speak with a Norwegian accent? Wheatley speaking with a British accent was still understandible as it's still a native accent, but a non-native accent? It quite frankly doesn't really make sense.
The game still had a number of great puzzles, but they were contrasted by a number of ones that were just frustrating and most probably a lot more fun to design than to actually play trough. However for a mod this game had some pretty incredible amount of effort put into it. Specially the areas that weren't puzzles were pretty much amazing and despite the only voicework that actully worked was AEGIS, a lot of effort was definitely put into it.

I'm playing the Exile mod; if you played ARMA 2 DayZ mod, it's pretty much the same thing but better, and my review will based on this mod and my experience with it so far. I LOVE this game, it's so much fun getting a group of buds together to accomplish personal tasks and goals.
*WARNING* This is not Call of Duty so take a hike if that's what you want. This is a very realistic military shooter. You have to account for every thing you can think of. You must maintain your hungery and thirst. Running will affect your weapon sway once you take aim. The more injured you are the more your aim will be affected as well. Vehicles handle realisticly and even require you to fill up on gas from time to time. There's bullet drop and each weapon has it's own unquie feel and velocity. Scopes need to be zeroed in inorder to have the most accurate shot. All of this combined creates the most INTENSE gameplay I have ever experienced. Wether you are in a intense fire fight, taking a shot on an unsuspecting enemy or getting shot on unsuspectingly yourself, my addrenaline kicks in and it's always fight or flight. Like I said, this isn't call of duty, if you run and gun you will die.
This game is great with friends. It's great going solo. It's a great experience overall and I guarantee you it's worth a buy, IF everything I said so far sounds good to you.

Review: Saints Row: The Third
Saints Row: The Third is an action game where the Saints try to defeat a new gang, the syndicate. This isn't just a linear game, it offers an open world experience for those who love open worlds.
Customize your character, get guns, ride aweome vehicles, ambush with awesome weapons, what more could you want? Not just the customizations are cool. It offers an amazing open world which will introduce you to the world of saints! Multiple different places to go, and a lot of fighting alongside it! The missions are really awesome, as you can team up with other saints as well!
Multiple different designs to look at, where the designs never stop. Some of these items include things like blood motorcycles, TF2 gear, and a whole lot more. The optimistic graphics aren't joking around, as they are really cool.
Considering that you can fiddle around with your world and other things, you'll probably have hours of fun playing Saints Row: The Third. If you want to crash land a car, beat up criminals with your bare-hands, and kill everybody, then this is your ideal game.
Gameplay: 10/10
Design: 10/10
Fun Factor: 9/10
Saints Row: The Third is a successful continuation of the other 2 games, as there is lots of things to do and not miss out on. Play this game, as it is a lot of fun.

Portal Stories: Mel is amazing. As a huge fan of Portal 2, this 15+ hour mod was an absolute treat. It oozes quality and refinement from the start and, if anything, only gets better as you delve deeper into its surprisingly developed story and unique take on the Aperture research facility.
The chambers and other more open areas of the facility are expertly designed and constructed. The use of lighting is masterful and some of the compositions are truly beautiful. As an occasional map designer myself, I’m in awe of what these guys have achieved and feel inspired to fire up Hammer again and have another go.
Some of the puzzles are
. Maybe I'm just rusty from not playing Portal for a while (or maybe I'm just stupid) but one or two of them took me literally hours to solve. From my point of view, this isn't a bad thing. I love to be challenged and that these puzzles force me to really
about how to reach the solution is fantastic. I didn't feel that any were unfair, either. All had perfectly reasonable and logical solutions and none were actually overly-complex. The difficulty came instead from original and unexpected uses of the various testing equipment.
I'm impressed there's a complete original soundtrack but, whilst the music is for the most part pretty good, my main complaint is regarding it. Portal 2 has a fantastic atmosphere and those moments when you're alone in an enormous test chamber, surrounded by the mysterious and unsettling creaks, groans, whirrs and bangs of the facility are some of my very favourites. Unfortunately, in PS:M, the music loops
, quickly becoming irritating and completely breaking that incredible ambience. I feel that a more restrained use of music would have benefitted the game hugely. That said, I soon muted the soundtrack and the original mood was immediately restored, so it's certainly not a deal breaker.
Another minor nit-pick is that, without going into too much detail, the finale ended up being more frustrating than fun due to having to manoeuvre around much too tight spaces and frequently getting objects stuck on the scenery.
None of that really matters, though, because I really do love PS:M and I’m so grateful to Prism Studios for creating and sharing it with us. It’s an amazing achievement and the amount of painstaking work that’s gone into every last nook and cranny of each facet of the mod is as evident as it is astonishing. If you liked Portal 2, play Portal Stories: Mel
!

The guys who made this game did a fine job, but it was just too hard - not in the good way.
This game isn't bad; it's just frustrating. It's no secret that there is a fine line between "challenging" and "frustrating," and the people who developed this game seemed to ignore that. In the walkthrough posted by the developers, even one of those who made this game admitted to being agitated from time to time, and I felt my patience with the puzzles slip away far faster than I think it should have.
The puzzle solutions are simply too specific; there's not enough information to hint at what you have to do (as opposed to what you SHOULD do; I felt like all of the solutions required you to use techniques similar to speedrunners of the original Portal games). I didn't feel accomplished after solving puzzles - I felt overwhelmed when another one was placed before me immediately afterwards. If there was maybe a break in between puzzles, that would have been fine. There were always two or three really big tasks placed before you (one right after another) in a single chamber, and I think it would have done well to split them up into their own chambers. Just put an elevator in between the big solutions and it would have been fine.

First of all I'd like to say, "THIS IS NOT A BAD GAME, AND I AM NOT A PUBG BANDWAGONER"
I bought this game during the summer sale, so I only paid 10$ for it. I was really interested into the battle royale genre. The way it runs is fine, but it is just to basic. I do agree that this game is very arcade-y, but that's my problem since I don't like it. The real reasons I don't like it are:
1.) There are only 4 main weapons. a shotgun, an AK, an AR-15 and an SMG (pretty much an mp7, oh and there's a rarely occuring sniper rifle.). This makes the game feel boring when I pretty much have no advantage over another not based on skill (If a skill based shooter is what you're looking for, try CS:GO or Seige), but on weapons because I will almost have the same gun as them.
2.) Customization is not available, as far as I know. I can only get Iron Sights, no scopes or laser sights. This makes it so the only person with a range advantage the one who finds the supply drop and gets a sniper. You can find this in Last Man Standing for free.
3.) Parachuting options are limited. I can only parachute from one point on the map, and can't freefall. This makes it all up to luck wether I spawn in at a general area that i can land in fields or a city. If I find a very good place to land directly below me the longest trip anyone will have.
So if you have like 10$ to spare, buy it on♥♥♥♥♥ or just get an alternative like LMS or Fortnite. Or if you have a good computer, just pay the extra 20-30$ for pubg.

I was playing a normal king of the hill type game with my friend. He and I wanted to be Gods. The only way to become Gods? We bought ourselves matching LSD-skin go carts. What fun! We could roll around and kill whoever, whenever.
We started them up. Ah! The roar of our engines. Such love it seemed. Off we went, down a dirt road to Marina. Hitting speeds of only around 50 mph, we thought nothing could go wrong. We were deceived...
He was in the map, blocking his field of vision. I decided to nudge his rear bumper with mine. It was harmless, a simple friendly nudge. Nothing would surely happen from this I thought. Mine exploded leaving me wounded on the side of the road. I was sure he was dead since his flew into the air about 200 feet and landed in the woods next to me. This was it. But no, over the mic I heard him say "Wtf I'm alive!?" I was overjoyed. I would no longer have to lose all my gear! He came to revive me only to get within a 5 meter radius from my fiery go cart, and there he die. He had apparently gotten to close to my LSD cart. There we lay on that tiny dirt road leading to Marina, not mad, but hysterically laughing. We could not harness the powers of the LSD go carts. We would never become Gods...
Together we died. I never saw him again, and it was then that I realized: "We only realize how much someone means to us when they are no longer with us."
Live long my friend. Eventually I will find you, and we will once again be united.

[Overview]
So you've killed a murderous supercomputer, got saved by a loveable idiot, had that loveable idiot betray you, escaped Old Aperture, saved the murderous supercomputer you killed before, and let the loveable idiot fly off into space. And yet is that enough for you? Probably not.
I, myself, wanted more Portal. When I saw the trailer for this game, I was highly intrigued. And after around 3 days of downloading on my crap internet speed, I finally managed to get to play it. So...
How was it? Let's find out.
[Gameplay]
Let me be honest here: Some of what you do in the test chambers are insanely clever. Things you've never even thought about doing get introduced here. That's a good thing, right? Well... for most of the time, no. There's absolutely NO hand holding or easing into the difficulty here. It's like once you get to the actual tests, you run face first into a giant cliff. Each test took at least 45 minutes for me to solve. Most of that time was spent just wandering around and looking everywhere to see what all I could do.
It's like the designers of this game have no concept of level progression. It feels as if each chamber introduces 2 new ways to solve them that you never were able to practice at all or were even explicitly shown. Take a look at the start of Portal 1 and Portal 2. All there is is a box, a button, and a door. Put box on button to open door up. See? The designers of this game never even thought of doing as simple as that test.
Admittedly, there were a FEW, I repeat, a FEW parts where they did that. Specifically, some parts behind the scenes. One where you had to put a fire out with water and one where turrets were shooting at cardboard cutouts.
But most of the time it was too much too fast. When playing through the game, it's almost as if the only people to playtest the game were the people who designed the levels to make sure they actually worked... like they didn't ever consider that anyone else would play this game. As I got further and further into the game, I got more and more frustrated. And the last test chambers, I had to quicksave every three seconds or have to go through another 3 minutes of tedium in order to get back where I was before. I finally had to resort to a walkthrough to know wtf to do. Still, though, I have to give props to the chamber you had to solve thrice. That was the only fun test chamber in the last parts of the game.
[Story]
The story... can leave some stuff to be desired if examined closely. When I first played this game, I wondered exactly how Mel got her long fall boots. I was left wondering if it was a plot hole or something or if some creepy scientists put them on her while she was sleeping. It turns out that you can only see them in a cutscene for less than a split second if you pause a video at the right time. And yes, a lead level designer HAS confirmed this.
Even moreso, things don't really ever get explained. Think of some of things from someone who was ripped out of 1952 to whatever time period Portal 2 is: What is Wi Fi? How do I use this Portal Gun? What is Repulsion and Propulsion Gel? What is an Emancipation Grid? What happened in between 1952 and now? Sure, the player knows, but Mel seels to just be caught in a never-ending sandtrap of things being introduced to her and nothing ever really being explained to her.
Other than that... the story really isn't the focus of the mod and nothing really significant happens until you A: Meet Virgil in the flesh and B: The final showdown & ending. It just feels like a game of cat and mouse... like it's more Slice of Life-ish than Portal 2. Yes, Mel and Virgil were accomplishing a lot and progressing a lot, but nothing really ever seemed to change the story in a significant way. Excuse Plot? Meet Expert Challenge Maps.
[Writing]
When first traveling through Aperture Science Innovators, you're greeted to Cave Johnson. However, his personality seems a little... off. It's like they focus more on the "Bad Boss" than the "Amoral Mad Scientist" parts of his personality. He makes frequent references to firing people during the opening tram ride and descent to the relaxation vault. However, there's vitrified doors which let his mad scientist parts of his personality shine and shine very well.
The humor is just as off-color and absurd as in Portal 1 & 2, though, and there are hints of Wheatley that pop up rarely in Virgil. Most of the time, he just seems exasperated at all the crap he has to go through to get Mel to safety, reacting in a somewhat over-the-top and comical way. He's more competent and intelligent than Wheatley, but competence and intelligence only goes so far. Like when someone can't even open a locked door. Or seems to be afraid of light. Or was about to go into an elevator that would likely lead to her death.
Virgil is still a wonderful character with a lot of depth. Plus I'd say he's my favorite core now. AEGIS is... AEGIS. Yeah, he seems a little flat, but that's only because he's a limited AI that didn't seem like he had a personality. Only logic. Even though she never talks throughout the game, Mel is ALSO given hints of a personality through what Virgil says.
[Music & Sounds]
The music throughout the game is just a delight. I can listen to it for hours on hours on end and never get tired of it at all. Every single track seems to fit the current situation and keep that electronic edge. However, as I progressed more and more of the game, I payed attention to less and less of the music. Only through GCFscape was I truly able to focus on the music and everything seemed fantastic. My three favorite tracks are Garden Destroyed, Past Power, and Faith Plate.
The voice acting? Eh... It's okay for the most Part. Cave Johnson has a deeper voice than the Cave Johnson in Portal 2, plus he pauses and breathes in deeply a little too much. Also, at first, I thought Virgil was Cave Johnson and didn't notice the accent change until the voice itself changed. Only on a second playthrough did I notice, which renders my first impression that Cave Johnson wouldn't really be trying to reassure you in such a painfuilly pitiful attempt as Virgil does.
Also there is a jumpscare in the game. Just putting that out there for everyone to see. Not that I hate jump scares. Other people might. However, I'm going to be an evil ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and not tell you WHEN that jumpscare happens. I, myself, laughed like a maniac after the jump scare. It was awesome. Please keep it in.
[Art]
Not much to say about the art style. Just uses standard ones from Portal 2: Old Aperture, Clean, Destroyed, and a few Wheatley-esque ones where you can see the behind the scenes stuff. However... the intro... Man, I think I spent way too long just gazing over the wood-built Old Aperture. There's so much detail put into the game. The few Ratman dens were appropriately Ratman Dens, and one of them even had a new drawing that was flawless.
[Final rating]
Gameplay: 3/10
Story: 4/10
Writing: 8/10
Music & Sounds: 10/10
Art: 8/10
OVERALL: 5/10

Holy crap this is insanely hard.
Did you think Portal 1 and 2 + coop were too easy? No? Well, sucks for you. Because, somehow, this is harder than all of them. Combined. Including the challenge chambers.
But seriously, this is one of the greatest things I've seen in a long time. The voice acting still does get a tiny bit cringe-y at times and there's still noticeable differences between the quality of this and *Valve* quality, such as how obvious some of the cues built in to guide the player are or how some of the puzzles will break physics and force you to not land in a portal you were jumping into because that would break the intended solution, but the fact that I'm able to sit down and nit pick these problems is itself a testement to how amazingly well done this mod is. Seriously, it's free, and it's good. It's definitely worth your time.
...Unless you're impatient and stuck-up and expect the hand-holding that Valve provided through most of their games. Because you won't get it. Briefly scroll through the negative reviews and it's literally the exact same thing over and over again - it's too hard. Some of the reviewers took the effort to dress it up and make it seem like this is a game-breaking thing. It's not. It's intentional. Valve made the intentional decision that, since they were making a game for the masses, hand-holding was necessary. These devs made the intentional decision that, since they were making a game for Portal fans, hand-holding was less necessary. If you're noclipping through the levels and complaining that that's what killed your enjoyment of the game, then that's your problem. If you're that type of guy, just go watch Harry101UK (one of the devs) play through this on his channel and be done. You're not going to enjoy this experience. For the rest of us - those of us who don't rage quit if we don't immediately have a giant spotlight pointed at the solution within 30 seconds, those of us who play puzzle games because we actually like being challenged by puzzles, those of us who aren't going to blame the devs of a puzzle game for not clearly explaining the solution to the puzzles in the game to you - this is one of the best things that'll ever come out of the vibrant, talented, gifted, devoted Portal community.

Alright, to start this review i've got to say- this is going to be a little bit biased, from the fact that well I have been playing this game since I was about 11-12 years old-ish.
To start lets talk about the gameplay: Its brilliant, you can spend thousands of hours playing this game and you would still learn something new, or expand on your exsisting skills. Mixing this with a movement system that rewards advanced movement with a high skill ceiling such as rocket jumping and you have a game that you can spend hundreds of hours learning just how to move!
However, there are always negatives- and there are a few issues. The big issues come from (in my opinion) the servers, too many cosmetics and ironically the skill ceiling. Starting off with the severs- its really random if you get something that detects your hits near perfectly or a server that just feels... wrong to play in. This can lead to fustrating incidents, when you know that you hit somebody or that you see that you hit somebody and it doesn't register! Although you can argue this is what community servers are for!
For cosmetics, the big issue comes from a few of them. The fact that cosmetics make Valve the most amount of money, makes it so that it's logical that they put so many in. However,does it have to be at the expense of the original artstyle ? I  know that people have harped on about it, but it needs to be said... a bannana hat really Valve,really?
And for the skill ceiling, its simple it does take too long to really 'gid gud' at the game. I mean im not twelve anymore, I have time but that comes from my management of time and how I work. You can still enjoy the game, but unless you have time- don't be surpised if you get 'destroyed' by people that have played far longer then you!
All in all, its an enjoyable game even if it has some issues and i hope you find this useful.

Before I get down to the nitty gritty of this game, let me pop open a Saint's Flow and get ready to give you guys the 4-11 on this game.  First off, before I even start the review, I want to make it clear that I am not a GTA fan.  GASP!  OMG!  WTH! How can I not like the game that millions of people like?  Well, I just don't dig how serious it is.  The game is good and I can see why people like it.  Now for those still reading after I alienated about half of the gaming population, on to my review of Saints Row: The Third.
The Good:
This game is funny.  If you like childish humor about body parts and you enjoy sexual innuendo, this game delivers and then some.  The gun play is not bad, not the greatest but it suffices.  The options to choose whether you are a male or female and all of the cloths and such you can get is pretty tight.  The game plays well when you are shooting and stealing cars.  By the time you are at RESPECT level 50, you are invincible so that is fun to just blow stuff up.  The voice acting is not bad, not the best by all means but it is all good.  The soundtrack is varied from heavy metal tracks, to rock, to rap, and even classical.  The controls work well with an X-BOX ONE controller.
The Bad:
Don't, I mean really don't, play this game after you play Saints Row IV.  You will not dig not having super powers.  Now that this is out of the way.  I am going to assume you are doing the games in order so I will focus on the bad just in this game.  One bad thing, the activities are kind of sucky....well, Heli Assault and Fraud for me were just blah.  The gun play is average at best but works.  The voice acting, well, some of them are just downright weird or off the wall even to this games standards.  If you don't like perverted jokes a twelve year old would tell, I wouldn't recommend this game either.
All in all, the game is a blast if you know what you are getting into.  If you swear that GTA is the best thing since sliced bread, you may not like this game.  However, if you are willing to take a well done, perverted, off the top GTA clone that does not take itself seriously, there is a lot of fun to be had.

Overall, it was fantastic. There were a few parts that if I had not watched a walkthrough, I would have been stuck for days. Often, when I went to alt-tab out it would crash the game, which is a little annoying. I got used to saving before tabbing out. Some really clever puzzles, though. What would have really made this game better would be more of a story. More of an emotional tie. I would say 4 out of 5 stars.

Holy crap this is insanely hard.
Did you think Portal 1 and 2 + coop were too easy? No? Well, sucks for you. Because, somehow, this is harder than all of them. Combined. Including the challenge chambers.
But seriously, this is one of the greatest things I've seen in a long time. The voice acting still does get a tiny bit cringe-y at times and there's still noticeable differences between the quality of this and *Valve* quality, such as how obvious some of the cues built in to guide the player are or how some of the puzzles will break physics and force you to not land in a portal you were jumping into because that would break the intended solution, but the fact that I'm able to sit down and nit pick these problems is itself a testement to how amazingly well done this mod is. Seriously, it's free, and it's good. It's definitely worth your time.
...Unless you're impatient and stuck-up and expect the hand-holding that Valve provided through most of their games. Because you won't get it. Briefly scroll through the negative reviews and it's literally the exact same thing over and over again - it's too hard. Some of the reviewers took the effort to dress it up and make it seem like this is a game-breaking thing. It's not. It's intentional. Valve made the intentional decision that, since they were making a game for the masses, hand-holding was necessary. These devs made the intentional decision that, since they were making a game for Portal fans, hand-holding was less necessary. If you're noclipping through the levels and complaining that that's what killed your enjoyment of the game, then that's your problem. If you're that type of guy, just go watch Harry101UK (one of the devs) play through this on his channel and be done. You're not going to enjoy this experience. For the rest of us - those of us who don't rage quit if we don't immediately have a giant spotlight pointed at the solution within 30 seconds, those of us who play puzzle games because we actually like being challenged by puzzles, those of us who aren't going to blame the devs of a puzzle game for not clearly explaining the solution to the puzzles in the game to you - this is one of the best things that'll ever come out of the vibrant, talented, gifted, devoted Portal community.

This game right here? This is not something that is meant to be played for fun. After sinking hours into each test chamber, then having to finally go to lookup a walkthrough to find the ONE missing piece that you're givin little to no hints at to finally solve that god forsaken chamber. Whoever made this? Hats off to you, you can make a mind bogglingly difficult test chamber. You also can ruin a perfectly good story by doing exactly that. The sheer annoyingly difficult chambers completely take the fun out of this, as you either figure it out in one fluid go, or you end up stuck for HOURs trying to solve one single puzzle. If the story had been given any sort of focus rather than just making everything obnoxiously hard to solve, this could be a very enjoyable modded story. But as it stands, there's just no enjoyment in getting stuck on puzzles and looking up the next step.
And to anyone reading this and thinking "oh he's just mad cause he can't solve it" I'm really not. I'm mad that that difficulty was the focus. In the standard game of Portal 2, the tests themselves were never the focus. They were well made and gradually grew in challenge as you played further and further, but there were always hints at the next step to make it atleast easier on the player. But the story always remained the focus, rather than difficulty, and a solution to a chamber felt like an achievement. In this mod, it feels more like a chore, and a solution is just a sigh of "well we finally got it done... now to the hell of the next one."
Throughout the first half of what I played, having reached as far as the run down old test chambers, the game ws enjoyable. Their was a bit of a challenge in figuring out where to go, due to it not often being made really clear and mostly relying on you to seek out the next door, but it was fun and the story kept me engaged. As it pushed on into the goo using chambers, things started getting a bit annoying in terms of solving. I found myself caught on one room unable to move on, admitedly to my own blindness to see an obvious solution to my dilemma, but that was only the first point of frustration.
As the game rogressed I found myself taking longer and longer to solve each chamber, then area in the old aperature employee areas. At first it was just generally annoying, but as I came to the room with the vault door I found myself stuck for a solid half hour at the bottom of the room. After wandering back and forth on the floor for aa good 20 minutes, I finally accidently sprayed some goo onto the right spot to open up a path to head further up, and slowly progressed from there. But once entering upper aperature? I found every chamber to be a burden as I progressed. The solutions weren't straightforward, they needed countless steps performed in perfect execution to succeed, and if you stumbled anywhere along the way you'd find yourself trapped in a position in which you had to restart from the beginning. And this right here, this is what ruined it.
The sheer amount of redoing the same process again and again trying to find what the correct next step was was utterly grating. I'm not saying that having to find the next piece was annoying, but having to restart the ENTIRE process you'd done so far just to try another idea made it overly time consuming and frustrating. If there'd been more points of reference, more checkpoints in the solutions or clues to what you were to do along the way of those strings of portals in correct places, maybe a panel here or a hinting arrow somewhere, akin to what the Ratman might leave, that would have been a tremendous relief. But as you're left totally alone and in silence after entering a room, with no delightful commentary aong the way it loses any enjoyment fast.
In short, would I reccomend playing this? No, but feel free to look up someone's playthrough on youtube so you can get the story, because the story seemed rather intriguing.

*Minor Spoilers only related to Gameplay and Characters*
Portal Stories: Mel is a miraculous feat for a free mod to an amazing game. It has everything a good game needs. A great story (AEGIS was cool), great graphics (Aperture Town looked great), and tolerable voice-actors (sorry Virgil, you just didn't do it for me). Sounds great right?
But:
There are major cons to this game. Major cons.
You might be wondering why I'm recommending this game then. It's Portal and it's free and plays just like regular Portal. There's no reason you shouldn't play it. In fact, not playing this game would be a shame as it's obvious the devs worked very hard to make this possible for us and I thank them for all their hard work.
But there is still the gameplay to consider.
And wow is it hard.
It probably sounds like a broken record at this point, but it isn't fun hard, like Super Meat Boy. This is the type of hard that'll have you staring at the puzzles and going "What am I looking at?" and then thinking "I don't need a walkthrough I never needed one for the other two games" and then finally "Gah. I give up" as you open up the in-game browser to see what you were supposed to do.
The worst part being: The solutions don't make sense.
Hear me out on this, hear me out. I know its not fair to compare games as every game should be its own experience, but it's almost necessary to compare this to Portal 2 (it is a mod for it).
There is a puzzle in this game, around Chapter 3, that (according to the walkthrough I used, because I would never have thought of this), requires you to cover your cube in orange gel, and then slide it down the hard light bridge. This turns off the red emancipation grills (the ones that kill you) just long enough for you to quickly run through the hallway of red emancipation grills.
I guess this sounds simple in concept (to some people) except I have only ever covered a cube in blue gel because it bounces. I have never covered a cube in orange gel. And maybe the devs did this on purpose, to encourage creativity or whatnot. I think it's just rationalizing for poor planning.
Speaking of poor planning, many puzzles in the game have given up good structure for "difficulty." For example, in the same puzzle in Chapter 3, you have to bounce across a chasm to reach a door with a button next to it. Obviously the devs were thinking "Hmm, smart people play Portal, so with some common sense, they'll take the cube with them before they jump." The thing is, Portal 2 never made that mistake. It had difficult puzzles that always allowed you to retrace your steps. If you jumped across the chasm in this level without the cube, there would be no portable surfaces and you would have to kill yourself in order to retrace your steps.
Sadly, this extremely difficult and torturing gameplay breaks the pacing of the story, which is a good one. I might spend 15-20 minutes on one puzzle (one of the beginning puzzles, this never happened in Portal or Portal 2), then come out of it with a line or two of dialogue from Virgil that apparently is related to the story but I already forgot because I spent the last 20 minutes trying to figure out how to get that cube to slide down the hard light beam.
Oh, wait.
You had to cover it in gel.
TL;DR
Get this Game! It's free, the story is great, and the graphics are awesome. The lack of coherent gameplay long with wannabe Wheatley voicing the main AI are its ultimate stumbling points, so be prepared!

Amazing mod deserving of all the hype it has been receiving. Its hard to even consider calling this a mod, as it is so professionally done, it feels like a studio blessed expansion showing off the teams hard work.
The bulk of the story takes place between the events of Portal and Portal 2 and introduces a couple new characters to the portal universe for the better. While the story is fairly cut-and-dry, it contains enough of the spirit and humor of Portal 2 to feel like it belongs in the same universe without feeling like an awkward attempt to introduce a new narrative.
The puzzles are both straight-forward and difficult without rehashing puzzle styles from Portal 2, making the player think a little differently. A lot of time can be wasted trying to figure out what seems like a difficult solution, only to have the "aha" moment, and realize it was quite simple.  Outside of the actual puzzles, however, the behind-the-scenes areas can be a little confusing to navigate at times leading to wasted (albeit beautiful) time.
If you haven't played this yet, do it immediately, because you will not regret it.

This is the only game I have played from this series so far, and the impressions I gained from this particular game has compelled me to take a look at a few others.
As playing I found myself likening many features to Grand Theft Auto IV, and Just Cause 2 - containing a similar and expansive city to GTA IV as well as a few other positive similarities, and some of the silliness and craziness of JC2. These combined with it's own unique features, well written, not overly long, and interestingly comedic story have made this a game I have hardly been able to put down over the past 4-5 days. Add to the fact that the game music and radio station music is very good just adds to the overall feeling of the game.
There are some issues however:
Whilst I do have a low-spec computer, I am generally able to get away with playing most games of this age and older with little or no lag issues, however, and points I did find this game to become unresponsive (especially when driving), and sometimes completely freeze for a few seconds.
I also had a little trouble following some of the names of the characters. Being new to the series probably didn't help, and for the start of some missions I was baffled as to who we were helping/fighting, etc.
Overall, I definitely recommend this game, and am probably going to get another ~20 hours out of this. I will probably end up playing through the story at least once more, which is something I do not often do.

I have seen some negative reviews on this game, and they mostly say this:
- Bad FPS in multiplayer
- I don't understand the controls
- A lot of bugs
- I have a high end rig, and it's still bad FPS
- There are DLC add popups in the game
Everyone needs to understand that comparing Arma to CoD or BF is like comparing Windows/Android to Mac/iOS. Windows is made to work with a lot of different software made by a lot of different parties, and therefore sometimes buggy. In the same way, Arma is made with modders in mind. Whenever you join a server, it is a 98% likelyhood that the server is running on mods. In some of these, the FPS can be sub par, I'll admit. However, that is because you are playing with software (mods) that is made by players as yourself, and they are doing this for free. Time spent on optimizations are therefore not always enough to give you high FPS. And remember, ALL mods are free. If you join a server without mods, the FPS is at 70-90 compared to 25-45 at heavily modded servers. Don't get me wrong though, a lot ot modders have done a great job with optimizations to get modded servers up to 90+ FPS.
As for the controls, yes there are a lot of them. Why? Because this game is at heart a foundation for a military simulator. If you only had BF/CoD controls at hand, 70% of the functions in the game would have been gone. Learning the controls is tricky, but also very rewarding.
The last thing I wonna say is that Bohemia Interactive is the most community friendly game developer I know of. They listen to the community, they give credit to modders, and their way of implementing DLCs should be the standard of the industry. A lot of negative reviews complain about adds in the game. That is because when Bohemia releases a DLC, it usually conains a lot of functions for free (Shooting from vehicles, better projectile trajectories etc). What you actually pay for is the new weapons and vehicles in each DLC. They are somewhat abundant as there is thousands of weapons and vehicles made by modders, so paying for the DLC is more about contributing to Bohemia rather than buying new weapons. And let me say, the adds only pops up when you use DLC weapons and vehicles in-game if you haven't purchased the DLC yet. Which means that there is no upbreaking of the community because of DLCs.
If you like the BF and CoD franchises, wonderful, I do too. If you wan't something a bit less arcade, try Arma. It's a beautiful game, and you really get hundreds of games in one.
You like zombie survival? Buy Arma, it's got it.
You like survival without zombies? Buy Arma, it's got it.
You like teambased infantry? Buy Arma, it's got it.

Maybe I'm stupid, not that good of a Portal player I thought I was, or right and this mod does have pitfalls.
Chapter one was the exact same trainride as Half-Life, only shorter and more static than it should be. I believe the intention was to show that Aperture was alive and working but, when you go down in the mines, you encounter absolutely no other NPC. This makes the business actually more empty than intended. Now a bit of nitpicking: Why would they use cars in the underground facility? It makes very little sense to use those as a mean of travel.
Then we have to talk about the puzzles in the game. They are clearly in the same league as the chambers in Portal: Prelude when you speak of difficulty. But the latter had an extra game mechanic that showed a bit of originality. In Portal Stories: Mel you didn't have a clue what exactly you were doing most of the time. Little indication of where the exit was and what the box was for that they gave you. Fair to say, looking back, the puzzles where more logical than skill. Yet the logic that you had to apply wasn't introduced in any way, leaving you dazed about what to do.
One chamber I did find satisfying was one of the final ones. It was difficult but not too difficult. If all were like that this review would be a lot more positive.
Now the BTS scenes weren't really that interesting. More then once I hadn't had an inkling about where to go; I just circled around the room until I found that one wall where you could place a portal on.
I do have to say that the levels look nice, and I see nothing wrong with the chambers. But maybe a bit too many levers to pull in the game. Eventually it gets boring when you have to walk to point C to get to point B.
Okay so lets talk story, which of course have spoilers so skip this bit if you haven't played. This mod was practically Portal 2 but shorter. Everything you did in the main game had found it's way into this mod. Vigil was Wheatly, telling about the decay of Aperture and telling Mel that everything was okay. At one point he tried to 'hack' his way into a computer which was the same as with Wheatly, only less funny because it has been done before. Also, Wi-Fi? Really? You want me to believe that old Apterture has access to Wi-Fi?
Cave Johnson humor was really, really overused. I don't think he would talk to just one test subject all the way from metro to relaxation vault (They had those in '52?). Unless she had one of those things they use in museums I say no.
One level was in complete darkness and the core had to turn on his flashlight, which was actually a fun part in the game.
The boss battle was a huge letdown for being, well, the final thing you do in the game. Like in Portal 2 you first had to shut down some acces for AEGIS and tamper with the turret line. Vigil told me to run across the targeting range but there was next to no danger for some reason and again it was searching for a portable wall in the distance. When you finally did get to AEGIS he eventually shuts down oxygen and starts a timer. Unlike the ending of both Portal and Portal 2, I felt no rush of actually completing it before the timer ends. I think that this was mainly because of the thing you actually had to do. If it where a bit more action pact the feeling that time was running out.
This mod shows potential and if they still plan on doing two more (If I remember correctly it would be a tiology) then they should focus a bit more on the actual level design. Don't assume someone will know how to use object x the way you think, but introduce the logic first, then make more puzzles out of that. I think it will help a lot.
Sadly because of the illogical placement of puzzles (Mel wouldn't be able to do that now would she?), the difficulty, and the lack of 'flow' I have to say no. Don't play this if you want a satisfying experience for puzzles, unless you actually want to be challenged to be at your wits' end, then be my guest.

Chapter one was the exact same trainride as Half-Life, only shorter and more static than it should be. I believe the intention was to show that Aperture was alive and working but, when you go down in the mines, you encounter absolutely no other NPC. This makes the business actually more empty than intended. Now a bit of nitpicking: Why would they use cars in the underground facility? It makes very little sense to use those as a mean of travel.
Then we have to talk about the puzzles in the game. They are clearly in the same league as the chambers in Portal: Prelude when you speak of difficulty. But the latter had an extra game mechanic that showed a bit of originality. In Portal Stories: Mel you didn't have a clue what exactly you were doing most of the time. Little indication of where the exit was and what the box was for that they gave you. Fair to say, looking back, the puzzles where more logical than skill. Yet the logic that you had to apply wasn't introduced in any way, leaving you dazed about what to do.
One chamber I did find satisfying was one of the final ones. It was difficult but not too difficult. If all were like that this review would be a lot more positive.
Now the BTS scenes weren't really that interesting. More then once I hadn't had an inkling about where to go; I just circled around the room until I found that one wall where you could place a portal on.
I do have to say that the levels look nice, and I see nothing wrong with the chambers. But maybe a bit too many levers to pull in the game. Eventually it gets boring when you have to walk to point C to get to point B.
Okay so lets talk story, which of course have spoilers so skip this bit if you haven't played. This mod was practically Portal 2 but shorter. Everything you did in the main game had found it's way into this mod. Vigil was Wheatly, telling about the decay of Aperture and telling Mel that everything was okay. At one point he tried to 'hack' his way into a computer which was the same as with Wheatly, only less funny because it has been done before. Also, Wi-Fi? Really? You want me to believe that old Apterture has access to Wi-Fi?
Cave Johnson humor was really, really overused. I don't think he would talk to just one test subject all the way from metro to relaxation vault (They had those in '52?). Unless she had one of those things they use in museums I say no.
One level was in complete darkness and the core had to turn on his flashlight, which was actually a fun part in the game.
The boss battle was a huge letdown for being, well, the final thing you do in the game. Like in Portal 2 you first had to shut down some acces for AEGIS and tamper with the turret line. Vigil told me to run across the targeting range but there was next to no danger for some reason and again it was searching for a portable wall in the distance. When you finally did get to AEGIS he eventually shuts down oxygen and starts a timer. Unlike the ending of both Portal and Portal 2, I felt no rush of actually completing it before the timer ends. I think that this was mainly because of the thing you actually had to do. If it where a bit more action pact the feeling that time was running out.
This mod shows potential and if they still plan on doing two more (If I remember correctly it would be a tiology) then they should focus a bit more on the actual level design. Don't assume someone will know how to use object x the way you think, but introduce the logic first, then make more puzzles out of that. I think it will help a lot.
Sadly because of the illogical placement of puzzles (Mel wouldn't be able to do that now would she?), the difficulty, and the lack of 'flow' I have to say no. Don't play this if you want a satisfying experience for puzzles, unless you actually want to be challenged to be at your wits' end, then be my guest.
