One of the sparkling gems to come out of fan works to the point where if I hadn't know it was a fan work I would have assumed it was a 'real' published game.
The story is cohesive and builds atmosphere, written in such a way that it can fit happily into portal continuity without changing anything.
The only bad thing I could possibly say about this game is the voice acting but it grew on me and by the end I had accepted even that on the strenght of everything else.
The level design is beautiful, atmospheric and robustly tested. Each test chabmer was a real challenge but I never felt that any part of it was lacking. Only once did I use a missing wall pannel to try to clamber up to complete a puzzle.
I'm pretty sure it's impossible to get stuck at any point during the game, I did try to get myself stuck in a few levels but I was always able to reset the puzzle without resorting to death.
The puzzles themselves where fairly hard. I stubbornly refused to use a guide and had to quit the game, go do something else, and come back with fresh eyes to complete a lot of the puzzles. I fully enjoyed doing it this way, with the added achievement of having figured out everything by myself.
The game uses all the set pieces and features of p 2 in some very interesting ways, particularly heavy use of the AS-MEG inside levels that you have to get boxes or yourself through without loosing portal placements but this worked really well to increase the difficulty over portal 2 itself. Its' almost impossible to blunder through levels like it was at certain points of P2, as you have to use each part of the puzzle in the right sequence to complete the whole. I'd often have to take my hands off the controlls and just stare at a test chamber for a few minutes to figure out how various parts worked, and how they could be made to work.
It took me a total of about 10 hours playtime to complete over the course of about a week. In a few months time when I've forgotten the puzzle solutions I will deffinatly be coming back to this game to play it again. Probably inbetween p1 and p2.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

So, this review will be in the style of "The good, The bad, The ugly." I am doing this review after a playthrough of the series. My progress through this game was a full story completion although I never bother to finish all the activities or collectables.
- The Good
1. Kept the story interesting by introducing a plethora of new characters, with their own backstory and problems.
2. Graphics are a clear upgrade from SR2.
3. Some of the activities are new to the series, keeping the world alive in its own segment at a time.
- The Bad
1. Most activities are extremly tedious and boring, and occasionally required for story progression, a lazy way to bulk out the game.
2. From SR2, to SR3, there was a huge portion of character development that was just skipped over, making some of the previous characters unrecognizeable to their SR2 counterparts.
3. The choices the game gives you have absolutely no impact through the story progression.
- The Ugly
1. The story lost alot of the edge that it had in SR2.
Overall, this game by itself if you're new to the series altoger, and just jumped in at SR3, I would put it at an 8/10, although comparing it to the series as a whole, it is the weakest link, and I would put it at a 6/10. If you like open world shooter shenanigans, this game is probably for you.

Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

So basically, if you're a Portal fan, I wouldn't get your hopes up. The mod looks great, but it just feels like a copy of Portal 2, except much harder.

ARMA 3 has done many things well, the combat system, movement, veichal atriculation, etc. ARMA 3 has also confused many who played it with the learning curve that every game in the series seems to have. In the wake of all these things however the game is created by a company who has a reputation for quality rather than quantity. While the game still has some bugs after the 4th year of its life, they are often either minor, funny as hell [tanks flipping when ramming trucks],or frustrating as hell. While I do Say this game is amazing it's learning curve turns many people who dont have the time or intrest to learn the game. Not many games have an edito or at least from my experience however ARMA 3 has done a funominal job with it's Eden Editor, which features all the maps [vanila and mod], NPCS, veichals, buildings, etc.. which are featured in the game and its dlc and mods. About 6 mounths ago or so the very hyped Apex expansion was realeased, I have never seen so many new players in a server on a game or expansion's release in my life. The game also features many sides, BlUFOR, OPFOR , Independent, and civilian, within these sides there are various factions such as NOTO, CSAT, AAF, FIA, Syndakit, civilian, and some others I think [And for those ARMA 2 fans pretty much all the ARMA 2 factions, maps, and veichals are avalible in the CUP mods]. When I first bought the game in 2014 I believe I thought I would never get good at it, however the game really grows on people after the first couple of hours. The modibility for this game is on Gmod levels of variety, anything from aditional uniforms and guns to player made missions which range from horrible, french, and amazing. Bohemia Interactive has even made a mod or two, one of which includes the P90 and it's varients, so i'd say that Bohemia is in touch with the community. A month ago an update rendered it nearly impossible for players to get into the game for a couple of days, and when the comunity revealed this on the fourms they fixed it almost imediatly, and thats more than most companies would do. Overall ARMA 3 and its DLC are worth every penny of its price, and for an experienced player like me, I would play this rather than its predacessors any day of the week.

Okay, first off, fantastic mod. Really, the story was great, the voice acting was done up well, and the test chambers... Well, they reminded me why I love Portal so much. They really made you think a lot, and it's been a while since I've gone in and had to question a chamber so extently. One of the reasons I haven't played much considering the PeTI (Perpetual Testing Initiative) maps that have plagued the Workshop. Anyway, I'm not going to open that can of beans again, so I'll continue typing.
Honestly, the mod was excellent. It doesn't even deserve to be called a mod at this point, so let me rephrase: This game was fantastic, and would be worth it if I had to pay for it. The detail that went into every part of the maps, not just those accessable to the player was fantastic. As a map maker myself, I notice the outside details, as well as what can be seen inside. I'm glad to see I'm not the only one who has a love for using sprites excessively. xD Seriously though, the details of each area is astounding.
I'll admit, when this mod started up and you took the name of the abandoned Co-Op character I was skepticle about how well it'd do, about a year into this mod's production my mind was changed instantly and I started following it on ModDB way back when. I dropped off the map a little after PeTI came out and sadly lost contact with this mod, among a few, that I had been keeping in touch with. I guess what I'm trying to say is, that all this time away from Portal has been wasted by me, and I'm actually going to continue mapping again after all this time. Your mod sparked a fire in me that has been dimmed since Valve abandoned this game and left it to the community to decide it's fate.
That said, the amount of dedication, and effort, and everything in between that went into this game makes me want to see what the community is truly made of. Outside of the stale white tile walls of Aperture, there are so many unique things to be shown here with this being the prime example of how well something can turn out. Maybe I'll even try to make a mod as intense as this one day. xD Although doubtful.
After going through the credits, I recognized a LOT of usernames that came up. I remember talking with a lot of you guys on
, and using assets like Lp's death fizzler.
Thank you for taking your time to make this, and this getting greenlit is by far the best greenlight decision I've seen, even better than that half mod that is Black Mesa. This is what a greenlit mod should be, not an hour of gameplay, or half a mod, but a fully fleshed out experiance for players to enjoy.
I'm glad I got to play it, and thank you for restoring my interest in Portal.
Sincerely,

UPDATE: The developers have payed attention, and have released an update to reduce the obtuse-ness of some puzzles. I don't know the details, but you can probably safely ignore the corrosponding cons in my review.
+Good, portal-themed music
+Good voice acting
+Difficult levels, stressing new ways of thinking with portals
+Interesting story
-Somewhat dissatisfying ending (good, but not as much as I'd have liked)
-Opening and closing cutscenes are fairly long (I didn't mind much, but for some people it might be annoying, especially if you want the whole story)
-Some questionable design choices (levels can be obtuse sometimes, and the objective may be hiding in plain sight.)
---
I experienced a drop in fps at the end, after playing the rest without dropping. It made the final puzzles less fun than they could have been. I have a FX-8350 at 4.6GHz and an R9 290, so with a Portal 2 mod, anything below 60 is a sign of bad level design. I suspect it was an engine limitation, not a hardware limitation, that caused the dips, occasionally below 30.
The music was very good, and while more present than normal portal music, it fit just fine. It, along with the voice acting, was superb, especially for a free mod.
Levels were difficult. I resorted to looking up the solutions a couple of times and I regret it. Usually the solution seems to be something you (I) would not have thought of. Think outside the portal, as it were. Use ALL the tools at your disposal.
Occasionally, the goal of a level / puzzle / area was unclear, which leads to frustration. I want to be able to know where I am supposed to go, so that I may try to get there. Often it is hiding in plain sight. Sometimes it truely is unexpected and unforseeable. I think more BETA testing would have been a good idea. Though, for a free mod, amazing nonetheless.
---
SUMMARY: If you liked Portal 2 but want more, harder puzzles, play it. It's well worth the time, and though it can be difficult, even frustrating, it's never impossible. It is extremely good quality, if you are willing to look over a few minor shortcomings.

Giving this a second chance review....
After finishing the new Story Mode and then retrying the "Advanced Mode", I realize that this game isn't exactly as bad as I was making it out to be, however, there are still some inconveniences that rubbed me the wrong way.   Inconveniences aside, this is a very well-made mod in the Portal community.
This game on Story Mode is a pinch tougher than Portal 2 and Advanced Mode is still expert level Portal 2  (That's not changing from my original review).  Guides seldomly seem needed in Story Mode (Which is a great thing), but after Virgil's tests (where you're in the overgrown map made by the "Two sadist scientists", that's where guides are going to be your best friend for the rest of the chapter)
The final boss isn't exactly rough, but he is harder than GLaDOS from P1 and Wheatley from P2, so he does have that going for him.  Still tame compared to most bosses, but probably the roughest compared to GLaDOS and Wheatley.
PROS:
Wonderful voice acting
Great core animation
Nice ending cutscenes
Brain teasing puzzles
Free (Extention for Portal 2)
Achievements
Wonderful job constructing the entire scenery for the entire mod
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE MORE TAME "STORY MODE"  (Thank you for listening, Devs)
A very clever final chapter with a great final battle scene that actually makes you feel pressured.
CONS:
Original story (which is now Advanced Mode) is still harsh and unforgiving
Somewhat stale sense of humor (I've just gotten used to it that I've become numb to it)
Virgil is quite similar to Wheatley...what sets him apart aside from the ending, his appearance,
and his accent?
Overall, it's not a bad mod and is well-constructed, well-coreographed, and well-designed.  I was hasty in my original review, but after completing this mod (finally), I like what I saw.  If you liked Portal 2, check it out.   If you're a Portal ninja, advanced mode may be up your alley (Don't try it if you're clingy to Youtube Guides)

Ok, let me back up and actually detail what's good before I go on a tirade because there's a lot to say here.
Voice acting is very solid. Only once or twice did I have an issue deciphering words amidst a Norwegian accent. Otherwise it worked well enough. Puzzle design is generally good, there's a decent enough understanding of the mechanics of Portal 2 that means you can never really land yourself in an unwinnable situation. The twist at the end of the game is kind of neat and I like a few of the concepts the game throws around, like a village for test subjects to live in underground, some of the testing procedures for the turrets and cubes. And, the music is fan-flipping-tastic. Literally my favourite part of the game, some really nice pieces to listen to amidst the puzzles.
But speaking of those puzzles, like I said, they're essentially made for those of you who've played Portal custom maps a lot. They get frustrating fast with using the game mechanics in a few ways you probably don't think of the first time round, a few sections where I have flat out no idea how you're supposed to get on your own. Have no shame in using a walkthrough because the stunts this game pulls will make you feel stupid constantly.
The story isn't great. It's just Portal 2 again, human and personality core solve tests to defeat evil AI. That's your meat and potatoes. The villain is flat and uninteresting which is a massive let down considering GLaDOS and Wheatley's repetoire. The side character is also pretty boring. He has one of two funny moments but otherwise, nothing stands out about him. Nothing else in particular happens over the course of the story that's worth going over. In general it just seems kind of underwritten with little charm of humour at all.
I also have a personal issue of the game crashing and closing sometimes whenever I alt tab, might just be me but I dunno. To wrap up, I still reccomend playing the mod. It's a labour of love and passion and that does show in a few choice areas. It's worth the experience when they're charging literally nothing for it at the end of the day.
So I reccommend playing it once. And only once.

Said content is also very high quality, pretty much only the frequent loading screens reveal it's a mod (if you've played custom chambers you know what to expect). Great voice acting coupled with plot progression, not to mention the chambers that are aesthetically pleasing and full of thematic details. The puzzles themselves are in fact mostly harder than those in Portal 1/2, yet using the exact same mechanics introduced in those. I would point out that in contrast to the description, there actually are a couple of execution-heavy puzzles at least compared to the standard in Portal 1/2, but of course logic is still the main element.
In short, this is worth your time. You will encouter rooms mocking your intellect and you will love it. Probably the best puzzle experience on Steam right after the official series.

Portal Stories: Mel ("Mel" as following) is, for sure, a
.
The story line, graphic, voice acting... every part of this game just feels awesome!
Overall graphic is just fantastic. I wouldn't even find out this is a Mod rather than a valve product if I didn't know in advance. But I'm not sure if it's my PC not powerful enough or what, it doesn't run as smooth as Portal 2 on my PC - Most times it runs at full speed (72 FPS in my case) but once in a while I experience a framerate drop by 10-20, not a deal breaker though, maybe the game needs more optimize.
The sound effects, voice acting an CGI movies are just professional! You know it's gonna be promising when you see Harry101UK on the staff (If you haven't, be sure to check his YouTube channel - you won't be disappointed)
However, the levels design are not as good as the original Portal 2 (but also not that bad). Most levels are fine but some of the levels makes you feel lost. The original Portal 2 really did find a perfect balance point between puzzle solving and action(which Mel overdid - not too much, but unnecessary) challenging - as for puzzles, the original Portal series did a great job making player knowing which part of the map is supposed to be used for solving which puzzle, but in Mel there's just too many times you have shoot Portals through a fence - most of the time it just creates chaos.
If you like the original Portal series, you will sure like Mel. The puzzles are hard, some might be frustrating, but when you solve them, you will feel as rewarded as you first played Portal 2.

The art style of TF2 is slowly deteriorating due to the addition of non-canon or unrelated hats like the Potassium Bonnet.
-
The game is so unoptimized that even a high-end PC would still sometimes experience sudden FPS drops.
Like any other community, there will always be the toxic players. There are also item scammers and hackers/cheaters that can ruin the game.
-
The game is old but thanks to it's strong playerbase and very 'supportive' dev team the game could still live for more than a decade. I recommend you play the game with your friends since it's more enjoyable.

I know I have next to 0 Steam playtime, I've owned it on PS3 since release week.
Short review: Damn fun game, absolutely worth the price now, especially on sale.
In depth:
Gameplay - Rock solid, I wouldn't call it revolutionary or anything. There's a good variety of weapons, absurd amount of customization including character, vehicles, and weapons to a limited extend (upgrades, which you can't undo for some reason). More effort went into the combat than the driving, so getting around can be a bit of a chore. Cars handle very arcade-like, most of them feel the same honestly.
Gunplay works, but like I said, nothing revolutionary. The biggest problem is the lack of challenge. Enemies are dumb. Even on harcore, most players will mow them down with ease since they tend to stand still or occasionally side step. The lack of challenge is one of the biggest problems the game has, though that may be more a matter of personal opinion.
Visuals - Meh. Objectively, the game looks fine. The lighting is decent, character models and faces are vastly improved from the last Saint's Row, with a subtle art style as opposed to realism. The setting however is a huge step down from the last game. Dull and boring, not a whole lot to see. Cutscenes for me are oddly stuck at around 10 frames a second, but regular gameplay is a smooth 60, MUCH MUCH better optimized than Saint's Row 2 for PC.
Audio - Competent enough. The Radio stations are a huge downgrade from the last game. Smaller and more questionable song choice will likely leave you tired of the radio pretty quickly. Dialogue is clear and well recorded, although any time someone talks to you, the audio is as if they're right next to you, including if they're on fire and being run over by a tank.
Lasting Appeal - I'm a bit conflicted. The gameplay is solid, but the lack of challenge for even moderately experienced players and general repetitiveness takes it down a notch from the last game. However, I've played a good couple hundred hours on PS3 and I bought it now on PC. It'll be great the first time and fun enough to come back to later.
Overall - Good fun game, I paid 60 dollars back in 2011 and I wasn't disappointed at all. On sale or not, chances are you won't be either. Returning players like myself, much much better port than SR2. I never bought any of the DLC and have no desire to, so I can't help you there. The problems like some repetitiveness, lack of real challenge, and a generally sloppy feel at times (scripted sequences that feel a bit too scripted, if that makes sense, or animations that don't line up, etc.) are outweighed by a fun, positive experience.
Final - 8/10

I don't recommend this game, not because it's a bad game, but because there is so much better user-made content for portal and portal 2.
The thing that made portal amazing, and the thing that I think Valve lost sight of, is that you could almost always see what you needed to do immediately; the fun part was figuring out how to do it.  It's when you can't see what the game wants you to do that you WANDER.  And wandering is not the fun part of the game.
Some designers think that bigger is better, and it will seem more epic, but that is not the case.  Also, I think a lot of them ran out of ideas for puzzles in small rooms, and switched to big rooms, where you could hide the solution more easily.  In any event, feel free to give it a try (since it's free), but again, you will find gameplay that is more fun for free online.

- Helicopters
- Mod Community

- ZEUS Missions!
The Problems
- Too expensive to play base game. (Small Player Base for this reason.)
- Vehicle/Tank physics terrible.
- AI/Player can easily glitch through walls.
- Object and vehicle damage is static and lacks simulation/physics.
- Building interior creativity lacking.
Overall Thought
Very few titles are near the realism simulated in Arma 3. Though if all the major issues I mentioned and community also have mentioned were fixed the game would probably be a lot more popular and become even more of a timeless title which it has proven itself to some degree.
Though I would give this title a 4.5 Star rating and put it on the shelf and wait for Arma 4 to be released as a Free to Play with a diverse marketplace to purchase vehicles/weapons/maps/etc. Until then...I recommend only buying when on sale.

I never review any game/mod, but this one certainly deserves it. It's a mod, alright, but aside from heavy reuse of Portal 2 assets (even though they DID create their own on top of them), it's one hell of a game on its own.
Let me first tell you what it's NOT:
-Bunch of maps for you to play with no link between them. NO, IT'S NOT.
-Portal 2 with added items. NO IT'S NOT.
-Maps becoming difficult merely hiding where Portals can be shot. NO, THEY DO NOT.
What it IS:
-Complete game in the Portal universe (between Portal and Portal 2). Including script, voice acting and similar sweeties.
-Cohesive history which certainly would help the canon "glue" itself.
-Features easy maps, complex maps and HELL maps. Not recommended if unconformable with Portal mechanics. Some are insane, but they are so insane because you always have all the pieces and if the level resists itself it's no one's fault but yours for not thinking hard enough. If at the end of Portal 2 you thought you had seen all... Think twice ;)
And on top of it. The ending is brilliant. No spoilers here, but it is. Trust me. And if you don't, trust the rest of the reviewers sharing my opining.
\end{MASTERPIECE}

How to describe a game based on planting various plants, to keep the zombie apocalypse from getting into your house and eating your brains? Maybe “
”? Basically, the game is all about using different plants to keep various types of zombies away from your house. There are several different levels each with their own challenge.
The story itself is very short, there isn’t much to say about it either. The game goes by pretty quickly but it is a lot of fun to play. And if you’re trying to squeeze out even more time, there are some great mini games to play. The “Whack a zombie”, might have given me carpal tunnel someday.
This is a strategy game, so you will need to select the plants you want to use, then place them in various orders that will hopefully ward off the hoards of zombies. Most of the games start slow, and really pick up in pace.
As I do for all my reviews, I also make note of the different achievements in the game  and the work to get them. To be honest I don’t’ really remember how difficult these achievements were. Most of them were unlocked as you played the game, although there were a few that required some setup. All in all, the achievements wouldn’t be a reason to get this game; this game would be fun with or without achievements. (I can hear everyone on my friends list gasp right now)
Plants vs. Zombies is normally $9.99 and I personally put 81 hours into the game, so in my mind that’s a fair trade, although it never hurts to wait for a 50% or 75% off sale. Occasionally older games like this go on 90% off sales, so it would be best to wait till then to get the most out of your money. However you wouldn’t be disappointed if you simply bought it right away.

Saints Row: The Third is the turning point in the franchise.  With the first and second games it seemed like the developers weren't sure wether they wanted a serious GTA style narrative or an over the top silly power fantasy game.  From this game on the series is firmly in the latter catagorey.
We joing the crew from the 2nd gang and right from the tutorial level we're shown just how over the top this game wants to be and if you don't mind silly this game is amazing.  It itsn't long before your kidnapped by a rival gang and end up in a new city with no resources.  And of course you decided to take over one block at a time.
Once again you have three gangs to deal with but this time there all working together to stop you.  Just like before each gang has there own theme and they each stand out more so then in the previous games mainly because when the heat gets high enough they don't just throw more guys at you.  Each gang has thee own special elite units that will terroize you like a helicoptor with snipers in it.  It does a nice job of making each game feel like its own threat rather than just a generic gang with different colors.
The writting keeps getting better.  The old crew is fleshed out much more than in the pervious game and we get some new characters that are all halarious fun.
Graphics have been improved but at a bit of a cost.  While you can still customize a ton of stuff in this game, you'll notice its far less then in saints row 2 which is a bit of a shame.  The new city is also a bit smaller and while it looks great it seems less memorable then stillwater.  there aren't any stand out loactions like the university.  Your either in midddle of city or in one of the less developed surrounding cities.  in saints row 2 i knew exactly where i was just by looking around but everything looks so similar in Saints the Third, which is strange because it looks so nice.
Theres a new upgrade system this time.  doing missions or one of the billion side quests gets you cash and experince.  As you gain levels you unlock the ability to purchase upgrades with cash, making money much more important in this game then before.
So a couple of things took a hit but alot got better too.  Overall this game is a blast.  Defaintly a must buy for sandbox fans or for people who enjoy over the top crazyness.

Saints Row: The Third scratches the itch that I've always want Grand Theft Auto to scratch. If you've played gta then the mechanics will be similar. Where the two differ is the outlandish comedy. Basically, if you like open world games like GTA vice city/san andreas or Sleeping Dogs (also great games), and are looking for some "comedy" (sometimes actually funny, sometimes just childish/"bro" humour) then give it a go. This was a really, REALLY, well made mod. At times I had trouble reminding myself it was a mod and not an official expansion or DLC.
Graphics: Obviously it looks the same as Portal 2 did in terms of graphics, but the design of the environments is spectacular, almost contesting the original game at times! The environments are lush and detailed and beautiful to look at. The opening sequence has some amazing shots of the Aperture Lab that are still stuck in my mind.
Ambiance: The music is really quite catchy and fits the Portal theme very well! It's similar to the original soundtrack, yet quirky enough to set it apart from the original. Great job there as well.
Gameplay: The puzzles are tough. I certainly had some trouble with them, and had to resort to a few walkthroughs. The design of the puzzles is phenomenal. It's basically like Portal 2, but amped up just a little bit for the more experienced players.
Story: This is the one area where I have a complaint. The story itself is well crafted and does a good job of bridging the gap between Portal 1 and 2. Unfortunately, I was not very happy with the voice acting/writing. At times I found myself cringing at the dialogue, either because of the line itself or the way it was delivered. They were clearly trying to do the Portal style humor which Wheatley delivered perfectly in Portal 2, but it just wasn't working quite right.
Other than the voice acting and writing, this is a fantastically made mod that definitely deserves to be played. There's a good amount of gameplay, hard puzzles, and good music to keep you busy for a few hours. 9/10

Having a good 7 to 8 years of hammer level design as a hobby myself, I would have to rate the overall level design of the mod in two different categories: Creativity, and Technical Detail.
Creativity 8/10 - The puzzles were all very well made and did their best to utilize concepts that weren't immediately obvious to players of Portal 2, which is a plus for originality. Unfortunately however, this made it so that many puzzles were very unclear as to what exactly you were supposed to do even when all the variables were available to you as you progressed through that puzzle.
I didn't exactly like how certain puzzles had cube droppers that stayed on after the button was pressed, because this was actually a variable in Portal 2 that was not taught this way. In Portal 2, you press the button once, you get one cube. If you wanted a new cube, you had to press the button again. In Portal Stories: Mel, many (or even all, I cannot recall) puzzles with a cube dropper utilized this feature where you press the button once, and the dropper constantly drops cubes over and over and over automatically the moment one cube is destroyed. This was incorporated into certain puzzles as something that you deliberately had to know of and use as a variable to complete the puzzle.
Portal Stories: Mel suffers from puzzles that are actually so intricate, it becomes more of a chore to complete them, but thankfully, it wasn't too often an occurrence to be stuck on a puzzle because of a variable that you did not know existed. Instead, it was because you had to use every single variable given to you in a very specific way, and with the later puzzles having lots more variables, you can see how this would become less fun and more chore-esque. There were points where I was starving for story, because I had been so mentally drained by trying to piece together everything given to me and execute it, sometimes in ways that only had a small opportunity to execute, which at first would make you think wasn't possible at all. I actually grew fatigued of the game via the puzzles given to me to the point that I had to take multiple breaks. When I did, I was discouraged from playing again because I knew all the puzzles I had yet to complete would make me feel equally frustrated and take over 10 or even 20 minutes to complete at the worst. This is why it took me days to complete a mod that was only about 6 hours or so for me in terms of play-time.
I also really did not like how if you ended up using one of these variables incorrectly, or in the wrong order, or accidentally dropped it while using it in the correct order, you would either have to reload a save you probably did not think to make, or you would have to essentially go sometimes all the way back to the beginning of the puzzle, respawn that variable (portal, cube, etc) and go through the entirety of the chunk of the puzzle you just went through to get back to where you were. It was very unforgiving and demanded the utmost chronological perfection, lest the player tear their hair out trying to run it through in their head, then execute it in just the right way. Figuring it out sometimes took just as long as actually doing it for me. I feel this is a bad thing but others may disagree and just feel like that's what a really tough well-made puzzle is, but again, I agree they were very well-made and quite possibly took months to design and perfect each, but it wasn't the same kind of fun as Portal or Portal 2 because of how precise and unforgiving and elaborate so many of them ended up being.
The mod is very creativite, but possibly too creative to the point that it was vastly harder than anything I had ever played in Portal, Portal 2, or any other decent Portal mod I have tried (though the portal mods I have tried are not many, mind you).
Technical Detail 7/10 - By "Technical Detail" I mean, there were a few issues here and there with things that looked like they would be walked on and might actually lead somewhere as the player tried to figure out where to go, but when you tried to drop onto them, you fall right through to your death. Other issues of this same area were not that big a deal though, like certain brushes being made func_illusions (which means the player cannot collide with them) but were in places where the player could absolutely collide with them should they press up against it to see detail behind the walls or what have you.
There was also a glitch I accidentally came across that allowed me to jump fron a light-bridge onto a catwalk I was never meant to get on, and allowed me to see a nodraw texture that was behind the puzzle, as the level designers did not anticipate players doing this. I legitimately thought it was the way I might have had to go instead of sticking around to finish the architecturally incomplete puzzle in the gameworld.
There was also a strange output glitch I believe I came across where an emancipation grill did not return after a cube was taken off of the button to deactivate it. This was either a glitch that helped me complete this confusing puzzle, or it was intentional, and thus a very stupid deisgn choice. You NEVER want to change a puzzle variable in the middle of the puzzlie to ensure the puzzle is completable.
There was another puzzle where I am almost positive there was no way in heck I was doing it right, but I was so irritated from the previous puzzles, I was ready and willing to break anything I was able to break to beat the puzzle easier (a player should never feel this way if you ask me). The puzzle had two emancipation grills beside each other, and a button turned off one, but turned on the other. I used a tiny little window of opportunity to shoot a portal through both just as they were switching between each other from on to off and off to on. I'm almost positive this was not how the puzzle was intended (and if it was, that is a really stupid design, because I just sat there stepping on and off the button, spamming my portal in hope that one of the shots went through to the other side in the fraction of a second I had to pull off the shot) but it never-the-less helped me progress in some way.
The gating and level design technicalities needed more work based around what players might try, instead of just what they were supposed to do.
The best parts of the mod by far were the behind-the-scenes segments and story-progression levels. It felt much more interactive, and seeing the massive levels you got to traverse was satisfying and very cool. Overall, it was a very good mod, but no mod can be called a mod without its flaws. Considering that I know how hard it is to make something like this, I am honored to play it, and I recommend this to anyone who thinks they are a pro portal puzzle solver, but want a little meat to the experience in between puzzles as well.

Saints Row: The Third is a third person shooter taking place in the open world city of Steelport. It's a game that doesn't really take itself too seriously which is either a good or bad thing for some and the graphics are cartoonish to go along with the humor of the game which might fall flat for some people at times.
In Steelport you'll be spending your time either completing the missions, doing activities and finding the collectables, or going around the city causing mayhem. The story itself is based around getting revenge for someone and thats about it, lasting roughly 10+ hours. To make it even worse; Saints Row 4 basically renders every action you did during this game entirely pointless. However the missions themselves are pretty enjoyable, and the interactions between the characters are interesting despite not being too fleshed out.
While the story isn't too particularily compelling and the game's humor and graphics may not appeal to everyone, Saints Row: The Third is solid overall and pretty fun to play by yourself or with a friend. It occassionally goes on sale for $3.74 and it's definitely worth purchasing for that amount.

I tend to be picky toward but I can say without a doubt a LOT of work went into this. The maps are challenging as hell but there's this feeling of satisfaction you get when you solve something you spent a good amount of time trying to get through. I like a challenge in my games but sometimes, I am guilty of ragequitting and looking up walkthroughs but hey, aside from that, I had a barrel of fun solving the puzzles.
The only thing I can complain about is that they didn't use the actual skin of Mel. Like blonde girl in a blue jumpsuit left unused in Portal 2. That would have been a really nice touch.
Everything else is top notch and feels very professional. I was amazed with the introduction seeing how fleshed out it was and how it set you immediatly in the mood. I loved the subtle references as well (I'm still uncertain the two ''cruel scientists'' referred in the mod is a subtle nod to Portal : Prelude seeing how that mod is even harder than this one)
Overall, like I said, it feels like a fully fleshed out game like some prequel DLC-ish title. The voice acting is great. My favorite addition is the music and it doesn't feel all that annoying in a loop when struggling to solve a test chamber so props to that.
All in all, I was a bit skeptical seeing how little chapters there were but the chapters and test chambers are pretty lenghty. I got around 15 hours of gameplay from start to finish.
If you are a die-hard portal fan, you have to download this mod.

Awesome. Buy this, even if only for the KOTH multiplayer, and if you want a fun team oriented challenge. This game has come a long way since its initial release. I was less than thrilled with it last year, and initially gave it a horrible review, but they have truly worked on the game and fixed a lot of issues that it had. The game is playable now. Dont expect stellar framerates (I avg 45-75 fps on a stock clocked fx8350 and msi gaming x rx480) or a game where you can just rock a preset and get good performance, in my opinion you really need to alter the games settings for your hardware. If you want a realistic military simulation where teamwork truly is a combat force multiplier than look no further. Its interesting and realistic to see how a team can overcome the enemy by communicating and working together, or how lack of teamwork can lead to you being annihilated by your enemy. Playing the objective is just as important as playing outside support for the people on the objective. DOes it have the latest greatest graphics? No, but I find the visuals satisfactory, especially when there are not any games comparable to what Arma 3 is trying to be as a whole, and the draw distances can be insane with people makeing 1000m+ kills with sniper rifles. If your a fan of realistic Military sims and want something large scale and as far from the call of duty/battlefield repetitiveness as you can get, why not give Arma 3 a try. DO NOT INSTALL ON A SSD UNLESS ITS DEDICATED TO ARMA 3. The game has a lot of downloads to play on individual servers, depending upon what mods etc the server you are trying to join is running, you could experience having to download 20gb to connect! That can fill an ssd quick. If you are going to dedicate an ssd to this game and are planning to play on modded servers, i.e. DayZ etc etc than get at least a 240gb ssd to do so. I have been using my 1tb sshd and am happy with my performance in game, cant justify personally needing an ssd.

A game you can pick up and play in minutes, useful for the odd few moments when you're unsure of what to play or have 5 mins and don't want to get stuck into something bigger. Plants Vs Zombies is a gun twist on a tower defense game and features you literally growing plants on your lawn, swimming pool and rooftop to stop the zombies from eating your brains.
The game is quite replayable, the first run through has several stages and keeps the gameplay interesting by adding hazards such as fog, mini-games like bowling & slots and even some puzzle modes to keep all audiences interested. 2x play throughs of the adventure mode are required to see everything and you can replay the mini games & puzzles at will once they're unlocked.
For the score setters, the game features survival modes & even an endless mode just to see how many waves you can last.
There's also a "Zen Garden" where you grow plants without figting zombies and can have several gardens and a tree of wisdom, providing tips and codes to modify the games visuals.
The game looks a little dated due to the developers sticking with a 4:3 resolution and maximised on a 1920 x 1080 screen this can look a little pixelated - that doesn't impact the gameplay and even adds some charm to the game itself.
If you're looking for a casual game that will keep you interested over a long period of time and isn't overly difficult in the process, pick this up.

I wholeheartedly recommend this mod and not just because it is free.  While it is a bit rough around the edges, the puzzles are the hardest I've seen in any Portal mod and well worth the time of any series fan.  They do occasionally lack the elegance of Valve's efforts but that is a forgivable sin.
While Portal puzzles usually have a more or less obvious objective, and the difficulty is in trying to reach it, these puzzles will have you scratching your head at where even to begin.  But that is not entirely unwelcome.  I will admit having to cheat twice on this mod, something I've never had to do before.  Thanks to drave drune on YouTube for his excellent walkthroughs.
I do wish it was a little better about clear directions outside the puzzles -- on a few occasions I found myself stumped as to where the game expected me to go or what it expected me to do next, which is something Valve's games excel at.
The mod is beautiful, and it is nice for once to not have to say, "I wish the developers had spent as much time on the game as on the environments."  The only complaint I have about the set design is that there are a few points in the mod where the developers are clearly showing off while you are doing nothing but walking or taking a tram or elevator from Point A to Point B.
At other points in the game there are far too many puzzles in a row without a break, and no narrative beyond apologies from the narrator for having no new information for you -- it seems like pacing could have been handled better to even these things out.
The narrative is interesting, set between Portal and Portal 2, and ties in well with existing Portal lore.  The dry humor, unfortunately, is not as effective here as it is in the Valve games, but it isn't really clear whether that is because of the writing or the delivery of the narrating AI core -- neither is terrible, but they also do not deserve particular acclaim.  The supporting voice actor does both a brilliant impression of J.K. Simmons as Cave Johnson and a great job as the game's antagonist.
Again, this is an unreserved recommendation -- if I sound critical it is only because a great mod could have been even better.  Pick this one up and look for future work by the developers.

Presentation is smooth and the puzzles are designed really well. The mod is A+ save for two gripes that I have with it.
First, the puzzle difficulty is a little inconsistent. I'd waltz around, taking a 2-5 minutes of thinking through the first levels until I came to this one level where I stood there for an hour asking myself "What the ♥♥♥♥ am I supposed to do". I youtubed the solution and had to do a double take because I couldn't process what the hell happened when the guy did it. While I'm glad that the creators of this mod aren't holding back on difficulty, it's really jarring when it's squashed between two noticeably easier puzzles.
Second, some of the puzzles get frustrating because the part where you have to run and/or jump requires a lot of accuracy-- you know what to do but you keep messing it up. This last point also happened in the original Portal games but it didn't feel as glaring as it does here.
In spite of these two flaws, I'm loving this. Good plot, great dialogue and this is overall top-quality content.

I really love the Arma series, but I cannot recommend this game, not as it is now at least. Somehow, even though my system meets all the minimum specs, performance is awful. When I am in cities or when there is a lot of action going on, my FPS drops from 40-45 to 18-20. It is practically unplayable.  Even players whose systems meet all the required specs experience low FPS and FPS drops in those situations. The first logical thing you do is setting everything to low, but it doesn't help . And if you search the internet, you will find  loads of tweaks and fixes that are said to significantly improve performance, but most of them don't seem to make any difference and,  when any of them do, you can barely notice it. Also, you can find different Arma 3 branches, roughly speaking, different  Arma 3 versions created by the devs with potential fixes,  which you can download, however in my case, none of them worked. Well, trying to fix it myself  took a lot of my time and, now, I'm done trying. At least, the game situation is not hopeless. The devs are working on those issues and maybe some time in the next year, hopefully, they may  release a patch or hotfix that will put and end to all of this. However, while that doesn't happen, I can't give a positive review nor recommend the game.
Edit 1:
-after so many attempts, I have finally figured out the game and GPU settings with which  the game runs a bit better;
-an FPS limiter helped me a lot; when set to lower framerates, around 36, it helps  keeping my laptop from overheating, quite a performance killer
-FPS still drops to 20 but it happens less often; I HOPE IT CAN BE FIXED

The first time I played SR3 I thought the story was pretty dumb and I just couldn’t understand the game’s sense of humor. Yes, everything felt epic, but also shallow at the same time. It took me some time to realize that this game was not meant to be taken seriously, but once I understood this, I couldn’t stop playing and had a lot of fun. I do still miss a bit of narrative depth in the game (like in GTA perhaps) but this is not the game’s style, and that’s not a bad thing at all: SR is all about having fun, giving the player as many choices as possible (no matter how silly they may be) and making sure you don’t put down the controller.
Performance wise, the game looks stunning and is really well optimized (I was able to run it at some decent 40fps in my really old laptop). I think it is a huge improvement over Saints Row 2, which in my opinion was already a really good game (yet a terrible PC port, unlike SR3). The only step backwards I've noticed is that Saints Row 2 had more customization options (such as clothing, styles, etc.) apart from that, I'd say the developers have done an awesome job.
So in conclusion I'd say that this game is a ton of fun, as long as you are willing to accept its… err, *relaxed* take on reality. Yup, I’d say go for it!

I really love the Arma series, but I cannot recommend this game, not as it is now at least. Somehow, even though my system meets all the minimum specs, performance is awful. When I am in cities or when there is a lot of action going on, my FPS drops from 40-45 to 18-20. It is practically unplayable.  Even players whose systems meet all the required specs experience low FPS and FPS drops in those situations. The first logical thing you do is setting everything to low, but it doesn't help . And if you search the internet, you will find  loads of tweaks and fixes that are said to significantly improve performance, but most of them don't seem to make any difference and,  when any of them do, you can barely notice it. Also, you can find different Arma 3 branches, roughly speaking, different  Arma 3 versions created by the devs with potential fixes,  which you can download, however in my case, none of them worked. Well, trying to fix it myself  took a lot of my time and, now, I'm done trying. At least, the game situation is not hopeless. The devs are working on those issues and maybe some time in the next year, hopefully, they may  release a patch or hotfix that will put and end to all of this. However, while that doesn't happen, I can't give a positive review nor recommend the game.
Edit 1:
-after so many attempts, I have finally figured out the game and GPU settings with which  the game runs a bit better;
-an FPS limiter helped me a lot; when set to lower framerates, around 36, it helps  keeping my laptop from overheating, quite a performance killer
-FPS still drops to 20 but it happens less often; I HOPE IT CAN BE FIXED

I REALLY want to like this game.  But my computer is slightly buggy and not 100% up-to-date.  Combine that with the bugs in this game, and it's nearly unplayable.  I get more severe motion sickness with this than I do with regular Portal, and the controls are a bit touchy.  When standing near a portal, a bit too far right to enter it, I click the key to strafe left once, and a fifth of a second later, I move, but I move too far to the left to enter.  And my jumps don't sync up with my movements, which makes jumping into portals for launching near impossible(or actually impossible...couldn't stick around to figure it out, had to go throw up).  I had to turn all my settings down on low in order to move at a non-mind-numbing pace in big spaces in the first chapter.
But there are people!  There are actual people walking around while you're walking around!  That's super cool, even if they don't interact with you at all.  And there's another personality core(only got to hear him in-game, though, before I gave up.)
The idea is pretty good, but the execution is miserable.  When Cave Johnson is speaking, the sound gets mixed up, like it's two entwined tracks (with parts of the same sound on each one) that are out of sync, kind of like talking on Skype to someone who uses speakers instead of headphones, with a fast but shoddy internet connection.
Also, chapter 1, which took me about 30 minutes to complete (and the first bit of chapter 2, up until the portal fall-launch), start out very slowly in terms of action.  I'd much prefer to hear that dialog a bit more compressed and closer together.  Most of chapter 1 isn't so much puzzle-solving as riding in an elevator and on a subway train and trying to find the right door.
My one complaint that isn't this game's developers' fault♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is the shattered-triangle aspect of the broken graphics.  If my computer could handle this type of graphics, I'd probably breeze through Ch1 in ten minutes of walking, and ten minutes of sitting around trying to wait for the train/elevator to stop.  As it is, I sometimes can't even tell what's a door and what's a ... something else, let alone if there's a red or green light on the top.  This happened for me in both Portal and Portal 2, and it happens in a lot of other 3d games.  Anything that moves or which is designed to move, the model of which is made out of triangular vector graphics, has the triangles disconnect and distort across my screen.  The fewer moving objects, the better in games like this.  But there were a lot of things that could have been background instead of moving in this game, such as the cars.  Not a single car I saw was actually moving, so they could have made them stationary, instead of movable like the train, the portal gun, etc.
Also, the between-area loading times suck, and the loading sequences break immersion.  It would be better to have just a pre-rendered image of the door you happen to be looking at when you move into the next area.  Instead, it fades out and shows you a bunch of big cover-shots, then fades back to the game and still holds you in place for a second or two before you can move.
But I REALLY want to get this storyline.  So what I'm going to do is search youtube for a play-through with audio by someone who has a high-end computer, or maybe a compilation of all the speaking-parts and plotpoints.

PROs:
+ Free
+ Very detailed world. More detailed than portal 1 or 2
+ Fun puzzles
+ Very long for a portal kind of game!
+ You dont need to do any crazy timing or quick shooting to beat the puzzles.
+ Some of the puzzles are real mind benders. If you expect easy puzzles, you are going to have a bad time. If you are completly lost, just close the game and try again later. It worked for me :). Almost all maps have 4 stages:
++ Acquaintance with the map
++ Frustation: this map is impossible to be solved like this, i think i found a bug
++ This crazy idea might work
++ Eureka!
+You are always heading up, witch makes your navigation between puzzles more intuitive
NOT PROs/CONs:
* I was able to solve at least 3 puzzles in a different way as they were intended to be solved. Which is both satisfiying and frustrating (I was not trying to be clever, I was just trying to make some crazy idea work out of frustration)
* Voice acting and general script was just okay. (Probably only because we have portal 2 there to compare)
CONs:
- They dont make clear at the begining that you dont need to make any crazy timing or quick shooting. I they did, I wouldnt had tried weird things out of frustration so many times.
- Puzzles offer you one viable solution only. By this i mean that If you see a portable surface, expect to use it at some point. There arent many portable surfaces left untouched. With this mindset, puzzles are a little easier.
- Script was not really funny. Kinda of annoying at times trying to have portal-like humor. It gets a little better towards the end, but in my opinion, they should had taken the chance to do their own unique style

+ Some of the puzzles are real mind benders. If you expect easy puzzles, you are going to have a bad time. If you are completly lost, just close the game and try again later. It worked for me :). Almost all maps have 4 stages:
++ Acquaintance with the map
++ Frustation: this map is impossible to be solved like this, i think i found a bug
++ This crazy idea might work
++ Eureka!
+You are always heading up, witch makes your navigation between puzzles more intuitive
NOT PROs/CONs:
* I was able to solve at least 3 puzzles in a different way as they were intended to be solved. Which is both satisfiying and frustrating (I was not trying to be clever, I was just trying to make some crazy idea work out of frustration)
* Voice acting and general script was just okay. (Probably only because we have portal 2 there to compare)
CONs:
- They dont make clear at the begining that you dont need to make any crazy timing or quick shooting. I they did, I wouldnt had tried weird things out of frustration so many times.
- Puzzles offer you one viable solution only. By this i mean that If you see a portable surface, expect to use it at some point. There arent many portable surfaces left untouched. With this mindset, puzzles are a little easier.
- Script was not really funny. Kinda of annoying at times trying to have portal-like humor. It gets a little better towards the end, but in my opinion, they should had taken the chance to do their own unique style
BONUS:

Review Info:
-Game: H1Z1
-Date: 13-12-2017
H1Z1: King Of The Kill is a real battle game in which up to 150 players compete against each other to be the last to survive. Players can choose to play alone, in pairs, or in groups of five, in order to be the final person or final team remaining.
Players start each game using a parachute from a random location above the map. Once they land, they must look for a way to defend themselves. This may be depending on the player's choice, such as picking up a gun and actively hunting other players or hiding while other players kill themselves. There are vehicles scattered around the world, allowing players to pursue opponents or make a quick escape. Players can avail a variety of supplies from their surroundings, including weapons, equipment and first aid kits. The game also features a crafting system that allows players to create impromptu tools such as deconstructing deleted items into functional bandages or body armor.
As the game progresses, a cloud of toxic gas squeezes the map, causing damage to the remaining players. This effectively makes the playable part of the map smaller, so that players are eventually forced to confront themselves closely. The gas spreads in timed increments, causing a greater degree of damage in the last stages of the match.

Portal Stories: Mel is a free standalone community made Portal 2 mod.  It centers around Mel, another unfortunate test subject in Aperture Laboratories.
Pros:
+ Decent voice acting
+ Well designed puzzles
+ More or less the size of a full game
+ Highly challenging (significantly more so than Portal 2)
Neutral:
* Hit or miss humor
Cons:
- Awful final challenge
Overall I think it's a really great game.  If you played Portal 2 and enjoyed the gameplay but wished it was more challenging, then this game is for you.  It's quite a meaty game.  Obviously, how long it takes you to figure out puzzles will have a massive effect of play time, but it should take 5-15 hours to complete.  The puzzles are consistently clever and difficult.  The only let down of the game is the terrible final challenge.  I won't go into detail because I don't want to spoil anything, but it centers on what was never meant to be a game mechanic in Portal 2, and thus is highly inconsistent.  Thus, in a game where mechanics function consistently and you use your brain to figure things out and proceed, it sucks to be stuck in a challenge that can be failed even when you have it figured out simply because the mechanic doesn't work properly.  It's the antithesis of everything Portal and everything previous in Portal Stories: Mel.  Everything before that is all about using your brain to figure out a solution, once you figure it out, the execution is simple.  The final challenge is the opposite, figuring out the solution is extremely simple.  Heck, you are told what to do for the only remotely tricky part to figure out, but the execution can be difficult because of the wonky mechanics failing seemingly randomly.  Still, it's the only part of the game I hated, everything up to the very end was great.

Playing using a controller is VERY awkward, it almost feels like the controller is attempting to emulate a keyboard and mouse rather than having native support, which is weird seeing as Portal 2 did not have this issue (I'm using a 360 pad).
The Cave Johnson impersonator is terrible. After the initial opening sequence (where he is passable), his voice takes on an almost.... eastern european tint and his pronounciations of certain words are incorrect. That, combined with janky controller support ruins the immersion for me.
Difficulty is.... odd. Within the first 15 minutes I encountered 2 seperate instances of "pixel hunting", searching for a tiny almost imperceptable area far off in the distance where placing a portal is possible. I'm a big fan of having to logically use your brain in order to work out a solution to a puzzle, but I can't stand this type of "puzzle" unless it's from a 1980's Lucasarts game.
I appreciate the time and effort that went into this, and I congratulate the developers on being able to put something like this together, but if you're looking for something as polished and playtested as the original 2, this is not it.
Unfortunatly, due to the reasons outlined above, I will not be continuing to play this so I cannot comment on if it gets better later on.
(Also just as a side note, I managed to get my character trapped inbetween a chair and a table within the first 5 minutes, meaning I had to restart and sit through the whole bloody train ride again.)

This is the most polished fan made work I have ever seen. Those of you wishing for a portal 3 should be happy, because this is nearly it.
Puzzles are difficult but fair, and will have you scratching your head multiple times. There are 5 chapters to keep you going. Yes, five! Trust me, the content for perplexing portal puzzling is here!
Also, it doesn't just take the portal story we know and rub it in your face. There are crossover hints, sure, but it doesn't ride off of the main game's success. Instead, it has it's own unique, and well refined story which will get you immersed i'm sure. The character's are likeable, the story is solid, and the resolution is well done.
Finally, it's FREAKIN' FREE! Pick it up, just do it! If you like puzzle games, at all, pick it up! The game is beautiful, and if you haven't gotten it, get it! You're missing out! I know I'll be coming back to it, time and time again ;)

Conclusion: If you liked the Portal franchise and/or would like some challenge thrown in your face this is a game for you! Have fun!

TL;DR: If you're looking for a real Portal challenge, then this is worth playing. If you're looking for a story experience much like in Portal 2, expect to be dissappointed.
This game is pretty interesting, the puzzles are often extremely hard and take alot of time to get solved, I for myself had to use walkthroughs for hints alot of times since I couldn't think of any solution. Also the story itself is consistent and nice, and the introduction chapter really blew my mind.
However there are also flaws in the game. For example at some points I was confused where I had to go since there was no way I could have seen it, which made the puzzles even more harder. Furthermore later in the story some doors (I mean those modern Aperture Science ones) looks as if they could be open, but did not, leaving my confused since they look exactly the same like those who can be opened. Also I encountered 2 pathways (one of them was in the final boss stage) which were clearly designed to be used, but you had to walk/jump right to get on them, which can be annoying, especially if you have a time limit.
The last flaw I will mention is a flawed immersion. The story seemed more of a filler than something that actually was important, which is a shame. You just go to level pack one to level pack two and in between you get a bit of story so that it doesn't feel like you're just playing a bunch of maps. Also making a fall in a seemingly deep hole so short that you can hear a thump 2 seconds after isn't really immersive, and making falls a bit longer shouldn't be a problem, since Portal 2 never had such things.

This is probably one of the best Portal modifications out there. It adds to the storyline of Portal 2, and is a must have for Portal fans/owners. Not only does it contain dialogue that sticks to the games storyline, but it also contains brand new, excrutiatingly challenging tests. If you liked the original tests though, do not worry, because there are some tests familiar to the old button-pressing challenges you would find in the Portal series. The storyline is unique, and the voice acting is EXTREMELY convincing. Along with having all original items from Portal 2, the game also contains new items/textures that add an even bigger challenge to the tests. Even though the start may seem a bit familiar, (with the beginning sequence looking a lot like Half-Life's opening sequence), it is an amazing mod/game and overall is a must have for fans of Portal.

Probably the better version. While it's PC only, and the PvZ brand lends itself well to mobile platforms, PvZ GOTY is the game it was meant to be. Gameplay progresses nicely, and the first play through is very much new zombie = new plant. It's linear in that regard. On the second playthough Crazy Dave has a surprise that makes a replay unique.
The side games and puzzles are a nice change too. Each of the games offers a new challenge. They're relatively easy to complete, but as a casual game, they offer a nice change to the base campaign. Added to this are the Zen Garden and Tree of Life. These provide longevity to the game, as filling your garden and growing the Tree require a lot of investment. Money comes quick, with half my Zen Garden filled I make about $10k in an hour. The garden, thankfully, gives the player the most bang for your time - over time the diminishing return increases. The Garden is a nice feature because you can advance the game, and go take a shower or something while your Snail collects the coins.
PvZ GOTY offers something for almost everyone. I like it because I can fit a level into a short time, making it a quick, fun, distraction.
I would recommend this game over buying PvZ2 on mobile - since EA took over, PvZ2 is heavily monitized and pushes micro transactions, including buy-to-win shortcuts.

They did a decent job with this. It's certainly fair to say that for a free expansion, this is better than a lot of games you'll have to pay for. They did an especially good job with the puzzles- they are true to the Portal premise (solve problems with portal gun) but require you to think entirely differently from how you had to solve the original portal puzzles. A couple of them stumped me, and I had to watch a video for those, which has never happened before, so in my opinion they are sufficiently challenging. A couple of them involve new functionality that has no overt introduction, so you can't possibly know what to do unless you happen to stumble upon it or watch someone else who has.
It isn't without a fair helping of bugs though. There are things like debris piles on the ground that you can walk through, wierd flashes and random streaks of light that happen briefely after passing through the portal, and choppy audio in the core's voice (which seems to never stop). At one point I got stuck in the floor and had to reload. Some of the puzzles have multiple possible solutions. I only know because I solved them the wrong way. (Not sure if that means I was bad or the puzzle.)
With all that said, I was expecting more for a 4.4 gb file. It took nearly 48hrs to download this and it is only good for a couple hours of play. I know it is a community project and hey, we get it for free, but it has left me dissappointed and I regret the time I spent on it. I think it needs less voice and video, and more plot. Had the story been as clever as some of the puzzel designs are, it might have been an A+++ production.

Let's take into account that this was THQ's last Saints Row game.
Don't get me wrong, the campaign is funny and cool but this game has so many flaws.
Pros:
-Story is fun
-Driving and Flying are a lot less clunky
-The game overall is whacky.
-It's not a horrible port.
-The DLC is pretty cool.
-New map to play on.
-Coop
-Cribs are slighly easier to get (do x mission and get crib instead of having to buy it)
- Losing Noriety is a lot easier (go into something you own and it's gone).
-No more respect req to do missions
Cons:
-Cribs are literally copy and pasted (the only unique ones are Kenzie's, Shaundi's Ex's and the Saints HQ)
-The vanilla game without DLC has a lot less customization.
-Tries to kill off Johnny Gat in the most vague way possible (just killing off Johnny Gat is kinda huge but trying to do it like they did in the campaign is just soo wrong, Johnny is the 2nd most important character of the series...)
-Once you 100% everything there is literally nothing to do (can only do survivals and replay minigames, no mission replays like in the previous ones).
-Permanent Changes to this city that cannot be changed (my god I wish i could just put the bridges up and down as much as i want)
- Cannot take off dual wield (I know this is small but still come on, in the other Saints you could choose to dual wield or not).
- Upgrades make you feel like superman without the kryptonite (yay I can just stand there and shoot with a 5 level noriety on me because i don't take any damage).
- Cannot remove upgrades
-CANNOT REPLAY MISSIONS (except dlc)
TL;DR:
Fun game overall but once you have finished the story (takes about 6-8 hours max to complete) the game gets pretty repetitive. Forbid you finish everything because then you have nothing to do. If you're looking for a game to just mess around with a friend then this game is for you (I've played easily 100 hours with my friend in this game just messing around). If you're looking for a game that you can still have something to do once you finish the game, this is not for you.

If you're a Portal fan, this is definitely worth your time. Taking place between Portal 1 and 2, this incredbily professional mod gives us a new cast of characters in the very familiar environs of the Aperture Labs testing facility. The mod is best played with a recent memory of the mechanics of Portal 2 as there is very little hand holding and many of the more advanced maneuvers from that game will show up. That said, the difficulty curve is pretty steady and while I spent at least half of my 8 hours with the game staring at walls, trying to suss out solutions, there were only a couple times that I was stumped and only once that I felt it was due in part to anything other than my own lack of imagination.
For the price of FREE, you can't go wrong with Portal Stories: Mel. I would have easily paid upwards of $30 for this.
