With Valve having seemingly given up game development, fans of their IP's have been wondering what the next game will be. Instead of waiting, Prism Studios decided to craft an unofficial prequel to Portal 2 in the mean time. The quality of the level design may not always be top class, but Portal Stories: Mel ends up feeling like a full retail product despite being a mod.
While a lot of that credit has to go to the prior work Valve did with Portal 2, to even craft puzzles or a story close to as engaging as Valve's work is a true blessing. A lot of the ideas get borrowed from Portal 2, but the character of Virgil ends up feeling alive and cheery.
The exploration of Aperture's past is also highly intriguing. While we got a lot more of an in-depth look at how the world of Portal comes to be in it's sequel, we now understand a bit more of how Cave Johnson ended up running the company into the ground and what helped GlaDOS ressurect herself.
Of course, this is all non-canon, but the sheer quality of it all is very engaging. After finishing the game, I almost wish this were an official part of the Portal storyline. We may be removing a bit of the mystery behind GlaDOS and Cave Johnson, but at least it all remains interesting.
As for the puzzles, they start off strong and begin to get repetitive near the end. The last few chapters are some of the best designed in the entire mod, but they come too little, too late. The boss encounter is very reminiscent of the original Half-Life and even a few levels take some ideas from Black Mesa.
The soundtrack is also incredible. For a fan project, I'm surprised we got an entirely original score, but it fits the mood extremely well. I was always partial to the atmosphere sounds of the original Portal and I'd say that is the only place where I felt Portal 2 did not live up to it's predecessor. I guess Prism thought so, too, as this score blows Portal 1's out of the water.
The slight alterations to the Source engine since Portal 2's release have yielded some better lighting and incredible looking water. Since PC's are also a bit more adept, extra foliage is present in the "Overgrown" segment. It looks worse for wear than in Portal 2, which kind of screws around with the idea of this being a prequel.
If it weren't for the middle section of the game, I'd say this is a homerun. Portal 2 had a strange reliance on ending most platforming/story segments with a half-open door that required you to portal out of. Portal Stories: Mel also does that quite a bit.
Right around the end of the middle segment, we also get treated to an incredible amount of block puzzles. The gels do make a return (and water gets utilized, which is nice), but a lot of the ideas are just more obtuse setups than what Portal 2 had.
I did have fun, but I can't deny that the ideas stopped being creative and exciting after awhile. The last 2 chapters really were a standout as they feel completely different from the official Portal series.
Still, at the price of free, why aren't you playing this? It's an easy recommendation and is quite well made, too. I hope the team at Prism Studios can someday make an original project. I'm sure they'll come up with something wholly awesome.

Modding is a strange innovation. Whether big or small, mods tend to change the game experience, they tend to turn the player's perceptions around. When dealing with a near-perfect series such as Portal, you do not need  to mix up what is a stellar experience. In fact, 'Portal Stories: Mel' addresses my only issue with the series- that it had to end! Hopefully, with mods like these, this can be somewhat addressed, even if temporarily.
I hesitate to call this a mod. Mods to me are latched onto their source games, however 'Portal Stories: Mel' does not appear to be. It perfectly replicates the tone and feel of 'Portal' and 'Portal 2', and to all intents and purposes (and if I did not know it to be otherwise), I would call it a rightful third installment to the series. I feel like I have robbed the creators somewhat in getting this work of brilliance for free.
The levels are frustrating but fascinating. The out-of-chamber sequences surpass those of their predecessors, and liven up the occasionally claustrophobic test chambers. Virgil, your companion for the game, is sumptuously scripted and delightfully voiced.
If time were no obstruction, I would play this again immediately.  I sincerely hope that one day we may get another Portal mod on par with this. I sincerely hope that the creators do themselves the service of charging us for this privilege- for that is what 'Portal Stories: Mel' is, a privilege.

Fantastic game, but they suck your money in. The only good DLC's are Gangstas In Space, Trouble With Clones, and Geinkeibowl IIV. Those contain fun addon missions that add 10+ more hours.
Take over the city
The game features territory that either belongs to the 3rd street saints (you), morningstar, luchadores, or deckers. Eliminate drug deals, buy stores, or complete fun activities to take the territory, and see your crew move into your new land. In doing so, get an hourly income so you can upgrade your guy, and more. Have "cribs" and safehouses for when you progress through the story, where you can access your arsenel of weapons, cars, and air vehicles, sometimes even boats.
Customization
Customize your guns to make them more powerful and badass, cars to make them more durable, powerful, and faster. Even upgrade your cribs A.K.A. strongholds to look bigger and give you better things with each upgrade. You can upgrade your person for more abilities, combat upgrades, health upgrades, and lots more.
Gameplay
The game is fun, kickass, and a good time. Find yourself just spending hours going around in a tank and cause chaos. Call in your "homies" to help in combat, and recruit them by holding Z to follow you. Drive many varieties of vehicles and use many types of guns. Complete assassinations, and steal cars for money.
Story
The story is fantastic, don't listen to what people say bad about it. Sure, it's way to unrealistic, but since when was this game unrealistic? Each mission is either an introduction into another activity, or a real big and non linear mission. 40 missions in game, 15 of which are activity starters, an the rest are fun missions to help rebuild your respect.

So this was the Saints Row game that began to venture into crazy territory, though it's not really as dirty as I thought it would be.  Actually, the Ho-ing and the Escort missions in SR2 have filthier dialogue.  Sure, you get to hit people with a giant purple willie in SR3, but that loses its novelty after awhile.
Anyway, this game plays much, much better than SR2, though part of the problem was that the PC port for SR2 is terrible.  Even so, the cars and aircraft are much easier to control and this might be the first crime sandbox game where I actually enjoyed flying.  The futuristic vehicles you get near the endgame and with DLC are extremely cool.
As for customization in terms of character, car and crib design, this game offers fewer choices than SR2, but enough that I didn't feel that I was missing too much.  I am not heavy on customization and I don't like to spend forever designing a character, so those who do might be disappointed.
Instead of Stillwater, you play in Steelport.  It's smaller than the area in SR2, but it looks and feels more like a real city because it doesn't segregate areas in ways like the "Factory" or the "University" districts. Instead, each zone contains more subtle differences such as the types of people, cars, and shops you encounter as well as the kinds of crime that the controlling gangs prefer to commit (Luchadores are big on gambling, for instance, so you see several casinos).
Honestly, I found Steelport more interesting to explore, which explains why I have more achievements in SR3 at the moment.  Bigger isn't always better, as I tend to get burned out in GTA: San Andreas by the time I hit San Fiero, though I also blame that horrible RC plane mission.
I loved the opening/closing song to this game, and the radio stations have some pretty good tracks, but I liked the ones in SR2 more overall.  SR3 has an Adult Swim channel that is pretty amusing, though.
The story is far less serious than the one in SR2, and I found it hilarous and engaging but a bit short.  For example, when you gain additional contacts to help you take out the three gangs, their initial missions are simply a way to direct you toward the minigames.  Even so, the gangs amused me (especially the Deckers) and the specialist enemies in SR3 give them a more distinct style than the gangs in SR2.
As for the minigames (AKA Activities and Diversions), SR2 and SR3 have the same number (SR3 has more if you get the Genkibowl DLC), and though not all of the ones from SR2 carried over, the overall quality has greatly improved and I only really missed Demolition Derby. Also, SR3 ties them more to the storyline by giving some of the games distinct looks.  For instance, the Snatch missions are not always about picking up Hos depending on where you start them.  I also loved the new minigames, especially Professor Genki's Super Ethical Realty Climax.

So this was the Saints Row game that began to venture into crazy territory, though it's not really as dirty as I thought it would be.  Actually, the Ho-ing and the Escort missions in SR2 have filthier dialogue.  Sure, you get to hit people with a giant purple willie in SR3, but that loses its novelty after awhile.
Anyway, this game plays much, much better than SR2, though part of the problem was that the PC port for SR2 is terrible.  Even so, the cars and aircraft are much easier to control and this might be the first crime sandbox game where I actually enjoyed flying.  The futuristic vehicles you get near the endgame and with DLC are extremely cool.
As for customization in terms of character, car and crib design, this game offers fewer choices than SR2, but enough that I didn't feel that I was missing too much.  I am not heavy on customization and I don't like to spend forever designing a character, so those who do might be disappointed.
Instead of Stillwater, you play in Steelport.  It's smaller than the area in SR2, but it looks and feels more like a real city because it doesn't segregate areas in ways like the "Factory" or the "University" districts. Instead, each zone contains more subtle differences such as the types of people, cars, and shops you encounter as well as the kinds of crime that the controlling gangs prefer to commit (Luchadores are big on gambling, for instance, so you see several casinos).
Honestly, I found Steelport more interesting to explore, which explains why I have more achievements in SR3 at the moment.  Bigger isn't always better, as I tend to get burned out in GTA: San Andreas by the time I hit San Fiero, though I also blame that horrible RC plane mission.
I loved the opening/closing song to this game, and the radio stations have some pretty good tracks, but I liked the ones in SR2 more overall.  SR3 has an Adult Swim channel that is pretty amusing, though.
The story is far less serious than the one in SR2, and I found it hilarous and engaging but a bit short.  For example, when you gain additional contacts to help you take out the three gangs, their initial missions are simply a way to direct you toward the minigames.  Even so, the gangs amused me (especially the Deckers) and the specialist enemies in SR3 give them a more distinct style than the gangs in SR2.
As for the minigames (AKA Activities and Diversions), SR2 and SR3 have the same number (SR3 has more if you get the Genkibowl DLC), and though not all of the ones from SR2 carried over, the overall quality has greatly improved and I only really missed Demolition Derby. Also, SR3 ties them more to the storyline by giving some of the games distinct looks.  For instance, the Snatch missions are not always about picking up Hos depending on where you start them.  I also loved the new minigames, especially Professor Genki's Super Ethical Realty Climax.
It's been awhile since I've played such a fun game, so it's hard to complain about it.  I guess the difficulty could have been increased because it's even easier than SR2, and SR2 is easier than GTA III, Vice City and San Andreas. If you get max respect, for instance, you can buy perks that make you invincible.
I guess I should switch to Hard difficulty from now on, but I can't always tell when that's a good idea because I grew up playing older games. This is a small gripe, however, because I don't generally play fun sandboxes like this for the challenge.
Overall, it's a great game and I highly recommend it.

To tell you the truth, I was not expecting too much from Portal Stories: Mel.
I based my low expectations on the fact that it was fan made and not developed by Valve.
Having now finished the game, I owe Prism Studios a sincere apology for my lack of faith.
This game/mod/whatever you want to call it is so well made that it feels almost on par with both of the main games.
The writing is top notch and it's full of that trademark dark humor that the series is famous for.
I often found myself stopping and having a laugh at the hilarious art pieces scattered throughout the levels.
When I completed it, I felt that Mel's tale could be considered canon. It is that good.
There is one aspect of the game that may polarize players though - the difficulty.
In my opinion, there are no easy puzzles. It is assumed that the player is an experienced Portal-er and therefore all situations you find yourself in are either intermediate or downright complex.
It does not start easy then gradually up the challenge as was the case in the previous games.
The good thing here is that you get plenty of well designed levels that will potentially keep you occupied for hours depending on how fast you can solve them. Also, in the words of the developers themselves, none of them will require ridiculous ninja moves to solve, only logic.
There are some very minor complaints I had while playing. However for the low price of free (since you are a person with great taste in games you will already have Portal 2 in your library and that is the only requirement for getting this mod), they are not even worth mentioning.
If you are a Portal fan, this is more than worth your time.

Plants vs Zombies (PvZ) is a very fun and addictive Indie game that had me playing for countless hours. It involves simple "tower-based" strategy in defending your house against zombies by using various plants as a line of defense. It includes a number of unlockables and mini-games that are made for quick 'n easy entertainment - ideal for laptops. It it also best ran in windowed mode as the game's resolution is fixed.

I seriously didn't expect to enjoy this as much as I did. I knew it would be good, but not THIS good. Everything is top-notch quality (except maybe the voice acting, but that's still not bad at all). The visuals are gorgeous, the writing is fantastic, the classic Portal 2 style humor is still there (sometimes, some jokes fall a little short), and the gameplay is brutally difficult.
When I first started, I got stuck in the first chamber for a good 15 minutes before giving up. I closed the game and almost lost interest completely because I'm terrible at puzzle games. Fortunately, I decided to give it one more shot and finally figured it out after another 10 minutes. I did okay for the next few chambers until I got stuck again and ended up finding a walkthrough. I hate to admit using one, but I truly couldn't figure out some solutions (which I blame myself for being terrible at puzzle games for, not the game itself). For the most part, I only needed the walkthrough to get through a single part of a chamber which would lead me to find the full solution on my own, so I didn't need to rely on it too many times.
At the very end, when you see the final cinematic, it dawned upon me just how large scale of a project this really was. Four years of development, and it was well spent. One of the best Valve game mods I have ever played.

Before the credits roll you'll catsit a tiger, play a hilarious text adventure, get a sex change, hack up Mexican wrestlers with a chainsaw, visit a Tron-like computer world, and participate in many other ridiculous leisure activities. Saints Row the Third can be accused of being many things, but repetitive isn't one of them.
Some games create atmospheric worlds that attempt to draw you in with moving stories about characters seeking a second chance, or cast you as troubled superheroes who push themselves to the limit to fight evil. Saints Row: The Third is not like those games. Rather, it's the kind of game that gives you weapons called apocafists with which you can punch people, instantly making them explode in a bloody mess. The Third won't impress you with knockout visuals, move you with an absorbing story, or engage you with challenging combat. What it does, better than just about any game before, is embrace the idea of an open world as a place for play, constantly giving you access to awesome new toys and providing you with no shortage of exciting opportunities to use them.
One thing you definitely shouldn't ignore is the main story. Within just the first few missions, you plummet out of a plane and into an airborne shoot-out, skydive into a penthouse that belongs to a rival gang, use a UAV drone to call in guided missiles on tanks, and more. The missions eventually become a bit predictable for a while, serving as introductions to the other activities and diversions available to you in Steelport. But before long, they get wild again, packing in numerous surprises before culminating in one of two outrageous final missions.
Saints Row: The Third is buoyed to great heights by terrific mission design and by the remarkable assortment of vehicles and weapons it gives you with which to take over Steelport. Whether you're buying up property to increase your hourly income, cruising the city in your favorite vehicle to collect photo ops, drug packages, and sex dolls, or punching people to bits with those crazy apocafists, there's rarely a dull moment. Saints Row: The Third succeeds tremendously at delivering its unique brand of raunchy, outrageous fun. If you have an appetite for this particular kind of absurdity, you won't be disappointed

Portal Stories: Mel is a big improvement over Aperture Tag. Not to mention there is no price tag on this one.
The question is therefore not whether if it's worth the price but rather, if it's worth your time. The answer is quite starightforward: If you enjoyed Portal and Portal 2 and want some additional, quite challenging levels you need to look no further.
Portal: Prelude, Aperture Tag, Portal Flash Map Pack all fall short when compared to this one.
The mod offers a fresh and suitable soundtrack, in addition the attention to detail encourages exploration in similar ways that Portal 2 does.
New and creative mechanics are introduced that make for a fresh experience even for hardened Portal veterans.
If you are new to the Portal franchise, I recommend you come back after finishing Portal and Portal 2.
Unfortunately, the mod also has its shortcomings.
I've found that several puzzles only offer rather un-intuitive solutions, leaving you unsatisfied even after you finally solve a puzzle.
In addition, as creative as the puzzle mechanics might be, the exact opposite happens when it comes to story and writing.
The antagonist is rather dull and generic when compared to the history of absolutely epic antagonists in the vanilla Portal games. It removes any ultimate satisfaction when completing the game and makes for an anticlimacting ending.
The mod also overuses jokes we've already heard from Portal 2 with very slight alterations (such as guessing passwords), thus taking away any uniqueness in terms of dialogue.
Story sequences such as shutting down turret-production or escaping test areas from the overseeing AI left me with a bit of a "I've seen this before..." feeling.
I would rather that the devs don't attempt to redo Portal 2 but instead create their own game with unique dialogue and characters.

I don't know how to write a game review, so I'm going to show my favorite Fish Pie recipe
Ingredients
400g skinless white fish fillet
400g skinless smoked haddock fillet
600ml full-fat milk
1 small onion
, quartered
4 cloves
2 bay leaf
4 egg
small bunch parsley
, leaves only, chopped
100g butter
50g plain flour
pinch freshly grated nutmeg
1kg floury potato
, peeled and cut into even-sized chunks
50g cheddar
, grated
Method
Poach the fish. Put the fish in the frying pan and pour over 500ml of the milk. Stud each onion quarter with a clove, then add to the milk, with the bay leaves. Bring the milk just to the boil – you will see a few small bubbles. Reduce the heat and simmer for 8 mins. Lift the fish onto a plate and strain the milk into a jug to cool. Flake the fish into large pieces in the baking dish.
Hard-boil the eggs. Bring a small pan of water to a gentle boil, then carefully lower the eggs in with a slotted spoon. Bring the water back to a gentle boil, with just a couple of bubbles rising to the surface. Set the timer for 8 mins, cook, then drain and cool in a bowl of cold water. Peel, slice into quarters and arrange on top of the fish, then scatter over the chopped parsley.
Make the sauce. Melt half the butter in a pan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 min over moderate heat. Take off the heat, pour in a little of the cold poaching milk, then stir until blended. Continue to add the milk gradually, mixing well until you have a smooth sauce. Return to the heat, bringto the boil and cook for 5 mins, stirring continually, until it coats the back of a spoon. Remove from the heat, season with salt, pepper and nutmeg, then pour over the fish.
Assemble and bake. Heat oven to 200C/fan 180C/gas 6. Boil the potatoes for 20 mins. Drain, season and mash with the remaining butter and milk. Use to top the pie, starting at the edge of the dish and working your way in – push the mash right to the edges to seal. Fluff the top with a fork, sprinkle with cheese, then bake for 30 mins. Make up to a day ahead, chill, then bake for 40 mins.

The third installation of the Saints Row series offers for mass-scale gang wars between yourself and 3 hostile gangs. You are leading the Saints to city dominance thorugh your new branding and product known as 'Saints Flow'. This game includes more of a comedy element than the previous 2 installations, and has bigger explosions, higher intensity gunfights and a narrative that's actually pretty awesome.
The gameplay handles just as well as you'd expect from a Saints Row game. The gunplay feels somewhat floaty yet satisfying to use, while the driving maintains to be as exciting as ever, whether being chased by the new binary opposites known as STAG, or a hostile gang.
The graphics are not of the highest quality I might expect from the third installation of the game, but they are of course satisfactory. The game feels as though its AAA, and the sounds compliment the aesthetic of gang warfare nicely, but don't expect anything incredible from the graphics in Saints Row: The Third.
The narrative of Saints Row: The Third is slowly drifting away from the idea of straight up gang warfare, and seems to be heading towards a much more comical series. While some fans may prefer the wacky stunts of Dr. Genki and the huge comedy edge to pretty much every mission, other fans may argue that the more traditional gang warfare theme is slowly heading out of reach, and that may not be for the better.
The game has an extensive story mode, and once you've completed this mode, you're free to roam the city causing mass destruction, helping to clean up the streets (yeah, right), or just have an all out war with the local military. The choice is yours, but this game definitely offers you a happily ever after mode, just Saints Row style.
The multiplayer gamemode is simple in theory. You may play through the standard campaign with one companion if you wish, which definitely has its benefits. Having a freidn play alongside the story with you definitely opens up more enjoyment for Saints Row: The Third, and I'd highly recommend you do this. But don't get me wrong, the game is still enjoyable with just one player, too!

I love Portal 2 and this is a really well made mod but it has a few problems in the level design and story department.
The problems witht he level design is that way too often you get stuck in a puzzle, trying to think what you have to do, when the solution is just white panel that isnt very visible. I spent so much time trying to solve puzzles and advance rooms just because the progress panel was not visible or in an awkard place. Also the fact that there are no new visuals apart from a brief moment in the intro (which is wayyy too long) and the old portalgun, makes this feel really stale and just...more of the same.
The problem with the story are two.
1. Virgil always sees you, always talks to you and overexplains everything making the non puzzle sections feeling super hand-holding and removes the mystery of whats ahead. He always says what you will find ahead and the only unexpected thing is a fire or debris blocking your path. Even he points out how annoying it is that theres always an obstacle when you try to go somewhere
2. The second and biggest problem is that the story is just portal 2 with, unfortunatly, NO originality at all. Everything that happens and every setpiece is just taken from portal 2.
a. Intro is just the Aperture version of half life 1 intro but with less interesting things to look at and an annoyingly slow train.
b. Cave johnson says cave Johnson stuff, i think everyone pretty much had enough of his snarcky comments. Why do we need him say 50 more instead of something interesting that develops a plot and character? He just says reiteration of stuff he already said.
c. Then you have the core that helps you, act silly and pretend that everything is fine.
d. Then he says that everything has gone to hell and he needs you help so both of you can escape. (Is there ever gonna be a first person puzzle game where the facility is not collapsing around you and you dont have to escape it?)
e. Evil AI shows up that unfortunatly has absolutly no character and sounds like a default transformer. He of coarse wants to kill you so you dont escape and you have to stop him bla bla bla. Its just the same story again.
f.
g.
h.
i.
j. Nothing you do connects in any way to the main story. I know its a mod but good writing (or more like fanfiction in the case of mods) can make an interesting story that connects to a prexisting element of the original story. Like, off the top of my head, how about have Virgil go mad because of something related to the evil ai and become the corrupted angry core you see in the end of portal 2? Just make something that ties even a small part of your mod to the original story.
All in all, i am unfortunatly really disapointed by this. I was hoping it would add something more besides just new puzzles but unfortunatly thats all it is. Dont expect something really new here. Just the same things reused and retold. But hey if you love portal then give it a go. Just dont forget to lower your expectations.

Did you like Portal 2? Did you feel Portal 2 didn't challenge you enough? Well good.
Portal Stories: Mel is the Portal 2 mod that you've been waiting for.
Immersing yourself in the large scale maps is probably the first thing you'll notice upon playing the mod. Each map seems almost endless at times, with plenty of room for looking around and exploration. The attention to detail at some parts really makes you think, "wow, this is just a mod?" The easter eggs hidden throughout only add to this experience, adding cruel jokes and other references on your way to the next puzzle.
And the puzzles. Oh my Gaben the puzzles.
Coming from Portal 2, some of the puzzles in Portal Stories: Mel make Portal 2 look like it was full of tutorial puzzles. All 6 hours of playtime I have (upon writing this review) were spent just trying to beat the game. There are puzzles in this beautiful mod that will cause you to stop, look at varying walls, repeat stuff among the lines of "but if that goes there then... well wait what about..." and scratch your head for a good few minutes. I loved Portal and Portal 2 for the puzzles, and this mod only refreshed and continued that love.
As for the looks of the mod, the main thing you need to remember is that this mod runs on the Portal 2 branch of the Source Engine. No new shaders or game-changing mechanics, just everything you've come to know and love from Portal 2. The portal gun in this version has its playfully yellow coloring and intriguing model, and the player model is that of Mel, the olympian sent on the interesting, puzzle-filled journey through Aperture Laboratories. This mod was just an overall beautiful compliment to the Source Engine.
In the end, this
mod is definitely worth the time to try. It took four years to create this wonderful piece of art, and in my opinion, should have had at least a $5 price tag, as I would have happily paid that much to play it.

Portal Stories: Mel is an absolutely awesome mod for Portal 2, and a definite recommend. The story is really quite compelling, and the voice acting in the game is great. While the Cave Johnson sound-alike was obviously not JK Simmons, it was a pretty good impression and captured the personality of Cave Johnson very well. As for level design, well, if you're a hardcore Portal fan, you can't go wrong. The puzzles on this mod were absolutely dumbfounding and really, really complex, and forced me to think a lot more about interacting with old mechanics in new ways to solve the puzzles. It made the vanilla games mechanics very refreshing. I will say, however, that I was forced to resort to the devs' official youtube runthrough of the mod a couple of times, and some of the puzzles' solutions did feel rather cheap or far too vague. Unlike Portal 2 itself, the mod's puzzles lack clear direction and assistance to the player in the form of various arrows, lights, or other indicators.
As for the story, most of the mod takes place in between Portal and Portal 2, but that's all I'll say about that. The story doesn't feel particularly tied-in to Chell's story, but seems to focus more on a new couple of characters that romp around the Enrichment Center dealing with a different AI menace while trying to escape.
The graphics are just as good as they were in Portal 2, and a great attention to detail has been made. Mel's animations with the portal gun in first person feel very smooth and realistic compared to the somewhat stiff and lifeless animation of Portal 2. The new (or old) portal gun design was given a lot of love, and looks really wonderful with some funny little details, like the jury-rigged zero-point energy device with a paper clip. It's also clear the mod's art designer(s) put great effort into the atmosphere, as lots of brand new posters and blueprints adorn the offices of the Enrichment Center, and really feel like they could have been in the vanilla game, too. The modders also took advantage of Source's great lighting effects and put a lot more light sources and foliage in the mod, in order to take advantage of more powerful PCs out there, and make an aged game look great.
All in all, I have to give this mod a 9/10. While it really is a great experience, what felt like cheap or completely obscure solutions to far too many of the puzzles in the game detracted from the overall experience, and frustration was felt very often. After seeing the solutions to the more frustrating puzzles on YouTube, my reaction was never an "oh, of course," or, "wow, I'm an idiot for not seeing that." It was more like "what, who would ever have thought to do that?" Despite what felt to me as needlessly complex and obscure level design, this mod is still a must-have for owners of Portal 2. It is free, and adds a great experience to a somewhat aged game series that has been without a new installment for over 3 years now.

Saints row 3 is a really quite decent little sandbox game that really surpassed my expectations, I was expecting a "Pound land" Grand theft auto but what I got was so much more...
It's the closest to completely open ended that I have ever personally played...dont want to play the main quest?; Dont. want to spend the entire opening of the game taking over the map and kicking all the rival gangs off the map?; go right on ahead...send a hulking great brute out to attack the local police for the hell of it? be my guest friend. it's all there and more.
Probably the best way to describe this game would be imagine if instead of making GTA 4 They had instead taken the sillier elements of GTA Vice City and San Andreas and ran with them. it's unbridled silliness and thats something I can really get behind...
The control setup is more or less Identical to the GTA games on PC  and feel really quite tight there are some moments where things get a bit slippy and one or two little bugs that will send you car/helicopter/boat flying through the air on fire...but there few and far between and rarely if at all interupting to game play...
Other than that the only other issue I can place with this game is that occasionally finding your bearings can be a bit awkward with a few minutes spent trying to figure out which way up your facing and where the missle launcher shots are coming from...other than that though its solid...
Your character is fully customizable and being british that meant dressing up in a bowler hat and John lennon glasses as a cockney  to deliver the biggest british♥♥♥♥♥whooping steelport could offer...
Graphically it's matured fairly well, it's about on a par with GTA4 but where it shines is the wonderful colour that is present in the game, quite a few games released in the past few years seem to have made friends with Brown and dreary colours that often make things feel a bit washed out But SR:3 glistens with high contrast colour which is a really welcome addition especially in HD.
Personally I would say this was the best game of 2011 just for it's sheer variety and replayability, there are so many quests and sidequests and offshoots and random events that you'll easily rack up 20+ hours just doing the basics (Which are great in themselves!) Definately reccommended pick it up, get to grips with it and im sure you'll love it.

Saints Row: The Third is a bit of a confusing title for me, and it's hard to actually have an opinion one way or another given how I feel about the title.  I had played Saints Row II to completion (never SR I), and loved it, so naturally I purchased this game.
They are not nearly as alike as you would expect a sequel to be.  Whereas Saints Row II was more serious, actually had a relatively feasible story-line similar to that of GTA games historically, Saints Row: The Third, scraps a lot of that in favor of a balls-out, ridiculous storyline full of questionable material.  Whilst I find the game fun, and enjoy the humor nearly all of the time, I can't help but think that they might have betrayed the series a bit by taking it in this direction that I had never expected.  Yes the game is fairly well made, but there are times I miss the serious nature of the Saints Row series.
The story itself is absolutely insane.  There are clones of dead people, oversized people hopped up on god-knows-what, guns that shoot bees, purple ♥♥♥♥♥♥ as melee weapons, strippers, escorts, and tons of other outlandish material.  Not to mention the obvious sexualization of the entire story in regards to all genders.
That said the game itself is fun, funny, and memorable for the most part.  The story is fun and ridiculous enough to keep your attention as long as you find the material to be funny.  The games controls/mechanics are well executed and fluid.  The driving is smooth and as fun as ever and the movement controls in vehicles (flying, land and water) and on foot alike are all nicely done.  Nothing is ever hard to control or clunky, the whole game feels really smooth.  The only time the combat mechanics seem to feel a little annoying is when you are knocked down and have to stand back up because sometimes you'll spend a while on the ground while your character just lays there, but you'll get up eventually.
The graphics are nice, but a little glossy for my tastes.  The soundtrack includes actual songs licensed from real artists, unlike the new GTA V and some other newer games, which is one of my favorite features.
The game also has a lot of side missions and fun DLC to participate in from everything to good-old insurance fraud by playing in traffic, to being the driver for an escort with a high profile client in the vehicle to participating in a new (and insane) game show the GenkiBowl.
That said, there are even fun, normal moments with some friends of your characters' in a vehicle with you and you'll sing along to music on the radio or whatnot, just some fun tidbits that seem pretty normal and humorously out of place in the crazy world the game created.
All in all, if you can handle the humor, then the game is worth it.  It's a fun experience that you don't have to take seriously whatsoever, which is sometimes all you need for a while.  If you are a fan of the original two games, you'll have to adjust to the direction they took with the game, but it's not all that bad really as long as you've got a sense of humor.

This mod is so well made that it feels like it's a real Portal game. It's about as long (maybe a little shorter) than Portal 2 and it is amazingly well made.  There's so many details that make it feel like Valve made it. It is VERY difficult, almost never borrowing tricks from the official Portal games, and not having tutorial levels. This is inteded for those who have played Portal and Portal 2, which I consider a good thing because the game is rife with references to those two. It fits neatly into the canon of the Half-Life and Portal universe while adding a lot of nice worldbuilding. The writing and voice acting are top notch and the relationship between Mel and Virgil feels great. I really felt like Virgil was a real person that played the game with me. If there's anything I can complain about it's that I felt like Harry Callaghan could've put a little more energy into Cave Johnson's voice. I absolutely loved the way you spoke, Mr. Callaghan, but I felt like some lines needed a bit more energy in their delivery. This is merely a nitpick, though, it was still very enjoyable to hear Cave Johnson. The only thing that could've made this game better was a passing Strider* in the scenic final cutscene (that was wonderfully animated, by the way!).
10/10, definitely worth the wait. A big thank you to all the wonderful people who worked on this wonderful mod!
*Then again, maybe a Strider would've affected canon should Half-LIfe 2 Episode 3 and/or Half-Life 3 reveal that by the time Portal 2 takes place, the Combine at large has been defeated. Might've been for the best not invoking that Half-Life reference.

At the time of this review I have about 37 hours logged on the game, and this is opinion based.
Saint's Row: The Third is the third installment of the Saint's Row series. While the first two games attempted (and successfully) paralleled the GTA series, for this game, Volition and Deep Silver went a different route. With wonderful consequences. Please note, if you're looking for a serious game, Saint's Row: The Third is not for you.
The game is a sort of reboot of the franchise, and I was able to pick it up easily with no prior Saint's Row exosure. Immediately I was thrown into the gameplay as opposed to being bogged down with tutorials. While many people could see that as annoying, for those of us who have had experience playing computer games of similar genre it was nice to not be told a bunch of information we already know.
The first mission is hilarious and off the top, and just when I thought the game was going to mellow out I was shown just how wrong I was. Without spoiling too much, here's what you can expect: Furries, wrestlers, hookers, autotune pimps, large naked men, d!ldo swords, being turned into a toilet, and mega brothel home bases.
As for some of the more behind the scenes features.
Pros:
+Character models both in and outside of cutscenes are well done.
+There are massive amounts of customization.
+There are a bunch of things to do outside of the main questline.
+Multiple endings and decisions that affect the rest of the game.
+An easy to use combat system.
+DID I MENTION D!LDO SWORDS????
+The dialogue is brilliant.
+A lot of effort goes into facial expressions and background characters when cutscenes are involved.
Cons:
-Collision detection can be buggy at times, particularly when cars are involved.
-The enemy and ally AI is pants on head ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
-Accidentally injuring an ally during a fight will cause them to abandon and attack you. While there is a way to get them back on your side, allies such as Oleg will likely kill you before you are able to calm them down and have them rejoin you.
-Model deformities. While this doesn't impact the game, sometimes characters or NPC's can glitch out with horrifying results.
-Spawning bugs. For the PC version this has been almost fixed with updates, but occasionally an important NPC will STILL spawn inside a wall making them impossible to kill or interact with, forcing you to restart from an earlier save.
-THE BELGIAN PROBLEM. This mission doesn't work properly on slower running computers and if your computer isn't powerful enough to run it, it is impossible to progress past it. Even turning down all my graphic settings my computer was BARELY able to handle it. The worst part is, the mission is only a couple hours into the game story wise.
TL;DR
Saints Row is like a silly version of GTA with a lot of stuff to do and customization out the wazoo. It has a lot of good things, and only one major game breaking glitch.

One of the things that bugged me the most about Portal 2 was the lack of challenging puzzles in the vein of the late test chambers in Portal 1. Part of this may be due to Portal 2's many new testing elements, which reduced most of its chambers to tutorials. Portal Stories: Mel only introduces one element (death fizzlers), and it's fairly incidental, only being used in a handful of puzzles. Because of this, Portal Stories: Mel can get away with focusing entirely on challenging puzzles, and boy are they a doozy! These tests will challenge any veteran Portal player, yet are always well-designed rather than creating fake difficulty from hidden portal placements.
Meanwhile, the storyline is surprisingly complex for a fanmade mod. Mel and Virgil's attempts to thwart AEGIS aare countered at every turn, and the eventual finale to the conflict is adrenaline-pumping and satisfying.
The visuals and sound are astounding as well. Aside from the great Hammer-fu done with existing assets from Portal 2, many impressively well detailed new assets exist as well. A highlight is the tacky 70s portal gun Mel acquires at the beginning of Chapter 2. The newly composed music is on par with Portal 2's fantastic soundtrack, while carving out its own style as well. I'd say the great music was instrumental to keeping me from going mad during the game's trickier puzzles.
Overall, a fantastic game, and it's free! If you played Portal 2, and even if you thought its puzzles were too simplistic, I highly recommend giving this a try.

Maybe the game would have been better if it eased you into it more. Reintroducing the gels for fans that hasn't touched the original in a long time, and maybe teaching the player a new set of logics would have helped tremendously i think.

Not expecting anything, I was hoping this would be a decent set of puzzles to occupy me for about an hour. I didn't expect to spend longer on this than I did Portal 2's singleplayer, god damn am I impressed.
The pacing and voice acting were really well done, and there was a pretty damn good Cave impression. The dialogue fit pretty well with the world, and overall the story was pretty good.
But holy crap, the level design. It was FANTASTIC. A lot of people were complaining that it was overly difficult, and while it was hard, it was the good kind of hard.
In a good puzzle game like this, you know exactly what you need to do, but have to figure out how to do it. In a bad one, you're at a loss as of what you need to do. Out of all the levels, this doesn't fall into the trap once. Every level is extremely clear in the goal, but some are brilliant in their complexity. Of the three times I was stuck for more than 30 seconds, two were me being an idiot, and one was a brilliant little puzzle. Honestly, I cannot praise the level design enough, it's simply sublime.

This is pretty much the perfect mod for anybody who's completed Portal 2 and is hungry for more. First of all: Gameplay. In terms of dificulty this game pretty much carries on from Portal 2, there's no tutorial, the first few chambers of this mod are roughly on par with the last chambers of Portal 2 in terms of difficulty, which makes sense when you consider the mod's target audience. I found the difficulty curve had a bit a weird fluctuation in the middle, getting easier and then harder again, but that could just be down to how I personally think, as the difficulty of a puzzle game is subjective. Overall I'd say actually gameplay is excellent, it carries on some ideas from Portal 2 whilst also ramping up the difficulty, and the tests were completely logical, with no "WTF, THAT was the solution!?" moments.
The game had great atmosphere and made great use of the art assets from Portal 2 as well as it's own original ones. It had an original soundtrack that suited each chamber/event perfectly. It was also interesting to see their take on what the original AHPD (Aperature Hand-held portal device) would have looked like, and I think it was well designed, with the perfect combination of retro and Sci-Fi, whilst making it look like something old Aperature would have produced.
The story and characters were good, to the point I wouldn't mind if they were actual cannon, heck, I'd actually quite like it, they did a good job of explaining how Portal 1 carried into Portal 2. Virgil was a pleasant surprise, from the launch trailer I thought he was just going to be Wheatley 2.0 but he is actually a well fleshed out character who seems believable. His voice acting was great and very convincing. AEGIS played his role well, as he came across less of a character and more of an impending doom with a deep voice, which is exactly what he was supposed to be, anything else would have essentially been a GLaDOS wannabe. He was Aperture's anti-virus, and you were malware, simple as.
All in all, this was excellent, it took me longer than Portal 2 (but I think that was purely down to it being harder rather than having more content) and both the story and gameplay were satisfied, and it was well polished other than a few minor glitches here and there (such as a cube dispenser that was rendering in front of some glass when it chould have been behind, and the time I escaped an elevator). The fact that this is free makes me question how on earth  Aperture: Tag costs £3.99 when this is infinitely better in almost every aspect. If you loved the Portal series and want more, download this mod in an instant, just ensure you've topped up on either brain food or patience because you'll need one or the other to complete these chambers.

SR3 is absolutely hilarious and you'll be laughing so hard you cry at some parts of the game. There are so many just perfect lines spoken by what I personally find to be some of the greatest voice actors out there. If you play a female character then you'll have Laura Bailey (Jaina Proudmoore) telling people to go *** themselves and murdering civillians. That and the tens of hundreds of pop culture references will have you either laughing so hard you cry or rolling your eyes and sighing. That's the thing,SR3 is a great leap from SR2/1 as now it's more silly and so the story and characters have to change to reflect that decision. There's less of the brutal gangster from SR2 and more of the♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bat swinging psychopath who yells pop culture references in almost every mission if you can catch them.This is all up to opinion but I think they balanced it pretty well. There's enough silly to last you a lifetime but also some more serious moments that may impact you as a fan of the series.
Theres probably close to 20-25 weapons in SR3,a solid amount I would say. Each weapon has up to 4 stages of upgrades you can buy from the gun store.Each one will upgrade the weapons with small cosmetic accessories like a scope or a silencer and will add bonuses that aren't neccessarily appropriate for the accessory.You may buy the upgrade for one of the assault rifles which adds a suppressor and you'll get extra damage.There are plenty of absolutely absurd weapons as well,in typical SR fasion, such as the♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bat,the RC Car Controller,and the Sonic Launcher.Each one of these special weapons will make you gidddy with joy when you're running around RC'ing cars into gas stations or beating a car till' it explodes with a huge♥♥♥♥♥♥♥These weapons fit with the settting and you progressively get more along the way as well.
Oddly enough for an open world game,the main story missions in SR3 don't have you trekking across the map in a blatent attempt to increase the game's longevity(*Cough* GTAV *Cough*).You actually are involved in some pretty fun missions and you get to pull some crazy stunts like fighting in a huge ground war with all factions grabbing a piece of the action,defending a skyscraper from VTOL's or even murdering zombies and meeting the mayor.The game's missions for the most part are fun and actually have enough context backing them up for them not to be just-go-here-pick-this-up-and-come-back type missions. They also have lot's of juicy dialogue for you to sink your teeth in while driving or watching one of the always entertaining cutscenes.
SR3 takes place in a city by the name of Stillwater,also the place where SR2 took place if I recall correctly,and man it really feels broken up and bland. The city is divided up into areas and each different gang has their own turf. One minute you're in one gangs turf and the next the entire area,scenery,and enemies just changes. This could have been executed well but I feel that they kinda botched it here. The world also feels very devoid of anything to do. Of course,there's your typical boring filler missions that every open world game seems to have these days but other than that you're pretty much limited to the story or just causing random carnage.

I have had so many graphical problems with SR3. From blatent ones like render distance being about as far as a ruler or the incredibly repulsive texture quality to smaller ones like trash not rendering properly in my experience the game is filled with graphical issues. First off,the game looks excruciatingly dated and has some real bad rendering issues. The rending issues made me want to vomit anytime I was in a helicopter or just in a position where I could see above the city. The rendering issues make every area look blurry and copy-pasted while simultaneously making it harder for me to play the game itself. I had multiple occurances on the final mission where I would be driving down the freeway and then out of nowhere a Luchadore truck would render in front of me and ram straight into me. These problems could be ignored if they were on a lesser scale but these are just too many and too blatent for a AAA developer.

Had this game for a long time now its about time I make a review for this.
This game for me is a gem in my library, others may not feel the same and may find this game a bit boring, slow paced or too large for their preferences especially those who prefere fast paced combat and arena shooters like CSGO, Battlefield or Call of Duty for example. However if you're a patient guy with a "GOOD PC" (seriously though this game will **** your PC if its bad, I've been there) who likes simulations and want to get on that next level of tactical and strategical depth i'd definately recommend this game.
Another mention I would like to add about the community is that there are groups who play this ranging from casual groups playing and creating mission for some fun to those who run military simulations (milsim groups) who take the game extremely seriously and try to base their group and structure based on the actual military. I do recommend that you get a group of friends or join a community because it makes the game experience more better and its up to you what kind of group you would prefere to join.
A little recommendation from myself if you want to join a group and I may seem a bit too harsh but try to avoid newly upstarting groups because ive seen many fall apart because of pointless and petty ARMA DRAMA which can even happen in the big groups. Try and find the big and/or successful groups as they're mainly guaranteed to last the longest and who have a closer community than those who keep opposing oneanother.
Most of the pros are also advertised and praised by Bohemia Interactive (obviously) but heres the facts they wont praise.
Just to finish things off finally is the fact that you'll really need a strong PC to play this game. If you don't then your frames will be reduced to something like 5fps basically playing the game in a 19th century slideshow with colour. In my oppinion the recommened specs to play the game is actually the minimum because the bigger the scenarios the more demanding they are. This game solely runs on the mathematical coding which your processor is responsible for handling. The weaker the processor is the weaker your performance will be.
If you want to play Arma then a good processor is the most important component to have. Next up is ram so it can process and help operate your components to ensure the game runs optimally. Then the graphics which is the least important because although this game has pretty graphics going from a fairly old gpu to a gtx 980ti for example will actually only increase the frames by 5-10fps.
Thanks for reading and I hope I shed some light about this game :)

Had this game for a long time now its about time I make a review for this.
This game for me is a gem in my library, others may not feel the same and may find this game a bit boring, slow paced or too large for their preferences especially those who prefere fast paced combat and arena shooters like CSGO, Battlefield or Call of Duty for example. However if you're a patient guy with a "GOOD PC" (seriously though this game will **** your PC if its bad, I've been there) who likes simulations and want to get on that next level of tactical and strategical depth i'd definately recommend this game.
Another mention I would like to add about the community is that there are groups who play this ranging from casual groups playing and creating mission for some fun to those who run military simulations (milsim groups) who take the game extremely seriously and try to base their group and structure based on the actual military. I do recommend that you get a group of friends or join a community because it makes the game experience more better and its up to you what kind of group you would prefere to join.
A little recommendation from myself if you want to join a group and I may seem a bit too harsh but try to avoid newly upstarting groups because ive seen many fall apart because of pointless and petty ARMA DRAMA which can even happen in the big groups. Try and find the big and/or successful groups as they're mainly guaranteed to last the longest and who have a closer community than those who keep opposing oneanother.
Most of the pros are also advertised and praised by Bohemia Interactive (obviously) but heres the facts they wont praise.
Just to finish things off finally is the fact that you'll really need a strong PC to play this game. If you don't then your frames will be reduced to something like 5fps basically playing the game in a 19th century slideshow with colour. In my oppinion the recommened specs to play the game is actually the minimum because the bigger the scenarios the more demanding they are. This game solely runs on the mathematical coding which your processor is responsible for handling. The weaker the processor is the weaker your performance will be.
If you want to play Arma then a good processor is the most important component to have. Next up is ram so it can process and help operate your components to ensure the game runs optimally. Then the graphics which is the least important because although this game has pretty graphics going from a fairly old gpu to a gtx 980ti for example will actually only increase the frames by 5-10fps.
Thanks for reading and I hope I shed some light about this game :)

I'm going to be honest, because if you're anything but in a review, then what's the point.
I didn't enjoy this very much.
One of the reasons for this was because some of the dialogue was not really very good, and I found it to be a bit cheesy, more so than in other Portal games, but the main reason I didn't enjoy this is because of the puzzles.
There is no learning curve as in other games, you just immediately start off with the gels at your disposal instead of using the portal gun normally for a bit and then getting the gels later, and I found the puzzles to be simply tedious. They used far too many steps when there could have been much less to do, and the puzzles were to complex from the start, they didn't ease you in, or have any sort of tutorial for how things worked as they would in the start of other games, and I think one of the reasons they did this was because you're expected to have played the other games first, which I have, but from the standpoint of Mel, the character in the game, she has never been here before or done any of this, so how would she know? She wouldn't.
Also, at what point did she get the long fall boots? I know the voice over said she had them, but when were they put on? She was asleep the whole time prior, so she wouldn't have done it herself, and the facility seemed ruined, so it wouldn't be very likely that someone came in and put them on for her.
It may seem like I'm nit picking, but I simply don't enjoy this game for these reasons, and unfortunately, I can't really recommend this game.

Saints Row: The Third is a 2011 open world action-adventure video game developed by Volition and published by THQ. It is the third title in the Saints Row series. As in the previous games, the player-character leads the Third Streets Saints gang in a turf war against three rival gangs using a variety of weapons and vehicles in single-player and cooperative play. The series, and especially this title, is known for its crazy scenarios and lighthearted gameplay. It was released on November 15, 2011 for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360, and later abroad.
Gameplay :
Saints Row: The Third is an action-adventure game played from the third-person perspective in an open world, such that players explore an unrestricted environment. Similar to the premise of the previous Saints Row games, the player's goal is to lead the Third Street Saints gang to overtake its rival gangs in the city turf war. While the protagonist is the same, the game introduces a new setting, the city of Steelport, with its new gangs: the Morningstar, Luchadores, and Deckers, together known as the Syndicate. Once The Syndicate is defeated, the government's Special Tactical Anti-Gang unit (STAG) is summoned to quell the Saints. The Third is the first in the series to intertwine the narratives of its three-gang structures, and also presents the player with story-altering decisions.

Since Portal 3 can not happen thanks to the events of Portal 2, Portal Stories: Mel is the spiritual successor to Portal 2. While the overall game is short with only having around 20 levels, Portal Stories takes its liberties in showing Aperture Science when it was still alive and well as well as fill in the gap between Portal and Portal 2.
The story introduces you to two new characters: Mel and Virgil, an AI robot similar in looks to Wheatley. You play Mel and you are an Olympian who went to Aperture Science for a 'short' sleep study in their new deep sleep chambers. You awake to find that you are no longer in the 1900's but much further in the future. You acquire a portal gun very quickly and begin to do puzzles while Virgil attempts to get you out. While lacking the humor of Portal and Portal 2 it makes up for it by having Virgil have some of Wheatley's characteristics but while being smarter than Wheatley and more caring towards you.

I wish I enjoyed this, and for a free mod it has a lot of producation value going for it.  The opening chapter does a great job of setting the scene, and there's the zany humor of Cave Johnson perfromed by a decent soundalike.
For what I was looking for though, Portal Stories: Mel didn't do it for me. After 130 hours or so of playing Portal 2 maps, I needed more than simply challenging maps to get me interested again.  Portal Stories appeared to have that narrative hook that I was looking for, and it's there that the game let me down.
For me, an enormous part of my dislike comes down to the story, particularly the voice acting of Virgil. I found his voice annoying to listen to, and it only grew more aggravating over time. Little changes in the story-the vast bulk of what you hear is simply a variation of Virgil telling you over and over that the path ahead is blocked, and that you'll have to find a way around it.
Puzzles were much more challenging than the main game, but I felt little satisfaction from solving them because I'd simply get annoyed because it meant I could expect to hear more of Virgil's lines and learn that, once again, something ahead was broken down and we would have to take another detour.  The added time it took to solve these puzzles prevented a smooth flow of the story, and after working for 45 minutes on some puzzles, I wanted more than a few rote lines delivered by a voice actor I didn't appreciate.
Had the narrative included more variety, ditched Virgil, or at least maintained more of the humor from Cave Johnson at the beginning of the game, I would have enjoyed the game more.
This review probably only applies to those people who, like me, feel like they've played so much Potal 2 that the standard gameplay is no longer as compelling. And, obviously, it's entirely subjective that you'll feel about the the story as I did, particulaly about Virgil.
If you're looking for nothing more than a succession of good looking and challenging maps, you'll love this mod.  If you wanted something more, you may be disappointed.

For a free mod that draws inspiration from one of Valve's most acclaimed series, Portal Stories: Mel is a commendably ambitious labor of love that finds itself stumbling in the same pitfalls as the similar Portal: Prelude from six years prior.
Narratively, the mod places the player in the perspective of Mel, a familiar heroine hailing to the original multiplayer character that would compliment Chell in co-op before the idea was scratched and replaced with the now iconic Atlas and Peabody.
The story sandwiches itself immediately before Portal 2, mimicking similar story elements to its source material. There's a quircky, overly-analytical personality core; a malevolent AI encased in a gargantuan lair, and endless series of crazy Aperture Science™ puzzles.
Unfortunately, the story is marred by the immensely frustrating level design and flat character motives. While the voice acting and writing is passable for an amateur fan-made effort, the actual game itself makes the iffy story an unwelcomed guest.
While there were moments early on that left me hopeful and laughing at the dialogue and design, as things progressed toward more puzzle elements and less story, my enjoyment waned.
The level design starts becoming teeth-grindingly difficult by the midway point, and doesn't ease up save for a few brief minutes of unskippable exposition. You'll be mashing the tilde key and toggling sv_cheats 1; noclip back and forth due to the unclear puzzle design.
The foggy objectives for each puzzle are victim to the mod designers missing one of the core functionalities of the original Portal games' design: Making experimentation fun, while working toward a clear goal.
More often than not, you will find yourself swimming in barriers and funnels that make things needlessly complicated for almost no reward. Beat one chamber, hear some exposition from a voice actor who can't pronounce the villain's name properly, enter another chamber with the exact same elements. Rinse and repeat till your identity is consumed by proving you're better than the game.
Additionally, one small mis-step will find you repeating several steps of finnicky portal placement and puzzle efforts. If a cube didn't land on a button properly or a laser isn't precisely lined up with a recepticle all of your hard work is for nothing.
I can't fault the efforts of the developers, they clearly did their homework. Sadly, the game leaves an unresolved frustration in place of the climax, and by the time the story becomes interesting, it's over. For something I was really excited about playing, I am sad to say this isn't worth the headache.
Pass on this unleass you're a Portal die-hard with a slice of masochistic tendencies.

Plants vs. Zombies Game Of The Year Edition (PvZ) is a tower defense game that appeals to casual players as well as hardcore RTS enthusiasts.  You protect your home backyard and roof from a zombie infestation with a garden you plant on the fly on a 2D, 5 row landscape.  You are given a plethora of tools to help you fight back the slow moving invaders, but you can only select a limited number of weapons you can take in to each battle.  The tools you have at your disposal include resource generators, shooters/lobbers, bombs, and walls, each having advantages and disadvantages.  The zombies aren't just limited to the slow moving walkers, but rather get wildly creative, and force you to adapt to all of the different tools you have available.  No single tool is over powered.  That is where the game has the greatest strength, earning the GOTY award.  The overall balance is so well done, that the replay value is incredibly high.  Beating the game on normal (which is pretty easy) unlocks the hard mode.  Hard mode is still not too hard, but the hardest mode is within the game is Endless Survival, where the waves don't stop coming.  Casual gamers will appreciate the challenge of hard mode, but the real die hard RTS will find the real gem of Endless Survival, where you can prove your skills through endurance.  The highest my friend has ever achieved is 107 waves, which is a bit harder than it sounds.
In short, if you were ever curious about how tower defense games work, you should check it out.  If you are an avid die hard rts fan, you owe it to yourself to check this one out.  What I'm saying is, check it out.

A really fun light hearted tower defense game with a healthy campaign and a lot of extra modes and mini games. The object of the game is to defend your home against zombies with plants. Sun jewels fall from the sky and you click on them. This gives you currency to buy plants to set them up in the path of zombies. If a zombie makes it to your house, then it eats your brain. The zombie enemies are diverse and quirky. Your plans that you defend your house with are equally fun and quirky.  The campaign is split into 5+ major chunks (front yard, pool, night yard, night pool, roof and so on). Each one of these major chunks has a few levels in it. Each level consists of 3+ waves of zombies marked on the bottom of the map. So its like an endurance sort of thing until the final wave.
There is plenty of reason to come back and keep playing. Especially since you pick your own plants. The mini games offer a lot of diversity. Things like bowling for zombies, whack a zombie, be-zombied, and even a mode where you need to make it through as zombies to eat brains. There is a ton of fun here for a week and then in a year another week of fun and in another year another week of fun. This isn't the type of game you play forever, but it is a lot of fun while it lasts.

I'm sure everyone and their mother has probably played this game already (mine has, for a fact) but I'll post something anyway, just in case. This is a fairly average flash game in the tower-defense genre. It's a somewhat illogical mashup of your towers (plants) versus the attackers (zombies), in which you are defending your lawn, backyard, and roof against the attackers who want to eat your grains, then your brains. The levels are static and only change every 10 missions, which means the variation in gameplay comes from your tower composition and the rock paper scissors you play with the different kinds of zombies. It's not particularly well balanced as some plants are plain useless and most are situational at best. The actual campaign is quite short (but still manages to feel overly long), but you accrue resources at such a slow rate that you can be sure that there's a lot of grinding to be done to unlock everything, for those people that enjoy that. Somewhat underwhelming as a PC game, but probably worth playing on your laptop or iDevice.

FIRST let me just say, this mod is HARD. If you're not familiar with Portal mechanics I don't think you'll enjoy this. There is no build up and working your way into harder tests like Portal 2; you're thrown in the deep end straight away. So be prepared to get stuck on puzzles when you play this.
The start of the game is awful, you literally stand in a train/elevator for the first 5 minutes. Anyways after that you get a good story, decent voice acting (probably the best voice acting i've heard in a portal mod). The music is top notch (Put a smile on my face when I saw it was done by Harry101UK) and the level design is high quality, for most tests. Difficult tests isn't a bad thing, in fact, I felt a sense of accomplishment after I had completed a test. Seriously, its rewarding finally figuring out the trick to completing a chamber. However, there were a couple of awful tests/sections. Occasionally you just get thrown into a skyscraper of a room with stuff going on everywhere, no sense of where to start. You kind of just fumble around those few sections.
I would have also liked to have seen a little breakup from the test solving at some point. Just to construct some more story and give the player a bit of time to relax. It was kind of a barrage of difficult test after difficult test. Anways, I really liked the whole ending area. I thought it was original and well made.
Basically I had a lot of fun playing this. This really is worth your time playing if you're a portal fan like me. Plus this is FREE! This makes Aperture Tag look like a pile of dog...(Yeah you finish). This is how a mod should be done. This is a portal mod done RIGHT. Seriously really enjoyable, well thought out game and level design. Definitely worth a play.
(Oh, did I mention its FREE!)

Positive:

I honestly can't think of anything. I mean, I have general problems with this version of the sandbox genre (for instance, there's no way to be a propa "Good Guy" or "Bad Guy", although, to me moral ambiguity is kinda a plus). There are some software-level issues, I guess, so...

I was reluctant to try out this Also-Ran among the Grand Theft Auto crowd. I was finally convinced to try it out because of Jim Sterling... and my view of his game opinions has been forever cemented. Yeah, I might not always agree, but holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ does the guy have taste.
Anyway, sucking on Jim aside, this game is fun - pure stupid fun - from the very moment you start a new game. There's literally nothing to complain about, which is something you can't say about the game's obvious inspiration. It really is, within the confines of the mechanics put forward, an open game. Be who you want to be, do  your thing, have fun. Games like this are what make the "sandbox" metaphor true.
It's not without issues, of course. You're trapped within the established paradigm - you're a gang leader, you do gang stuff. There's no opportunity to play the opposition from any angle. To me, that's a minor complaint, especially since the "gang" in question is so popular and beloved, that you literally begin the game in a reality show featuring the gang's antics.
The port is... fine. It's obvious that the game was meant to be played on consoles. Better grab an Xbox controller before you play, is what I'm saying. It also isn't as pretty as what could be supported at the time - a critique made even more obvious by the sequel - but it looks fine for what it is.
Final Opinion: Is it worthe me money? Hell yeah. It's a fantastic lark with more cusomization than you could ever hope for. Don't wait for a sale - get it now.
Unless you already have the PS3/360 version - in which case, don't bother. Nothing that matters has changed.

Excellent! I really can't believe something so polished and with so much content was released as a free mod.
Gameplay follows standard Portal 2 conventions, but is significantly more challenging than the original game. Personally, I liked the added challenge. My only complaint is that some solutions are a bit counterintuitive and require physics abuse, like repeatedly spamming a portal with an excursion funnel to slowly move a cube over a pit. Perhaps the developers will modify a few of the chambers after receiving feedback from the wide release?
The voice acting is very good for a community-made mod. I think the largest complaint is that the voice of Cave Johnson (is naming him really a spoiler if he starts speaking within minutes?) is imitatated, but what do players really expect? His voice is critical for the story, and J. K. Simmons doesn't work for free. I liked Virgil, who narrates for most of the game anyway.
If you liked Portal 2, this is a must-have addition!

I was really looking forward to playing this, It looked great, and clearly the developers have put an incredible amount of work into it. Personally, I was far more frustrated than anything else.
There were very few moments where I could say that I actually enjoyed myself. Visually, it's very inconsistent. Especially in the beginning, various areas have a very blocky, rough sort of look to them, but most of the prettier areas do a good job of matching Portal 2's style. The voice acting and writing didn't do anything for me, and I didn't find it terribly interesting. I appreciated what it was trying to do, but matching the style and wit of Portal 2 without resorting to lazily copying it is a tall order. Aside from a few moments of begging for silence, I didn't mind it much. My bigger issue was with the puzzles themselves, which quickly went from interesting to challenging to impenetrable. Generally speaking, most of them don't feel intuitive. The arrangement of the chambers themselves don't do much to guide or help the player, and many feel like working a game of chess backwards to figure out the steps required to get to the obvious solution. As another reviewer noted, solving most of them felt like a relief rather than rewarding.
I feel like this should probably have a disclaimer, so I'll just that I might not be the target audience, and that maybe this is geared more towards people who can chew up and spit out the Workshop maps with ease. Personally, I found it harder than those, much harder than Portal and Portal 2's official campaigns, and far less fun.

I just finished this, and the experience comes HIGHLY recommended with only a few small caveats:
Gameplay: 9/10. The puzzle design meets that of Valve in the original game in my book, and the difficulty far exceeds both full games. Not for the faint of heart. One frequently used mechanic is turning Emancipation Grilles on and off with buttons, which might start to grind on some.
Story: 8/10. It's clearly a well-written story that a lot of thought went into, and I enjoyed it, but it felt very intrusive. I spent large portions of the game listening to dialogue, and there are 2-3 cutscenes that feel different from the rest of the game. (Like the ending of Portal 2) Still enjoyed it.
Voicework: 9/10. Would have been a perfect 10 but for the fact that, at the beginning, they actually use clips of Cave Johnson with their own voice actor. And that man is NOT Mr. J.K. Simmons, so I felt a bit of "They changed it so it's bad" coming on. However, all of the other characters are excellently voiced with full personality ranges, to the point where they feel like they have just as much of a right to be there as Glados and Wheatley.
Soundtrack: 8/10. The music is excellent, the only issue being that it plays constantly. This can be a bit frustrating if you're stuck for a long time. But still, the music is probably some of the best music to be stuck in a test chamber with.
General Craftsmanship: 10/10. The whole area where it takes place feels just as dynamic as Portal 2 did with its moving panels and test chambers on rails. A pleasant change from other Portal 2 mods, which shows delicate effort in every nook and cranny.
Length: 9/10 Just like the second game, it tries to avoid staying its welcome. You never get long sequences of test chambers that look the same, due to the great world design.
Value: ∞/10. It's FREE. I don't even know why you need a review, it's free. There's not even a WAY to spend money on this game! Download it now!
