Portal Stories: Mel is no standard Workshop mod. Mel features 22 fully custom-made levels, full voice acting, custom animations and cutscenes. All for the price of free. I got almost eight hours of play but they rate it at around 6-10 hours. It’ll depend on how good you’re at logic puzzles. It really feels like they went all out even with a custom soundtrack done by Harry Callaghan, whose Portal music video parodies you might have seen on YouTube. Said music was pretty good too. One little note here though: getting achievements for how you die really isn’t much of an achievement.
You’re Mel, an Olympian who decided to take up Cave Johnson’s offer to be a test subject. Mistake number one. Mistake number two was agreeing to be put to sleep for “a short period of time” for a test. Well, we all know what’s going to happen then. Mel is awakened many, many years later by a personality core: Virgil. Virgil needs your help and is willing to work with you to help you escape Aperture. So, escape the deep depths of old 1950s Aperture, survive the machinations of AEGIS and the rather difficult puzzles. Oh, who’s AEGIS? An AI that views you and Virgil as a threat to Aperture. We humans are really good at being threatening when all we want to do is escape. GLaDOS is nowhere in sight, so, you’ll be left wondering: what happened?
If you’ve played any of the Half Life series or previous Portal games, Mel seems to take a lot of inspiration from those titles. The opening scene has you in a cart going into the Aperture Laboratories facility much like Half Life 1. The end level feels very inspired by the ending of Portal 1. So does the character design of AEGIS. Structurally, Mel holds its own as a side-story to the main universe of Portal, even if it isn’t an official story. The voice acting is a bit wonky at times. Cave Johnson is perhaps the most out of place because it’s another actor trying to imitate him and well….it’s not the best impression.
Virgil is a different take on the personality cores. He's a lot more grounded than previous ones I've encountered, no real eccentric personality quirks. Though he's a nervous little ball of steel, he's the type that you can trust to pull you through a situation. AEGIS on the other hand is an uncaring, solid and unstoppable personality. There's no arguing with him, there's just avoiding or out-thinking him. Which you'll have to do quite a bit.
It’s not the most perfect story on the planet and it doesn’t stray far from the formula that Portal 2 created but Portal Stories: Mel still holds its own. Somehow, getting to explore more of old and new Aperture again is a treat. Even though we already did this in Portal 2, they somehow make it compelling again. It's hard to lock down why that is. There is certainly a lot of dialogue to keep it moving along. Though it doesn’t hurt that it has been awhile since I played Portal 2’s campaign.
You’ll need to have played Portal 2 before you take this game on. These guys aren’t messing around. The puzzles are tough, even the first one, and while logic based, can be extremely trying at times. It didn’t help that some felt really unintuitive either. I’ll admit it, I looked up the official guide for solving the puzzles often. For the most part, I had the puzzles largely figured out but there was always that one step to the solution that I couldn’t get my mind around. I’m not sure whether to blame the mod or my own inability. Either way, this is a game designed for veterans.
So, if you’re not looking for a challenge, don’t take Mel on. The levels are all about the same level of difficulty, which is hard, and they don’t lighten up at any point. Well, except maybe the end levels….no...no they’re a little more frustrating than difficult. I didn’t like the usage of the turrets at the end. The basic idea is to use turrets to take out objects in a large room and do it within four minutes. Considering how easy those turrets are to knock over and you have a room full of objects to move around...well, let’s just say that’s something I’d like to not see repeated in the future. To be honest, the mod feels almost a little too long with how many puzzles it has.
Mel uses the same engine and settings menu that exists in Portal 2, so I won’t repeat myself. Go read the Portal 2 review for my PC Settings Menu breakdown. While it does use the same engine, I noticed an odd hitching to the movement that I couldn’t fix. It mostly went away as I progressed through the game and/or I ignored it. I also noticed some random slowdowns but I’m not going to blame the mod for it, I might have had the graphics settings a bit too high.  No crashing or game breaking bugs were encountered in my playthrough. For the most part, (minus a Linux launching problem) the mod seems to be working fine for most other players.
For me, Portal Stories: Mel is what I really enjoy about the modding community. Though I don’t expect every single mod to come with this much creativity, time and effort, Mel has it in spades. If you’re looking for a new challenge in Portal 2 from the modding community but want a quality that feels on par with Valve, Mel is the mod to get. Well done to the developers, I enjoy my time with this one. Even if the puzzles were aggravating at times.

Portal 2, after having it and playing it for about two or three years, I'm starting to get bored of it. The Portal 2 Workshop is even putting me to sleep. Wait, what's this?  Another free mod for Portal 2, but this time it has no new custom elements, and it doesn't steal the PETI like Aperture Tag and Thinking With Time Machine? Let's check it out!
Portal Stories: Mel is an interesting new mod for Portal 2. It looks like Portal 2, it plays like Portal 2, it sounds like Portal 2, it even SMELLS like Portal 2.
If you have played both Portal games, you'll probably notice that this game is a prequel for both. It takes place before Portal (for a little bit), and it takes place right before Portal 2. The gameplay is like any other Portal game or Portal mod, go through your portals and finish the test. The gameplay is not really anything different, but it still has that Portal pizzazz.
It has a new brand new story that fills up a lot of plot-holes that Valve left in Portal 1 and 2. Word on the review street says that there are some problems with the story but I haven't noticed any of them. The story is great, it really fills the gaps between both Portal games. The voices for the characters were also very well chosen.
The puzzles are logic based, which is unlike any Portal 2 community made map I've seen but this is a good thing. The puzzles do get very, very, VERY hard really, really, REALLY fast, but hey, at least they're logic based! You might find yourself ripping your hair out during one of the tests. The puzzles are hard, but they are easier to finish once you get the whole logic thing and once you understand that these things were made for people that are REALLY good at this game.
Great mod, great story, great puzzles, and great gameplay. But I do have one question, WHY ISIN'T THE STORY FROM THIS THING CANON?!?!? WHY?!?! Come on Valve! Buy this thing from Prism Studios and the Portal Stories Team, make it longer, and call it Portal 3! PLEASE!!!
The mod is considerably short, but it's a mod, so what do you expect? The increasingly hard difficulty does make up for its 5 chapter-long shortness.
Overall, this thing is so good it should be at least a Portal 2.5 made by Valve.
And, it's FREE! So what do you have to lose, the time you're spending NOT playing this awesome mod? This game NEEDS your attention! GET IT NOW, YA DUMB-DUMBS!
9.9/10 Would solve science again.
P.S. The music is friggin' awesome too.
A Very Long P.P.S. Before I go, there is something else you should know about this mod. Since Mel doesn't focus on new elements or have any at all, the creators of this mod did the same thing that Valve did while making Portal 2, although it's not the same case, there are some similarities here, check this out: During early development of Portal 2, Valve was going to focus only on all new mechanics and made this thing called "Eth-Stop", which was the focus of development for 3 months. Eth-Stop did get some positive feedback, but every play tester was disappointed at the lack of portals in the game, so Eth-Stop was cut and put aside for use in another game and Valve put their focus back on the whole portal concept. So what the Portal Stories Team did in Mel was the opposite of what Valve did when creating Eth-Stop, instead of focusing on brand new mechanics (or making any at all), they instead stuck to their guns (Valve's guns) and tried to capture what Portal 2 had and what made it great: Portals. On the contrary, the guys who made Thinking With Time Machine and Aperture Tag did the exact opposite of what both of the other two parties did, they instead focused on all new mechanics and barely added any portals in their games. So in reality, Portal Stories: Mel is actually better than both Aperture Tag and Thinking With Time Machine, because of what Portal Stories is, Portal Stories: Mel, PORTAL, no questions asked. Some interesting fun facts, don't you think?

While playing Portal 2 with dev commentary, there's one commentary that talks about puzzles needing to be hard enough to let folks feel smart when they get the "ah HA" moment, but not so hard they feel like idiots that are faced with constant road blocks.
Mel's Story is the latter. The puzzle design is just ... I had to give up. I guess if you've burned through a lot of user-made puzzles and can wrap your mind around every obtuse possible way to solve things then you can grind through this. Likewise, if you can manage the brain space to connect the dots on huge puzzles, you'll also have an advantage. For a casual Portal player, though, you're going to suffer. It's rather unsatisfying playing a game when you have to constantly alt-tab out to see a walk-thru. I felt rather like an idiot most of the time on the puzzles, and it frustrated me enough to give up mid-way.
This is sad, because it looks good. It provides a new back story. They have Cave Johnson sounding like a younger, less confident version of himself that just started a company (as opposed to the cocky guy that progresses you through the Portal 2 levels as he and his company age).
Folks complaining that this doesn't seem to have the polish to look and feel as original Portal 2 .. Portal 2 was created by a game design company that made their own engine, knew it inside and out, had lots of people with advanced degrees doing mathmatecal comp sci magic to produce crazy effects, and generally abuse everything about their game engine they could for the time it was made. This mod team is not a professional team. But, they put a lot of TLC into this mod, and compared to most mods this is amazing. (hell, half the mods folks make start out and fizzle never to see the light of day, so seeing a mod of this caliber make it to finalization is amazing.)
My gripe would be that they tried to recapture too much of Portal 2 to such an extent that they don't set themselves apart. The new AI core is basically a Wheatly clone without a British accent. He tries to use that "oh, don't worry about that serious stuff happening" sense of parlay that made Wheatly Wheatly. So, basically recreating a core that seems like a shadow of Wheatly's personality seems like a missed opportunity. The initial Aperture intro with Cave Johnson talking you through, while entertaining, seemed a bit much. He talks to you around every turn, even though you're just one person walking through an entire area. He even talks to you as you enter a town ... a single person entering a town, yet Aperture seems to want to take the time to have Cave talk to you. It then eludes that he's watching your experiment directly, because he seems to know when everything is setup and good to go, yet other conversations suggest its all prerecorded. So, I guess he's prerecording his assumptions that everything is going fine as he walks you through things?
Likewise, the beginning of the mod where Cave Johnson spends too much time walking you through the most mundane activity ever (walking around a level to find the place to go) is then contrasted by puzzle levels that offer no help whatsoever. First the game wants to talk your ear off explaining every door, elevator and step to take ... then it just leaves you alone, clueless, as to how to solve a puzzle. The contrast was just .... stark.
Again, I like this mod. I like that it was made, finished, and they put effort into it. But, ultimately, he seems they spent so much time on style they forgot the core substance of the game ... that substance is that people need to be able to solve puzzles, otherwise they feel like idiots and give up. They don't need hand-holding, but they need enough clues to figure out on their own within a little bit of time what should go where and what to do. Otherwise they either fallback on a walk-thru in order to progress the story (to which they basically negate the purpose of the game, which is to enjoy puzzles), or they give up and quit all-together ... which defeats the reason to even make a mod; a mod that people give up playing is basically a mod that had a lot of time spent on it to become utterly pointless (since folks won't play it).
If you're a hardcore Portal fan, and have a lot of user-made levels under your belt (especially the hard ones), give this a try. If you're a casual player and just want more story, expect to swallow your pride and bust out a walk-thru.

Alright, so Arma 2 was better in a lot of ways, but that doesn't stop ArmA 3 from being a great game in it's own right.
And to prove that point, here's a list of fun things you can do in ArmA 3:
You can enjoy an immersive black ops mission.
You can create a mission on the fly, watching your friends struggle to survive against an entire battalion of enemy troops.
You can practice parachuting from a falling helicoper.
You can bounce a tank into orbit, just like the original Halo.
You can create a complex loadout mixing and matching the right weapons with the right attachments to suit the task at hand.
You can destroy a helicopter with nothing more than a rappel line.
You can fill a backpack with three hundred glowsticks.
You can hold a midnight glowstick rave, while getting shot at by the rave police.
You can realise that your complex loadout was completely useless and spend another hour trying to perfect a new one.
You can strap a goat to yourself and use it as a meatshield.
You can surprise your friends by rigging a go-kart with explosives.
So, disclaimer: All of these things I have either done personally, am planning to do in the future, or have witnessed a friend do.
The ArmA series has always been very flexible, and ArmA 3 has really capitalized on that aspect. It might struggle to reach 30 fps sometimes, but in spite of that, it's still a highly enjoyable experience.

I have been playing ArmA since it was Operation Flashpoint, almost 16 years now, and the game has been upgraded, with better graphics, better AI, more weapons, bigger maps, but the core game is unchanged, and is still as amazing and breathtaking today as it was in 2001.
No other game has yet to succeed in making me flat out panic for a full minute. ArmA has done it to me several times.
The landscapes are now huge, and so beautiful that I've quite often thought that many of the maps would be great holiday destinations if only they weren't on fire. The lighting takes this pretty good landscape and makes it spectacular, with weather that can change a scenario from a quick firefight to a long and miserable hunt for enemies or even your own position.
The AI are evil, sneaky horrors, presenting a challenge few other games have come close to.
But where ArmA really excels is in a good session of multiplayer, with a bunch of other semi-serious or above players it is unsurpassed in realism and breadth of scope, and really few other games have come close to the level of involvement and camaraderie of ArmA. It is truly a different and better experience from almost anything else out there, such that it makes people the sort of fervent fanatic I sound like in this review.
If you want to have a go at being in a war from the comfort of your own home, this is as good as it gets. Real enough to put you off the whole idea of actually going to war.

Alright, so Arma 2 was better in a lot of ways, but that doesn't stop ArmA 3 from being a great game in it's own right.
And to prove that point, here's a list of fun things you can do in ArmA 3:
You can enjoy an immersive black ops mission.
You can create a mission on the fly, watching your friends struggle to survive against an entire battalion of enemy troops.
You can practice parachuting from a falling helicoper.
You can bounce a tank into orbit, just like the original Halo.
You can create a complex loadout mixing and matching the right weapons with the right attachments to suit the task at hand.
You can destroy a helicopter with nothing more than a rappel line.
You can fill a backpack with three hundred glowsticks.
You can hold a midnight glowstick rave, while getting shot at by the rave police.
You can realise that your complex loadout was completely useless and spend another hour trying to perfect a new one.
You can strap a goat to yourself and use it as a meatshield.
You can surprise your friends by rigging a go-kart with explosives.
So, disclaimer: All of these things I have either done personally, am planning to do in the future, or have witnessed a friend do.
The ArmA series has always been very flexible, and ArmA 3 has really capitalized on that aspect. It might struggle to reach 30 fps sometimes, but in spite of that, it's still a highly enjoyable experience.

I have been playing ArmA since it was Operation Flashpoint, almost 16 years now, and the game has been upgraded, with better graphics, better AI, more weapons, bigger maps, but the core game is unchanged, and is still as amazing and breathtaking today as it was in 2001.
No other game has yet to succeed in making me flat out panic for a full minute. ArmA has done it to me several times.
The landscapes are now huge, and so beautiful that I've quite often thought that many of the maps would be great holiday destinations if only they weren't on fire. The lighting takes this pretty good landscape and makes it spectacular, with weather that can change a scenario from a quick firefight to a long and miserable hunt for enemies or even your own position.
The AI are evil, sneaky horrors, presenting a challenge few other games have come close to.
But where ArmA really excels is in a good session of multiplayer, with a bunch of other semi-serious or above players it is unsurpassed in realism and breadth of scope, and really few other games have come close to the level of involvement and camaraderie of ArmA. It is truly a different and better experience from almost anything else out there, such that it makes people the sort of fervent fanatic I sound like in this review.
If you want to have a go at being in a war from the comfort of your own home, this is as good as it gets. Real enough to put you off the whole idea of actually going to war.

After almost 1200 hours I must say that this game is the absolute king of military simulators. It really shows the superiority of PC gaming compared to consoles in all aspects including graphics, modding, controls and the average IQ of players +much more. If you're looking for an arcade shooter such as CoD of Battlefield, don't buy Arma. You think that Counter-Strike is close to Arma series? It's nowhere near (CS of course is a competitive tactical shooter but Arma is a simulator).
Arma 3 although mainly being a mil-sim game, it's not only that. The original singleplayer campaign and missions created by Bohemia Interactive are very little part of the game. If I would have to say one thing I would like to be better in Arma it would be more singleplayer campaigns/missions. Most of the content creation responsibility has been left for the community. Modders and mission file developers have done a huge job in creating so much playable content in to the game. Mods bring you new missions, vehicles, weapons, maps and much more. Server developers have created gamemodes such as battle royale, king of the hill, altis life and hundreds of others. Want to roleplay as the drug lord of Altis, commander of the Police or a poor fisher in Kavala? Sure. Maybe you just want some random fast-paced shooting? Sure. Or maybe you want to be a soldier in a mil-sim group with communications and realism to the max? Sure.
There are currently four official maps in the game. Greek island Altis being the HUGE 270 km2 main map, followed by the small Stratis. Apex DLC brings you Tanoa, the beautiful jungle map being almost as big as Altis. As of June 2017 they also added a rework of Malden to Arma 3, sized between Stratis and Tanoa.
+Graphics
+Realism
+Variety of gamemodes
+Mods
+Maps, beautiful and big
+Multiplayer, depending on gamemode and server very mature players and communicationing in mil-sim groups (cringey for cod players ofc)
+A lot of vanilla weapons and vehicles.
+You don't need the DLC's. You should get Apex but other DLC's are small.
+The only sp campaign and it's soundtrack
-Bad optimization, you will need a high end pc to run it. And even then you're not reaching stable 60 fps in multiplayer due o performance highly depending on the servers
-Low amount of official missions and other playable content
-Hard to learn, harder to master. There are A LOT of controls and learning the bullet drops etc. is not easy
-Controlling AI units if playing singleplayer is very poor
-AI is stupid overall but the game shines in multiplayer

While the story is definitely set out well and Virgil, the new core, is a joyful addition to the game this can often be undercut by the difficulty of the game, as it will often take vigorous methodical work to even get close to an answer for a course that is something you wouldn't even consider as it goes against the puzzle solving mechanics of the original two games.
However, the voice-acting, interactions with Virgil and the very pleasant old timey feel of the game helps to push you through it, and at a total of zero dollars makes for an enjoyable journey through the old Portal universe that you've been missing for four years. I would definitely recommend it for those who've been waiting for Portal 3, as it may be the closest we'll ever get, but maybe not for those with short patience, as it is definitely a game of hard thinking.
The ending is superb, it has a beautiful soundtrack, Virgil is a splendid character to take you on the adventure and in the end the game just FEELS like a new Portal game. It is fantastically well done and fantastically difficult.

Plants v. Zombies is the definition of a modern casual game.  It is super accessible, has simple but clean graphics, and offers a variety of play modes.  It is a tower defense game for those who have never heard of toweer defense games.
The story mode progresses steadily until the end, adding tougher zombies as you ascend levels, but also rewarding you with different defensive plants.  In secondary plays, the story mode adds more challenges as your crazy neighbor starts to pick some of your plants for you.  For those who find story or puzzle mode too hard, you can always stare at your garden, water all your plants and poke your snail.

After almost 1200 hours I must say that this game is the absolute king of military simulators. It really shows the superiority of PC gaming compared to consoles in all aspects including graphics, modding, controls and the average IQ of players +much more. If you're looking for an arcade shooter such as CoD of Battlefield, don't buy Arma. You think that Counter-Strike is close to Arma series? It's nowhere near (CS of course is a competitive tactical shooter but Arma is a simulator).
Arma 3 although mainly being a mil-sim game, it's not only that. The original singleplayer campaign and missions created by Bohemia Interactive are very little part of the game. If I would have to say one thing I would like to be better in Arma it would be more singleplayer campaigns/missions. Most of the content creation responsibility has been left for the community. Modders and mission file developers have done a huge job in creating so much playable content in to the game. Mods bring you new missions, vehicles, weapons, maps and much more. Server developers have created gamemodes such as battle royale, king of the hill, altis life and hundreds of others. Want to roleplay as the drug lord of Altis, commander of the Police or a poor fisher in Kavala? Sure. Maybe you just want some random fast-paced shooting? Sure. Or maybe you want to be a soldier in a mil-sim group with communications and realism to the max? Sure.
There are currently four official maps in the game. Greek island Altis being the HUGE 270 km2 main map, followed by the small Stratis. Apex DLC brings you Tanoa, the beautiful jungle map being almost as big as Altis. As of June 2017 they also added a rework of Malden to Arma 3, sized between Stratis and Tanoa.
+Graphics
+Realism
+Variety of gamemodes
+Mods
+Maps, beautiful and big
+Multiplayer, depending on gamemode and server very mature players and communicationing in mil-sim groups (cringey for cod players ofc)
+A lot of vanilla weapons and vehicles.
+You don't need the DLC's. You should get Apex but other DLC's are small.
+The only sp campaign and it's soundtrack
-Bad optimization, you will need a high end pc to run it. And even then you're not reaching stable 60 fps in multiplayer due o performance highly depending on the servers
-Low amount of official missions and other playable content
-Hard to learn, harder to master. There are A LOT of controls and learning the bullet drops etc. is not easy
-Controlling AI units if playing singleplayer is very poor
-AI is stupid overall but the game shines in multiplayer

There's really just something about this game. Easy to learn, as with many other PopCap titles, but this one's got a lot of meat to the story mode. Plenty of levels to get through and progressively more and more options become available as you go.
Control the plants on your front lawn and use their various powers to stop the invading zombies before they enter your house and eat your brains.
Humor is laced throughout this title, and it really is fun for just about any skill level, though the game becomes genuinely challenging the further you go in the story mode, and some of the numerous extra modes that unlock as you play will keep you busy for many more hours as you try to complete the various objectives.

Saints Row: The Third was actually my first introduction to the Saints Row series. It reminds me of a mixture of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas meets Rambo, with all the shooting, guns, explosions, and the body count you leave in your wake. I've heard negative things about the game over the years, which is why I avoided trying it, and now I regret that decision. Saints Row: The Third is non-stop action. From the opening scenes where you are committing a robbery gone haywire, to jumping out of a plane without a parachute and performing stunts that rival those seen from hollywood, this game is a lot of fun. Basically, you start off after choosing or creating your own character, as the leader of the Saints, a once prestigous gang, who now has no money, and no respect. Slowly you must work to turn around your fortunes and build a criminal empire.
While I did enjoy Saints Row: The Third, even on hardcore the game seemed a little to easy. Visually, it doesn't look bad for a game thats been out a few years now. The action scenes, were pretty good, immersive, and fun to both watch and play through. All in all it's a pretty good game.

This was a very impressive mod, featuring a full story, voiceover, and music.  It's also fairly challenging compared to the base game, but in a completely fair way where you have to carefully consider all of your available options with the tools around you.  Several times I got stuck and took a break out of frustration, but 15 minutes later I would get excited to go back in and try to figure out the puzzle.  It's rare to find a game that can so quickly overcome my frustrations!
The story is excellent, and the voice acting is good (though Cave Johnson is obviously an impersonator, and Virgil's accent throws me off a bit) and the music is just as good as Portal 2's, in my opinion.  The level design is visually on par with Portal 2, but I got stuck on scenery, fell through solid objects or just got somewhere where I wasn't supposed to go on several occasions.  Those events didn't detract from gameplay too much, aside form the occasion when it made it difficult to judge what was an wasn't a viable target to land on)
Overall, this was a fantastic game and one of the better mods I've played.  And it's free!   If you liked Portal or Portal 2 and want a challenge, I totally recommend playing this!

I'd been looking forward to this mod, and while I knew a lot of work had gone into it, I was still worried that something would be off--voice acting, characters, things not fitting with the official story, and so on.
My worries were completely unfounded. This mod is amazing.
The first thing that struck me was the environments. You start in a train ride into Aperture, and suddenly I felt like I was playing Half-Life for the first time. The train drove by different little underground stations, giving glimpses into what life there was like. And that was just the beginning. The town you arrive at, the Aperture buildings themselves, and even the testing spheres--everything completely blew me away. And yes, I know, you see the testing spheres in Portal 2. But you don't see them INTRODUCED like they are in this game. All of the environments are gorgeous--I spent ages exploring them and poking around wherever I could, and even though I've finished the game, I STILL haven't seen everything. Poke your portal gun wherever you can--there's a lot to see!
Then there's the new characters--Mel, Virgil, and a few others I won't spoil. I wasn't sure what to think of Virgil at first, but I very quickly grew to liking him. I was worried he might be an attempt at imitating Wheatley, but he's very much his own character, and a very good character at that. His voice acting is great, and his emotions really show through, which greatly helps certain scenes... He's also a very funny character and had me laughing at a few points. Mel herself is pretty cool too--while we don't get to find out too much about her, it's neat to see that she was one of the original Olympians that Cave Johnson hired. Her model looks great, too! As for the other characters... again, I won't spoil anything, but they're quite creative and cool.
The storyline is amazing, but I really can't say that much without spoiling it! It deserves to be experienced firsthand. But I will say that it does mesh with the canon timeline very well, so if you're someone who obsesses over canon details like I do, you won't have to worry here. Oh... and the story WILL make you feel things. Trust me, it will.
The music is also totally fantastic, which I fully expected, given it most of it was composed by Harry101UK! There's also an original jazz number, which is very very nice. I actually didn't realize it was an original song when it was first played, because it sounds so much like a 1950s jazz number! It fits in perfectly with 1950s Aperture.
As for the gameplay itself... You've likely heard this before, but the test chambers are hard. They're not unbeatable, but they are hard. Extremely hard. This is more difficult even than any mod or PeTI chamber I've played (or well, the well-designed ones anyway--I've played chambers in PeTI that were difficult because they were poorly designed, but that's not the case here--these tests are just HARD). It's very satisfying to finish the test chambers, and I was able to do many of them on my own (with a LOT of thought and a few headaches), but I also had to ask for help on a lot of them. If there's a downside to this game, it's that some of the test chambers are a little too hellish.
Other than that little detail? This mod is amazing. If you own Portal 2, you have no excuse--this mod is free, so get it! If you don't own Portal 2 on the PC, go watch a playthrough. DO IT!

I'd been looking forward to this mod, and while I knew a lot of work had gone into it, I was still worried that something would be off--voice acting, characters, things not fitting with the official story, and so on.
My worries were completely unfounded. This mod is amazing.
The first thing that struck me was the environments. You start in a train ride into Aperture, and suddenly I felt like I was playing Half-Life for the first time. The train drove by different little underground stations, giving glimpses into what life there was like. And that was just the beginning. The town you arrive at, the Aperture buildings themselves, and even the testing spheres--everything completely blew me away. And yes, I know, you see the testing spheres in Portal 2. But you don't see them INTRODUCED like they are in this game. All of the environments are gorgeous--I spent ages exploring them and poking around wherever I could, and even though I've finished the game, I STILL haven't seen everything. Poke your portal gun wherever you can--there's a lot to see!
Then there's the new characters--Mel, Virgil, and a few others I won't spoil. I wasn't sure what to think of Virgil at first, but I very quickly grew to liking him. I was worried he might be an attempt at imitating Wheatley, but he's very much his own character, and a very good character at that. His voice acting is great, and his emotions really show through, which greatly helps certain scenes... He's also a very funny character and had me laughing at a few points. Mel herself is pretty cool too--while we don't get to find out too much about her, it's neat to see that she was one of the original Olympians that Cave Johnson hired. Her model looks great, too! As for the other characters... again, I won't spoil anything, but they're quite creative and cool.
The storyline is amazing, but I really can't say that much without spoiling it! It deserves to be experienced firsthand. But I will say that it does mesh with the canon timeline very well, so if you're someone who obsesses over canon details like I do, you won't have to worry here. Oh... and the story WILL make you feel things. Trust me, it will.
The music is also totally fantastic, which I fully expected, given it most of it was composed by Harry101UK! There's also an original jazz number, which is very very nice. I actually didn't realize it was an original song when it was first played, because it sounds so much like a 1950s jazz number! It fits in perfectly with 1950s Aperture.
As for the gameplay itself... You've likely heard this before, but the test chambers are hard. They're not unbeatable, but they are hard. Extremely hard. This is more difficult even than any mod or PeTI chamber I've played (or well, the well-designed ones anyway--I've played chambers in PeTI that were difficult because they were poorly designed, but that's not the case here--these tests are just HARD). It's very satisfying to finish the test chambers, and I was able to do many of them on my own (with a LOT of thought and a few headaches), but I also had to ask for help on a lot of them. If there's a downside to this game, it's that some of the test chambers are a little too hellish.
Other than that little detail? This mod is amazing. If you own Portal 2, you have no excuse--this mod is free, so get it! If you don't own Portal 2 on the PC, go watch a playthrough. DO IT!

I wish steam had a middle for whether or not you could recommend a game. There are pluses and minuses here. It's a great community effort. It looks really good. But, it's pretty clear they did a poor job polishing it. The graphics are great. Seeing more of old apeture is also great. However, it should be noted that even gameplay needs editing. You're going to spend too much time in the opening walking.
When I say the game lacks polish...what I mean is: the cool thing about Portal, and Portal 2 were the visual cues in each of the level that helped you figure out the flow. What to do first, how to at least begin. None of this kind of polish is there in this title. The puzzles are fun. But sometimes you'll spend an inordinate amount of time trying to start. It can get frustrating after a time.
The voices are great, but I feel like the script...is a lot of "trying too hard". You have Cave and what amounts to a wheatley clone. Cave was well done, for a substitute...but they played it out a bit too much. A bit way too much. A sphere with a wholly different personality would have been better. Again, a good editor for the VO's could have solved a lot of these issues. Hopefully the team addresses this if they elect to do more in the future.
All in all though, it's not a bad game. But, I feel had they polished up the sequencing a bit more...as well as the voice scripting it could have been great. Don't pass up this game, but don't be too disappointed by it either.

Even after 10 years, there are people at Valve (approximately 10 in all) who still love this game and want to see ot thrive. Are the updates scarce? Yes. Do they make mistakes? Yes. Does Valve keep it alive for the money? Yes. But what matters is that people at Valve care about it to the point of not working on new projects such as Virtual Reality and instead dedicate their time to updating and fixing a ten year old game. Even with the arrival of new competition with varying degrees of success from dead (Battleborn), mild (Paladins), and extremely popular (Overwatch) and disaterous updates such as the infamous Meet Your Match update in July of 2016, TF2 is still alive and quickly and shows very little signs of becoming Battleborn-level dead anytime soon; I'd personally say that it still has a few more years left in it. The dedication shown by the team to keep the game alive and deliver new content and updates (even though it can take a year to create and release one due to the small size) is the reason why I nominated it for the "Labor of Love" award. Others might disagree, and I can respect that, but for me, it deserves AT LEAST a nomination in my personal opinion.

Although being a mod,
is an excellent follow up for those who desire for more portal after having played the first two official games. In fact, the whole mod has a overall great level of quality as you would expect from an official game. It's not perfect in any means, but tries its best at it.
It's too be warned tough, as negative reviews point out, this mod is indeed pointed towards more experienced portal players by using several mechanics that don't tend to be that obvious at first. Sometimes you might get stuck in some chambers trying to figure something that's actually pretty obvious. You probably should play some easier mods or workshop maps before attempting a challenge like this. In case you are up to the challenge, chances are you will actually enjoy it and feel very rewarded by the end.
Despite the difficulty, some of the things I found the strongest in the whole game was the overall presentation. The chambers in their specific architectures were very well done as well as the whole details and secrets that's the developers left on it. Soundtrack and Voice Acting are also top notch, and although one or another might sound off-placing at the times, they eventually build up your momentum to continue exploring the chambers. Voice Acting is really a plus, as it makes Virgil really feel like a more solid and stronger character than he already is. It's also a big plus that the developers found a way to make the game fit into the main lore without breaking or making anything official be non cannon.
In overall, I have to recommend this mod to anyone who wishes to have a bigger challenge at Portal's mechanics meanwhile enjoying a very decent presentation.

Take everything that was good and great about Portal 2 make it slightly clumsy and you have Portal Stories: Mel.
If your a fan of "old aperture" I highly recommend playing Portal Stories : Mel.
Valve managed gold with a couple "Cave Johnson" voice over lines, Mel comes a close second pulling entire levels worth of content out of those same three or four voice over lines.
The Story is top notch, the Art is great, The Companion Core is frankly less annoying than Wheatly, and Aperture feels like a facility.  Feeling like a facility is actually where Mel shines the best. A lot of the level design while ambitious was rubbish, but there was just enough of a light touch of Portal Two content that the whole thing jelled making it a part of Aperture.
Now for the bad.
-A lot of the level design was rubbish.
Mel totally flunked out of the "less is more" school of level design in a bad bad way.  Offices upon empty offices followed by more empty offices all using the same clutter far to close together.  Or the level has been tied into a knot so tight tracing the path is as important as working the puzzles. Note I say working not solving one mechanic is common to almost every puzzle...........sigh.
- NPC
I actually did a squeal of joy at the couple NPC in Mel. Then I cried that they were less animated than the turrets. Early on they had the perfect excuse to have it empty, or be ambitious with them. The middle ground they walked was very unfinished.
-Puzzles
I want to roll my eyes I really do. The puzzles do not scale well, and to be brutally honest I noclipped around more then a few midgame puzzles because of the abusive over use of emancipation grills. I get it using grills made the levels harder but there are other mechanics. The overall puzzle design is either recognizably Portal Two or the rooms have been made so convoluted the goal path of the puzzle has been obscured. There are even a couple places where guide images have been placed where it is bloody obvious changing the level to improve the puzzle was refused. Yeah "oh hey look here LOOK RIGHT HERE!!!!!!".
-Intro
The entire intro level is more or less a straight ripoff of the black mesa intro sequence in HL1. It deserved to be the training level where the bulk of the mechanics were explained but instead it was just nothing.
I still recommend Mel it's fun and looks great and has enough character to stand nose to nose with Valve's Portal.

Some people complained about the challenging puzzles, but honestly, if you have the ability to think with portals, you can finish them. My first casual playthrough took around 8 hours to complete, which is probably longer than most, but I enjoyed every moment. Except for when I was stumped on some of the puzzles.
The music, produced by Harry101UK, sounds like it's from Portal 2, and it always fits the setting, including funnel versions of the songs. The textures are high-quality and look, again, like it's from Portal 2.
I have legitimately no complaints with this mod. It's fun, challenging, and hilarious, as well as using water in a useful way, something very foreign, but very cool. This mod, overall, was worth the 4 years of development it took to make, and I loved it. Get this mod, or wait 'till 2056 for Portal 3.

Ok, so I don't write reviews very often... but every so often a game is so awesome that it prompts me to give it the praise it deserves. Portal Stories: Mel is one of those games.
I have not finished it yet, I'm on Chapter 4 but I have been loving this so far! This mod expands on the Portal storyline (and seems to do a great job of that), it features some areas that even the original 2 Portal titles don't, showing more unexplored areas of Aperture Science. It has it's own silly but ridiculously loveable personality core and of course a new AI enemy trying to hold you back as you move along. The puzzles are significantly more difficult than you'll find in Portal 2 and that adds a great set of new challenges to overcome.
Lastly this mod offers QUALITY! Yes, it's up there with the likes of Valve's own work. The map designs are gorgeous and massive and include all sorts of neat new types of areas. The Storyline is well done and fits with the existeing Portal storyline. The characters are funny and complex and the voice acting is quite well done, along with really funny and immersive dialouge. Immersion is something that most mods have a hard time achieving but this mod does it very, very well.
If you love the Portal games then you will love this! Expect a bit of a challenge, though, this mod is for experienced Portal players and has an environment and story that is sure to immerse you back into the world of Aperture Science!

Pretty Good Game Review Considering (PGGRC)
15 Hours to Complete (Played on Xbox 360)
TL;DR - It feels weaker and lazier compared to GTA but is a great sandbox to enjoy yourself from the start of the game.
In depth:
Performance - Solid because the graphics are above average. Will run of many old systems so no complaints here.
Graphics - Above Average. They are quite lack luster from triple A company. Textures in some places are extremely murky and washed out. Particle effects are very nice however textures are more important and are the biggest factor in making a game look good. Other than that I expected more but it does not hold back too much for the game.
Gameplay - Story feels pieced together relatively poorly and with the death of the best character it starts it off bad. It does reel it back on with some areas where you make choices with somewhat affect the game, not much however. Adding in zombies and gimp clubs spice up areas though are quite out of place. Gameplay is passable. Every gun is unique in impact and feels which helps vary combat considering that’s the corner stone of this game. Cars, planes, boats and upgrades also help with different scenarios.
Replayability - Lots of missions that offer a replay either because they are sweet or just like what the ♥♥♥♥ happened plus the choices it has some backbone.
Conclusion - Overall the game is good for what it is. A lighter hearted but lazy version of GTA. What it lacks in meaty gameplay it makes up for ♥♥♥♥ jokes, which for me is not a strong point. But I can’t help but like the characters and the random and unique weapons. It’s just for pure fun, what games used to be aiming for. It some ways it works and in some it falls.

This mod taught me the awesomeness of REALLY difficult and challenging puzzles. It is said one needs six to ten hours for the whole game, but even just after easily playing the original Portal 2 again, some puzzles here nearly let my head explode, needing somewhat more than an hour just for one chamber.
Where the designers of the original seemed only to see the predestined function of the several components, the designers of this mod were so incredibly creative about the mechanics (also introducing some new), they created a whole new experience.
That's possibly a reason why it is (at least for me) so difficult. You have to think out of the box of the original, combine the components in different and not at all obvious manners and sometimes even doing stupid looking stuff. Additionally the portion of timing puzzles is pretty low (I can't think of one at all at the moment). I also like that very much, because the puzzles are therefore completely solved by brainpower.
You are an athlete or so, which is put into hypersleep just to wake up to a completely destroyed Aperture-Facility, where you have to get out (no spoilers). I'm not through yet, but the story up to now is nice, the level design seems not a little bit worse than in the original and they recorded professional voice acting for different characters, making it even more similar to a full-price game (I love Virgil's character).
As mentioned in another review, I also feel nearly ashamed, that this mod is free, just because it is so splendidly and lovingly created, and is a REAL challenge to your brain. I would have paid for this without hesitation, so a grand thank you to the creators for this masterpiece.

Always in poor taste, and at times poorly coded, I cannot recommend Saints Row: The Third... enough. "A stupid game that goes out of its way to make sure you're always having fun," is how I describe it. It's like Grand Theft Auto, but fun. And it never takes itself seriously. But is it a good game? Well, it's a lot of fun. There are a few unfair parts, and they may prevent you from getting 100% without cheats, but they won't stop you from beating the game. Things like timers that run when you don't have control of the character, and AI weirdness. There are also technical issues, issues with graphics and sound (on a more than capable machine with updated drivers). All in all the game is playable, and its flaws add to its charms. It wouldn't be the same game with everything working right. It would seem too "normal." So leave your expectations and standards at the door, kick off your shoes, let your hair down, and have some fun with the Third Street Saints. (One tip, guaranteed spoiler free: If you're gonna play as a woman, use the Female 1 voice; if you're going to play as a man, it's Male 3. Female 1 is Laura Bailey; she was Serana in Skyrim, Lust in Fullmetal Alchemist, and numerous other roles. The guy is Robin Atkin Downes; he was Brynjolf in Skyrim, and a ton of other stuff — they both do. Nothing against the other voice actors, but these two are, by far, the best. Only issue is, they let Laura Bailey improvise on many lines, so if you have the subtitles on, you're going to be confused. Don't let that deter you from using her voice, though.)

Portal Stories: Mel is a free standalone mod for Portal 2. It's a different story even if there are a lot of similarities. You play as Mel, a person who was chosen to be part of a test experiment but there is an explosion in the facility during your first night there. It's up to you to escape this place.
First of all, the difficulty. I would say that the game is adressed to the people who already finished Portal 2 and wanted harder puzzles. The first puzzles in Portal Stories Mel aren't really tutorial levels. They are really hard puzzles that need a lot of reflexion. The game is about 7 to 10 hours long, depending of your capacity to understand the puzzles fast. For a free mod, this is definitely something I did not expected at all. It's as long as Portal 2 and it's also really well done.
The game is really similar to Portal 2 in term of the architecture of the levels. You'll find similar-looking rooms and a lot of things that you already saw in Portal 2. There is nothing new except maybe the new look of the Portal Gun.
The game is meant to be funny.  Virgil (the robot who accompanies you to escape the facility) always try to be funny but I would say that it didn't really worked for me as well as the humor in Portal 2. At least it stays true to the Portal series but that's something that could have been better.
In conclusion, if you liked Portal 2, you should definitely try this mod. It's a whole new story and it's always a pleasure to get back to the Portal universe.

So uuuh, yeah, Portal Stories: Mel. What to say about it? That we need "mixed feelings" rating.
From design part, this mod is bloody well crafted. Aesthetics are amazing, almost on par with Valve's work and that is an accomplisment! You got to see how Aperture Facility looked and worked back in the day and the impression is quite believeable. Respect to the Cave Johnson impersonator who managed to nail the voice and attitude of the guy quite well. Virgil, your core friend on the hand is well... can't say anything else besides annoying as heck. I get that they are trying to capture impression of Wheatly into this character but it fell flat on it's face and bursted into flames before setting your brain on fire as well because Virgil just keeps talking and talking and
. Then again, this is purely community made mod so it's expected, especially in voice acting department, that not everything will be flawless. Kudos for trying tho. Portal Device model is quite well made though there are some minor issues with the extra effects attached to it like some bright lines going over your screen when going trough portals. Also the animations might a wee bit exaggerated but that's just me nitpicking. Thought with all those models and stuff, one would thing they could spare some extra time on those citizen models they used to make them not look so ten-minutes-retexture worthy, especially since you get to study one from quite up close
Now onto puzzles which is of course big part of this mod as expected being mod for an amazing even though a bit easy puzzle game Portal 2. Well, I can't deny they tried. Tried and failed sadly. Simply put, puzzles aren't fun. Bear in mind I am someone who finished P2 Co-op campaign with a friend not that great at puzzles so I was mostly solving stuff on my own. So to cut any thoughts of that type that surely will arise, no, I am not afraid of challenge or too stupid to find the solution. Actually I was quite looking forward to this. But in most cases, the puzzles ultimately failed to deliver increased difficulty and delivered only increased tediousness. There are generally 2 types of test chambers:
Chamber problems aside, the game generally tests your witt, reflexes and timing so that's a good thing. But again, what's it worth when it's doing it in the most annoying way?
In the end, is this mod worth your time? Yeah, it's not like you are actually paying anything for this so you might as well give it a go. Maybe you are bigger P2 enthusiast than I am, maybe you have more patience with these extremely obnoxious tests than I do, maybe you are way hungrier for some quality P2 mods than I am, maybe you are mentally-self-harming-loving freak which I am not. If any of these matches with you, this mod is just for you! If P2 puzzles were hard for you and if the Co-op broke you though, stay away, you want none of this.
And minor tip for the devs: next time, when developing a puzzle game, get some playtesters. Those that will inform you about missteps and flaws to make the final experience better, not those who will suck on your wee-wee just because you are developing a mod for their favourite game. Really, this mod shows your dire need of them. Valve may get backlash for ending the game before the puzzles gets actually difficult thanks to their below-average-IQ playtesters, but you never had problem with one concept getting so repeated until you wanted shove one of the devs into deadly Emanctipation Grid.

Portal Stories: Mel, is probably one of the greatest mods, I have played to date for Portal 2 aside from the Steam community made levels. The difficulty on this is quite surprising as some solutions to the testing tracks were simple (The beginning ones mostly), some made me angry and some solutions I got instantly without me even realizing that I just made the moves necessary to do so. The intro storyline should bring joy to both Half Life and Portal fans alike thanks to a bit of exploration made for curious players and though some people may begin saying things such as "WHEN DO I GET TO PLAY WITH A PORTAL GUN?", try and have a bit of fun. If you are playing this game trying to rush it then you will definitely get frustrated. So have fun exploring at the beginning as there are lot of funny posters and offices you can visit. The ending brought me to tears, and though the core Virgil was not very witty as Wheatley in Portal 2, he had his own contributions and provided much more useful atmosphere than Wheatley would have and we basically have Virgil to thank for waking her up. Mel deserved her own story and this is exactly the ending she deserved after walking into something like Aperature Science Innovaters and finding out after waking up years later not expecting the type of things she would have to go through. Overall A solid game and recommend every die-hard Portal fan try it out. It will test your creativity and patience.

Saints Row: The Third is an Open World Action Adventure game. The story follows the Third Street Saints, a street gang that evolved into huge multimedia celebrity icons. After losing their most respected member, Johnny Gat, in an attempt to kill the Syndcate leader, the Saints are led by "The Boss" (Who is your character) to get revenge and try to take over the rest of the gangs that lay in the city of Steelport however they can, ensuring the Saints are the only ones in charge.
If you're more of a fan of the serious and realistic tone the first two Saints Row games did, you might be disappointed here. The game is more about comedy and crazy situations now. That's a good thing in one way though, because it leaves tons of room for variety and interesting settings, plus very good writing and humor done by the team, Volition. You could be riding a motorcycle in cyberspace, going into a zombie infested area of Steelport, or just unleash mayhem in a huge tank. Lots of scenarios and possibilities, always keeping the game fresh. I really do believe the character and story is the highlight of this game. It's funny, memorable, and has great characters. Even The Boss, the character you create, is a witty and interesting person, but has a serious side too when the job needs to be done. I'll say it again, the scenarios you're put in along with the great writing makes this game worth playing just for the story alone. You'll love it.
The gameplay is pretty similar to Grand Theft Auto. You can go around Steelport, do whatever you want, you have "Noterity" which is basically your wanted level (Noteriety can be caught by other gangs or the police, depending on what you do). There's main missions, side missions, minigames, secrets, collectables, lots of stuff to do you'd expect in a game like this. The main story might take you about 6 hours if you don't care to do anything else. Doing everything else however, will more than double your time for sure, it really adds onto the gameplay. In my opinion, some minigames are better than others, but they're fun overall. There's reasons why, which I'll get to in a minute.
The side stuff you can do is very huge. You can literally play in traffic and hurt yourself a bunch of times by running into cars to get points. That's the randomness factor here. You can also go in a tank and blow things up, rescue hookers to recruit them to be saints, escort friends to make deals while you defend their position, or blowing up things with an RPG in a helicopter on the side of a building. And soooo much more. The only problem is... The AI can be very, VERY terrible at times, and it's generally not good when it's your friends. Your friends are so stupid when they try to go back in the car with you, run somewhere, or do anything really. Some missions like escort missions are an absolute pain because of it. And when your partner is driving, it's likely they can get stuck on a tiny piece of metal. Shameful.
(Side note: If you own certain DLC, you got even more side mission variety avaliable to you.)
Customization is a big part of this game. You can make The Boss look however you like, and if you own all the DLC, you already have tons of options from the start. Also, I'm not kidding when I say that, you can make him/her look like anything. Or just completely naked. That works too. I think creative players will have a great time trying to make a character they really enjoy. There's also 3 Male voices, and 3 Female voices, so you even got some voice variety here too. Weapons and your vehicles have lots of customization too, same as above.
So overall, Saints Row The Third is a brilliantly written and funny game with a memorable story and fun gameplay with lots of variety thanks to the random nature and setting you're put in. If you're looking for a sillier, more different GTA that keeps you on the edge of your seat with a little less polish, you'll definitely love Saints Row 3 and 4.

You can probably tell the game doesn't take itself very seriously and neither should you.
Even if the replay value is not very high theoretically (you can do mostly everything the game has to offer in maybe 40 hours if you're taking your time), I keep coming back to it. The main reasons for that are probably a) the wide range of character customisation possibilities and b) that the first couple of missions are brilliantly designed to suck you right into the action - something SRIV tried hard to achieve but just didn't do it nearly as well as its prequel.
Here's a pros and cons list if you're too lazy to read full sentences.
+ visuals and sound design
+ story
+ gameplay with no major annoyances (this is so much rarer than it should be)
+ loads of optional stuff to do
- driving 3 kilometers for a mission that only involves watching a cutscene
- some characters can be annoying (Zimos, I'm looking at you.)
Just get this instead of SRIV unless you're really into Spiderman.
DON'T get this if the sentence "the game doesn't take itself seriously" sounds like a bad thing to you.

Who doesn't like a free portal mod?
Portal stories: Mel is charming in a lot of aspects, and embarassing in others.
The gameplay shows no mercy, and declines to hold your hand every step of the way. You'll spend your time looking around trying to figure out what to do next, which can be complicating for some people, and easy for people who are good at solving problems by doing a little bit of exploration. (which is fine, because the mod offers decent scenery and things to look at along the way).
I've played about an hours worth so far, and I can say its over all worth the play.
My only gripe is the constant advances the scripts take to try and make you laugh. The voice acting is...good quality, but the script work is really not that funny, as they carry over the same joke one after another.
After you wake up, the voice actor seems to change his inflection and tone, and you're left not knowing if its still Cave Johnson speaking or not.
For a free mod, you can't beat the challenging puzzles they have provided, and the unique experience.
But it's just that, It simply feels like a mod, and not an actual game to take seriously.
I give it 6/10, but I do recommend a play through.

TF2 is one of the most simple FPS games that is walk, look, shot, dodge and capture. Its fun and enjoyable when you have a good (forgiving) team to play with, releaving when dodging a Crit. I have played it for 1000 hours and its a fun and a good game when you put effort into it
The game will reward you when your picked class does not die and lets you live on to fight and help your team. And put on amazing stunts you can't really do in any other game, its rewarding and satisfying when you use it to your advantage when you pick soldier. If playing scout you can do many unpredictable stunts many times. If playing pyro, with newly added weapons, you can fly across map and suprise players on opposite teams. If demoman, like soldier, can do stunts with their sticky launcher and stop enemy players from unpredicting high places. If heavy, hold of the enemy team or push at the enemy team or flank enemy team. If Engineer, help your whole team by protecting an area with giving ammo and health to them or helping them move to a flanking position. If medic, be a true doctor and heal everyone you see. If spy, cloak, run behind enemy lines and delay enemy pushing. If sniper, like spy, snipe buff players at a unseeing position. And if dodging all attacks when doing these make you feel so releaved and shotting them will make you happy.
And thats only the stock weapons and just a tiny bit of the game itself. One thing is the weapons in TF2 make the classes have more varity to flank other players with their weapons and skills. Btw this game is free so there is nothing wrong at trying out, just give it another chance if you die alot, that happens in other FPS games.
On other hand, maps, classes, weapons, user interface are all great but the game explaining itself is not good.It does help you around the main menu but after that you have to figure it out yourself. If first starting, I say watch other people play this game so you get a better understanding of what the weapons are and how to get them, of what the classes have and at what health they got or what you can do in general and how to do amazing stunts (it does take many practices).
Thats all that really makes me play it, again its free so go try it. Btw it took me about 50-100-500 hours for me to understand the game and I might have still have things to know about it but it might be quicker for you.
BTW. This game does have microtransactions for customization for classes, other weapons, keys and crates. Okay now its you to find out the system of the game.
So try it, nothing bad will happen if you do
P.S Good Luck

I've been looking forward to Portal Stories: Mel for a very, very long time.  It was worth it.
Let's start by talking about gameplay:  Mel uses the exact same mechanics as Portal 2 in terms of puzzles, only adding in a red emancipation grid that kills you as well as anything you put through it.  Despite this, the game challenges you to use these mechanics in new and interesting ways (I don't think I've ever had to coat a cube in orange gel before, even in custom maps,) and the game's level system differs entirely from P2.  In the original game, the bulk of your experience came from point-a-to-point-b chambers, and while Mel does include its fair share of these the highlight of the mod comes from open-ended exploration based rooms.  I definitely enjoyed myself when walking through these areas, and while making my way through them has definitely been a puzzle I never really felt lost.
Moving on from that, let's get to story.  The plotline of Portal 2 was honestly the one thing that I always loved most from the game, and the gameplay itself, while brilliant in its own right, always fell second.  Surprisingly, Mel does the same, and it's story holds up well to the original two games.  The new side character, Virgil, is a joy to listen to, as he's a strong personality that fits right in to the portal universe.  The 'villain' of the game is portrayed more or less as a mindless machine without any morals or life whatsoever.  This makes him threatening in a way completely different than Portal 2's original villains:  He's not a cold, calculating, witty enemy like GLaDOS, nor is he a complete idiot who simply can't keep himself or anybody in his care alive like Wheatley.  He honestly has no idea he's going to kill you:  he's running protocol, and does not have the self-awareness needed to see why that's a short-sighted decision.
Mel is actually developed as a character as well, surprisingly.  Unlike Chell, Mel has a given backstory (being a former track runner in the Olympics now testing for Aperture,)  and she's called out by name by the characters (Virgil actually calling me 'Mel' was an enormous surprise to me, as for some reason none of the characters in Portal 2 want to say each other's names.)  This makes for a much more cinematic experience, as I feel like I'm experiencing Mel and Virgil's story as I would by reading a book or watching a movie.
The game has an amazing since of urgency to it:  a constant mystery as to who the villain is combined with a constant threat of unseen danger makes this game an exciting ride.  I absolutely loved my experience walking through Aperture's doors once again, and I'll be returning to replay Mel pretty often.
Other notes:
--For some reason there's a strance particle glitch whenever you walk through a portal.  I'm expecting this to be fixed in an update.
--The voice acting is incredibly high-quality, holding up to Portal 2's voiceover.
--Expect to spend quite a while solving some of the later tests, this game gets ever so slightly more difficult than Portal 2's final levels.
--There is no hand holding or tutorial level in this mod, so if you're a little rusty with the puzzle mechanics, try replaying Portal 2 first.
--I am looking forward to see what this studio does next, if anything.  Weather it be another Portal Stories or a completely original project.
--I got stuck in impossible-to-get-out-of places about three times.  Twice it was because I didn't know I was supposed to bring a cube with me, and the other time was just a glitch.
--The ending to this game is actually kind of emotional.  I feel like I've actually come to know Virgil and Mel throughout the mod.
--As usual, Harry Callahan brings his a-game with the soundtrack.  Even if you don't plan on playing the mod, download the music.  It's brilliant.

Clearly well made addition to portal franchise!
Firstly I'd like to say that even with all the minuses this mod has, this is a brilliant result for a team of 8 people. And I'd like to thank all of them for extending portal universe and creating this game.
But even the game is good, it has its own shortcomings.
Unfortunately almost each level has design defects and mistakes which ruin your gameplay sometimes. Through the game I had a feeling that I solve the puzzles in the wrong way, and not because they could possibly have several solving ways but just because of exploits. I spent about half of time solving each test by just searching things... And this is my second and last note for bad level design - some tests were to seem illogical, because of THAT ONE portal apply surface which was hiding behind all the debris.
About tests. Some of them are really difficult to solve, and this is GREAT! I definitely loved the "Hardest chamber in the track". After it took about 40 minutes to solve, I was happier than a child who got a new 'muscled rhino who fires lasers from his eyes' toy!
Also, a big plus is an own storyline with AEGIS. Even it borrows and in some cases replicates the original game scenario, it's still a thing! I really loved that idea about hiding within the plants ;)
And the music which played all along clearly added 'scientific' atmosphere to the game.
In the end, special thanks to a person who made this old looking portal device, this thing is epic! Here, have a heart - <3
If you're feeling the lack of Portal in your life or are tired of workshop chambres - this game is for you! You won't regret.

As far as mods go, this isnt so much a mod but is actually more like a full fledged game. it delivers exactly what it promises to: "a free modification for Portal 2 based in the Portal universe. It tells the story of Mel, who meets a new personality core and faces an undiscovered threat to the Aperture facility."
But it goes further than that. it features custom textures, new ways of using existing game play elements and a slew of challenging puzzels along with some pretty stellar voice acting to go with it all.
The reason i say its more like its own game is because it genuinly does take at least 6 hours or more to complete on the first play through (I completed it in 8 hours at the time of writing) and at times i forgot i was actually playing a FREE community made mod. Right now the giant of the battle royal games is PUBG, its almost impossible to not bring up pubg when talking about h1z1 but i think that h1z1 is a more enjoyable experience than pubg. The way i see it is if you are looking for a "realistic" battle royal game, then pubg is more suited for you, but if you are like me and don't care for the more "realistic" slower pace of pubg than H1Z1 is perfect for you. H1Z1 is a very active game just by nature, nobody (for the most part) likes to camp in buildings or sit out of near by firefights, there is always action around you and you are always looking for your next encounter with another player. when it comes to weapons there is not a huge variety but the weapons that are in the game get the job done and i feel like they dont need to add more into the game. There are two assault rifles in the game, the ar15 and the ak-47. Both these weapons are very good at medium range with the ar15 being better at long range fights than the ak-47 is but the ak-47 is better at close range fights. Another important weapon in this game is the shotgun, when you kill somebody with this weapon be prepared to hear the salt pour from their mouths as you loot their body, it is a VERY good weapon at close range with the capability to kill someone in a single shot and you do need this weapon if you want a semi-reliable way of winning very close range engagements. There are other weapons like pistols and crossbows but i won'tgo into detail about them because they do not play a big part in the game other than the first couple seconds of the game. There are also grenades including explosive, smoke, gas, concussion, and molotov coctail. All of the grenades are very useful in certain situations and can be the deciding factor in a firefight. The gameplay and movement of this game is very arcade-like and is a lot of fun once you embrace that type of gameplay, it is a lot of fun learning to master the movement and how you should act while you are in combat to dodge other peoples shots. Throught the world you will also be able to find vehicles, there are 4 types of vehicles (police car, jeep, quad bike, and truck) and all of the vehicles act differently but are all very nice to have. In conclusion, if you want a fun and exciting arcade-like experience in a 3rd person shooter than this game is for you and you WILL put a lot of hours into it.

While the mod is free, the question brings: is this worth my time? Should I try it?
The answer is: Absolutely! YES!
Portal Stories: Mel is like Super Mario Bros 2: Lost Levels to Super Mario Bros. This game is the hard version of portal 2. It feels more like a game Valve made than a fangame. It takes all mechanics of solving puzzles from Portal 2, and it combines them in each test chamber in order to challenge the player. There is no holding the player hand in this game! The learning curve in the most part is very fair, but not perfect. The begining chambers are designed to help the player learn new tricks in a critical thinking way. Rather than giving you what to do, you have to think your way through it, and trust me, it will be very satisfying to learn it. So, I highly recommend not giving up and looking up a guide or else you will find the future chambers impossible to solve! Some of these actually require thinking outside the box and analyzing every little detail on how to solve a puzzle. For example, one chamber actually required destroying a cube and letting it  respawn over and over until I reached my destination. Then, I stop it from respawning with a portal and brought it to its plate. You'd never have do something as silly as that in Portal 2, so you would never imagine to even do that. However, my only little complain is in most of these maps, one little mistake could cause you to start over entirely. It felt really irritating and almost made me want to give up. Admitting and I'm shamed too, I actually look up how to beat one chamber, only to realize that I was doing it right, but I kept mixing up my blue and orange portal placements.
Shockly, all of these levels don't look the same. I actually thought it's just a regular mod and they just grab maps from the steam worshop using the creation kit and slap in the game. I was wrong  as a ton of effort into making this game. All of these maps look very original, and at least points I thought I was playing entire new portal rather than a mod. It's very professional and it makes me feel bad that it free.
Being honest, I only played this mod for the maps, butt the story is what grasped my attention and made me want to play more. Without spoiling too much, you play as a woman named Mel who was part of group of olympians, war heroes, and astronauts that were put to sleep in the "Aperture: Science Innovators Short-Term Relaxation Vault", and a mysterious voice claiming to be Cave Johnson is asking you to do a few test chambers for him. (Fun fact, a character named "Mel" was actually supposed to be the main protagonist of Portal 2 with an entirely difference story called F-Stop, but was later replaced for Chell in the final product.) The story itself is very portalish. In some degree, it is a bit cliche as. In a nutshell, your goal is to solve chambers and help a core just like portal 2. However, it stands out on its own with uquinie few characters with great voice actors that are up to par with Portal 2's characters.
To me and I BET MANY OF US, we want more like this!!! A portal mod that takes the story of portal 2 and uses it to tell another alterative story; more "what if *this happen*" or that.The portal 2 story is full of many mysteries, and this mod is the perfect example for demonstrating the good fanfics are welcome to try to fill or answer our questions. I also want more mods that do not involve introducing new grimmicks! I'm sorry but that was my biggest complain for the other portal 2 mods. The portal gun will never be topped and I want to play Portal 2 the way it was meant to be.
I higly recommend this game especially if you're a portal fanaddict like me!

TL;DR
I'd recommend this mod; however, not without a few major gripes that inhibit enjoyment.
The environment design is pretty great; however, especially in the beginning sections, it all feels incredibly empty and dead. One does wonder why they'd put so much work into detailing all these environments with their side-rooms and branching paths, only to have no interaction to speak of or no incentive to explore any of it.
Plus, there was a LOT of walking around and riding various trains/elevators while listening to dialogue that is too short and, thus, leaves you just standing there and staring into the aether while being very slowly moved to your destination in silence. This mod has a serious case of sightseeing syndrome.
Once the puzzles do begin, it starts kicking it up quite nicely. The music is waaaay too prominent for my taste, though; the original game only had upbeat and "present" music during transitional and story parts for a reason. The music in the chambers was kept atmospheric and in the background, which is something that this mod doesn't seem to be doing at all. The loops are quite noticable, and the music gets repetitive very quickly.
All in all, solid effort. Props to the creators of the mod, but it's definitely noticable that this is the work of amateurs - as in the sense of "non-professionals", not in the sense of "beginners" or "inexperienced people". There has obviously been a lot of quality work put into this, but as a whole, there are glaring issues that, while not game-breaking or lessening enjoyment by any stretch, do detract from the polish of the whole thing.
