TL: DR – Saints Row the Third is an outrageous, low-brow, over the top, open-city action game very similar to the Grand Theft Auto series, but with a lot more focus on humor and blowing things up. 9/10
I’m reviewing this game as someone who never played Saints Row 1 & 2 and only having played a little bit of Grand Theft Auto. I had no problem jumping into the story and following along, so don’t let that hold you back. If you enjoyed Grand Theft Auto and wished it wasn’t so serious, or wished that you could participate in Mexican wrestling matches with giant♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bats, then come on down to Steelport and party with the Third Street Saints.
In Saints Row the Third, you play the “Boss of the Saints” (a customizable character) who runs the fun loving gang with his trusted friends Shaundi, Pierce, and Johnny Gat. Under your leadership, the Saints have become pop culture icons, with their own clothing stores, sports drink, and television reality shows. Yes, you still blow♥♥♥♥♥♥up and kill people, but the common folk love you. A new threat is on the horizon though, the Syndicate is a combination of a number of distinct and powerful gangs coming after the Saints to get a piece of the action. And above it all, the military anti-gang task force STAG is drawing closer, ready to drop the hammer on all the gangs with their advanced weapons and technology.
As you probably know, Saints Row the Third is a third person shooter game similar to Just Cause, Sleeping Dogs, and Prototype. Just like in those games, you are in a large open city filled with activities and gang violence, with vehicles that you can carjack to get around faster. If you try to run, it would take you hours to cross the entire city (there is no “fast travel” in this game) so get used to driving. You have a few cribs (safe houses) around the city where you can stash and access your guns, ammo, and vehicles, as well as hide if there are too many enemies after you. One thing to note is that like the Just Cause games, you don’t really have a huge combat advantage over enemy units (no special powers). If there are too many bad guys, you’ll have to run. Mostly you rely on superior firepower and the ability to escape in a vehicle.
If you’ve played the Ezio Assassin’s Creed games, you may remember a gameplay element where you can buy buildings around the city, which produce money per hour that you can use to purchase upgrades for your character (or buy more buildings). In Saints Row 3 you do this as well, and probably most of your money will come from this passive investment system. The rest will come mostly from completing missions and activities. Enemies drop money, but it’s so little that you probably won’t even notice. Besides buying buildings, you’re going to spend most of your money upgrading your weapons and buying character upgrades, such as increased health and ammo capacity. When you reach the absolute maximum level, you can buy invulnerability upgrades as well (they don’t disable Steam achievements).
I feel I should mention that Saints Row 3 has a ton of DLC, most of which is sort of “pay to win” because they give such powerful bonuses to your character. There are 3 or 4 story DLCs though, such as Gangstas in Space, which can give you a few hours of gameplay. The DLC missions are sort of standalone missions from the base game, using weapons/vehicles that only appear during those missions, so you can play them early or late in your playthrough and it wouldn’t make too much of a difference.
Pros:
+A lot of humor and fun ridiculous storylines
+There is a lot of variety in the gameplay, not just silly weapons/enemies (bee launcher/shark gun), but many creative mission types as well.
+There is so much to do that you can pretty easily play this game for 20+ hours for a single playthrough and not really get bored. You definitely get your money’s worth. I was planning to go for a Steam achievement where you play for over 30 hours, and it popped when I was about halfway through the DLCs after beating the main game. I didn’t even try to go for the “collectibles” which would probably have taken an additional 5 hours at least.
Cons:
-If you have the complete edition, I recommend playing the game first without any DLCs installed. You get such a huge boost from the DLCs that it’s practically cheating. It’s like playing an RPG with high level equipment right from the start. You can choose which DLC are installed by right clicking the game in your Steam library and choosing “View Downloadable Content” then deselecting them individually.
-If you’re like me and don’t really like chasing thousands of collectibles in an open world game, you’re going to leave a lot of the game “incomplete.” I just don’t have time to explore the whole world searching for stuff that I don’t need.
Overall the game is awesome and you’ll have a blast playing through it.

The puzzle allows you to leave once you bounce over a body of water by jumping through a portal onto a surface you cover with repulsion gel. I would either smack into a piece of set design above the landing area and fall into the water or I would smack into the wall to the right of the landing area.
I also found the humor to be very meh. I felt it was trying too hard to replicate the humor from Portal 2 but was not succeeding. Rather than getting someone to try to imitate KJ Simmons, they should have just gone with a new character rather than attempting to do Cave Johnson. For the rest of the voice over work, I couldn’t tell if the problem was the script, the voice actors, or a combination of both.

YOU WILL HAVE TO READ THE COMMENTS TO GET THE FULL REVIEW! LENGTH ISSUE!
Portal Stores: Mel is, honestly, one of the best mods I have ever played. The amount of work and effort that has gone into creating this is staggering - it shows everywhere you look. This review will have a small section before it starts to alleviate some criticism I have had with the review. The rest of the review is for the more casual players who only really played the campaign, maybe a couple of community maps - however the information I feel is still relevant.
This review will contain mild to medium spoilers. Summaries of each 'section' will be marked with [SUMMARY] for Ctrl+F convenience. There will be a [TL;DR] at the bottom.
For experienced Portal 2 players:
I am not an experienced Portal 2 player, however I have heard time and time again from other experienced Portal 2 players that this mod is not as hard as people say. If you are an experienced person reading this, then that is probably the case; as the community style maps are most definitely made in a different style from Valve's almost babysat puzzles. I cannot agree with this due to lack of experience, however the mod is so brilliantly crafted with fantastic assets, that I would wholeheartedly suggest you just try it for yourself.
Onto the review:
As I have said before, this mod is amazing. I wouldn't say it is professional quality, but for 'amateur' developers, you probably won't get better than this. The attention to detail here is phenomenal, and everything ties in well with the lore established in Valve's series.
The aesthetic design is really one of its strongest points in the earlier parts of the game, and it really brings to life the side of Aperture that Valve has only touched on slightly. The developer's interpretations of what the new technology could have evolved from are very nice. They've done a cracking job on keeping the crazy science feeling of Aperture, while still staying within the crude, retro look. The first Handheld Portal Device, the turrets - you will smile when you see these. They all use completely custom assets, and they look fantastic.
A lot of the early game is explained to you by Cave Johnson as you go through the facility. The actor who voiced Cave did a ruddy good job of doing so, to where it is at times indistinguishable when you listen to it for a while. A minor point is that sometimes saying "the" and "there" becomes "duh" and "dere", but that's nitpicking.
The dialogue from Cave is very explanatory, and goes into good depth of the Aperture Science facility and what the hell is it doing on top of a massive cave system. (A salt mine nonetheless!) The lore given is very in-universe, and frankly it's so convincing I'd happily consider it canon.
However, Cave may have been great to listen to, not so the Personality Core you get assigned to work with. He is very, almost gratingly, enthusiastic, so props to them for keeping the annoying nature of the Cores consistent. At times he can be genuinely funny to hear, although sometimes he can be extortionately annoying. In the early levels of the game, there is a running 'gag' so to say which after half an hour gets quite repetitive.
Right. Aesthetics out of the way. They've done a great job. Here is the summary:
[SUMMARY] Aesthetics
Pros:
+ Fantastic attention to detail.
+ Expands upon the lore brilliantly, to a level where you could easily consider it canon.
+ Very good voice acting from Cave, not quite as good but still good acting from Virgil.
+ Custom assets are lore-friendly - fitting in-universe but keeping the retro theme solid.
Cons:
- Virgil dialogue can get a bit dull at times, sometimes repetitive.
Quick mention of the music. The music, while it generally sounds cool, is generally mainly a con. Portal 2 used music for atmospheric purposes, or for boosting the reaction you get while doing things such as flying in the air or running away from crushers and whatnot. Here, the electronic music plays constantly throughout the background. It doesn't fit the Portal style of music playing, but this mod does many things new, so that's not so bad. What is bad though, is that after a while you will notice the music looping. And it will start to get very repetitive and annoying. Hats off to Harry101UK for the great soundtrack, but they could have used it more cleverly in order to maximise its novelty before it wore off.
Now onto the gameplay. The first 10-20 minutes of you is free reign. You get the choice of whether to just follow Cave's instructions to the letter as you go to your destination, or you get the opportunity to explore the 1952 Aperture Science facility. For some, this will be a welcome change for the Portal games, while others will get tired of waiting for the puzzles to start. However I warn you, they do come all right, and they don't hold their punches.
There are two different types of puzzle rooms here: The big open rooms that contain destroyed parts of the facility, pipes, walkways, etc. And there's the test chambers. Both have their own little niggles that make the mod a pain for the more casual player.
Firstly the big open rooms. They're designed very well. This mod looks great. The room appearances fit great, they've really set the bar high and kept it there.
However, the way they're solved is what makes them so aggravating. The vast majority require you to spend a lot of time looking for a single small white patch that holds the secret to solving the room. These can be very well hidden - you can spend a tediously long time searching for the white patch. The issue wouldn't be too bad if they were spread out, but the large rooms follow more large rooms, and soon you've spent easily half an hour just looking for white patches. (Again, this could be the norm for the community designed maps though, so don't be put off if you're an experienced Portal 2 player.)
Next, we move onto the test chambers. They have a different design feel to them than Valve's, but that's not a bad thing. They still fit easily within the Aperture universe - they aren't too outlandish to be used as tests, but they are definitely pack a bit more punch than Valve's. I have been told they aren't too difficult, however, as a more casual Portal 2 player, the different style of puzzle is definitely much harder than the base game.
Generally, each room has a way of either outright killing you, or setting you back several minutes. The risk factor is good, but sometimes it can get a bit much if you keep dying constantly. Speaking of being put back several minutes, a big recurring theme in the puzzles are emancipation grids. There are probably more grids in the first couple of chapters than in the whole Portal 2 game. A lot of the puzzles revolve around getting a cube past a grid while only using one portal, often while not moving. This can get a little bit repetitive after a while.
A common complaint amongst the more casual Portal 2 players is that the test chambers are far too hard. While they certainly have a challenge aspect that the casual player can enjoy, they completely lack the guiding nature of Valve's puzzles. In Valve's, you can hop into the room, start throwing portals down in a few seconds and end up at the end of the test chamber within a few minutes. In this? No hints.
While this does mean that the solutions feel more ingenious as you have to work them out, and some can feel very unintuitive; their elegance or rather lack thereof, doesn't make the experience as satisfying as the Valve ones. It feels more a relief that you're not stuck any more rather than a sense of accomplishment. However they aren't all like that. There are a few very well made rooms which are an absolute delight to solve, giving the same "Ah-ha!" moment that the Valve levels do, so hats off to the level designers for those, because they are fantastic.

I'l be honest...I initially liked this mod a lot but somewhere after chapter 2 it went off the rails..
I usually don't spend much time with fan mods generally because they're either not well thought out or buggy.  From the first few hours I honestly thought this one was different.
Is it as engrossing a story as the original game, almost.   But then we all know the story so well that we really can't expect too many surprises from a bridge story.  Think of Portal Stories:Mel the same way you think of Star Wars: The clone wars.  Yeah, a lot is familiar but there's also a lot of questions that get answered.  Admit it, when you were running around Portal 2 and found the old test facilities weren't you just a little bit curious?  This game fills in the blanks that could only be touched on in Portal 2.
Unfortunately, once you get to the actual tests it's all downhill...
Are the puzzles difficult? Yes and no which is absolutely wonderful at least at first.  I spent almost an hour just trying to get out of the first chapter.  Know what, that's ok because it was exactlythe same in Portal 2.  It will take you just to the brink of exasperation and suddenly you see the solution.
At least that was how it started out....
The visuals are good and worthy of a few screenshots.  THe voice acting is ok.  However, I prefer the REAL voice of Cave Johnson (J. K. Simmons )
The lack of GlaDos starts to become evident when what is apparently her predecessor tries to actively engage in killing you.  Just another ominonus male robotic voice like something out of a bad sci-fi movie
The problem with this game is that it got too ambitious like most Portal Mods do.  They were right on track up to about the middle of chapter 2 then things got stupid.
Stupid as in presenting puzzles that weren't evident from your immediate surrounding.  It seems the game suddenly switched from brain teaser to masochism.  It was less about portals anmd more about hopping over desks so as not to get electrocuted.  Too much time spent on things that had little to do with portal games.  After awhile it got annoying.
The main difference between playing this and a REAL portal game is the thought that went into the maps.  In the entirety of my time with Portal and Portal 2 I can count on one hand the number of times I had to go look for a walkthough vid.  This game drove me to activating the cheats just to get out of an area (sv_cheats 1)(noclip)
My mind doesn't like to work on needlessly complex puzzles.  This game crossed the line from challenging to abusive.  Portal was never easy but you always had everything you needed right in front of you even if it wasn't immediaely obvious.  None of this going back an forth into rooms 3 times to open a door only to have to do it all over again to open another.  That's a mark of bad level design.  If I have to keep going back to the same place just to finish that means there wasn't enough imagination involved to create a complete level.
I call those "Boomerang" maps and  unfortunately, this mod is full of them.  It almost seems like the first half and the last half of the game were designed by different teams.  Almost as if the game itself developed multiple personality disorder mid way through its development.
Meaning I can only recommend the first 2 chapters of this  game and maybe half of the third one.
The puzzles aren't too hard, they'just  feel like the result of some level designer being mean.
This game makes me cry. Anger. Frustration. Joy. Wonder. I love it.

ArmA 3 is a great game for the price with massive amounts of replayability and variety in missions; from realistic mil-sim gameplay to zombie survival.
Multiplayer PvE is one of the best ways to experience ArmA, working alongside teammates to accomplish a common goal.
PvP however, is not the best due to laggy server registration and low FPS which is common across all larger servers, no matter how good your PC is. This makes close quarters combat very unrealistic and frustrating, with a significant number of encounters ending with both players trading kills with each other.
The combat is also weakened by the clunky movement system and player animations. This not only spoils the combat and fluidity of the gameplay, but takes away from the immersive, realistic experience ArmA 3 is supposed to offer.
Don't let those last few points affect your opinion on the game too much however since it is overall a very good purchase that will provide you will endless hours of playtime if you can find a server to suit your tastes.

My first A3L experience:
*Le me speeding down the street in my car when suddenly a wild police officer appears from alley*
"10-20 on the 10-72; Kavala Square." He says into his radio, his sirens wailing and lights flickering. I take a sharp turn to the left, making the officer fly 20 feet into the sky, his hatchback giving its final, saddening yell before plummeting to the ground, exploding and killing the officer on impact.
I turn around, a Hunter and two SUVs headed my way: I must escape quickly! I held shift, accelerating my car by 10km/h. I proceeded down the road that I originally aimed for, soon turning into a dark alley to avoid contact with the law-enforcement.
"NEEEEEEOW!"
A series of blue lights and sirens sounded past my location. I was safe; or at least I thought so. Before I could realise, a PD helicopter was patrolling the skies, soon discovering and announcing my location. As its beam of light beaconed at me, I reversed from the tight space, and sped to the town centre - Kavala square.
Disobeying the speeding limit, I held my finger firmly on the shift key, knowing that if I let go I'd be trampled and macerated by the Hunters that persued me. Realising that the whole of Kavala PD was now shadowing me, I lead them to their unexpected deaths: attempting to de-sync ram those like the detective I eliminated before. It wasn't long until they raced down the street - I stuck the front of my vehicle out of the gap, sending the impenetrable Hunter to its destined death.
Untouched, my car remained in pristine condition, however I was still in pursuit. Locked onto me, the chopper hovered above, revealing my position. Intimidated, I abandoned my Offroad and scrapped my clothes, sprinting to the suit-store. I purchased a cheap hobo-outfit and ran back to my car, only to realise it is now under the jurisdiction of the cops as they formed a road-block, defending the crime-scene.
Attempting to explain to the officers that the vehicle belongs to "my friend", they stated that I should leave. In protest, I stole (however I do not think of it as stealing, rather borrowing my own ride) the OffRoad, detonating two police cars and myself during the process.
TLDR: I rammed some cops, abandoned the car, changed clothes, stole the vehicle back and we all exploded.

It's interesting to say the least. If you enjoyed Portal 2's single player campaign, I'd say this is hands down worth a try.
It excels in story, music, visuals, and the chambers themselves. While this mod's story obviously doesn't have the breadth of Portal 2, it's fantastic for it's length. The music is wonderful and provides great atmosphere without being intrusive. The models and textures are as good as the original game. Voice acting is also very high quality.
Overall, despite some small areas that lack polish, it's very high quality. If Prism Studios were to make another mod or game like this, I would be willing to pay money for it.
The difficulty factor on the chambers is higher than Portal or it's sequel, and I welcomed that. Even better, unlike Portal: Prelude for example, the difficulty in this mod is only increased in the puzzle-solving aspects. Once you understand the solution it's fairly easy to execute. Most other portal mods and maps are simple to understand, but require insanely hard movement and coordination. I think this mod provides a more enjoyable flavor of gameplay.
Some parts come off as _very_ similar both in story and gameplay to sections of Portal 2's campaign. This would be unacceptable in a standalone game that wasn't otherwise related to Portal 2. Keep in mind however, that this is a free mod directly based off of Portal 2, and as such should be judged by different standards.
Bottom line, give it a try. I honestly don't think you'll regret it. If you do, you can always get a refund for the $0 you spent.

This Mod offers a fairly high amount of those moments, when you sit there, wondering: "Am i really this stupid? ... Oh that's how it's done!". Once you find the solution, there is nothing more satisfying and you just want to give yourself a little applause and tap on the shoulder. The Puzzles are slightly more difficult than the ones in the original game, which offers a fun, new and challenging experience and the length of this Mod could probably qualify this as an official DLC. Even the Story is definatly worth paying attention to, due to the on-point voice acting. Sure, there are some hickups here and there, but this is a community made Mod, not a thousand-dollar-project. Some ideas got recycled, which you will definetly notice throughout the game and some ideas are new to the Portal universe, which you will enjoy, since it offers a fresh and innovative feeling. The Level design is pretty amazing and offers a really unique atmosphere that lets you forget the few "too-dark" or "too-unthemed" areas (which are very rare!). Also, the custom Models are brilliantly made, not just the Portal-gun.
All in all, this raises the bar for future Mods to an unreachable level. Unless someone comes up with something super unique and stunning, this will be the #01 Portal 2 Mod. Probably until the game dies.
